session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: Today (August 18, 2025) I started the 16:8 intermittent fasting method. I had a roast meat combo rice and Hong Kong-style milk tea at 12:00 PM, finished before 1:00 PM, and had dinner on time at 5:30 PM. Is this arrangement correct? Are there any other things I should pay attention to?

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: Your schedule is basically correct: 16 hours of fasting from 17:30 to 9:30 the next day. However, Hong Kong-style milk tea contains high sugar, which may stimulate insulin and affect the fasting effect. It is recommended to switch to a sugar-free drink. Within the eating window, pay attention to balanced nutrition: increase vegetables and high-quality protein (such as chicken breast and fish), and control the proportion of refined carbohydrates.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: Got it. Then what should I do in the afternoon if I feel hungry or my energy drops? I usually do interval running. How should I coordinate that with fasting?

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: When hungry, drinking water or black coffee can help relieve it. Interval running is recommended to be scheduled at the end of the eating window (e.g., before 5 p.m.) or as a fasted morning run, and protein should be replenished promptly after exercise. Monitor your body's responses to avoid hypoglycemia; in the early stage, you can appropriately shorten the fasting period to adapt gradually.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: This morning I did 400m x 8 intervals at Kowloon Tsai Park, pace 4:50, training in light rain. I stretched afterward, but my knees and hamstrings still feel sore and tight, and I'm worried it will affect my upcoming marathon training.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: Interval running is quite intense, and soreness in the knees and hamstrings is common, possibly due to patellar pressure or muscle fatigue. Tomorrow morning, it is recommended to rest or do an easy run first. Today, you can ice the knees for 15 minutes and roll the hamstrings with a foam roller.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: Can I use ice and a foam roller in the evening? Are there any more effective stretches to prevent runner's knee?

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: Yes. Ice within 2 hours after exercise is best, and keep the foam roller away from bones. I recommend doing 3 sets each of wall sits and hamstring static stretches every day, and move slowly. If pain or swelling persists, see a doctor to check for chondromalacia patellae.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: Hello, tonight I studied Chapter 1 of the CFP investment module, on asset allocation and the Sharpe ratio. Some concepts are not clear to me. For example, how exactly is the Sharpe ratio calculated? What practical use does it have for me when I recommend savings insurance to clients?

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: The Sharpe ratio measures how much excess return an investment portfolio earns per unit of risk, with the formula (portfolio return - risk-free return) / portfolio standard deviation. In insurance sales, it can be used to compare the risk-adjusted returns of different savings insurance products and help high-net-worth clients make rational choices. Asset allocation, on the other hand, emphasizes diversification by allocating proportions of stocks, bonds, and other assets according to the client's risk tolerance.

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_230.text: I see. So suppose I have a client who wants to compare two savings insurance products — one with slightly higher returns but greater volatility, and the other with stable but lower returns. Can the Sharpe ratio tell us which one offers better value?

session_230.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_230.text: Right, the higher the Sharpe ratio, the better the return per unit of risk. If the data allows, you can calculate the Sharpe ratios of the two products (be sure to use the same risk-free rate) and make a recommendation based on the client’s risk preference. Also, the CFP exam may ask you to calculate or interpret the Sharpe ratio, so it’s a good idea to do more practice questions to consolidate your understanding.

session_233.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_233.text: ETF tracking error refers to the deviation between the fund's net value and the index. Active fund fees include management fees, custodian fees, and sales service fees, which can be as high as 1.5%-2%, and long-term holding can significantly erode returns. Simple rule: ETFs are cheaper but may deviate; active funds are more expensive but aim for excess returns.

When answering exam questions, focus on the key points: ETFs have tracking error and passive replication, while active funds have higher fee costs but offer stock-picking flexibility. I suggest you compare the actual fee schedules of the Tracker Fund and an active fund to deepen your memory.

session_237.text: In my options practice questions, I always mix up the relationships between these Greek letters — Delta, Gamma, Vega — and volatility, especially Vega's impact when implied volatility rises. Can you help me sort this out?

session_237.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_237.text: You seem to be confusing the intuitive meanings of the Greek letters and their relationship with volatility assumptions. I suggest remembering them from a 'risk exposure' perspective: Delta is price sensitivity, Gamma is the rate of change of Delta, Vega is implied volatility sensitivity, and Theta is time decay. When implied volatility rises, Vega, being positively correlated, pushes option prices up; as time approaches expiration, Theta, being negatively correlated, accelerates decay. Would you like me to use a concrete example to help you consolidate this?

session_237.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_237.text: Right, the questions I got wrong are about Gamma hedging and the effect of Vega, such as how a call option's price changes when volatility rises. Can you give a simple example?

session_237.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_237.text: Suppose an at-the-money call option with the underlying price at 100, implied volatility rises from 20% to 30%, Vega = 0.35, then the option price will rise by about 0.35 × (30% - 20%) = 3.5 yuan. As for Gamma, when the underlying price is 100, Gamma is largest and Delta changes quickly; if you want neutral hedging, you need to continuously adjust the Delta position — high-frequency hedging reduces risk, while low-frequency can rely on Gamma scalping. It is recommended to memorize it using the mnemonic 'As volatility rises, Vega gains; as time passes, Theta loses,' combined with the 'positive/negative sign' rules of the Greek letters in the practice problems.

session_240.text: I just finished calculating the expected return and risk of a stock portfolio using the CAPM model and the variance-covariance matrix, but I feel the weighted average method I used to calculate the portfolio beta may not be rigorous. Could you help me double-check the logic? Also, I'm a bit unclear about the relationship between the efficient frontier and the capital market line.

session_240.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_240.text: Are you worried that the weighted average beta ignores the covariance between stocks? In fact, portfolio beta does equal the market-cap-weighted average of individual stock betas, which is guaranteed by the linear property of CAPM; but the portfolio return variance requires the covariance matrix. As for the efficient frontier and CAL: the efficient frontier is the optimal set of risky asset portfolios. After adding the risk-free asset, the tangency point of the CAL and the efficient frontier is the market portfolio, and this line is the capital market line (CML). Do you need me to break down the derivation steps in detail?

session_240.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_240.text: Yes, I'm just torn about whether the weighted average can accurately reflect portfolio risk, and the meaning of the tangency point between the CML and the efficient frontier. Can you give me a solution template for a similar problem to compare?

session_240.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_240.text: Okay, let me provide a typical template: 1) Collect the betas and weights of individual stocks, and weight them to get the portfolio beta; 2) Use the variance-covariance matrix to calculate the portfolio variance (note the covariance terms); 3) Substitute into CAPM to find the expected return; 4) If a risk-free asset is considered, the slope of the CML is (market portfolio return - risk-free rate) / market portfolio standard deviation. The line connecting each point on the efficient frontier to Rf is the CAL, and the tangency point is the optimal risky portfolio. If you follow these steps in your homework, it should be fine. Would you like me to turn this template into a step-by-step checklist?

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_243.text: This morning I ran an 18 km LSD with a running buddy along the Whampoa Waterfront Promenade at a pace of 6:40. I stretched for 15 minutes after the run, but my calves still feel tight, and the old injury on my ankle is aching faintly. I'm worried it may relapse. Is there a scientific recovery method?

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_243.text: Recommendations: 1) Apply ice to the ankle immediately for 15 minutes, and use a warm compress in the evening to promote blood circulation; 2) Focus on static stretches of the soleus and gastrocnemius muscles, holding each movement for 30 seconds, and use a foam roller to relax the hips; 3) Replenish protein and electrolytes, especially paying attention to hydration and branched-chain amino acids. If the pain persists, it is recommended to pause high-intensity training.

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_243.text: Okay, I'll try. How should next week's training plan be adjusted? There's a race next month. I don't want my performance to slip, but I'm afraid of getting injured.

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_243.text: It is recommended to use a cutback week next week: run a 10 km aerobic run on Wednesday (pace 7:00), do 40 minutes of cross-training on Friday (such as swimming or cycling), do a 15 km LSD on Saturday (pace 6:50), and rest completely on Sunday. Focus on strengthening ankle stability training, such as calf raises and elastic band resistance eversion, and activate the gluteus medius before each session to reduce ankle strain.

Considering that you are busy with work and family, you can set aside 30 minutes of fragmented time each day for practice questions and use 1 hour at night to tackle difficult points. Would you like me to help you put together a detailed schedule or recommend materials?

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_243.text: This plan is quite practical, especially for learning in fragmented time. Could you recommend a few high-quality mock exam sets? I want to first gauge my current level.

session_243.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_243.text: I recommend using the official mock exams from the CFP Association and the supplementary exercises in Principles of Financial Planning. Also, the CAPM calculation questions you just finished are key, so you can do 2 timed practice sets each week. If you're short on time, focus first on the wrong questions and formula derivations. Would you like me to help you make a four-week review plan?

session_244.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_244.text: Just finished 10 x 400m interval runs at Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground. The last set was at a 4:45/km pace, and I hit a flow state—it felt amazing! session_244.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_244.text: The flow experience is great, indicating that your current pace matches your neural focus well. Suggestions: 1) Do interval running 1-2 times per week, control recovery time between sets to 90-120 seconds, and start the next set only after your heart rate drops to 65% of your maximum heart rate; 2) Apply ice to your left ankle for 15 minutes each time, immediately after training; if soreness persists, adjust the intensity; 3) During the mid-phase of race preparation, you can use interval running as a means to increase speed, combined with long-distance endurance running and yoga cross-training, to avoid a single training load.

session_244.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_244.text: Got it. How exactly should I set the threshold for heart rate monitoring? I usually use a running watch, but I don't know what data to look at during intervals.

session_244.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_244.text: During interval efforts, heart rate can reach 85%–90% of maximum heart rate (about 170–180 bpm), and recover to 65% (about 130 bpm) between sets before starting the next set. Watch for heart rate drift: if your heart rate drops slowly during recovery, the intensity is overloaded, so you need to extend rest or reduce pace. In addition, Coach Zhao Zhiming’s advice may be more personalized; you can also give him feedback on your flow state and left ankle reaction.

session_245.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_245.text: I'm reviewing CFP investment planning tonight. I don't fully understand the capital asset pricing model questions, especially the beta coefficient and its practical application. Can you help me clarify it?

session_245.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_245.text: Your main confusion is about the CAPM formula, the meaning of the beta coefficient, and how to apply it to client asset allocation, right?

session_245.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_245.text: Yes, for example, when allocating education funds, how should CAPM be used to evaluate risk and return?

session_245.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_245.text: CAPM core: expected return = risk-free rate + β × (market risk premium). β measures a stock's volatility relative to the market; β > 1 indicates higher risk. In practice, first set the target portfolio's β, then match it to the client's risk tolerance; for example, for a conservative allocation choose assets with β < 1. Want me to give an example?

session_245.text: After doing yoga today, my left ankle feels a bit better, but it was somewhat uncomfortable during activity this morning. session_245.text: You are worried that the old injury to your left ankle will affect your training, so you need to distinguish between fatigue-related discomfort and warning signs of injury, and also get targeted stability training and advice on adjusting tomorrow's running plan.

session_245.speaker: Yu Xiaowei

session_245.text: It is recommended to do a pain-free test first: stand on one leg for 30 seconds and do 10 calf raises. If there is no severe pain, you can shorten it to a 5 km low-intensity run, slowing down the pace and adding dynamic warm-ups before running (ankle circles, high knees) and a 10-minute ice pack after running. At home, you can use yoga blocks or resistance bands for ankle eversion and calf raise exercises, 2 sets per day. If there is obvious pain during the test, it is recommended to rest and see a doctor for examination.

session_246.text: Today I signed a big high-end medical insurance deal in Shenzhen, and I feel a great sense of accomplishment! But my boss reminded me to balance the Shenzhen market with maintaining local clients. I'm feeling a bit conflicted and would like to hear your advice.

session_246.text: Congratulations! It really is worth being happy about. What you need is probably a concrete strategy for efficiently maintaining local clients while expanding into new markets, such as how to screen clients, manage time, or communicate?

session_246.text: Yes, I plan to make 20 calls tomorrow for policy reviews, but I'm worried it will affect family time, and I also want to keep my running habit.

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_246.text: You could try setting aside two fixed days a week for Shenzhen business and using the rest of the time for focused local visits. Before calls, classify clients by value: 15 minutes for key clients, 5 minutes for regular clients. For family, reserve one hour for work after dinner and spend the rest of the time wholeheartedly with them. Schedule running in the morning; there's no conflict.

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_246.text: After a 3 km morning run today, my left ankle felt a bit uncomfortable. I've already applied ice for 10 minutes. I have a history of ankle sprains and am worried about a recurrence. I still need to run 16 km on Sunday. What should I do?

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_246.text: There is mild discomfort now and you've been icing it, but first you need to check for swelling or restricted movement. Compare both ankles for redness and swelling, press for tender points, and test the ankle's range of motion in all directions. If there's anything abnormal, I don't recommend the long run on Sunday; if it's normal, you can continue with recovery measures.

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_246.text: There is no obvious swelling, and movement is normal, just a faint sensation. How should recovery and training be arranged for the next few days?

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_246.text: Suggestions: 1) Ice 3-4 times a day, 15 minutes each time, with 2 hours between applications; 2) Do non-weight-bearing ankle mobility exercises, such as writing letters in the air; 3) Pause running and switch to swimming or upper-body strength training; 4) Do a low-intensity dynamic warm-up test on Saturday; if there is no discomfort, run 8 km at a slower pace on Sunday, and don’t force 16 km. For long-term prevention: strengthen the muscles around the ankle, such as heel raises and resistance band exercises.

session_246.text: On Sunday morning, my running buddy and I agreed to meet at 7 a.m. at Hung Hom Pier to run 16 kilometers round trip along the Kwun Tong Promenade. Can you check the weather and sea breeze conditions for that time? Also, is the route closed due to construction?

session_246.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_246.text: Right, tell me more specifically what hydration and energy gels to bring, and how to warm up after meeting up with running friends? Also, how should I adjust my diet and rest on Saturday?

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_254.text: Hello, tonight I am in my study preparing for the CFP. I just finished 20 risk management practice questions and got 4 wrong. One of them was about types of reinsurance, and I wrote down the question: 'What exactly is the difference between proportional and non-proportional reinsurance?' Can you explain it now with a plain example?

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_254.text: Of course. Proportional reinsurance is sharing risk by insured amount, such as quota share reinsurance (ceding premiums and losses by a fixed percentage) and surplus reinsurance (ceding the portion above the retention proportionally). Non-proportional reinsurance is sharing by loss amount, such as excess of loss reinsurance (the part above the agreed deductible is borne by the reinsurer) and stop-loss reinsurance (triggered when the annual loss ratio exceeds a threshold). Simply put: proportional is 'cutting the cake', non-proportional is 'guarding against catastrophe'.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_254.text: Mhm, that analogy is good. Can you give a practical example? For instance, a case from auto insurance or property insurance, to help me understand it better.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_254.text: Okay. Suppose the primary insurer underwrites a car insurance policy with a sum insured of 500,000 yuan and a retention of 200,000 yuan. Under quota share reinsurance with a 50% cession, 250,000 yuan would be ceded; under surplus reinsurance, the portion exceeding 200,000 yuan (300,000 yuan) would be fully ceded. This is proportional reinsurance. Non-proportional reinsurance, such as per-risk excess of loss: assume the deductible for each accident is set at 100,000 yuan; if the loss is 250,000 yuan, the excess of 150,000 yuan is borne by the reinsurer. It is suitable for frequent small losses. You can use the logic framework 'proportional shares the amount insured, non-proportional shares the loss' to remember.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_254.text: I understand. Proportional means both premiums and claims are shared proportionally, while non-proportional only looks at whether claims exceed the threshold. So 'stop-loss' reinsurance is non-proportional, right? This was mentioned in my practice errors.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_254.text: Correct. Stop-loss reinsurance (loss ratio excess of loss) is indeed a type of non-proportional reinsurance. It sets a threshold based on the overall loss ratio within a year; for example, the portion of the loss ratio exceeding 80% is borne by the reinsurer. It is often used to guard against accumulation risk. I suggest you write on a sticky note: Proportional (quota share/surplus) -> ceded sum insured; Non-proportional (per risk/per occurrence/loss ratio excess of loss) -> ceded loss. That way, it will be clear at a glance when you review on the weekend.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_254.text: I understand your concern. You want to find a way to explain things that suits an active boy (ENFP), while also confirming whether your tutoring approach is reasonable. I suggest three steps: first, use a shopping scenario (like calculating the total price) to introduce the arithmetic concept; then break down the vertical calculation steps (multiply the ones digit, multiply the tens digit, then add); finally, use building blocks or games to reinforce carrying and alignment. Your patience and persistence are already a good foundation, and you can combine these techniques to tutor more easily.

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_254.text: I did teach step-by-step calculation first, but the child tends to ignore carrying and misalign the digits. Are there any specific fun little tricks to prevent mistakes?

session_254.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_254.text: You can try the "carrying train" method: use two slips of paper to represent the ones and tens places, and after each calculation step, "drive the train" to send the carried digit to the next place. In addition, use colored pens to mark the place values (ones in red, tens in blue), align them, and then calculate. This visualization both prevents distraction and adds a sense of play. Your method tonight was completely correct; just adding these details will make it more efficient.

session_265.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_265.text: I understand. In Hong Kong estate tax exemption, 'continuous residence' means actually living in Hong Kong during the 3 years immediately before death. Exceptions include: leaving Hong Kong for official duties (e.g., business trips representing the Hong Kong government) or medical treatment (e.g., going overseas for treatment), each absence not exceeding 30 days; these days still count toward the residence period. For example, if Mr. Wang took business trips totaling 45 days over the 3 years, but no single trip exceeded 30 days, he still meets the continuous residence condition. The exam often tests the 'single trip' rather than 'cumulative' limit, so this needs attention.

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_266.text: I'm reviewing CFP estate tax planning and I'm not clear about the calculation of insurance exemption rules and dynamic adjustment of deductions. Can you help me break down a typical example?

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_266.text: Okay. Suppose a client's total estate is 20 million yuan, with a spousal exemption of 5 million yuan, charitable donations of 2 million yuan, a tax-exempt amount of 10 million yuan, and a progressive tax rate of 10%-20%. If the 3 million yuan in insurance proceeds has a designated beneficiary and meets the exemption conditions, it is not included in the estate. Calculation steps: first determine the taxable estate = total estate - tax-exempt amount - various deductions - exempt insurance proceeds, then calculate the tax in brackets according to the excess progressive tax rate. Do you need me to explain each step in detail?

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_266.text: Yes, for example, what does dynamic adjustment of the deduction mean? Does the insurance premium waiver require the beneficiary to be the spouse?

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_266.text: Dynamic adjustment means that the allowable deductions may change with inflation or legal revisions; for example, in 2025 the spousal exemption was raised from 5 million to 5.5 million. The insurance proceeds exemption requires that the beneficiary is not the estate executor; a spouse or other designated person is acceptable, but if the policy's cash value belongs to the deceased, it must be included. I suggest that when practicing, you first confirm the taxpayer's identity and exemption conditions, then apply the latest deduction standards.

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_266.text: I'm insurance agent Yu Xiaowei. The client, Mrs. Chen, is 48 years old, a homemaker, with a history of thyroid nodules. She wants to increase her critical illness coverage by 30% and also add protection for her new home. What are the latest industry standards for underwriting thyroid nodules? What are the common underwriting decisions (extra premium/exclusion) among insurance companies? How should a comprehensive plan that includes coverage for the new home be designed?

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_266.text: Underwriting for thyroid nodules is mainly based on the TI-RADS grade: Grades 1-2 are usually covered under standard terms; Grade 3 may be subject to exclusions or an additional premium (approximately 10-30%); Grades 4 and above are generally declined or postponed. Common underwriting decisions include excluding thyroid cancer and its metastases. For new home protection, it is recommended to pair with mortgage insurance (such as term life insurance or decreasing term life insurance), with the sum insured covering the remaining loan. Critical illness insurance and mortgage insurance can be purchased in combination; pay attention to the total premium budget.

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_266.text: Understood. Suppose Mrs. Chen's current coverage amount is 500,000 yuan; after a 30% increase, it becomes 650,000 yuan. If the underwriting result is thyroid exclusion, what would the approximate additional premium percentage be? Could you provide a premium estimate?

session_266.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_266.text: Taking a common market product as an example, an exclusion clause usually does not increase the premium; it only excludes thyroid cancer coverage. If a premium loading is applied, based on an approximate 20% loading for Grade 3 nodules: assuming the original premium for a 48-year-old woman with a 20-year payment period is about 300 yuan per 10,000 yuan of sum assured, the annual premium for 650,000 yuan of sum assured is about 19,500 yuan, and after the loading it is about 23,400 yuan. The actual result is subject to the insurance company's underwriting. It is recommended to prioritize the exclusion clause option to lower the premium; if a loading is applied, consider reducing the sum assured to 600,000 yuan. For the new home protection, you can separately buy a 1 million yuan mortgage insurance with an annual premium of about 800-1,200 yuan for a 20-year term.

After obtaining the posterior return, re-optimize. The final stock weight may rise to 68%. It is recommended to do a written calculation problem, focusing on mastering the view-combining formula and parameter settings.

session_284.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant

You can calculate the annualized cost difference. For example, the threshold strategy trades two more times, costing about 1% versus 0.5%, and the returns need to cover that.

session_285.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_285.text: Right, the rebalancing frequency question compares excess returns and costs under calendar-based and threshold-based strategies; the CAPM question gives the risk-free rate and market return, and asks for a stock's beta and expected return.

session_285.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_285.text: Understood. Rebalancing frequency: threshold rebalancing can flexibly control deviation costs, but a deviation threshold (e.g., 5%) needs to be set, and it suits volatile markets; calendar rebalancing has a simple fixed cycle and suits cost-sensitive investors. CAPM beta calculation: first take the covariance between the stock and the market portfolio divided by the market variance, then plug in Rf and Rm to get the expected return. I suggest you work through a typical problem by hand and compare similar variations in past exam questions.

session_288.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_288.text: I just learned about overconfidence, confirmation bias, and loss aversion in behavioral finance. Can you give me an example related to insurance sales?

session_288.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_288.text: Overconfidence in insurance sales often shows up as clients thinking that risk is far away from them; you need to use data to explain the probability of accidents. Confirmation bias means clients focus only on information that matches their own views; you can guide clients to consider risks comprehensively. Loss aversion means that emphasizing the potential losses of not buying insurance is more likely to close a policy than emphasizing the benefits.

session_288.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_288.text: That makes sense! Also, I came across a multiple-choice question I'm not sure about: a client only pays attention to news about stock market rises and ignores the risk of declines. What kind of bias is this?

session_288.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_288.text: It is confirmation bias. The client subconsciously filters out information that supports their existing beliefs and ignores contradicting evidence. When answering, note the distinction — confirmation bias concerns selective reception of information, while overconfidence is more about exaggeration in self-assessment.

session_295.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_295.text: I just reviewed the beta coefficient and the Sharpe ratio, but I'm not clear about their boundaries and limitations in practical application. Could you explain them in plain terms?

session_295.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_295.text: Beta coefficient measures a stock's sensitivity relative to the market, but it applies only to assets that are listed and have historical data, and it assumes market risk is the only pricing factor. The Sharpe ratio compares risk-adjusted returns, but it depends heavily on the choice of risk-free rate and can easily become distorted for high-risk assets with skewed or fat-tailed distributions. Now that you understand these, would you like a comprehensive self-test question to reinforce it?

session_295.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_295.text: Yes, please give me a practice question, preferably one that combines the practical application of these two concepts.

session_295.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_295.text: Question: A technology fund has a beta of 1.8, an annual return of 22%, and the market return over the same period is 12%, with a risk-free rate of 2%. Another bond fund has a beta of 0.4, an annual return of 6%, and a risk-free rate of 2%. Use the Sharpe ratio to compare which one offers better value, and explain the limitations of the beta coefficient in this context. (Hint: First calculate the Sharpe ratio of each fund separately, then consider whether a high beta means higher risk-adjusted returns.)

session_302.text: Today I used the Pomodoro Technique to do 12 CFP investment planning calculation questions. session_302.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_302.text: Understood. You have questions about calculating the standard deviation of an investment portfolio and applying the CAPM model. Specifically, are you stuck on deriving the formula, plugging in the data, or interpreting the final result? Could you tell me the key values or conditions in the problem?

session_302.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_302.text: I'm mainly stuck on calculating the variance of two asset portfolios. For example, after being given weights, standard deviations, and correlation coefficients, I always mix up the signs when substituting into the formula. Also, I'm not sure about selecting the beta coefficient and market risk premium in CAPM.

session_302.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_302.text: Okay. The portfolio variance formula is σ²_p = w₁²σ₁² + w₂²σ₂² + 2w₁w₂σ₁σ₂ρ. Note that the last term has a plus sign; if ρ is negative, it naturally becomes subtraction. In CAPM, beta is calculated by dividing the covariance of asset returns and market returns by the market variance. The risk premium is the expected market return minus the risk-free rate. I suggest you first organize the weights and correlation coefficients, then calculate step by step.

session_302.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_302.text: Got it, I'll recalculate. By the way, do these types of questions have common traps in the exam? For example, the sign of the correlation coefficient or the range of beta values?

session_302.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_302.text: Common pitfalls include: ignoring the direction of the correlation coefficient, leading to sign errors; forgetting to standardize when using historical data to calculate beta; and mistakenly using the nominal interest rate instead of the real interest rate for the risk premium. It is recommended to check whether data units are consistent when practicing, and pay attention to implicit conditions in the question.

session_303.text: Okay, please calculate: Suppose an asset has an expected return of 15%, the risk-free rate is 3%, and the standard deviation is 20%; the market portfolio has an expected return of 10% and a standard deviation of 15%, and the asset's correlation with the market is 0.8. session_303.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_303.text: Sharpe ratio = (15%-3%)/20% = 0.6; for Jensen's alpha, first calculate beta = 0.8*(20%/15%) = 1.067, then alpha = 15% - [3% + 1.067*(10%-3%)] = 15% - 10.47% = 4.53%. Is that correct?

session_314.text: I just came back from Guangzhou. I tried seed stitch, but I'm unsure about the combination of stitches and the composition. Can you give me some advice?

session_314.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_314.text: I understand you want to use cool tones and layering to present the tranquility and luminosity of the snow scene. I suggest using the rolling stitch for the river's glistening light, seed stitch for the snowflakes, and straight stitch to outline the Canton Tower. For colors, transition with white and silver-gray silk threads; choose dark blue or gray-blue fabric to better highlight the luminous effect. Would you like me to further refine the composition sections?

session_314.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_314.text: Right, combining the rolling stitch and seed stitch sounds nice. I'm also worried about the overall layout—how should the pagoda and the river surface be proportioned to emphasize that hazy winter feel?

session_314.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_314.text: Use the rule of thirds for the composition: leave the top third blank or lightly embroider clouds; use the middle third for a simplified outline of the Canton Tower (satin stitch + fine stem stitch); and use the bottom third for the river surface (seed stitch to dot small snowflakes, and long stem stitches at an angle to embroider the glimmering water). For the tower body, use a silver-gray gradient; for the river, brighten it with white silk thread. You can add a small snowflake detail in the lower right corner as a finishing touch. session_322.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_322.text: My father told me last night that he bought a non-principal-protected structured product through an old friend's introduction, and it has now lost 30%, amounting to HK$100,000. I am an insurance agent but do not understand this type of investment, and I feel very guilty and anxious. I would like to ask you to analyze what this product is, why it has lost money, and how I can stop the loss or recover it?

session_322.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_322.text: Non-principal-protected structured products usually have returns linked to an underlying asset (such as stocks or an index). A 30% loss suggests that a high-leverage clause may have been triggered, and the current market is quite volatile. I suggest you first communicate calmly with your father to confirm the product term, the underlying asset, and the termination conditions. For short-term loss control, you can ask the bank whether there is an early redemption option, but note that part of the lost principal may already be locked in. Be cautious when using the family emergency fund; I recommend keeping 3-6 months of living expenses first, and then evaluate whether the rest can be replenished. Don't blame yourself too much. You've already recognized the risk; handling it in time is what matters.

session_322.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_322.text: Thank you for your analysis. I plan to talk to my father alone this week. But he is quite stubborn. How can I gently help him accept reality and cooperate with me on follow-up handling? Also, if the product cannot be redeemed, is it reasonable to use part of the emergency fund to cover the gap in his pension?

session_322.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_322.text: When communicating, first show empathy, for example, “I know you're doing this for your family; no one expected the market to be this bad,” then rationally present the loss facts and remaining value. Avoid blame and emphasize solving things together. As for the emergency fund, I suggest not touching it; the loss has already occurred, and the pension gap is best made up through extra savings by you and your younger brother or by adjusting the long-term family allocation. The emergency fund should be used only for unexpected emergencies. If needed, I can help you sort out a stop-loss checklist and communication scripts.

Early redemption usually requires a penalty of 3-5%, and the value is already low. During the weekend communication, it is suggested to focus on risk rather than blame.

Given your conservative style, I suggest prioritizing keeping at least 6 months of living expenses as an emergency fund, and only consider short-term support from the remaining amount, while replenishing the gap as soon as possible through surplus funds or conservative financial products such as fixed deposits and government bonds.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Tomorrow at 3 p.m., I'm taking my father to the bank in Kowloon City to handle the conversion of his fixed-term wealth management product. I have the procedure and documents ready, but I want to double-check everything again to avoid any omissions.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: Okay. The standard procedure is: take a number after arriving at the bank; if you have an appointment, you can get priority. Materials needed: your father's original ID card, a photocopy, wealth management contract, and insurance policy documents. Since your father is elderly, he must sign in person; you can accompany him to confirm. When converting, pay attention to handling fees and redemption time, and it is recommended to learn about the risk level of the new product in advance.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Thank you. Does my father need to bring the original ID card? How many copies are needed? Also, is there a big difference in risk between bank wealth management products and insurance wealth management products?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: Prepare 2 copies as backup. Bank wealth management products usually protect the principal or carry low risk, while insurance-based wealth management focuses on long-term savings, combining returns and protection. It is recommended to choose based on your father's risk tolerance; if he prefers a conservative approach, selecting a principal-guaranteed bank product is safer.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Understood. I'll work first tomorrow and leave at 2:30 pm. Is that enough time?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: More than enough. It takes about half an hour from home to the bank; arriving 15 minutes early is fine. Remember to bring the complete folder. If your father is in good spirits, the communication will go more smoothly.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: I just finished the training on the new critical illness product. I want to sort out the core selling points, especially the details of multiple cancer payouts and cardiovascular coverage, so I can recommend it to clients.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: You need to confirm the waiting period, number of payouts, and coverage limits for multiple cancer claims, as well as the scope of coverage for cardiovascular diseases? At the same time, compare market competitors to create differentiated sales scripts?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Yes, for example, is the interval for multiple cancer payouts 3 years or 5 years? What specific diseases are covered under cardiovascular protection? And what about the impact of premium adjustments on existing customers?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: The new product's interval for multiple cancer claims is 3 years, with a maximum of 2 payouts, each paying 100% of the sum insured. Cardiovascular coverage includes 12 conditions such as acute myocardial infarction and coronary artery bypass graft surgery. As for premium policy, existing customers who convert to the new policy can enjoy a 20% discount in the first year. Compared with similar products from Prudential and Manulife, our cancer claim conditions are more lenient, and our cardiovascular disease coverage is more comprehensive.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Good. Then for a wealthy housewife like Chen Meiling, how can I naturally open the pitch? I'm afraid that bringing up illness directly will turn her off.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: Suggestion: approach from the angle of family health protection, for example: 'Sister Meiling, the company recently upgraded its critical illness coverage, with special enhancements for women's and cardiovascular protection. I know you have always cared about your family's health. Would you like to take 3 minutes to look at the highlights of the upgrade?' Emphasize "upgrade" rather than "new product" to lower her guard.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: My son Zhang Zixuan won his weekend football match. I want to encourage him to keep improving, but I’m afraid it will affect his studies. Any good suggestions?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: You hope to find encouragement strategies that can both unleash his football potential and keep his studies balanced, and you might also want to know how to specifically praise his successes and build time-management habits, right?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: Yes, sometimes a simple response isn't enough. I want to guide him more strategically, and I'm also worried that exercise is taking up too much time.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: It is recommended to use "process praise" instead of outcome praise, for example praising his active tackling or teamwork. At the same time, set fixed weekly slots for sports and study (e.g., practice ball after school on Wednesdays/Fridays, matches on weekend mornings, and focused homework in the evenings), and use Hong Kong community football courses or school team tryouts to develop his abilities.

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_342.text: This suggestion is great; the specific praise approach is very inspiring. Do you have any recommendations for community courses?

session_342.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_342.text: The Leisure and Cultural Services Department's "Community Sports Club" offers children's football classes that focus on fundamentals and fun. You can also look into the Hong Kong Football Association's "Youth Development Program", which is suitable for an 8-year-old to improve his skills. You could also let him join the school team, which offers both social interaction and training. If you need coach resources, I can provide more information later.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: After today's performance review, Liang Zhenhua postponed my promotion to June or July next year. Although I met my performance targets, I still feel a lot of pressure and want to talk to someone.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: It sounds like you've put in a lot of effort but haven't received immediate recognition. Would you like me to help you analyze the specific feelings and sort out the next steps?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: Yes, I proactively paused the Shenzhen market and decided to focus on Hong Kong's local mid-to-high-end segment, but I'm not sure whether this adjustment will let me deliver results in half a year, and I also have two children at home to take care of.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: Your strategic adjustment was very decisive. I suggest visiting 15 existing clients on a fixed weekly basis for the next six months, launching an “exclusive referral gift pack for existing clients” to boost loyalty, and also signing up for CFP or RFP certification to add professional credibility. On the family side, set a fixed weekend family time with your husband—for example, Saturday mornings with the children and afternoons focused on work. This way, you can quickly produce local results and also balance family.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: Today I accompanied my father to Bank of Communications to handle a wealth management product conversion. He is 62 years old and retired, conservative in personality, and only chooses low-risk fixed-income products. My own family has an annual income of 400,000 yuan, and my investment style is also very conservative—our assets are only property and a car. I would like to know how to build a steady asset allocation for my father. At the same time, my family hopes to achieve a promotion within the next three years and travel to Japan within five years. How should we adjust our financial planning?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: You are mainly concerned with two levels: first, the liquidity, safety, and moderate returns of your father's pension; second, shifting your own family from overly conservative to more reasonable asset allocation to support the five-year medium-term goal (travel) and a promotion within three years (which may come with a higher income). Is that right?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: Right, my father's money absolutely cannot lose value, and I don't want to take too much risk myself either, but I feel it's too conservative now and returns can't keep up with inflation. I hope for a balanced plan.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: Pension advice for Father: allocate 70% to large-denomination certificates of deposit or government bonds from major banks (safety + liquidity), 20% to short-term annuity insurance (locking in interest rates), and 10% to money market funds for emergencies. For your own family: convert 40% of annual savings to 'fixed income +' funds (80% bonds + 20% stocks, low volatility), put 30% into 3-year time deposits or large-denomination CDs, use 20% to regularly invest in short-term bond funds for travel goals, and allocate 10% to term medical insurance (to guard against unexpected expenses). This way, overall risk is controllable and the goals can be achieved.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: This approach is good, especially the "fixed income +" funds, which I hadn't looked into before. I can go back and research it. Regarding my father, he just signed the wealth management product conversion. Does he have to wait until maturity before operating?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: Yes, bank wealth management products usually have a lock-up period or are open at regular intervals. It's better to first confirm the maturity date or redemption rules of the product your father just signed. Redeeming before maturity will incur a fee loss. You can use the new plan as a reference for adjustments at the next maturity.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: Tonight I'm embroidering the withered tree branches in 'Winter' with satin stitch, but it doesn't feel vigorous enough. Any technique suggestions?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: To depict withered branches in Cantonese embroidery, twisted stitches or seed stitches can be used for texture; thicker seed stitches at the base of the branch can show nodules, and fine twisted stitches at the tip can show the twists and turns.

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_343.text: Combining twisted stitch and seed stitch does add more depth. Next I plan to embroider a flying bird. Any design suggestions?

session_343.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_343.text: For the flying bird, you can use satin stitch and stem stitch, using silk thread and negative space to express the movement of the wings, and place it slightly above the branch tip to create a contrast between motion and stillness with the withered branch.

session_350.text: I suggest dividing the lecture into three parts: 15 minutes to tell the history of Cantonese embroidery and classic pieces (such as the Cantonese embroidered dragon robe) through stories, 15 minutes to display your works and explain basic stitches (you can bring the actual pieces so they can be passed around), and the final 15 minutes for interaction — have each student embroider a small pattern (such as a five-petal flower or auspicious cloud) using an embroidery frame and colored thread. The difficulty is low, and it can be completed in 5 minutes, with the remaining time for comments and sharing. The interactive segment can liven up the atmosphere and matches middle school students' interest in hands-on activities.

session_350.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_350.text: That's a good idea. But middle school students' hands-on skills vary widely. Would on-site embroidery be too difficult? Is there a simpler interactive alternative?

session_350.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_350.text: I understand your concerns. It can be adjusted to: prepare cardstock with printed outlines in advance (patterns such as lychees and lion dance), have students use pearl pins to pin out the shapes along the outlines, or use plastic embroidery boards with thick yarn to practice running stitch. This way even beginners can get started quickly, the cost is low, and the finished pieces give a sense of accomplishment. In addition, interspersing a 'guess the stitch' Q&A (showing part of an embroidered piece and letting students guess the stitch used) can also increase engagement.

session_351.text: I was diagnosed with a damaged skin barrier and just bought La Roche-Posay B5 repairing cream, Avène Thermal Spring Water, and Freeplus facial cleanser. What is the correct order and frequency of use? Can I layer other soothing ingredients during the repair period?

session_351.text: Suggested order: After cleansing, first use Avène spray to soothe, then apply La Roche-Posay B5 repairing cream thinly on affected areas, once every morning and evening. During repair, avoid layering other ingredients; use only these three products for at least two weeks. Wait until your skin stabilizes before considering adding ceramide or centella asiatica.

session_351.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_351.text: Got it. Do I need to avoid certain foods? Roughly how long before I see improvement? I still feel tightness in my cheeks—is that normal?

session_351.text: Dietary recommendations: avoid spicy food, seafood, alcohol, and high-sugar foods to reduce inflammation. Tightness is a normal part of the early stage of healing; it usually eases within one to two weeks. The disappearance of stinging pain and fading of redness are signs of improvement. Initial improvement can be seen within two weeks, but complete healing may take four to six weeks.

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_355.text: I want to send a few old Hong Kong dollar notes to a friend in Shenzhen. Which courier is safer? Are there any packaging and customs declaration precautions?

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_355.text: Recommend Hongkong Post's registered mail / EZ-Post service, which is low-cost and trackable; or SF Express's cross-border service. For packaging, sandwich the banknotes between cardboard, put them in a waterproof bag, declare them as “souvenirs or collectibles,” write a nominal value, and no need to insure.

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_355.text: Then do I need to insure it? I'm worried in case it gets lost.

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_355.text: For small-value old coins, it is usually not recommended to insure them, as the insurance fee increases cost and the procedures are complicated. Both registered mail and courier provide basic compensation, and the probability of loss is very low. Registered mail is recommended as it is more economical.

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_355.text: I'm embroidering the snowflakes in "Winter" using white silk thread in a flat stitch, but I always feel they lack a three-dimensional effect. Are there any more suitable stitch techniques you would recommend?

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_355.text: You can try the seed stitch to express the sparkling, grainy texture of the snowflake center, or use long-and-short stitch gradients to build layers. In Cantonese embroidery, splitting the thread to 1/4 or even 1/8 of the original, combined with light gray or light blue silk threads for shadow transitions, enhances the three-dimensional effect.

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei
session_355.text: Would seed stitch make the snowflake look too heavy? I want to keep it light and airy. Also, should I add some shimmering silk thread in certain areas?

session_355.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_355.text: Seed stitch is only used for the flower center or highlight points; with a small area it won't look heavy. For the edges, use long-and-short stitch with sparse gradation. I suggest adding a little silver silk thread to the center of the snowflake (traditional Cantonese embroidery often uses gold thread for accents); it will look crystalline under reflected light.

session_364.speaker: Yu Xiaowei's Assistant
session_364.text: The framework has three parts: 1) Analyze Mr. Chen's company cash flow (estimate funding needs within six months); 2) Recommend short-term, high-liquidity savings products (e.g., 3-month or 6-month terms, comparing returns); 3) Currency hedging suggestions (paired with foreign currency wealth management). Key talking points: first acknowledge liquidity concerns, then show that the product can be withdrawn early with returns still better than demand deposits, and finally use case examples to illustrate long-term returns.

session_364.text: Tonight, while soaking my feet, I listened to guqin music. Then, with a face mask on, I embroidered the snowflakes for 'Winter.' Every stitch was deeply immersive, and I felt completely relaxed. Do you know that soothing feeling that traditional craftsmanship brings?

session_364.text: Try on the basis of random stitch: use two strands of silk thread to first outline the main skeleton of the snowflake, then use a single strand of fine silk to fill the gaps with a wandering stitch along the skeleton direction. This gives it both layering and the light, airy feel of a snowflake. When finished, it can be mounted in a light-colored wooden frame and displayed with warm lighting.

Before the interruption, I had maintained a good running frequency (running on April 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9), but from April 10 onward I did not run. The key event was that on April 11 my mother-in-law sprained her ankle and I had to rush over to deal with it; on April 14 she was injured a second time (spraining her lower back), and I started nearly three weeks of family caregiving, shuttling between my own home and my mother-in-law's every day without the time or energy to run. On April 22 her follow-up visit confirmed recovery, and the next day (April 23) I did a recovery jog.

qa.question: (Question time: 2025-12-31)What obvious differences are there in my spending in the first half and the second half of April 2025? What do these changes reveal about my mindset and life priorities?
qa.answer: In the first half of the month (1st to 15th), spending was restrained, focused on family obligations and self-investment: on April 3, she bought Qingming Festival offerings for about 200 HKD; on April 8, she made a reservation at Tsui Wah Restaurant for about 300 HKD; on April 12, she signed up for a Japanese course for 2,000 HKD. This change reflects a shift from the restrained state of handling family events (Qingming, her mother-in-law's injury) in the first half of the month to, in the second half after stress was released, self-regulation through consumption (impulsive shopping), resuming health management (running shoes), and maintaining family emotional bonds (buying fabric, ballet renewal, buying fish maw), while also beginning to plan finances rationally. Overall, it reflects a recovery in her sense of control over life.

session_1.text: I went to Shenghuali Pottery Studio this afternoon and got the class schedule. I want to sign up for the Saturday morning class. But I have rotating days off as a doctor, and I may not be free every Saturday. Do you think this time works?

session_1.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_1.text: The Saturday morning class is usually 9:00-12:00 and lasts 8 weeks. It's best to check next month's schedule first. session_1.text: Indeed, I sometimes work weekends too. So as a beginner, do I need to prepare my own apron and tools?

session_1.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_1.text: The studio usually provides aprons and basic tools, but it is recommended to bring your own non-slip rubber shoes and hand cream — kneading clay affects the skin. Also, as a doctor, you need to protect hand flexibility, so use the palm for force and avoid overusing your fingertips.

session_1.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_1.text: Got it. So how do I balance work and learning pottery? I'm afraid I'll be too tired after work to keep it up.

session_1.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_1.text: You can set aside one fixed evening each week as pottery time and treat it as relaxation rather than a task. In the early stage, start with kneading clay, with 15 minutes of finger warm-up each time, and progress step by step. Remember that the New Year goal is to learn the basics within a year, so there is no need to rush.

session_1.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_1.text: I suggest you make every Sunday your fixed studio day. That afternoon, start with pottery to relax, and in the evening go for a half-hour jog, forming a regular block of 'creation + exercise.' This way, you keep a sense of ritual and strengthen your motivation to persevere.

session_3.text: The data direction is correct. Existing meta-analyses have shown that IL-18 is elevated by an average of 5-10 times in active Still's disease, with a specificity of about 85%. I suggest you could compile a “quick-reference table for the differential diagnosis of fever of unknown origin” in your work, including indicators such as ferritin, IL-18, and CRP/PCT ratio, for direct reference next time.

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_3.text: I just practiced “chrysanthemum kneading” with a dry towel for ten minutes, but I'm not sure if the movements are standard. Can you tell me the correct key points and common mistakes of this technique?

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_3.text: The key to chrysanthemum kneading is to use wrist strength to drive the palm, pressing in a spiral from the center outward while keeping the fingers naturally spread to assist in shaping. Common mistakes are using too much force with the fingers or keeping the palm angle too flat. It is recommended to close your eyes during practice to feel the changes in clay resistance. You can simulate with a towel, but note that a towel has no elasticity, so focus on the movement trajectory of your hands.

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_3.text: When I practice with the towel again, I need to pay attention to the pressing angle and wrist stability, right? Are there other ways to reinforce it at home?

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_3.text: Yes, keep your palm at about a 45-degree angle to the table and rotate your wrist at a steady speed. In daily practice, you can simulate the clay-kneading motion with empty hands, coordinating with your breathing rhythm, for 5 minutes each time to strengthen muscle memory. Before the next class, arrive at the classroom early, warm up with wet clay for 10 minutes, and ask Master Zheng about the details of your movements.

When shipping, pack them to prevent compression. There is a temperature drop in Luoyang next week, so mailing them this weekend is perfect.

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_3.text: Are there any safety reminders for use? I'm afraid that my mother won't be careful enough when using it.

session_3.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_3.text: It is recommended to stick it on the outer side of the undergarment, not directly on the skin, to avoid burns. Each patch should not be used for more than 8 hours, especially don't use it while sleeping. Also, you can ask them whether they need an electric blanket or hot water bottle, but pay attention to electrical safety.

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_4.text: I just reviewed the myocardial ischemia chapter on ECG in Practical Internal Medicine. I keep mixing up the distinguishing points between ST-segment elevation and tall T waves. Are there any memory tricks?

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_4.text: You can use the mnemonic: "Tall, peaked T waves indicate early ischemia; ST segment arching upward indicates typical infarction." Note that tall, peaked T waves are often accompanied by QT interval shortening and appear in the hyperacute phase; ST-segment elevation with an upward arch ≥0.1 mV lasting more than half an hour suggests acute myocardial infarction. It is recommended to repeatedly compare typical electrocardiogram examples and to pay attention to ruling out early repolarization syndrome.

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_4.text: This mnemonic is very clear. Also, in the ECG chapter review, which key points are frequently tested and easily mistaken in the attending physician exam?

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_4.text: High-frequency error-prone points include: criteria for ventricular rate control during atrial fibrillation, the diagnostic contradiction between left bundle branch block and myocardial infarction, recognition of Wellens syndrome, and analysis of pacemaker ECGs. It is recommended that you organize a mistake notebook and self-test 2–3 times a week with case images, combined with actual cases seen in the department to deepen your understanding.

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_4.text: I bought heat packs to send to my mother in Luoyang, whose knees are sensitive to cold. Can heat packs be applied directly to the skin? Where should they be placed for best results? What comprehensive advice is there for elderly joint care in winter?

session_4.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_4.text: Never apply a heat pack directly to the skin; it should be placed on the outside of the underwear, preferably just above or on the inner side of the knee, for no more than 6 hours at a time to avoid low-temperature burns. Daily care recommendations: increase heat therapy and gentle massage on the knee, choose highly elastic thermal knee pads; ensure adequate intake of calcium, vitamin D, and collagen in the diet; if pain is significant, seek medical evaluation to determine whether glucosamine supplementation is needed.

session_6.text: I am organizing the case of a 72-year-old patient with heart failure and renal failure. I am unsure about the classification of cardiorenal syndrome, diuretic dose adjustment, and the timing of nutritional support. Can you help me analyze it?

session_6.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_6.text: You are writing a case analysis framework, focusing on the CRS type 1-5 classification, dosing strategies for diuretics (such as furosemide) in volume management during renal insufficiency, and the timing for choosing between nasogastric feeding and parenteral nutrition, right?

session_6.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_6.text: Yes, especially the adjustment of diuretic doses and ACEI/ARB, as well as the patient's blood glucose control targets.

session_6.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_6.text: According to the latest literature: For CRS type 1, intravenous loop diuretics can be used. In renal insufficiency, the initial dose should be doubled (e.g., furosemide 40-80 mg IV). If there is a poor response, consider ultrafiltration. ACEI/ARB should be used with caution or reduced in dose when eGFR < 30. The glycemic control target is 7.8-10.0 mmol/L. For nutritional support, enteral nutrition is preferred; if the target amount cannot be achieved within 48 hours, consider parenteral nutrition.

session_7.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_7.text: In this afternoon's case discussion, I presented the patient with CKD stage 4 complicated by heart failure. The director pointed out that I had missed the anemia and CKD-MBD assessments. I searched the literature tonight and would like to ask: for anemia evaluation, how should the sequence of ferritin, folate, and vitamin B12 tests be arranged? What is the starting threshold for erythropoietin? Also, for calcium-phosphate metabolism disorders, what are the preferred principles for phosphate binders such as calcium acetate and sevelamer? I want to confirm whether my adjustment of treatment priorities is reasonable.

session_7.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_7.text: Dr. Yu, your analysis is spot on. For anemia evaluation, it is recommended to first check iron metabolism (ferritin and transferrin saturation) to determine whether there is absolute iron deficiency; if normal, then check folate and vitamin B12. The starting threshold for erythropoietin is generally hemoglobin <100 g/L, but it should be adjusted based on the patient's iron stores, cardiovascular risk, and symptoms. For phosphate binders, if the patient has hypercalcemia or a high risk of vascular calcification, sevelamer is the first choice; if hyperphosphatemia is dominant and serum calcium is low, calcium acetate is more appropriate. It is recommended to optimize volume management simultaneously, preferably by adjusting diuretics first, then gradually incorporating these treatments.

session_7.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_7.text: Understood. Then I will first complete the iron metabolism tests, and based on the results consider erythropoietin; for the phosphate binder, I would choose sevelamer first. I plan to add a section to the progress notes about the diagnostic and treatment approach for anemia and CKD-MBD, and note the adjustment of volume management. Is that reasonable?

session_7.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_7.text: Perfectly reasonable. I suggest writing in the progress note in the following order: first record today's discussion meeting opinions, then add the conclusions from the literature you studied, and finally list the next steps for examination and treatment (such as iron metabolism, PTH, serum calcium and phosphorus, the timing for starting erythropoietin, and the rationale for choosing sevelamer). This reflects an evidence-based approach and makes it easier for your supervisor to review. Keep it up!

session_8.text: I designed a teacup with a chrysanthemum pattern. Su Ya suggested raising the base by two millimeters. How can I adjust it without damaging the pattern? Will it affect firing?

session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_8.text: When the clay body is half dry, gently pat the outside of the cup bottom with a damp sponge, then use a carving knife to evenly scrape away a layer of clay from the inside of the bottom, keeping the texture intact. After the adjustment, reshape the bottom, control humidity to avoid cracking, and it is recommended to use fine clay to reduce shrinkage and deformation.

session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_8.text: If it is made taller, will the pattern deform? What tool should be used to fix the chrysanthemum pattern?

session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_8.text: The texture won't deform because the working area is at the bottom. It is recommended to cover the textured part with plastic wrap to prevent cracking. When trimming the bottom, use a trimming tool or sponge stick, and let it air dry naturally once stable. Before firing, cracks can be repaired with slip, but keep the overall surface even.

session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_8.text: Understood. After high-intensity exercise, you developed muscle soreness and an abrasion on your right knee, and you are worried it may affect work the next day. The abrasion shows no redness, swelling, or broken skin, but persistent stinging warrants attention; the muscle soreness may be due to lactic acid buildup or minor muscle damage. session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_8.text: Yes, exactly these. Does the abrasion need disinfection and bandaging? Also, are there more effective stretches for the calves and hip flexors?

session_8.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_8.text: Abrasions: wipe gently with povidone-iodine, then apply a breathable band-aid and avoid friction; ice for 10 minutes tonight (with a towel in between) to relieve stinging. Muscle soreness: before bed, do static calf stretches (lunge with bent knee, 30 seconds per side) and hip flexor relaxation (single-knee kneeling, push the hips forward). Tomorrow morning, do a light warm-up (jumping jacks for 30 seconds + high knees for 20 seconds) to activate the muscles. If the knee stinging persists or there is redness and swelling, it is recommended to see a doctor to rule out ligament problems.

session_9.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_9.text: Congratulations on finishing it smoothly! The common cause of coil collapse is uneven moisture or joints not being compacted firmly. session_9.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_9.text: The coil method is suitable for making irregularly shaped teapot bodies, but a teapot needs a well-sealed lid and spout. It is recommended to build the body with coiling, and make the spout and handle with slab rolling or hand shaping, then adjust by trimming. session_15.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_15.text: My father just became left-sided hemiplegic and aphasic due to cerebral infarction. After thrombolysis, he needs systematic rehabilitation guidance. Please provide key points for acute-phase care and the golden window period for rehabilitation training. I have a medical background, but neurorehabilitation is not my specialty.

session_15.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_15.text: Key points for the acute phase (24-72 hours): turn the patient every 2 hours to prevent pressure ulcers, perform ankle pump exercises to prevent deep vein thrombosis, and elevate the head of the bed 30° to prevent aspiration. The golden window for rehabilitation is 1-3 months after onset, and passive exercises should be started as early as possible. Aphasia training can begin with picture naming and simple commands.

session_15.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_15.text: How exactly should passive exercises for left-side hemiplegia be performed? Do the joints need to be fixed? Also, my father has high blood pressure; how should the antiplatelet medication be adjusted?

session_15.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_15.text: Passive exercise: from proximal to distal, shoulder abduction - elbow flexion/extension - wrist and finger joint movements; hold each movement for 5 seconds, gently to avoid pulling. Antiplatelet drugs: if not accompanied by atrial fibrillation, aspirin 100 mg/day or clopidogrel 75 mg/day; blood pressure control target <140/90 mmHg. Neurology consultation is recommended to adjust medication.

session_15.text: I can feel how heavy and powerless you are right now. You have already done so well—rushing back immediately and staying by your father's side; these choices themselves are the deepest love. Your fear and self-blame are normal reactions. Allow them to exist, okay?

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_17.text: I am Yu Xiaowen. My father, Yu Jianguo, has left-sided limb hemiplegia after a cerebral infarction. This afternoon I tried passive range-of-motion training, but I'm not sure whether I performed it correctly. What is the standard procedure in the rehabilitation department? For example, how many times a day, how long each time? Where should the movement sequence start?

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_17.text: Recommended 2-3 times a day, 15-20 minutes each time. The sequence of movements goes from large joints to small joints: shoulder → elbow → wrist → hip → knee → ankle. For each joint, slowly flex, extend, and rotate 5-10 times within the pain-free range, avoiding excessive stretching and forceful movements. Monitor blood pressure during activity, ensuring systolic pressure <160 mmHg. Coordinating with breathing and soft music works better.

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_17.text: Thank you. Then how can I judge whether the range of motion is appropriate? I'm worried that improper force might cause injury. Are there specific force feedback standards?

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_17.text: The criterion is that the patient does not experience pain or facial tension. During passive movement, stop if resistance is encountered and never force the stretch. It is recommended to measure and record the joint range of motion before and after activity. In addition, rule out bleeding risk (such as abnormal coagulation function). If your father has hypertension, measure his blood pressure first. You can take weekly photos to record progress.

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_17.text: Understood. I will adjust my operations according to your advice and carefully observe my father's reactions. Thank you for the professional guidance!

session_17.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_18.text: My father has left-side paralysis after a cerebral infarction. Every day I do passive range-of-motion exercises for his shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, and ankle—10 repetitions per joint. I want to confirm whether my method is correct, and whether there are more effective rehabilitation techniques?

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_18.text: After the acute phase, passive movement is necessary. It is recommended to do it 2-3 times a day, moving each joint slowly to its maximum pain-free range each time, holding for 5-10 seconds. Watch your father's facial expressions and muscle tone carefully; stop immediately if spasms or pain occur. Combining breathing relaxation and listening to music (such as 'Chaoyanggou') can improve the effect.

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_18.text: Then, is the current frequency and range appropriate? Should some movements be added or reduced?

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_18.text: Appropriately increase shoulder external rotation and finger extension to avoid shoulder-hand syndrome. Avoid forceful pulling; follow the range of motion and patient tolerance. Keep the total daily duration within 30 minutes, and it is safer to do it in multiple sessions.

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_18.text: My father is hospitalized in Luoyang, and I work in Zhengzhou. I need to understand the complete reimbursement process for cross-city medical insurance. I have already checked the official website and called, but a few details are unclear: how are drugs with a high out-of-pocket ratio calculated? Do I need to register in Zhengzhou in advance? Can I settle directly upon discharge? Can my father's social security card be used in Luoyang?

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_18.text: Your situation involves seeking medical treatment across different cities within Henan Province. According to Henan Province's policy, the filing requirement for cross-city medical treatment has been cancelled. If you are insured in Zhengzhou and hospitalized in Luoyang, you can settle directly at discharge, and the social security card is valid nationwide. The reimbursement ratio, deductible, and cap are implemented according to Luoyang's standards. However, for drugs with a high out-of-pocket ratio, you need to check the medical insurance drug list; some items may require you to pay a certain proportion out of pocket before reimbursement. It is recommended that you register for cross-city medical treatment at the Luoyang hospital before discharge. The required materials are already prepared: ID card, social security card, and diagnostic certificate.

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen
session_18.text: Then the list I prepared: ID card, social security card, diagnosis certificate. We don't need a referral certificate or employer certificate, right? Also, will the reimbursement be deducted on the spot or credited later? If the documents are incomplete, how do I reapply?

session_18.speaker: Yu Xiaowen's Assistant
session_18.text: The list you compiled is very complete. For cross-city medical treatment within the same province, no referral certificate or employer certificate is needed. At discharge settlement, the medical insurance reimbursement portion will be deducted directly; you only need to pay the portion you are personally responsible for, and the reimbursement will not be credited separately. If the materials are incomplete, you can bring supplementary materials to the Medical Insurance Office of Luoyang Hospital within 15 days after discharge for supplementary processing, or contact the Zhengzhou Medical Insurance Center for manual reimbursement. I suggest you call again today to confirm whether the hospital has any special requirements.
