session_10.text: You want to confirm the feasibility of zero-knowledge proofs in financial data sharing, and also understand the impact of the CSRC's latest regulatory guidance on robo-advisor products?

session_10.text: Consortium blockchains achieve privacy protection through permissioned nodes and encrypted channels, but their audit transparency is lower than that of public blockchains. session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_15.text: In CFA quantitative analysis, I encountered a question I got wrong, involving the application of PV and FV formulas under different compounding frequencies. Can you help me sort out how to distinguish between scenarios?

session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_15.text: Is your confusion mainly about the conversion between interest compounding periods and number of periods in formula variants? Please provide the specific problem conditions, and I'll help you break down the steps.

session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_15.text: The problem gave an annual interest rate of 8% compounded quarterly, asking for the future value after 5 years. I used the continuous compounding formula and got it wrong.

session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_15.text: The error was confusing discrete compounding with continuous compounding. The correct approach: for quarterly compounding, use FV = PV×(1 + r/m)^(n×m), r=8%, m=4, n=5; for continuous compounding, use e^(r×n). You need to choose based on whether the question explicitly says "continuous" or "quarterly".

session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_15.text: Got it! Also, how do PEST and the Five Forces model in strategic management apply to real-world cases?

session_15.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_15.text: You can take the financial industry as an example: PEST analysis covers policy (new asset management regulations), economy (interest rate trends), society (financial concepts), and technology (AI investment advisors); the Five Forces model assesses the competitive landscape. Combining the two can enhance your case analysis ability for MBA exam preparation.

session_17.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_17.text: I just did 5 practice problems on hypothesis testing, but I'm still confused about the criteria for choosing between the t-statistic and the z-statistic, especially when the population variance is unknown but the sample size is large. How do I decide?

session_17.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_17.text: When the population variance is unknown, the t statistic should be used theoretically; but if the sample size is large enough (e.g., n>30), the t distribution approximates the normal distribution, so the z statistic can be used to simplify calculations. However, in exams, strictly choose the t statistic according to the conditions. Recommended mnemonic: use t when variance is unknown; for large samples, z can be approximated.

session_17.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_17.text: I see. Then what about the relationship between test power and the two types of errors? I always get them mixed up when doing problems.

session_17.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_17.text: Statistical power = 1 - probability of Type II error. A Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis, and a Type II error is failing to reject a false null hypothesis. Increasing the sample size and raising the significance level can both increase power. It is recommended to draw a 2x2 matrix to help memorize: when rejecting H0, if H0 is true, it is a Type I error; if H0 is false, it is correct. When not rejecting H0, if H0 is true, it is correct; if H0 is false, it is a Type II error.

session_19.text: I completed 100 practice questions in the CFA hypothesis testing chapter today and organized the wrong questions and error-prone flashcards, but I am still a bit confused about concepts such as Type I errors, Type II errors, and the meaning of p-value. Could you explain them in simple terms? Also, could you confirm whether my summary of wrong questions covers the key test points?

session_19.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_19.text: Your summary of wrong questions is very systematic. Core exam points such as Type I and Type II errors (α and β), p-value (rejecting the null hypothesis when it is less than the significance level), and selection of test statistics (z/t distribution) should all be covered. In simple terms: Type I error is 'accusing an innocent person' (rejecting a true null hypothesis), with probability α; Type II error is 'letting a guilty person go free' (accepting a false null hypothesis), with probability β. The p-value is the observed significance level; the smaller it is, the more it supports rejecting the null hypothesis. It is recommended that in the next stage, you prioritize reviewing the difference between parametric tests (such as mean and variance) and non-parametric tests, and consolidate them with typical example problems.

It is best to persuade her to go to a community hospital for an X-ray to rule out a fracture. You can say, 'The community hospital is simple and fast, and the X-ray will give us peace of mind; I've booked it for you.' For daily care, you can prepare Voltaren ointment for external use, and use red flower oil only after the acute phase has passed. During your daily video calls, ask about her recovery in a caring tone, and share the nursing knowledge you've found, so she feels cared for rather than blamed.

session_21.text: I'm preparing for the CFA exam. I always confuse Type I and Type II errors in hypothesis testing. Can you help me distinguish them with examples?

session_21.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_21.text: Of course. A Type I error is rejecting a true null hypothesis (false positive), for example, a new drug is ineffective but mistakenly considered effective; risk α is controlled by the significance level. A Type II error is accepting a false null hypothesis (false negative), for example, an effective drug is mistakenly judged ineffective; risk β. In finance, lowering α when backtesting a trading strategy may increase β. You can remember it as 'wronging a good person' (α) and 'letting a bad person go' (β).

session_21.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_21.text: This memory method is good. Then in actual investment analysis, how do you balance the risks of the two?

session_21.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_21.text: Usually, the trade-off depends on the scenario. If the consequences are severe, such as drug safety testing, α must be strictly controlled (set a low significance level, e.g., 0.01); if the opportunity cost of missing out is high, such as trading strategy validation, α can be appropriately relaxed (e.g., 0.1), while reducing β by increasing the sample size. This is a common CFA exam point: when α decreases, β increases (with sample size unchanged).

session_22.text: Okay, heteroscedasticity tests usually involve the Breusch-Pagan test or the White test. session_22.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_22.text: Breusch-Pagan test steps: 1) Run OLS regression on the original model to obtain residuals and square them; 2) Use the squared residuals as the dependent variable and perform an auxiliary regression on the original independent variables; 3) Multiply the R² from the auxiliary regression by the sample size n to get the LM statistic; 4) Look up the chi-square distribution table (degrees of freedom = number of independent variables). If the p-value is less than 0.05, reject the homoscedasticity assumption. I suggest you manually work through a typical example from the CFA textbook to deepen your understanding. session_24.text: Standard steps for Bayes' formula: ① Define the prior probability P(A) and conditional probability P(B|A); ② Calculate the total probability P(B)=∑P(B|A_i)P(A_i); ③ Substitute into the posterior P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B). session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_25.text: I am self-studying CFA macroeconomics and just finished the linkage between fiscal policy and monetary policy. But I still don't fully grasp the policy effectiveness of the IS-LM model under a liquidity trap, especially the coordination mechanism between the central bank and the Ministry of Finance. Can you explain it to me in a more vivid way?

session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_25.text: It seems you're stuck on the Keynesian extreme case—the classic paradox of ineffective monetary policy and fiscal dominance in a liquidity trap. Are you specifically confused about why the IS curve shifts without changing interest rates, or about the actual game-theoretic logic between the central bank and the finance ministry?

session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_25.text: Yes, exactly. Why does monetary policy completely fail when interest rates are unchanged, while the fiscal multiplier doubles? The textbook says the central bank buys bonds but interest rates are locked, which feels abstract.

session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_25.text: Imagine an extreme economic predicament: interest rates are near 0% and the public hoards cash. At this point, the central bank buying bonds → money supply increases, but interest rates cannot drop further, and investment cannot be stimulated. However, if the finance ministry directly issues bonds and spends (such as infrastructure construction) → aggregate demand increases directly, and since it does not rely on interest rate transmission, the multiplier is enormous. Memory tip: under a liquidity trap, "fiscal policy is the only force that can push the door open."

session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_25.text: This analogy makes it easier to understand. So how will the exam test this point? What pitfalls are easy to fall into?

session_25.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_25.text: The CFA often asks: 'Which policy is most effective at the zero lower bound?' Trap: mistakenly choosing QE (quantitative easing) or interest rate cuts. The correct answer is expansionary fiscal policy. Test yourself: Judge whether 'the central bank purchasing government bonds in a liquidity trap is an open market operation that can lower long-term interest rates' — this is correct, but note that if deflation is expected, long-term rates may also be locked. It is recommended to compare the post-2008 US case of QE plus fiscal stimulus.

session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_35.text: My mother has just been diagnosed with grade 2 hypertension and hyperlipidemia. I have already bought a blood pressure monitor and medication, but I would like more professional daily management advice, such as the correct way and frequency to measure blood pressure and precautions for taking medication.

session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_35.text: It is recommended to measure blood pressure twice a day, in the morning and evening (within 1 hour after waking up and before going to bed), sit quietly for 5 minutes before measurement, and keep the cuff at the same height as the heart. Take medication on time. Amlodipine besylate tablets may cause ankle edema, and atorvastatin calcium tablets should not be taken with grapefruit juice. Strictly control a low-fat, low-salt diet, with daily salt <5 grams and saturated fat <7% of total calories. For exercise, walk briskly for 6000 steps after meals, and control heart rate at around (170 - age). Record blood pressure and weight at least three times a week, and recheck blood lipids monthly.

session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_35.text: Can you be specific about which foods to avoid? And how should exercise intensity be managed? My mother is 56.

session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_35.text: Foods to avoid: high-salt pickled foods (pickled vegetables, cured meat), high-fat red meat (fat beef, pork belly), fried foods, animal organs, and whole-milk dairy products. It is recommended to choose more fish, chicken breast, soy products, and whole grains. For exercise, brisk walking, jogging, or swimming is best. Target heart rate ≈ (220-56) × 60%~70% ≈ 98~115 bpm. Be sure to progress gradually and stop immediately if dizziness or chest tightness occurs. Emotional management is also important; you can teach her to use deep breathing to relieve tension.

session_35.text: You need a systematic strategy for studying while working, prioritizing modules that have a high weight and strong logic, while using fragmented time for light study. It is recommended to start with 'Ethics and Professional Standards', 'Quantitative Methods', and 'Financial Statement Analysis' in that order. For time allocation, invest 12-15 hours per week, mainly on weekday evenings, and use commute and lunch breaks to watch videos or do practice questions. session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_35.text: This sequencing and time allocation approach is reasonable, but I'm used to morning running and reading; could I also use morning running time to listen to audio? Also, quantitative methods have been placed in the primary module; how will it connect with other subjects later?

session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_35.text: Listening to audio during morning runs is completely feasible. I recommend using Bloomberg or CFA Institute podcast content (such as the 'CFA Exam Prep' channel), but note to use it only as background input, and not recommend doing high-intensity memorization at the same time. After completing Quantitative Methods, it is recommended to follow with 'Economics' and 'Financial Statement Analysis' because the three are highly logically related; then follow the order of 'Corporate Finance', 'Equity Investments', 'Fixed Income', 'Derivatives and Alternative Investments', and finally focus on reviewing 'Portfolio Management' and 'Ethics'. session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_35.text: This connection approach is very clear, and the suggestions for organizing wrong answers and weekend review are practical. session_35.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_35.text: Key misconceptions: 1) Over-relying on Notes while ignoring detail-oriented questions in official textbooks; 2) Doing too few practice questions in the early stage, leading to falling behind later; 3) Using fragmented time to watch long videos, which is inefficient and distracting; it is recommended to break them down into 5-10 minute small tasks; 4) Neglecting periodic self-assessment; it is recommended to do a Mock Exam every two weeks, strictly timed, to simulate real exam pacing. session_47.text: I just finished a phone call with my father. He suggested I look into convertible bond fund A and secondary debt fund B, and I'm going to talk to my account manager next week. Can you explain the investment logic and main differences between these two types of funds? For example, how do they generate returns and where are the risks?

session_47.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_47.text: Convertible bond funds mainly invest in convertible bonds and have dual attributes of equity and debt: in bull markets, they can share in the gains of the stock market; in bear markets, they have bond floor protection. Secondary bond funds usually have an equity position of no more than 20%, and their returns rely more on coupons and moderate equity positions. The difference between the two is: convertible bond funds have greater elasticity and are affected by both interest rates and the underlying stock price; secondary bond funds are relatively stable, but the stock position amplifies volatility. In the current environment of changing interest rates, both need to pay attention to the duration risk of fixed income.

session_47.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_47.text: Understood. Regarding subscription fees, how are these two types of funds usually charged? My father specifically reminded me to pay attention to interest rate changes. How exactly do they affect their performance?

session_47.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_47.text: Subscription fees are generally 0.6%-1.5%. Class C shares have no subscription fee but charge a sales service fee. When interest rates rise, bond prices fall, and the bond floor support of convertible bonds weakens, but a rise in the underlying stock may offset that. For secondary bond funds, the pure bond portion suffers, while the equity portion may actually benefit if allocated appropriately. When you ask your account manager on Monday, I suggest focusing on comparing the two funds' concentration of holdings, the fund managers' turnover rates, and their historical maximum drawdowns under different interest rate environments.

session_60.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_60.text: I encountered a wrong question during practice: A company recognized revenue early, net profit increased but cash flow did not keep pace. How does this affect the income statement and cash flow statement? How exactly should the timing of revenue recognition be judged under accrual accounting?

session_60.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_60.text: For example, if a manufacturing company ships goods in December but the customer pays in January of the following year, under accrual accounting, revenue is recognized in the current year. Accounts receivable on the income statement increases and net profit rises; however, there is no cash inflow on the cash flow statement, so net operating cash flow is lower than net profit. Exams often design this difference as a trap comparing the income statement and cash flow statement. I suggest you focus on the adjustment of 'accounts receivable/advance receipts' changes to current period profit.

session_70.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_70.text: I just finished an online course on long-term liabilities and leases. To verify my understanding, I manually prepared a trial balance. Could you help me check whether the articulation logic is correct: interest expense on the income statement affects net profit through financial expenses, and then affects the balance sheet through retained earnings?

session_70.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_70.text: Understood, you want to confirm the complete transmission path from the interest expense on the income statement to the owner's equity on the balance sheet, and whether the trial balance is balanced, right? Specifically tell me the key steps and doubts you had when preparing it.

session_70.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_70.text: Yes. I assumed that a new loan was taken out in the current period, recognized interest expense of 1 million as finance costs, and net profit decreased by 750,000 (tax rate 25%). Then retained earnings decreased by 750,000, owners' equity decreased accordingly, and liabilities increased by the loan principal. Total assets remained unchanged, but the trial balance did not balance. I suspect I misunderstood whether interest expense should be capitalized or expensed.

session_70.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_70.text: Your reconciliation direction is correct, but the problem lies in the impact of interest expense on cash: interest expense of 1,000,000 reduces net profit by 750,000, but paying the interest reduces cash, causing the asset side to also decrease by 750,000 (assuming the loan principal remains unchanged). So the trial balance should be: liabilities +1,000,000 (new borrowing), equity -750,000 (retained earnings), assets +1,000,000 (cash increase? No, actually the asset side cash decreases by 750,000 due to interest payment, while borrowing increases by 1,000,000, so net asset increase of 250,000? Let's break it down step by step: the new borrowing increases cash by 1,000,000, paying interest reduces cash by 1,000,000 (assuming full cash payment), so net cash change is 0; interest expense causes net profit -750,000, equity -750,000, no change on the asset side, but liabilities increase by 1,000,000 (borrowing). The left side of the equation (assets) is unchanged, the right side has liabilities +1,000,000 and equity -750,000, so the right side increases by 250,000, and it is unbalanced. This is because although interest expense reduced profit, the liability increase did not correspond to an asset increase. In reality, there is a cash inflow of 1,000,000 from borrowing and a cash outflow of 1,000,000 for interest, so net cash change is 0, but the interest expense is recorded in the income statement, causing net profit to decrease by 750,000, retained earnings to decrease by 750,000, and equity to decrease by 750,000, while liabilities increase by 1,000,000, making the right side increase by 250,000, and the left side assets unchanged. Therefore, the asset side must be adjusted: prepaid interest or interest payable would create an asset or liability. The correct entry is: debit finance expense 1,000,000, credit interest payable 1,000,000 (liability). Thus liabilities increase by 1,000,000 (interest payable), while net profit decreases by 750,000 and equity decreases by 750,000, so the right side increases by 250,000? No, interest payable is a liability increase, and finance expense affects equity decrease. The right side net change: liabilities +1,000,000, equity -750,000, net +250,000; left side assets unchanged? Should be re-confirmed. I suggest you check whether you missed the short-term liability account for interest payable, and the cash decrease when the interest is paid.

This better fits Huang Siqi's risk target.

session_73.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_73.text: Makes sense, the distribution rate constraint is key. session_77.text: While reviewing the interest coverage ratio for CFA Level II, I am confused about the value of interest expense in EBIT. The textbook says EBIT = net income + interest expense + income tax, but is capitalized interest included? What are the differences under GAAP and IFRS? Could you explain in both Chinese and English, and give examples of how to handle it in actual analysis?

session_77.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_77.text: Interest Coverage Ratio = EBIT / Interest Expense. Interest expense usually refers to 'Interest Expense' (pre-tax) in the income statement, excluding capitalized interest. Under US GAAP, operating lease interest is included in lease liability amortization; under IFRS, all leases are capitalized, and interest expense includes lease liability interest, resulting in slightly higher EBIT. For example, Aier Eye Hospital's interest coverage ratio is >50 times, mainly because non-recurring gains (such as investment income) account for a high proportion of net profit, so EBIT needs to be adjusted to exclude one-time items.

session_77.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_77.text: I see, so capitalized interest is not included in the denominator, but should it be added back when calculating EBIT? Also, should related-party financing interest be excluded?

session_77.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_77.text: Capitalized interest cannot be added back (not a period expense). If the interest rate on related-party financing is not at arm's length, it is recommended to adjust it to a reasonable level. In practice, Moody's method can be referenced: use (EBIT + lease interest) / (interest expense + lease interest) to more accurately reflect debt service capacity. Specifically for the CFA exam, strictly follow the income statement data in the textbook.

session_83.text: When analyzing REITs, it is recommended to focus on the 'net operating asset net profit margin' and the 'leverage contribution ratio.' The net operating asset net profit margin reflects the operating efficiency of the underlying assets, while the leverage contribution ratio reflects the amplifying effect of debt on shareholder returns. You can first break down the net operating asset net profit margin to see whether the operating differential rate is positive.

session_83.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_83.text: How are operating spread and leverage contribution ratio calculated in REITs? Compared with the Sharpe ratio, what aspect does DuPont analysis focus more on?

session_83.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_83.text: Operating differential rate = net operating asset net profit margin - after-tax interest rate; a positive value indicates that debt can enhance ROE. Leverage contribution rate = operating differential rate × net financial leverage. The Sharpe ratio emphasizes risk-adjusted returns, while DuPont analysis focuses more on profit drivers—ROE decomposition; the two complement each other. In your REITs plan, you can first use DuPont analysis to identify profitability weaknesses, then use the Sharpe ratio to assess portfolio risk.

session_88.text: In CFA Level II Financial Statement Analysis, I always have trouble sorting out the difficult points: deferred income taxes, lease accounting, and pension accounting. My notes are also insufficient. I want to catch up on my progress in April. Could you help me clarify the core logic and memory techniques?

session_88.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_88.text: The core of deferred income tax is the difference between tax and accounting: the balance sheet method recognizes DTA/DTL; just remember 'temporary difference × tax rate'. The key to lease accounting: operating leases recognize expenses on a straight-line basis, finance leases split interest and depreciation. Pension accounting focuses on distinguishing defined contribution (payment is the obligation) from defined benefit (actuarial assumptions affect it). I suggest using 'comparison tables + mnemonics' to strengthen memory, such as 'DTA is deductible in the future, DTL is taxable in the future'.

session_88.text: Understood, these comparison points are very clear. Also, I can listen to podcasts during my morning and evening commutes and morning runs. Do you have any recommended resources? How should I structure the April review plan?

session_88.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_88.text: Recommended listening: 'CFA Level II Financial Statement Analysis Intensive' podcast (such as Bloomberg or Gaodun's short audio). Listen to key chapters for 20 minutes during your morning run. April plan suggestion: spend 2 hours per day on difficult points in the first two weeks (1 hour in the morning and 1 hour in the evening), then do practice questions and review mistakes in the last two weeks; use Anki cards to memorize formulas and journal entries during spare time.

session_101.text: Today at the roundtable discussion at the Shanghai International Financial Summit, I spoke as the third guest, talking about cross-border REITs investment balancing returns and liquidity. session_101.text: When doing mindfulness meditation tonight, I kept getting distracted, thinking about the socializing at tomorrow's breakout session. How can I improve focus?

session_101.text: You want to find a way to deal with distracting thoughts during meditation, and at the same time relieve anxiety about tomorrow, right?

session_101.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_101.text: You can try the "labeling method": when your mind wanders, silently say "plan" in your mind, then gently bring your attention back to your breath. Before bed, use the 4-7-8 breathing technique (inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 7 seconds, exhale for 8 seconds) to help relax.

session_101.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_101.text: The labeling method sounds good. Can the 4-7-8 breathing technique help me fall asleep faster? I need to get up early tomorrow.

session_101.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_101.text: Yes, the 4-7-8 breathing technique can activate the parasympathetic nervous system, and usually after 4-5 cycles you start to feel sleepy. Combined with Headspace's body scan meditation, the effect is even better.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: At today's Shanghai REITs Forum roundtable, as the youngest guest, I shared for 15 minutes. The moderator and peers gave high praise, and I also met two senior investors, which gave me a strong sense of achievement.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: This is really remarkable! Your idea of using a dynamic discounted cash flow model to revise the static rental yield is quite innovative. Gaining recognition from industry seniors shows that your professional depth and communication skills are both outstanding.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: Yeah, I was a bit nervous at first, but after I finished and saw everyone's reaction, I became more confident. Do you think there's any room for optimization in this approach in practice?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: Your model has already captured the key differences. If in the future you can incorporate cash flow volatility coefficients for different asset types, or add policy risk adjustment factors, it may make the framework more robust—of course, this depends on the amount of case data you have.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: I just worked out a health management plan for my parents with my sister, but the details of the follow-up checkup are still unclear. My father is 58 and needs long-term medication; my mother is 56 and has high blood pressure. During the May Day holiday, I want to take them to Wuhan Tongji Hospital for a comprehensive checkup. Which departments should we register for? What items are needed?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: It is recommended that your father see the geriatrics or cardiology department, with a focus on carotid Doppler ultrasound, ambulatory electrocardiogram, and liver and kidney function tests; your mother should see the hypertension specialty for 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, blood lipid, and fundus examinations. Appointments can be made through the Tongji Hospital official WeChat account, which releases slots one week in advance. To avoid the May Day peak, it is suggested to choose a working day morning before or after the holiday.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: How much of these items can be reimbursed by medical insurance? Also, my parents are quite resistant to physical examinations. How can I persuade them to cooperate?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: The medical insurance reimbursement rate for outpatient check-ups is about 50%-70%; you can call the Wuhan Medical Insurance Bureau at 027-12393 for confirmation. When communicating, it is recommended to emphasize that 'this is accompanying you for routine health maintenance, not seeing a doctor,' and invite them to participate in registration and recording to give them a sense of control. You can make a simple checklist and schedule for the check-ups, and talk through the details with them one day in advance to ease their anxiety.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: This afternoon I took dozens of street photos in Lujiazui, capturing some contrasts of “stillness and motion,” but I'm not satisfied with the composition of a few shots and would like your advice.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: Do you want me to help you analyze specific photos from the perspective of composition techniques and storytelling? Can you describe one or two works you care about or feel confused about?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: There is a candid shot of father and son skateboarding: the father pushes the child on a skateboard, with the reflection of a glass curtain wall in the background. I used a high-angle shot at the time, but the picture felt a bit messy.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: This photo has a strong storytelling feel. I suggest trying a vertical crop, placing the father and son on the lower right third line, using the reflective lines of the glass as leading lines, and removing the extra pedestrian on the left to highlight the subject. In post-processing, you can lower the highlights and increase contrast.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: I just finished reading the chapters on 'overconfidence' and 'representativeness bias' in behavioral finance. Some viewpoints at today's forum made me reflect: for example, did the asset management institutions' question about valuing third- and fourth-tier commercial properties imply some kind of bias? Can you help me clarify these two concepts and their real-world applications?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: Overconfidence refers to investors overestimating their predictive abilities, such as trading frequently yet underperforming the market; representativeness bias refers to people drawing quick conclusions based on superficial characteristics (such as recent performance) while ignoring statistical probabilities. The forum question may reflect the 'availability heuristic'—overly focusing on recent popular cases (such as successful projects in first-tier cities) while underestimating risks in third- and fourth-tier cities. Your 'dynamic discounted cash flow model' is exactly a good way to counter static bias.

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_102.text: Yes, I am indeed thinking about whether I have representativeness bias: for example, if a guest on the forum is bullish on a tech stock, I subconsciously think of recent soaring cases without closely looking at the fundamentals. How can I avoid making similar mistakes in daily work?

session_102.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_102.text: Create a 'bias checklist': for each investment recommendation, first ask yourself, 'Am I relying only on recent data?' 'Have I underestimated the base rate?' Also record the rationale and outcomes of decisions, and review them regularly. For example, next time you recommend a fund to a client, present long-term performance and peer comparisons at the same time.

session_108.text: Tonight I practiced the neck flexion resistance and lateral flexion resistance exercises the doctor newly taught me. After doing them, I feel slight soreness in my neck. Is this a normal reaction or incorrect form? Can you help me describe the correct steps and common mistakes of these two exercises in detail?

session_108.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_108.text: Mild soreness and swelling are normal reactions after training, indicating the muscles have been stimulated. However, tingling or numbness should be avoided. Neck forward flexion resistance: cross your hands and place them on your forehead, push your head and neck forward while your hands resist backward, keeping the head and neck still for 5 seconds. Lateral flexion resistance: place the palm of the same side on the side of your head, push your head and neck sideways while the hand resists in the opposite direction. Common mistakes: shrugging shoulders, holding breath, and using too much force. During the exercises, breathe evenly and keep shoulders relaxed.

session_108.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_108.text: It is recommended to hold each movement for 5 seconds, 8-10 reps per set, 2-3 sets per day, with 30 seconds rest between sets. After practice, do static stretches for the neck: extension and lateral flexion, 15 seconds each. On the high-speed rail, you can do: slowly turn your head left and right, tuck your chin, and shrug and roll your shoulders, 5 times each, once every hour. For daily office work, get up and move every 40 minutes, and raise your computer screen to keep it at eye level.

session_114.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_114.text: I just finished a CFA financial reporting mock exam with a 72% accuracy rate. The mistakes are concentrated on goodwill impairment, foreign currency translation, and cash flow adjustments. These three areas always confuse me. Could you help me explain the logic and calculation steps in an accessible way?

session_114.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_114.text: OK, let me help you clarify with simple examples: 1) Goodwill impairment: first allocate goodwill to the cash-generating unit, then compare carrying amount with recoverable amount; any excess first offsets goodwill; 2) Foreign currency translation: under the temporal method, monetary items use the current rate, non-monetary items use historical rates; the current rate method uses the year-end rate for everything; 3) Indirect method cash flow: interest expense should be excluded (since it is already included in net profit, it needs to be added back), and interest income is also added back (because it is non-operating). Would you like me to create three similar practice problems?

session_114.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_114.text: Yes, I especially want to know how to allocate goodwill to asset groups in goodwill impairment testing, and example questions on the difference between the temporal method and the current rate method.

session_114.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_114.text: Understood. Example: Company A's carrying amount includes goodwill of 1 million, and the asset group's carrying amount is 4 million. The recoverable amount is 4.2 million. First allocate the goodwill of 1 million, the asset group's carrying amount becomes 5 million, subtract 4.2 million to get an impairment of 0.8 million, which is entirely offset against goodwill. Goodwill remains 0.2 million. Foreign currency example: Company B has inventory with a cost of ¥80 and a market price of ¥100, and its functional currency is the US dollar. Under the temporal method, inventory uses the historical exchange rate (1:6) to get $13.33; under the current rate method, it uses the period-end rate (1:7) to get $14.29. The difference is the impact of the translation method. I suggest you organize a comparison table by question type to strengthen your memory.

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_118.text: I just redid 15 derivative practice problems, but I'm still a bit unclear on the breakeven point calculation principle for butterfly spreads, FRA pricing logic, and the steps for binomial tree American options. Can you help me sort them out?

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_118.text: No problem. Butterfly spread breakeven points: buy the two wing options (out-of-the-money/in-the-money) and sell the middle at-the-money option. There are two breakeven points: the lower breakeven = lower strike price + net premium, and the higher breakeven = higher strike price - net premium. FRA pricing is based on no-arbitrage; the forward rate is implied by spot rates, and settlement is based on the discounted difference between the contract rate and the market rate. Binomial American option pricing discounts backward from the terminal nodes, and at each node compares the holding value with the early exercise value, taking the larger one.

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_118.text: Then what's the main difference between FRAs and interest rate futures? They feel easy to confuse.

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_118.text: Key differences: FRA is settled once over the counter, while interest rate futures are marked to market daily on the exchange; FRA’s quotation is a forward rate, while futures prices imply a rate but are subject to convexity adjustment; FRA settlement uses actual days/360, while futures use standardized contracts. My advice: remember that FRA is a “forward contract” and futures are “standardized forwards,” plus the convexity adjustment – that’s it.

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_118.text: Got it. I hadn't noticed the convexity adjustment part before. Can you summarize the high-frequency exam points and common pitfalls of CFA derivatives again?

session_118.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_118.text: High-frequency exam points: 1) Profit and loss diagrams for option strategies (spreads, combinations); 2) Forward/futures pricing and cost-of-carry model; 3) Swap valuation (interest rate swap pricing); 4) Two-step binomial tree model. Common error points: confusing the pricing steps of European and American options, ignoring the FRA discount factor, and omitting the net premium when calculating the breakeven point of a butterfly spread. It is recommended to use charts for comparative memorization, such as drawing profit/loss diagrams for each strategy.

session_125.text: Yes, for those two questions, I just overlooked the early exercise check for American put options at intermediate nodes. Also, I'm still a bit unclear about the intrinsic relationship between the BS model and the binomial tree. Can you explain it?

session_125.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_125.text: The binomial tree is the discrete-time version, and BS is the continuous limit. When the time step tends to infinity, the price path of the binomial tree converges to geometric Brownian motion, and the pricing formula corresponding to the risk-neutral probability evolves into the BS formula. Understanding this can help you unify memory: the setting of u and d in the binomial tree corresponds to the volatility in BS. It is recommended that you compare the one-step binomial tree with BS delta hedging; the two are essentially the same.

Could you help me break down the steps in an intuitive way?

session_132.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_132.text: The core is that the present value of the floating leg equals the face value: because each period's floating cash flow is determined by the forward rate, discounting to that payment date exactly equals the face value. You can use the bond method, decomposing the swap into a fixed-rate bond and a floating-rate bond. After resets on payment dates, the floating bond's face value remains unchanged, so its present value is always 1 (notional principal). For discount factors, select spot rates of corresponding maturities, and discount each period's cash flows from the current time point.

session_134.text: Today I reviewed CFA Level II swap pricing. The mark-to-market and CVA parts are a bit tricky. Can you break it down with a simple example? For example, how does CVA specifically affect swap value?

session_134.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_134.text: Okay. Suppose a swap paying a fixed interest rate has a risk-free value of 1 million. If the counterparty default probability is 2% and the recovery rate is 40%, then CVA = 1 million × 2% × (1-40%) = 12,000. So the true value of the swap should subtract this 12,000 credit risk adjustment.

session_134.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_134.text: So CVA is essentially the discounting of expected losses? And mark-to-market is recalculating the swap value at market interest rates on each settlement date, right?

session_134.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_134.text: That's right. Mark-to-market means resetting the swap's value daily at the current interest rate. If interest rates rise, the fixed-rate payer has positive value; conversely, negative value. CVA, on the other hand, is the discounted expected loss after considering the counterparty's default. Only by combining the two can we obtain a swap price that accounts for credit risk.

session_136.text: In this afternoon's photography class, I reviewed the dodge and burn method with curves and the high-frequency/low-frequency separation, but the steps are still not clear. Could you explain in detail the operating principles and key techniques of the dodge and burn with curves?

session_136.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_136.text: The core of dual-curve skin retouching is separating skin light and shadow from texture. In Photoshop, you need to create two curve adjustment layers: one to brighten (to inspect shadows) and one to darken (to inspect highlights), with black masks. Then paint on the mask with a white brush, keeping flow and opacity at 10%-20%, gradually correcting uneven light and shadow. First create a blank layer and use the healing brush to fix obvious blemishes, then start fine-tuning with the dual curves.

session_136.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_136.text: What about high- and low-frequency processing? What situations are they each suitable for? I'm worried about uneven color blocks or harsh edges during operation.

session_136.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_136.text: High-frequency and low-frequency separation is suitable for unifying skin tone while preserving texture. The high-frequency layer retains details (applying the image minus the low frequency), and the low-frequency layer handles skin tone transitions (Gaussian blur). When operating, note: the low-frequency blur radius should not be too large (typically 3-5 pixels), and the high-frequency layer's blend mode should be set to linear light. Uneven color patches are usually caused by insufficient low-frequency blur or excessive brush flow; hard edges can be solved by using a soft-edged brush and reducing flow. It is recommended to try once with the practice image from class, following the steps.

session_136.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_136.text: Got it. I plan to practice with a street portrait this weekend. Are there quicker tips for setting up the observation group?

session_136.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_136.text: The fastest way to create an observation group: create a new black-and-white adjustment layer (desaturate) on the layer, then create a new curves layer and pull it into an S shape to increase contrast, so you can see light and shadow flaws more clearly. Then group these two layers, name it 'Observation Group', and when using it, only show that group to avoid interference. It's recommended to mark the areas that need correction first, then process them one by one for higher efficiency.

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_158.text: I'm reading about the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) in 'Consumer Behavior'. I'm not clear about the difference between the central route and the peripheral route. Can you explain it in simple terms?

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_158.text: ELM explains how people are persuaded. Central route: you carefully analyze arguments, logic, and data, such as researching a company's financial reports to decide on an investment; peripheral route: you are attracted by the spokesperson, emotion, or packaging, such as following a fund manager because of their fame. In short, the central route requires cognitive effort, while the peripheral route relies on peripheral cues.

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_158.text: Got it. So when analyzing retail investor behavior, how is this model used? Is it related to the cognitive biases in CFA behavioral finance?

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_158.text: Retail investors, under information scarcity or time pressure, often take the peripheral route, such as following big-name influencers or buying high and selling low, leading to overconfidence, herding, and other biases. Investors who take the central route analyze fundamentals and are less disturbed by noise. You can use ELM as a framework to identify different decision paths, and then combine it with representativeness bias and availability bias from behavioral finance to understand specific behaviors.

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_158.text: Good point! There is also the Howard-Sheth model. Can you give an example of its application in an investment scenario?

session_158.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_158.text: The Howard-Sheth model emphasizes that purchase decisions are influenced by input variables (such as product information), perceptual structure (consumer understanding), and learning structure (past experience). In investing: for a newly launched ETF (input variable), retail investors form expectations through historical returns and expert reviews (perceptual structure); if they have made money buying similar products in the past (learning structure), they are more likely to buy. You can use this model to analyze the diffusion of new products and investor adoption behavior in the market.

session_170.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_170.text: For Ethiopian beans, the recommended water temperature is 90-92°C, with a medium-fine grind size (similar to granulated sugar). session_170.text: For the bloom, the recommended water amount is 36ml (twice the coffee grounds weight), and the time is 30-40 seconds, until the grounds expand and finish degassing. Your 30ml is a bit low; next time try 36ml and keep the grounds evenly wet during the bloom. For review, record the coffee-to-water ratio, water temperature, and time, and adjust slightly according to taste: if it's sour, lower the water temperature or increase the grind size; if bitter, do the opposite.

session_177.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_177.text: Avoid strenuous exercise, such as rock climbing or high-intensity morning running, within 24 hours after physical therapy. While working at a desk, get up and move your neck every 30 minutes, and you can use a rolled towel to support the back of your neck. If numbness or increased pain occurs before the next physical therapy session, seek an early evaluation.

session_177.text: At work, adjust the screen to eye level, use a standing desk or set regular reminders (e.g., micro-exercise every 45 minutes). Before climbing, do dynamic neck warm-ups (slowly rotate left and right, nod forward and backward); avoid jerking your head during the activity, and tighten your core when landing to reduce impact on the neck. Combine with morning runs to improve cervical spine circulation; it is recommended to choose cushioned running shoes.

session_182.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_182.text: Understood. The core is the equivalence formula: fixed rate = 1 - terminal discount factor / sum of discount factors for each period. I suggest you refer to your mistake notebook, first draw the cash flow timeline, then apply the formula.

session_204.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_204.text: My right knee is sore and swollen. The physical therapist said it's a running form problem and that I need to strengthen my mid-back and glutes. Can you explain in detail why this can relieve knee pressure? Also, he taught me 3 corrective exercises but didn't give written instructions. Can you describe the standard technique in detail?

session_204.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_204.text: Runner's knee (patellofemoral pain syndrome) is often caused by weakness in the gluteal and mid-back muscles, leading to pelvic instability and knee valgus, which increases patellofemoral joint stress. Strengthening the glutes and mid-back can improve lower limb alignment. Three common corrective exercises: 1. Glute bridge - lie supine with knees bent, drive hips up using the glutes until shoulders, hips, and knees form a straight line, hold for 2 seconds; 2. Single-leg squat - hold onto a wall, squat down on one leg, keeping the knee from going past the toes; 3. Resistance band side walk - with knees slightly bent and a band around the ankles, step sideways while maintaining tension. Do 3 sets of 12 reps for each exercise. Before tomorrow morning's run, a dynamic warm-up is recommended, with pace 30 sec/km slower than usual and cadence at 180 steps/min. If pain worsens, stop immediately.

session_204.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_204.text: Got it. I'll go for a 5km slow jog tomorrow morning, focusing on core stability and glute activation. Is it enough to warm up with glute bridges and lateral band walks before the run? If my knees don't feel sore during the run, can I maintain the original pace?

session_204.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_204.text: Before running, it is recommended to add high knees and jumping jacks for 1 minute each to activate the heart and lungs, then complete 2 sets of glute bridges and lateral band walks. During the run, even if there is no soreness, first slow down by 10%-15% and complete the first 2 kilometers as an adaptation period to confirm the body's feedback. Keep the core engaged throughout, actively push the ground with the hips, and maintain a cadence no lower than 170. Stick with it for two weeks before evaluating the results.

session_215.text: I just set up a half-marathon training plan with my running buddies, running every Wednesday and Sunday. session_222.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_222.text: Do I need to wash off the aloe vera gel before applying a new layer? Also, is my sunscreen spray's SPF not high enough? Can I keep morning running while sunburned?

session_222.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_222.text: Aloe vera gel does not need to be rinsed off; you can simply layer other products over it. Sunscreen spray usually has lower protection, so it's better to switch to sunscreen cream or an applied sunscreen. Before the redness and swelling of the sunburned area subsides, stop high-intensity training and switch to indoor stretching or low-intensity activities to avoid further damage to the stratum corneum.

Then compare the extraction rates of the two brews to help you systematically optimize parameters.

session_242.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_242.text: I suggest building it in three layers: the first layer is a daily dashboard, monitoring exposure concentration, volatility, and correlation coefficients; the second layer is VaR and stress testing, designing historical and hypothetical scenarios; the third layer is a macro event-driven module, linking key events such as non-farm payrolls and interest rate decisions with position sensitivity to automatically trigger alerts.

session_242.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_242.text: This framework is very clear. But how should the weights of macro events be set? For example, how should we assess the impact of the Fed's hawkish remarks on Lin Zhihao's account?

session_242.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_242.text: First allocate basic weights based on the correlation between historical holdings and interest rates and exchange rates, then dynamically adjust based on current market sentiment and implied volatility. For example, if Lin Zhihao holds interest-rate-sensitive bonds, hawkish comments would increase the weight of duration exposure. It is recommended to first test with imported holdings, and then fine-tune the parameters with your professional judgment.

session_243.text: Today I ran 10 km on the Yuelu Mountain road in 59:42, finally breaking the 1-hour mark! Next, in September, I'm preparing for my first half marathon. Can you help me analyze this result and create a training plan?

session_243.text: Congratulations! Breaking 1 hour for 10K is an important milestone, with a pace of 5:58/km, showing a good aerobic base. The half marathon goal can be set at 2:10-2:15, with a focus on improving endurance. I suggest adding one LSD long run per week, gradually increasing from 12 km to 18 km, at a pace 20-30 seconds slower than your target half marathon pace. session_243.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_243.text: It is recommended to run 3-4 times a week: 1 interval run (e.g., 800m x 5 sets at 5:20 pace), 1 tempo run (5-8 km at 5:45 pace), and 1 LSD run (10-12 km on weekdays, 12-18 km on weekends). Do strength training twice a week, focusing on the core and lower body, such as squats, lunges, and planks. Within 30 minutes after a run, replenish carbs and protein, such as a banana and protein powder. On race day, keep your pace between 6:00 and 6:15, and speed up later if you have energy left.

For salt tablets, you can take one after 15 km if you sweat a lot to prevent cramps. Use your Garmin watch to set heart rate zones: LSD heart rate 140-155, tempo run 165-175. Wearing a heart rate strap on race day is more accurate. Wishing you success in meeting your goal in your first half marathon!

session_250.text: I just scraped my left calf with an electric scooter—it's a superficial abrasion. The doctor told me to stop running for a week. How should I care for the wound to heal quickly? Are there alternative exercises that won't affect the wound?

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_250.text: After disinfection, use breathable dressing and change it daily; protect with a waterproof patch when showering. For alternative exercise, recommend elliptical machine or upper limb strength training; avoid swimming (the wound has not healed). Persist with core activation and stretching to maintain cardiorespiratory endurance.

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_250.text: Should I apply antibiotic ointment? Is changing the dressing once a day enough?

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_250.text: When there are no signs of infection (redness, swelling, or pus), no antibiotic ointment is needed; ordinary abrasions should be kept dry and clean. Changing the dressing once a day is normal; if the dressing becomes wet or contaminated, it should be changed immediately.

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_250.text: I have an injury in my calf, but I want to train on a fingerboard at home, like hangs and grips. I'm worried about pulling the wound. Any good suggestions?

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_250.text: What you need is a plan that does not rely on leg power and can safely improve finger strength. It is recommended to use seated hangs or half pull-ups, with a chair assisting to reduce the burden on the lower body; for the fingerboard, use an open-hand grip as the main grip, and avoid tensing your calves when using a lock grip.

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_250.text: Yes, I'm just worried that my body swaying while dangling will strain my calves. Also, can I do core training like planks?

session_250.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_250.text: You can do planks and dead bugs, keeping your core tight and your legs relaxed. It is recommended to ice your calves for 15 minutes before training to increase tolerance; extend rest periods between sets to 2 minutes to avoid compensation from fatigue. Later, you can ask coach Li Qiang to adjust the training plan and add more seated and supine finger strength exercises.

session_259.text: Tonight I read the chapter 'Clearly Expressing Needs' in 'Nonviolent Communication' and found it very helpful for work scenarios. session_259.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant

session_259.speaker: Feng Haoran

session_259.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_259.text: It's suggested to use the structure 'fact + feeling + need + specific request'. For example, with a client: first state 'I've observed that the market has been volatile recently', then express 'I'm worried that your return expectations may diverge from reality', then say 'we need to jointly clarify the risk preference', and finally request 'could we have a detailed plan presentation next Tuesday?' session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_260.text: Feng Haoran, a 27-year-old financial advisor, just completed the initial asset allocation draft for client Lin Zhihao today: 60% fixed income + 25% equity + 15% alternatives. The stress test results are acceptable. Is this portfolio logic reasonable? Should the allocation to private quantitative products within the alternative assets be adjusted?

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_260.text: The client will not use the funds for five years and has a steady but slightly aggressive risk preference, so the current framework is reasonable. Although private quantitative funds can increase returns, their liquidity is low; I suggest reducing the allocation from 15% to 10% and reallocating the 5% to a gold ETF to hedge market risk and improve liquidity.

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_260.text: That makes sense. I have increased my attention to the consumer sector as per Mr. Qian's suggestion. How should I specifically select targets? And when presenting the stress test results to the client, which risk points should I emphasize?

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_260.text: For the consumer sector, we recommend white-horse consumer leaders within the CSI 300, paired with consumer sub-sector leaders from the CSI 500. The stress test focuses on demonstrating that in extreme scenarios the maximum drawdown does not exceed 12%, annualized volatility stays within 8%, and it emphasizes the portfolio's low sensitivity to interest rates.

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_260.text: Got it. Then in the reporting language, how should I briefly explain why alternative assets were adjusted from 15% to 10%?

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_260.text: Suggested script: "Mr. Lin, to balance returns and liquidity, we will appropriately reduce the allocation of private quantitative funds in alternative assets and increase gold ETFs to ensure we can respond to market changes at any time within the five-year period." This is easy for the client to understand.

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_260.text: Video-called my younger sister tonight. She was anxious about losses from chasing rises and selling on dips. I suggested she switch to ETF dollar-cost averaging, and she felt better. But I'm worried she can't stick to the discipline. I want to systematically help her build long-term investing habits. Do you have any specific suggestions?

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_260.text: You hope to guide your sister from short-term speculation to long-term investing in a gentle and effective way, while also consolidating your own investment philosophy. You could consider recommending broad-based ETFs (such as CSI 300 and CSI 500) and sector ETFs, setting up a monthly fixed-amount smart investment plan, and using mental accounting theory to help her separate emotions from decisions.

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_260.text: Yes, mental accounting is a good angle. But how specifically can we use nonviolent communication to persuade her to persist? For example, she might want to stop the regular investment when she sees a decline.

session_260.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_260.text: You can use the 'wrong account' technique: have her treat the regular investment account as a 'future fund', keep separate records, and not mix it with other accounts. Whenever she wants to operate, first record her emotions and expectations before acting. You can also share examples of your own discipline in managing your portfolio, using empathy rather than lecturing.

session_275.text: You are worried that tight cash flow after buying a house will affect your investment pace, while hoping to maintain the long-term goal of a 1 million investment portfolio. session_275.text: Yes, my original investments were mainly in stocks and funds. After the monthly payment, I need to maintain liquidity for 3-6 months of living expenses, and I also want to take advantage of the mortgage rate differential for arbitrage.

session_275.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_275.text: Suggestions: 1. Transfer 20% of high-risk stocks to money market funds or treasury bond reverse repos as an emergency reserve; 2. session_289.text: My phone was stolen, and I lost two weeks of street photography photos and draft investment notes in the cloud drive. I tried several recovery software programs without success. I've already bought an encrypted external hard drive and enabled automatic cloud backup, but I'm still not confident. Are there more professional recovery methods? session_289.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_289.text: You are mainly concerned about two points: first, whether professional methods can recover the lost data; second, whether the current cloud + external hard drive solution is reliable enough. Did I understand correctly?

session_289.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_289.text: Yes, both the photos and notes are key—I want to be absolutely sure.

session_289.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_289.text: For data recovery, you can try Disk Drill or Recuva for deep scanning of the phone's memory card. If the phone is no longer available, contact a professional company. For backup, the 3-2-1 rule is recommended: keep 3 copies of backups (local external hard drive, cloud, and another device), use 2 types of media (hard drive + cloud), with 1 copy stored offsite (e.g., office safe). Also enable the version history feature on cloud drives, and regularly manually export key photos and notes to cold storage.

session_289.text: It is recommended to use professional mode: fix ISO at 100 to reduce noise, shutter speed 2-4 seconds, with a tripod or stable posture; enable AI enhancement to automatically optimize colors; for post-processing, recommend the Lightroom mobile app to adjust exposure and reduce noise.

session_297.text: Tonight at the hotel I used Lightroom to process the photos taken in Zhangjiajie during the day, but the golden color of the mountain and the skin tones look unnatural. How can I adjust to achieve a warmer sunset tone?

For skin tones, you can use tone curves to add warmth to midtones. For group photos, use a gradient filter to brighten facial areas to avoid backlighting underexposure. Before shooting tomorrow, set the in-camera white balance to cloudy mode and select the landscape picture style to enhance color contrast.

session_297.text: How exactly do you fix backlit portraits? And can a batch watermark script save time?

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: Today I took my parents to Zhangjiajie for the day. In particular, my mom successfully took on the glass skywalk. Even though she's afraid of heights, she walked the whole way with a smile in the end—it gave her a real sense of accomplishment!

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: I can hear how proud and satisfied you are. It's touching that your mother was able to overcome her fear with your company. Can you talk about how you comforted her at that moment?

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: Yeah, I held her hand the whole time, telling stories about her taking me to the park when I was little to distract her, while dad recorded videos to encourage her. In the evening, when we cast these photos to the screen at the hotel, mom's eyes were red, and our whole family burst out laughing.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: So heartwarming! You not only gave mom courage, but also created precious memories for the whole family. This way of expressing love through action is more meaningful than any achievement. Tomorrow on the return trip, continue to enjoy this warmth too.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: I plan to drive back to Changsha from Zhangjiajie tomorrow, leaving around 9 o'clock, taking the Changsha-Zhangjiajie Expressway, with my parents. Can you help me check tomorrow's traffic conditions, weather, and any things I need to pay attention to?

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: According to the forecast, on October 26 it will be cloudy along the Zhangjiajie to Changsha route, with temperatures of 16-22°C, no rain or snow, suitable for driving. The Changsha-Zhangjiajie Expressway currently has no reports of construction or accidents, but the Cili to Changde section has heavy traffic; it is recommended to take a rest at the Cili Service Area. In addition, it is recommended to check the spare tire, drinking water, and food in the trunk. Your mother has a history of motion sickness, so please prepare motion sickness medication and remind her not to eat too greasy at breakfast.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: Okay, is one rest stop at the service area enough? Also, do we need to refuel beforehand?

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: The whole journey is about 320 kilometers, and one rest stop at Cili Service Area is enough. It is recommended to fill up the tank in Zhangjiajie before departure; there are also plenty of gas stations at service areas along the way, but avoid peak-hour queues. If the tank is more than half empty, you can refuel at Cili Service Area. In addition, it is recommended to check real-time traffic conditions again before leaving at 8:30, and be aware of the morning rush from Zhangjiajie city to the highway entrance.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: This afternoon I accompanied my mom on the Zhangjiajie glass walkway. She has a fear of heights, so I held her hand the whole way and told stories to distract her. I looked calm on the surface, but I was actually panicking inside, afraid she would break down.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: At that time, you had to comfort your mother while also controlling your expression so she wouldn't see your nervousness. That must have been very stressful, right? Do you need to talk about the emotions brought on by this sense of responsibility?

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_298.text: Yes, halfway through she wanted to back out. While I was steadying her, my mind was filled with 'I can't let anything go wrong.' In the end she finished safely, and when she saw the photos she laughed until she cried. Only then did I breathe a sigh of relief.

session_298.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_298.text: You are amazing. You used calmness and strategy to turn tension into a protective force. This sense of responsibility not only accomplished the challenge, but also made your mother feel a sense of security, and deserves recognition.

session_300.text: Just finished a meeting with Lin Zhihao. He is satisfied with the cross-border REITs plan, but I want to double-check the technical details of capital pooling, such as the SPV structure and custodian bank arrangements, as well as the signing process checklist, compliance points, and tax treatment for next week. Can you help me sort this out?

session_300.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_300.text: In terms of capital pooling, an SPV can be set up as the intermediate holding entity, with a custodian bank responsible for separate account management, and funds going outbound through a cross-border two-way RMB cash pool. For signing, you need to prepare: investment intention letters, SPV establishment documents, custody agreements, and tax filing forms. For compliance, pay attention to ODI filing and anti-money laundering review. For tax, it is recommended to use the Hong Kong-Mainland tax agreement to reduce withholding tax, and hedge exchange rate risk with forward contracts.

session_300.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_300.text: OK, regarding the specific operations of exchange rate hedging, if the client is sensitive to cost, are there more flexible tools? Also, before signing, what other key points should I remind him about when communicating with the client?

session_300.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_300.text: You can suggest that the client use an options combination (such as a risk reversal option), which costs less than a forward but requires bearing some volatility risk. When communicating, emphasize: the timeline for funds going offshore, custodian bank fee sharing, the breakeven exchange rate, and the expected net return after tax planning, to avoid the client having doubts about hidden costs after signing.

However, distributed ledgers can track cash flows in real time, reducing the credit risk of multi-layer intermediaries, which ties in well with the cross-border REITs plan you handled during the day.

session_301.text: I just discussed the implementation difficulties of distributed ledger technology in asset securitization with Professor Chen after class, and he gave a lot of guidance. session_301.text: Of course. Would you like me to organize it according to the structure of pain points–solutions–column application, or focus more on the academic viewpoints provided by the professor?

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_301.text: Yes, focusing on pain points and solution ideas; I need to be able to use them directly in the column. In addition, the professor recommended a few papers that can be compiled together as well.

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_301.text: Okay, I suggest organizing it this way: the first paragraph briefly describes three core pain points of DLT in asset securitization; the second paragraph cites the professor's solutions (e.g., hierarchical encryption, consortium chain coordination mechanism); the third paragraph connects to investment practice and adds references recommended by the paper. Do you think I should generate a draft right away?

session_301.text: Lin Zhihao is going to sign the contract next week. Please help me list a pre-signing preparation checklist, including documents, clause confirmation, and client questions.

session_301.text: I took a few autumn photos of Yuelu Mountain during my morning run today. I picked 3 and color-graded them. Could you comment on the composition and lighting?

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_301.text: Would you like professional advice on composition techniques and post-processing color grading for the photos of the lake view in the morning light and mist, and the silhouette of the elderly tai chi practitioner?

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_301.text: Yes, especially how to preserve details in backlighting, and the exposure parameters for silhouettes.

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_301.text: For backlit morning mist, lower exposure by 0.3 stops to protect highlights, then brighten shadows in post-processing. For silhouette shots, use spot metering on the bright part of the sky to keep the subject fully black with a clear outline. Your photo uses the rule of thirds, placing the lake horizon on the upper third and the old man at the lower-right intersection point—the composition is very appropriate.

session_301.speaker: Feng Haoran

session_301.text: For film street photography, I recommend an ISO 400 all-purpose roll. During the day, use f/8 to f/11 with hyperfocal distance for more relaxed candid shots. Pay attention to light and shadow contrast on the street, and take advantage of early morning oblique light.

session_313.text: My parents are having a senior health check-up tomorrow. Could you tell me what to pay attention to before the check-up, especially regarding fasting and medication? My mother has high blood pressure—should she stop taking her blood pressure medication?

session_313.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_313.text: Generally, you should fast for 8-12 hours before a physical examination. Blood pressure medication usually does not need to be stopped; you can take it with a small amount of water in the morning. But the specifics should follow the appointment sheet or the doctor's instructions. Other tests such as blood lipids and blood glucose require fasting; you can remind them to take their medication normally before the physical exam.

session_313.speaker: Feng Haoran

session_313.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_313.text: Common reference values for the elderly: blood pressure <140/90 mmHg, fasting blood glucose 3.9-6.1 mmol/L, total cholesterol <5.2 mmol/L. If abnormal, it is recommended to retest first, record the results, and then discuss medication or lifestyle adjustments with the community doctor. After the physical examination report is issued, you can come to me for interpretation.

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_314.text: Hello, my father was just diagnosed with high blood pressure. The doctor prescribed medication and also required dietary control. I'm an only child, and my parents live in our hometown. I'm worried he won't stick with it. Can you give me some advice on daily management and medication?

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_314.text: I understand your concerns. The core of hypertension management is: 1) Medication: take it on an empty stomach in the morning as prescribed, do not stop or adjust the dose on your own, and set an alarm as a reminder. 2) Diet: less than 5 grams of salt per day, less oil, no alcohol, and eat more vegetables and whole grains. 3) Exercise: moderate-intensity brisk walking or tai chi 5 times a week, 30 minutes each time. 4) Monitoring: measure blood pressure once in the morning and once in the evening, and record the values. Regularly recheck blood lipids and kidney function every 1-3 months.

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_314.text: Thanks, I've remembered these. I'm still afraid they won't take it seriously. How should I communicate so they can stick with it?

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_314.text: It is recommended to use a three-step communication approach: 1) Empathize rather than lecture—first acknowledge his hard work for the family, then convey "for your health, we will work together." 2) Use tools as assistance—help parents buy a medication organizer with reminder function and a portable blood pressure monitor, and review the data together during nightly video calls. 3) Reinforce positive feedback—encourage with praise or small gifts (such as his favorite books) after each week of persistence. If conditions allow, go back for an in-person guidance session on the weekend; the effect is even better.

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran
session_314.text: I have about 30 street photography works that suit a café atmosphere. I can spare 6-8 hours per week. I've discussed collaboration intentions with Shen Xinyi; she will provide exhibition space, and revenue sharing is negotiable. What I'm currently worried about is pricing and whether it will affect my main job.

session_314.speaker: Feng Haoran's Assistant
session_314.text: Based on your situation, a three-step approach is recommended: 1) Initially launch 3-5 framed paintings and postcards, with pricing based on the average customer spend on artwork in similar cafés (framed paintings 200-400 yuan, postcards 15-25 yuan). 2) The co-branded coffee package can be set as 'buy a painting and get a designated drink' or 'spend over 80 yuan to draw a limited edition postcard' to boost conversion. 3) Keep weekly input within 6 hours, use Moments and photography communities for warm-up promotion, and rely on the café's existing foot traffic, so the risk is low. Trial run for the first 3 months, then assess the returns before deciding whether to expand.
