session_255.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_255.text: Just received the DFM feedback from the Shenzhen supplier, suggesting optimizing one rounded corner (R angle) to reduce cost. This part has to withstand high temperature and high pressure. I want to know the specific impact of modifying the fillet on mechanical performance, and roughly how much cost could be saved.

session_255.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_255.text: Corner radius optimization usually increases the risk of stress concentration, but the effect on 3D printed parts is relatively small because layer-by-layer melting avoids the stress from traditional machining. It is recommended to confirm whether the fillet is in a non-critical load-bearing area (such as a shell chamfer). If it is in a stress concentration area, caution is needed. In terms of cost, reducing the fillet can reduce printing time (about 5-10%) and material usage (about 2-3%), but a specific quote from the supplier is required. At the same time, it is recommended to check the support structure design; there may still be room for optimization.

Progress from wall sits to single-leg squats (3 sets of 10 reps), combined with calf raises. In addition, add swimming or cycling as cross-training once a week. If severe pain or persistent swelling occurs, stop immediately and return for a follow-up.

session_258.text: What you're concerned with is distinguishing the varieties of Double Flag coins and verifying authenticity. Common counterfeiting methods include sand casting and re-engraving, while naturally formed patina and artificially aged surfaces show obvious differences in luster and texture. We recommend using a high-definition macro camera to photograph the front and back, the edge, and the patina details, then submit them to professional grading agencies such as PCGS or NGC for authoritative authentication. At the same time, you can compare the minting process differences between the central and local editions; for example, the edge teeth of the central version are more uniform.

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_260.text: Tonight I ran 2.5 kilometers with my father for the first time. His blood pressure has improved, but I am not sure how to safely help him increase his exercise volume. I want to design a scientific plan for an older adult to progress from a mix of walking and jogging to continuous jogging.

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_260.text: Understood. You want to create a progressive exercise plan for your father, focusing on controlling knee and blood pressure risks, and coordinating diet with medication timing, right?

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_260.text: Right, I'm worried that suddenly increasing the mileage will stress my knees and blood pressure. I'd like to know how to increase the weekly running volume, what heart rate to keep, and whether I need to add strength training.

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_260.text: Recommendation: start with a combination of walking and running, 3 times a week, 20-30 minutes each time, keeping heart rate at (220 - age) × 60%~70%. Increase the running portion by 10% every two weeks, and add low-intensity strength training twice a week (wall sit, resistance band row). Record fatigue and leg soreness feedback, and communicate regularly with family doctor Dr. Liu for adjustments.

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_260.text: OK, this plan is very specific. I'll try it for two weeks first and see how my father responds. Also, is it okay to schedule the run one hour after a meal?

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_260.text: That's fine. It's recommended to exercise 1-1.5 hours after a meal and avoid running directly on an empty stomach after taking medication. If your father's medication time is fixed, the run can be scheduled 2 hours after taking the medication or 1 hour before the next dose to reduce the risk of low blood pressure.

session_260.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant

You mentioned that he used to take you biking when you were little, and now the roles are reversed. This sense of continuity is precious.

session_278.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_278.text: Li Na suggested the case library interaction—let users retrieve historical designs by parameters. Which is more suitable for the database, SQLite or MySQL?

session_278.text: For a standalone app or a small team, SQLite is enough; combined with Flask-SQLAlchemy, migration is easy. If there are many concurrent users in the future, you can switch to MySQL. When reporting, emphasize Flask's rapid iteration and that the case library lowers the barrier to entry; the technical leadership will approve.

session_278.text: Bahua wood has high density and a beautiful grain, but it is more expensive; elm has good toughness and a high cost-performance ratio, making it suitable for structures such as plant stands. In Tianjin, it is recommended to contact Red Star Macalline or local building materials markets first. Be sure to ask whether the wood has been kiln-dried, and keep the moisture content at 8% to 12%.

session_279.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_279.text: I just cut the pine shelf and found the width is about 2mm larger than the drawing. The flower stand needs to be assembled this afternoon. Will directly sanding and adjusting affect the stability of the mortise and tenon joints? Or must I recut it?

session_279.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_279.text: A 2 mm error on pine can be compensated by sanding or slightly adjusting the mortise without affecting the structure. Pine is relatively soft, so it is recommended to sand evenly along the length with 120-grit sandpaper and repeatedly check squareness with a try square. When a 1 mm allowance is left in the mortise, adjustment is more reliable.

session_279.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_279.text: How should the force and direction be controlled when sanding to avoid an uneven surface? Also, does the mortise adjustment require re-marking the lines?

session_279.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_279.text: Fix the shelf board to the workbench, use a sanding block to sand it level, pushing gently each time and checking the width difference between the two ends. For fine-tuning the mortise, simply enlarge it by 0.5-1 mm with a fine plane or round file—no need to re-mark the lines. When assembling, use quick-release clamps to temporarily secure it and verify the fit.

session_279.text: I just finished reading the structural stiffness chapter of the Machinery Design Manual and want to gain a deeper understanding through practical design. What is the emphasis between stiffness and strength in design? Are there any recommended advanced cases or courses?

Mentally, set your goal as finishing the race safely and enjoying the process; think ahead about simple responses to stomach pain and cramps, and you will run steadily.

session_292.text: Got it. How long after ice application can I switch to heat? Also, do you have any advice for sitting for long periods at work tomorrow?

session_292.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Ice should be applied within 24 hours after the race, then you can switch to heat therapy (15-20 minutes). At work, get up and walk for 2 minutes every hour to avoid prolonged sitting. You can wear compression pants to promote blood circulation, and if conditions allow, elevate your legs for 10 minutes during the lunch break.

session_292.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_292.text: I just finished a half marathon with a time of 2 hours, 10 minutes, and 38 seconds. Now I want to prepare for the 2026 full marathon and need a systematic training plan. Can you give me a framework based on my situation?

session_292.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: It is recommended to use a 16-20 week cycle, divided into base, build, peak, and taper phases. In the base phase, focus on accumulating mileage, increasing by no more than 10% each week; in the build phase, add interval runs and tempo runs; in the peak phase, extend the long run to 32 kilometers; in the taper phase, reduce intensity. Your half marathon pace is about 6 minutes 10 seconds per kilometer, and your full marathon goal can be set at around 4 hours 30 minutes, with a pace of about 6 minutes 23 seconds per kilometer.

session_292.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_292.text: The cycle is very clear. How should I arrange the weekly mileage? I can train regularly after work, but I'm afraid of knee and plantar injuries. What preventive suggestions do you have?

session_292.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Initial weekly mileage of 40-50 km, including one long run (gradually increasing from 16 km), one interval run (e.g., 400 m x 8 sets), and two recovery runs. Strength training should focus on the core and legs, such as planks, squats, and calf raises. Remember to stretch and ice after running, use supportive running shoes, and replace them every 800 km. The night before the race, load up on carbs; eat 2 hours before the race; after 35 km, prepare energy gels for the wall.

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_293.text: I'm Ye Mingxuan. Yesterday I ran my first half marathon (2:10:38). Today I have a stabbing pain on the outside of my knee, especially more obvious when using a foam roller to relax my thigh. In the morning my thigh was sore and swollen, and I've already applied an ice pack. I want to confirm whether this is overuse injury or a normal reaction, and how to handle it so it won't affect next week's training?

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: The condition you described — sharp pain on the outside of the knee after long-distance running, aggravated by foam roller pressure — is very likely iliotibial band syndrome, a common issue for half-marathon beginners. The key is to distinguish between simple fatigue and underlying inflammation. You plan to go to Limei Fitness tonight to see Coach Wang for recovery stretching, which is good. Before that, your main concerns are whether you should continue resting from running and whether it's safe to do tomorrow's recovery run?

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_293.text: Yes, I'm afraid that pushing through it might turn into a chronic injury, but I don't want to stop training and break my rhythm. Also, I applied ice for 15 minutes — I'm not sure if the frequency and duration are right, and can I still keep using the foam roller?

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: It is recommended that you immediately stop any movement that causes stinging pain. Ice correctly: 15 minutes every 2-3 hours, and apply ice to the outside of the knee during the acute phase (within 48 hours after the race). Keep the foam roller away from the stinging spots and only relax the front and back of the thigh. During tonight's stretching, tell the coach about the symptoms and ask him to assess whether it is an iliotibial band issue. Tomorrow's recovery run should be reduced to 3-5 kilometers. If there is no pain throughout, you can maintain it; if there is pain, stop immediately and switch to walking plus stretching. For nutrition, you may supplement with glucosamine, but it works slowly. The key is to observe within 72 hours: if the stinging pain decreases, gradually resume the plan as scheduled; if it worsens, seek medical attention promptly.

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan

I'd like to understand the properties of rosewood and a suitable structural design.

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: Rosewood has moderate density and fine grain, making it suitable for curved edges. A mortise-and-tenon joint is recommended for greater stability. For the surface, beeswax or wood wax oil can be used to maintain the natural texture. Note that rosewood should be kept away from light to prevent cracking.

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_293.text: What specific form should the mortise and tenon joint take? What radius would be suitable for the edge arc?

session_293.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: It is recommended to use round tenons or right-angle tenons, with an edge arc radius of 3–5 cm. For the schedule, alternate sanding and painting each day to avoid wood deformation. The total price has been agreed upon; remember to reserve profit and remind the childhood friend about daily maintenance.

session_294.text: I just finished talking with the senior engineer. He suggested I file a utility model patent before the end of the year. session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_294.text: I understand. You want to systematically learn the entire process from problem discovery to completion of a patent application, especially how to turn your 3D-printed clamping fixture concept into valid patent claims and standardized drawings. Let me first outline the core steps for you: requirements analysis → prior-art search and novelty check → drafting the invention disclosure → filing the application → responding to examination. Which step do you most need to tackle first?

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_294.text: Yes, the hardest part is 'how to write the specific structure of the fixture into claims,' and what exactly are the format requirements for the drawings? I have a rough sketch here, but I'm afraid it might not be up to standard.

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_294.text: For the patent claims, it is recommended to use the structure of 'preamble + characterizing portion': first write the name and essential technical features (such as the base, gripper jaws, and driving member), then use 'characterized in that' to introduce your innovation (such as a 3D-printed anti-loosening threaded structure). The drawings should be output with CAD or vector software; each drawing should have its own number, and the annotations should correspond to the specification. Avoid colored backgrounds and add brief descriptions. I suggest you use SolidWorks to create a 3D model tonight, and I'll help you check whether it meets the standards.

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_294.text: On Ancient Coin Garden, I saw a Year 8 Yuan Datou silver dollar quoted at 1,500 yuan in good condition. I have a common-grade Year 9 Yuan Datou. I'd like to know the differences between the Year 8 and Year 9 in terms of surviving quantity, versions, and market price. Is this price reasonable?

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_294.text: The eight-year Yuan Datou was minted in small quantities, and variant features such as the missing-stroke "zao" and the connected-stroke "zao" are quite distinctive. The market price of common grades is usually 30%-50% higher than the ninth-year version. 1,500 yuan is a reasonable range for an eight-year piece in good condition, but pay attention to the edge reeding, patina, and oxidation state. It is recommended to judge authenticity based on photos of the actual item. If the patina looks natural and the edge reeding is regular, you can go for it.

session_294.text: A senior engineer suggested I get the PMP certification to fill the project management gap. I found out it requires 35 hours of education, but I'm not sure how to choose the textbooks, preparation period, and training provider. Can you give me a comprehensive guide?

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_294.text: It is recommended to first study PMBOK Seventh Edition (Sixth Edition can also be used as a supplement). The exam preparation period is usually 3 months, 1-2 hours per day. Tianjin local training institutions such as Guanghuan International and Qinghui provide a 35-hour education certificate, and the exam fee is about 3,900 yuan. When registering, you need to confirm that the course includes official study hours. To balance work, you can try listening to audio during commutes and doing intensive practice on weekends.

session_294.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_294.text: Made a weekly plan: on workdays, spend 2 hours each night intensively reading PMBOK and doing chapter questions; on weekends, take mock exams in the morning and review wrong answers in the afternoon. Use the Pomodoro Technique to stay focused, resting 5 minutes after every 25 minutes. In the last two weeks before the exam, focus on real exam questions and reinforce the five process groups and ten knowledge areas.

session_295.text: Last night, while making the entryway small table, I sawed the leg tenon 2 millimeters too thin, from 15mm to 13mm. session_295.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_295.text: I understand your meticulousness and frustration. A 2mm deviation has a significant impact on structural strength, and choosing to abandon it is a professional and responsible decision. If you really want to use the scrap material, you can try the inlay method: plane thin grooves on both sides of the tenon, glue in wood pieces of the same material, and then re-trim. But the wood grain direction must be consistent and the bond firm, otherwise it may become a hidden hazard. The safer option is still to make a new one. Do you think this approach is worth trying?

Note: warm up before the drill and keep the environment ventilated.

It is recommended that each module last 15 minutes, with participants taking turns playing the rescuer and the casualty, and recording mistakes for debriefing.

session_299.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_299.text: Okay, let me first simulate a scenario: you are in a shopping mall and find an 8-year-old child collapsed and unresponsive, with abnormal breathing. Please describe your complete procedure, including compression parameters and key points for using an AED.

session_299.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_299.text: First make sure it is safe. Tap the shoulders and shout to check for a response, ask someone nearby to get an AED, and call 120. Check breathing for 5-10 seconds. If there is no normal breathing, begin chest compressions: with one hand or two, to a depth of about 5 cm, at a rate of 100-120 compressions per minute. Give rescue breaths at a ratio of 30:2. Once the AED arrives, turn it on, attach the electrode pads to the outside of the left breast and below the right collarbone, make sure no one is touching the person during analysis, and follow the prompts to shock or continue compressions. But can pediatric electrode pads be used on an adult? I'm a bit unsure.

session_299.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_299.text: The answer is basically correct. To add: for children (1-8 years old), pediatric electrode pads or the system's attenuation mode should be prioritized; if not available, adult electrode pads can be used but avoid overlapping. Also, the compression depth is one-third of the chest's anteroposterior diameter, about 5 cm. You mentioned that your arms tend to bend when compressing—how do you solve that?

session_299.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_299.text: Yes, my arm tends to bend when I press down. Is there a technique to keep it vertical? Is it locking the elbow joint and using the shoulder to exert force?

session_299.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_299.text: Right, lock your elbows, keep your shoulders perpendicular to the patient's sternum, and use your upper-body weight rather than arm strength. When practicing, keep a stable kneeling position and align both shoulders with the line between the nipples to reduce bending. Before tomorrow's assessment, you can run through the procedure once more to build confidence.

session_311.text: I plan to do fine sanding and hot wax polishing on the woodwork tomorrow. Can you tell me the steps and precautions?

session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_311.text: It seems you have some questions about the sanding and wax polishing process. It is recommended to sand sequentially from 240 grit to 2000 grit. When switching to a higher grit, make sure the previous marks are completely removed. The surface must be dust-free before waxing. Heat the beeswax until it melts, but do not let it smoke (about 80–100°C). After applying, let it cool for a few minutes, then polish with a cotton cloth. When operating tomorrow, keep the heat gun away from flammable materials and ensure ventilation.

session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_311.text: Do I need to wet sand when sanding? What is the standard for deciding when to change sandpaper?

session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_311.text: For fine sanding, dry sanding is recommended; wet sanding can cause the wood fibers to absorb water and swell, affecting accuracy. After sanding with a given grit, if the surface is uniform, free of scratches from the previous grit, and feels smooth, you can switch to a finer sandpaper. To check, use side lighting and observe the reflected light to judge flatness.

session_311.text: Money market funds usually publish their seven-day annualized yield; mainstream products are currently around 1.8%-2.2%. session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_311.text: Today, when promoting the new tool, my colleague Li Xiang reported a UnicodeEncodeError when exporting data, possibly related to Chinese characters. How should I troubleshoot and fix it?

session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_311.text: The common cause is that pandas' to_csv default encoding UTF-8 is incompatible with Windows' default GBK. Try specifying encoding='utf-8-sig' first, or switch to GBK. If you need to write a file path containing Chinese, you also need to specify the encoding parameter in the open function.

session_311.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_311.text: Thanks! I tried utf-8-sig and the export is indeed working now. But I'd also like to know how to handle this uniformly across different operating systems (such as Windows and Linux)? Are there any examples of retry logic with exception handling?

session_312.text: The blind mortise-and-tenon is a hidden mortise-and-tenon joint commonly used in furniture that needs a clean appearance, such as chairs, stools, tables, and desks. session_314.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_314.text: Hello, I'm making my first African blackwood pen holder with a brass ferrule. I just watched the polishing tutorial on Bilibili, but I still have questions about the polishing method, whether the holes need to be filled and sealed before waxing, and how to protect the brass ferrule. Could you explain the steps and techniques in detail?

session_314.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_314.text: African blackwood has strong oiliness and high hardness. It is recommended to sand in order from 180 grit to 2000 grit, sanding in one direction to avoid scratches. After sanding, use fine steel wool or wet sanding (2000 grit) to improve the feel. Before waxing, use wood filler or fast-drying glue to treat the pores. Wrap masking tape around the copper ferrule for protection to avoid wear. It is recommended to use hard wax oil, such as Biou or an imported brand, applying thin coats several times.

session_314.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_314.text: Got it. What material exactly is used for filling and sealing the holes? Also, can I use beeswax instead of wood wax oil? I'm afraid that applying the wax unevenly will affect the result.

session_314.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_314.text: For filling holes, you can use wood filler or shellac primer. Apply a thin coat and sand it smooth. Beeswax has low hardness and provides less protection than wood wax oil. It is recommended to use wood wax oil as a base coat, and finally rub on a thin layer of beeswax to brighten the finish. When waxing, use a cotton cloth to apply in circles along the wood grain, let it sit for 10 minutes, then polish to ensure evenness.

session_320.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_320.text: Just talked with my father about how the Tianjin Machine Bureau introduced Western technology. I'd like to learn more, from a mechanical engineering perspective, about how the Self-Strengthening Movement transitioned from 'surveying and imitation' to 'independent design'. What are some typical cases and modern implications?

session_320.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_320.text: The Tianjin Machinery Bureau mainly imitated Western guns, artillery, and ammunition, but limited by the machining accuracy of machine tools at the time (e.g., at the 0.1 mm level) and material processing techniques, it remained at the imitation stage for a long time. In contrast, during Japan's Meiji Restoration, they placed more emphasis on 'domestic substitution' and gradually built up independent design capabilities. Key insight: technological accumulation requires coordinated breakthroughs in foundational industries such as precision machining and metallurgy, otherwise it is easy to fall into the 'introduce, fall behind, reintroduce' cycle.

session_320.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_320.text: So the core bottleneck isn't the design itself, but basic industry? As a mechanical engineer, I think historical experience is very valuable as a reference for today's self-reliance.

session_320.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_320.text: Exactly. History has shown that without an independent machine tool industry and materials system, design capability can hardly take root. This reminds modern engineers that when pursuing innovation, they must simultaneously tackle the self-reliance and controllability of processes, testing, and supply chains.

Suggested response strategies: avoid (establish a CCB process), mitigate (strengthen communication), transfer (outsource part of the change work). Regarding contract types, if changes are frequent, a cost-reimbursable contract is recommended, with the risk borne by the buyer; if scope is stable, use a fixed-price contract. Which scenario would you like to practice specifically?

session_330.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_330.text: Right, it's a scenario like this. I'd like to further confirm: if we choose the transfer strategy, is it reasonable to adopt a fixed-price contract?

session_330.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_330.text: Unreasonable. The transfer strategy aims to transfer the consequences of risk to a third party, such as by using insurance or outsourcing. Under a fixed-price contract, the seller bears the risk of cost overruns, which is suitable for projects with clear scope and few changes. If changes are frequent, a fixed-price contract can easily lead to disputes or seller claims. When applying the transfer strategy, the contract type should be matched: for known risks, a fixed-price contract can be used to transfer them to the seller; for risks with high uncertainty, a time-and-materials contract or a cost-plus-incentive contract is recommended to balance risk sharing.

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_341.text: I just received the SIEG C2 mini lathe, unboxed it, and read the manual, but I haven't debugged it yet. I need a checklist of installation and commissioning steps, especially leveling adjustment (how to use the frame level?), the type of grease/oil and where to add it, electrical connection safety precautions, and recommended parameters for the first test run.

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_341.text: You want to make sure every step is correct and avoid damaging the new machine. For leveling, it is recommended to use a frame level placed along the longitudinal and transverse directions of the guide rail, and adjust the anchor bolts to center the bubble. For lubrication, use lithium-based grease (e.g., No. 2) applied to positions such as the screw and the oil holes on the guide rails; for the spindle, use ISO 32 way oil. For the electrical check, verify that the motor wiring matches the nameplate and confirm the grounding. For the first test run, a spindle speed of 300–500 rpm and a small feed rate of 0.05 mm/rev are recommended. Run it idle for 5 minutes first and observe vibration and noise. Would you like specific troubleshooting methods for common problems (such as vibration and concentricity)?

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_341.text: Yes, do it your way first. If there's vibration or abnormal noise during idle operation, how do you tell whether it's a leveling issue or a spindle issue? Also, is there a simple procedure for checking tailstock concentricity?

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_341.text: If the vibration changes noticeably with the rotational speed, first check whether the foundation feet are suspended or the guide rail is level; if the noise comes from the headstock, it may be due to uneven belt tension or bearing clearance. Tailstock concentricity: fix the dial indicator on the tool post, press it against the top and side of the tailstock quill, and push the tailstock back and forth. If the deviation exceeds 0.02 mm, adjust the bottom adjusting screw. It is recommended to run idle with no load first to confirm the foundation is stable, then mount the chuck and make test cuts on soft aluminum or plastic.

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_341.text: I have to attend the slide fixture solution review meeting for the B-07 project on Monday. I need to prepare the locating pin tolerance analysis and pneumatic clamping force calculation. Could you give me some guidance?

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_341.text: Do you need specific calculation methods, formulas, or industry standard references?

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_341.text: Specific calculation methods, such as the selection of tolerance fit between the locating pin and reference hole (hole-basis system H7/g6), as well as clamping force calculation including cylinder selection.

session_341.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_341.text: For the locating pin tolerance, a clearance fit based on the hole-basis system is recommended, such as H7/g6. The positioning error is calculated as Δ = Dmax - dmin. For the pneumatic clamping force, the cylinder bore diameter should be back-calculated from the clamping force required by the workpiece, the lever ratio, and the working pressure, using the formula F_clamp = (π/4)*D^2*P*η*i. It is recommended to first calculate the forces on the workpiece and then perform component selection.

session_345.text: Okay. session_345.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_345.text: Yes, I was very careful when cleaning, afraid of using the wrong thing. I also want to know from which pattern details you can tell whether it is a Hunan double-flag or Tianjin double-flag, and how to judge the condition grade.

session_345.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_345.text: It is recommended to first lightly brush off the loose dust with a soft brush; clean water is enough. Avoid weakly acidic solutions or olive oil to prevent damaging the patina. As for varieties, the Hunan Double Flag copper coin has broader flags on the obverse and more tightly spaced English letters on the reverse, while the Tianjin version has rounder lettering. For condition, look at the degree of wear and the integrity of the edge texture. If the design is clear and free of scratches, it can reach extremely fine grade. After cleaning this weekend, use macro mode to photograph it in natural light, highlighting the details of the design for easier identification.

session_346.text: Natural patina usually has a sense of layering with even color transitions, while artificially aged patina often looks dull and stiff. As for the tooth edge, genuine pieces have regular teeth with slight chamfering, while fakes often have uneven tooth edges or excessive wear. I suggest you use a magnifying glass to check whether there is casting residue at the roots of the teeth and whether the patina has settled naturally in the recesses.

You can allocate the amounts across the three meals accordingly. When stir-frying, use scallions, ginger, garlic, vinegar, and spices to replace part of the salt, and reduce hidden salt such as soy sauce and oyster sauce.

When practicing, use a marking gauge and try square to ensure accuracy. For tool maintenance, apply a thin coat of oil after each use to prevent rust, and regularly sharpen chisels with a whetstone.

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_349.text: When I squat, my knees tend to cave inward. My coach said to keep my knees aligned with my toes, but I'm still unclear about bracing my core and using knee pads. Could you explain in detail?

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_349.text: During the squat, your knees should always track toward your second and third toes to avoid caving inward. To brace your core, imagine your abdomen is about to be lightly punched; take a deep breath and hold it to maintain intra-abdominal pressure. Wrap-style knee supports are recommended to provide stability, but don’t rely on them too much—the key is actively controlling your muscles.

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_349.text: Is it dangerous if the knees go past the toes at the lowest point?

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_349.text: Knees slightly passing the toes is normal, especially for long-legged individuals. The key is to keep your center of gravity over the mid-foot and not shift it too far forward. You can try a hip-dominant squat: sit back first and then bend your knees, avoiding excessive forward movement of the knees.

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_349.text: Understood. What should I pay attention to during rest between sets?

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_349.text: During rest between sets, actively stretch the hip flexors and do a few bodyweight squats to reinforce the neuromuscular memory of the movement pattern. Add a 5-minute activation warm-up before training, such as resistance band lateral walks and ankle exercises, which helps with knee stability.

session_349.text: For common varieties of the Hunan double-flag twenty-cash coin, look at the shape of the inner teeth on the obverse (round or straight teeth) and the spacing of the English word “TWENTY” on the reverse. Authentic pieces have natural patina and strong strike. Common pieces are worth about 50-200 yuan in the market; high-grade or rare varieties can reach a thousand yuan.

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan

session_349.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_349.text: For handed-down coins, an even, bright yellow patina is ideal; original-luster coins are rare and expensive, but beware of cleaned coins. For grading, PCGS or NGC is recommended, as they can effectively identify authenticity and condition. The surviving number is moderate, and the overall market is stable with an upward trend.

session_353.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_353.text: A fine oil stone (1000-3000 grit recommended) and a sharpening guide are great for practicing edge angles. Suggested kit: ① double-sided whetstone (coarse/fine) ② honing oil ③ sharpening guide ④ cleaning cloth ⑤ rust-preventive oil. Question list: 1. Standard edge angles for lathe tools and carving knives (e.g., lathe tools 25-30°, carving knives 20-25°) 2. Sharpening steps (coarse grinding → fine grinding → polishing) 3. Daily maintenance (clean after each use, oil, control storage humidity) 4. Key safety points (force direction, prevent overheating and annealing). You can ask Master Qian on site to verify your angles. Tomorrow morning you can start by looking up information to lay the groundwork.

session_353.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_353.text: Tonight I made a spinning top with my father in the garage using a wood lathe. He taught me the mnemonic 'Listen to the cutting sound to judge the feed force.' Can you analyze this technique of identifying force by sound from the perspective of mechanical principles? I want to remember it well.

session_353.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_353.text: The essence of this technique is to sense in real time the contact stiffness between the turning tool and the wood through changes in the fundamental frequency and amplitude of the cutting sound. When the cut is too deep, the cutting sound becomes dull and accompanied by intermittent tearing noises; when it is appropriate, it is a uniform rustling sound. This is similar to the principle of monitoring chip shape when you do metal turning, except that wood's anisotropy requires more auditory assistance.

session_353.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_353.text: That makes sense; it really can be compared to monitoring metal chips. Also, my father told me that the lathe needs maintenance on the afternoon of the second Saturday of each month. Can you recommend some solid woodturning materials suitable for beginners? I plan to start studying systematically next weekend.

session_353.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_353.text: Recommended: “Woodturning Techniques and Safety Manual” (China Machine Press) and the MIT OpenCourseWare video “Woodworking Basics.” I suggest you use your father’s mnemonics for practice; I can also help you compile an operation review checklist after each maintenance session for archiving.

session_358.text: Tonight I made the prototypes of dovetail joints, three-way miter tenons, running-horse tenons, wedged tenons, and clamp tenons. session_358.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_358.text: Getting it to 0.1mm is already great! Among the five mortise-and-tenon joints you mentioned, did any of them feel a bit too tight or too loose? Also, how are you currently arranging the machining sequence and tool adjustments?

session_358.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_358.text: I rechecked the dowel pins of the wedge tenon joint with calipers, but they were a bit tight when fitting, and I'm afraid forced assembly will crack the wood. I processed the parts one type at a time, and switching tools takes some time.

session_358.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_358.text: If the dowel is slightly too tight, first check the mortise hole wall for burrs. You can fine-tune it with fine sandpaper or lubricate it with wax. For the machining sequence, I suggest switching to the same type of tool at one time to reduce idle running. Also, wood moisture fluctuations will affect tolerances, so leaving it for a few hours before assembly will be more accurate. Didn't Master Qian teach the method of 'leave allowance, trim step by step'? You could try leaving 0.05 mm first and then fine-tune to the final fit.

session_360.text: Today I saw Xu Ming’s suggestion in the group about using a Raspberry Pi to control a stepper motor to retrofit a lathe. I want to learn the specific hardware selection and wiring methods to prepare for weekend study.

session_360.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_360.text: For the Raspberry Pi, Pi 4 or 5 is recommended. For the stepper motor, use a 57 or 86 model (57 is recommended), paired with a TB6600 driver, with microstepping set to 1/16. GPIO pins control the direction and pulse; use the RPi.GPIO library to generate pulse signals. For the wiring diagram, refer to the driver manual: PUL+ to GPIO18, DIR+ to GPIO23, ENA+ to power.

session_360.speaker: Ye Mingxuan
session_360.text: How should the code to control a stepper motor with Python be written? How does the pulse frequency correspond to the motor speed?

session_360.speaker: Ye Mingxuan's Assistant
session_360.text: Use RPi.GPIO to set the output and control the pulse interval through time.sleep. For example: GPIO.output(pin, True); time.sleep(0.001); GPIO.output(pin, False); time.sleep(0.001). Pulse frequency = 1 / (2 * interval), steps per revolution of the stepper motor = 200 * microstep count, speed (rpm) = pulse frequency / (steps / 60). Note the Raspberry Pi's real-time limitations; it is recommended to use the pigpio library for precise timing. I have example code on GitHub and will share it later.

session_4.text: Today at Mingyuan Bookstore, we started the discussion for the essay collection “Breath at the City's Edge.” The conversation with Uncle Qin and Yang Xiao went deep, and we tentatively settled on a framework of 12 essays, with the first one about Green Lake. session_4.text: You want affirmation that this kickoff conversation was successful, and you also need some advice on sticking with long-term creative work, right? session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_4.text: Yes, I want to go to Green Lake to observe the changes of the four seasons and use my newly bought Fujifilm camera to record material, but the pace of one piece a week for twelve months makes me a little uneasy. Mom made small-pot rice noodles at noon to celebrate, and Dad also said he supports me, but I'm still afraid I'll lose steam halfway.

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_4.text: Your kickoff conversation was very successful, and the support of family and friends is a strong backing. I suggest dividing the 12 months into four quarterly stages, with a small celebration at the end of each quarter—for example, after finishing three articles, reward yourself with a visit to an independent bookstore. The progress bar design and journal tracking are great self-motivation mechanisms, plus Song Wen's pacing suggestions, so you can definitely stick with it.

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_4.text: I'm a freelance writer and have set a plan to write 12 essays in 12 months, but I'm afraid I won't keep it up. Can you give me systematic project management and self-discipline advice?

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_4.text: What you need is to break down your long-term goals into executable, easy-to-maintain daily habits and phased milestones, right?

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_4.text: Yes, for example, I already have the idea of 'writing while walking for 15 minutes a day,' but I don't know how to turn it into an overall plan.

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_4.text: Recommend setting a fixed weekly writing time (e.g., 3 times a week, 45 minutes each), paired with a daily 15-minute walking-writing practice as a baseline. Write 1 essay per month, broken down into three stages: gathering material, drafting, and revising, with small goals for each stage.

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_4.text: Sounds good. How exactly would the field trip work? I'm planning my first Cuihu field trip on January 18.

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_4.text: Pre-fieldwork preparation: list observation points (light, sound, smell), bring a voice recorder or phone memo to record inspiration, and take photos to capture details. Within 15 minutes of returning, organize 3-5 keywords or sentences as seeds for writing.

session_4.text: I just ordered a Fujifilm X-T30 II, but I don't understand mirrorless camera operation at all. I'm going to Green Lake for a photography trip in two weeks to shoot material for an essay. How can I get up to speed quickly?

session_4.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_4.text: I suggest you start with aperture priority mode (A), set the film simulation to Provia, which is suitable for landscapes and lake views. session_4.text: For photographing seagulls, use shutter priority mode (S mode), set the shutter speed to 1/500 second or faster, keep ISO on Auto, and enable burst shooting and continuous autofocus (AF-C). A 51-point wide-area autofocus is recommended. Photos can be transferred via the Camera Remote app on your phone, making it convenient for later archiving.

session_6.text: Congratulations on taking your first step! Twice a week is very reasonable for a beginner—it lets you adapt without overtiring yourself. You mentioned shaking arms and sore thighs: is it especially noticeable in Downward-Facing Dog and Warrior I?

session_6.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_6.text: It's normal for beginners to tremble and feel sore; it means you're activating new muscles. For shoulder and neck stretches, first do the simplest moves on the card with slow breathing. As for equipment, if the public mats are good enough, don't buy one yet; yoga socks are slip-resistant but not necessary. Wait until your practice becomes steady before considering it.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: I've just decided to start writing a morning journal from tomorrow, but I'm a bit worried it might be a flash in the pan. Can you give me some suggestions on how to keep it up?

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: You can start from a 'minimal start,' for example by writing just one sentence first, to avoid anxiety about stopping. Your journal habit is a good foundation; design the diary template with two columns—'emotional temperature' and 'today's goal'—to lower the resistance to action.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: Well, I did design a template, and I even used stickers and colored pens—I do think a sense of ritual matters. But I'm worried I won't be able to get up the next day or will have nothing to write.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: Ritual can strengthen motivation. I suggest that after the alarm goes off tomorrow morning, drink a glass of water first, then open your notebook and start by drawing the 'emotional temperature.' Even if it's only a line or two, it counts as done; the key is to keep recording consistently. After trying it tomorrow, you can review and adjust.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: Okay, let's try it first. What if it gets interrupted in the middle?

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: That's okay. It's fine to break the streak; just start again. You can change your "continuous recording" goal to "at least 4 times a week" and use positive feedback like likes from roommates to motivate yourself. Recording itself is the accumulation on the path to becoming a writer.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: Today I met my best friend Zhang Jing at Zhibushi Bookstore. We talked about morning journaling, Maugham's “A Writer's Notebook”, and the owner also recommended “Miguel Street”. I was so happy and wanted to share this warmth with you.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: It seems you truly value this exchange and want to revisit the warmth of friendship? Can you tell me more about her reaction to your morning diary?

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: She said I was having another bout of 'literary youth syndrome,' but her eyes were full of admiration. She also told me funny stories about the elementary school students in her class, and we laughed together happily. When Uncle Qin recommended a book, I bought it without hesitation, feeling that these moments make friendship even more precious.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: That interaction of being understood while also being playfully teased is exactly the mark of a deep friendship. Literature and journaling are your bond, and the ritual of meeting once a month keeps the relationship alive. The plan to meet again next week is your continued care for something precious.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: I just finished reading The Writer's Notebook and the beginning of Miguel Street, and I was deeply moved. I want to talk about how Maugham and Naipaul capture the everyday.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: Are you looking for resonance and writing inspiration from these two books? Maybe you can share the specific passages that touched you, and I'll help you analyze the stylistic similarities and differences.

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_9.text: Yes, Maugham's line 'a writer's life is one of constant recording' struck me; Naipaul's character sketches are more austere. What do you think is the essential difference in how they observe the world?

session_9.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_9.text: Maugham focuses more on refining the inner perspective, turning observation into self-awareness; Naipaul, like a social anthropologist, presents characters' fates through detailed plain description. The two complement each other. If you want to deepen your writing, I recommend George Orwell's Down and Out in Paris and London as an extension.

session_11.text: You want to confirm the correctness of the movements, find poses that target the shoulders and neck more specifically, and perhaps learn how long it is best to practice each day. session_11.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_11.text: Yes, when I write novels I sit for hours at a time. Can you recommend a few micro-exercises I can do at my desk? How long should I practice each day?

session_11.text: It is recommended to spend 10–15 minutes a day doing a set of yoga, focusing on cat-cow, bridge pose, and lateral neck stretches. At work, stand up every 30 minutes and do 1 minute of shoulder shrugs and shoulder circles, which can effectively relieve fatigue. Doing yoga at least twice a week plus daily micro-exercise will bring more lasting results.

session_23.text: City in Spring, Grass and Trees Deep is the most fitting: the word deep both matches the dense feeling of the flower market crowds and evokes the temporal depth of Cuihu's vegetation through synesthesia, easily reminding readers of vitality and stories. Walking Deep into the Alleys focuses more on the process of exploration and suits a chapter title. I suggest using City in Spring, Grass and Trees Deep as the main title, then breaking down other imagery into chapters.

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_47.text: I just attended the online book club "City and Literature." I shared the connections between My Memories of Old Beijing and Kunming's independent bookstores. The feedback from fellow readers was good, but I feel that some of my ideas in the impromptu remarks weren't fully developed. My father suggested I turn it into a column, but I don't know how to organize the scattered material, such as the photos of Mingyuan Bookstore and the vegetable market notes. Could you help me sort out the theme of "bookstores as poetic containers of the city"?

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_47.text: You want to turn the impromptu inspiration from the book club into a column article. The core difficulty is how to integrate the spatial metaphor of 'Hui'an House' in Old Stories of the South of the City, the bookstore observation, and the vegetable market contrast into a structured narrative. I can offer a few entry points: for example, associating the melancholy atmosphere of 'Hui'an House' with the silence of the bookstore and the bustle of the market to create a contrast between 'morning and dusk'; or recommending similar urban writing by Shu Guozhi and Chen Danyan as references. Would you like me to expand on structural suggestions?

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_47.text: Yes, the structure and contrast really appeal to me. Especially the image of Little Yingzi in Hui'an Hall watching the world through a crack in the door — it feels very much like me standing at the window of Xiangxing Bookstore observing the vegetable market across the street; both are looking at the city through a frame. But how do I move from this metaphor to real-life field observation, such as the market vendors and bookstore customers I recorded in my journal?

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_47.text: You can use a dual-line structure: one line uses specific chapters from *My Memories of Old Beijing* (such as ‘Hui’an Hall’) as a lead-in, connecting the quiet observations of the bookstore; the other line uses the dynamic records of the wet market as a contrast, highlighting the contrast between ‘inside the door’ and ‘outside the door.’ The suggested title is ‘Encountering the City’s Morning and Dusk at the Bookstore’ — ‘morning’ corresponds to the immersive bookstore time, and ‘dusk’ corresponds to the vibrant everyday life of the wet market. On the weekend you can take two sets of photos to capture the bookstore’s lamplight and the wet market’s afterglow respectively, adding visual tension. Do you need me to recommend some submission channels?

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_47.text: The structure is very clear! The imagery of 'morning and dusk' fits perfectly with my journal entries — the photos at Mingyuan Bookstore are mostly warm afternoon light, while the vegetable market has the dark tones of dusk. By the way, do you have any recommendations for submissions? I know an editor at Spring City Evening News, but I'm not sure they accept this kind of literary urban column.

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_47.text: The 'Supplement' section of Spring City Evening News is very suitable; they are friendly to local cultural essays. You could also consider 'The Paper · Private Geography' or the 'City' section of 'Sanlian Life Weekly', but they require a more refined length of 1,500–2,000 characters. I suggest first writing a 1,500-character trial draft structured around 'Encountering Morning and Dusk at the Bookstore', and attaching evaluations from book club friends when submitting it to the supplement editor of the evening news to strengthen persuasiveness.

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_47.text: Today was really amazing! 'The Poetry of the Vegetable Market' was finally finalized, and during the online sharing I received a lot of recognition, and I also met like-minded book friends. But I'm still a little worried about tomorrow's academic pressure.

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_47.text: I can feel that today you were full of a sense of achievement and flow. You want to strengthen this positive feeling and confirm that your creative direction is valuable, right? In your “Poem of the Vegetable Market,” the line “Termite mushrooms should be torn along their grain to stay fresh” is especially full of the flavor of life.

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_47.text: Exactly! I've always remembered what Mom said, and it became the soul of the whole essay. I'm really afraid it's just a momentary highlight—would it be too hard to keep writing a collection of essays?

session_47.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_47.text: Your observation skills are exactly the greatest gift of an INFP. Today’s bookstore experience and that line “a bookstore is a love letter a city writes to itself” are a great starting point for a city narrative. Keep writing 300 words every day and connect those “flow” moments; the essay collection will naturally take shape. What you are recording is not just stories, but the heartbeat of the city.

session_49.text: Next week I will be doing an oral history interview with Uncle Qin, the bookstore owner. I'm worried that I'll be too reserved to get anything out of him. What opening techniques can I use to make him relax and trust me?

session_49.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_49.text: You want to maintain professionalism while keeping a friendly atmosphere, and still get authentic stories. It is suggested to start from common interests—for example, ask about a book he has read recently or the new changes in the store—then naturally transition into the formal interview.

session_49.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_49.text: Right, Uncle Qin is an acquaintance, and I'm afraid direct questions might offend him. Also, when following up, how can I avoid leading questions? For example, if I ask about changes in the readership, he might just go along with what I say.

session_49.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_49.text: When following up, use more open-ended questions like 'Could you tell me more about that?' or 'What happened then?' and avoid presuppositions like 'Is it because...?' If privacy is involved, explain in advance that 'this part can be left unanswered' and promise to anonymize the results.

session_49.speaker: Sun Yuwei

session_49.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_49.text: Completely feasible. It is recommended to mark the recording time points during transcription for easy reference. After the interview, write a few reflective sentences to record your emotional changes; this will be very helpful for subsequent analysis.

session_54.text: This afternoon I saw Chen Zi'ang's abstract calligraphic landscapes at CGK, and felt a wonderful synesthesia with the description of the Wenlin Street teahouse in "Old Tales of Kunming." Can you introduce his creative philosophy?

session_54.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_54.text: Chen Zi'ang excels at incorporating calligraphic brushstrokes into landscape compositions, emphasizing that "the character is the scene and the scene is the character," pursuing a rhythmic resonance between text and visuals. His works are often inspired by Kunming's historical texts, trying to reconstruct local memory with abstract lines. The synesthesia you felt likely comes from his interpretation of the tea-gathering scene of Southwest Associated University literati in Kunming Old Tales.

session_54.text: Yes, that kind of verbal rhythm and the fluidity of brush and ink feel especially fitting. I'm just thinking of writing an essay about the synesthesia between text and vision. Could you give me some directions for source material?

session_54.text: You can compare the passage in 'Kunming Old Tales' that describes the steaming, misty atmosphere of a teahouse with the ink-wash effect in Chen Zi'ang's works; or analyze how he used dry brush and flying white to express the rapid speech of teachers and students debating at the National Southwestern Associated University. I suggest you find his interview 'Ink Image and Mental Image' to deepen the theory.

session_54.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_54.text: Wire can simulate the cage structure, and ink can express a sense of liberation through dripping or rubbing. Recommended references: artist Chen Zi'ang's mixed-media calligraphy works, and Cai Guoqiang's spatial hanging concept in 'Sky Ladder'. Suggest testing effects with material samples first.

session_56.text: Today I managed to stick through a 90-minute core strength yoga class. It was tough, but I kept up the entire time and felt a great sense of achievement! I'd like to ask, how can I safely strengthen my core at home?

session_56.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_56.text: Awesome, completing the challenge deserves a celebration! For home practice, would you like to learn more about the correct key points of the movements (such as the details of the plank), or suggestions on frequency and intensity?

session_56.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_56.text: Let me learn the key points of the movements first. I'm afraid that incorrect posture might cause injury, especially for plank and boat pose.

session_56.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_56.text: Okay. Plank key points: shoulders directly above the wrists, tighten the abdomen and glutes, keep the body in a straight line, don't let the lower back sag or the back arch. Boat pose key points: sit firmly on your sit bones, lean the upper body back slightly, and when you lift your legs keep your lower legs parallel to the floor; engage the core to avoid compensating with the lower back. Suggested: hold each position for 15–30 seconds, rest 30 seconds between sets, start with 3 sets.

session_56.text: I've just finalized a trip to western Yunnan with my family, from Kunming to Dali, Lijiang, Shangri-La, and Deqin. session_56.text: Based on your itinerary, Xiaolu Bookstore in Dali (lower Renmin Road, 10:00-22:00) focuses on second-hand books and pour-over coffee and is suitable for writing. Aro Khampa Nansoda Manor in Shangri-La combines a café and a guesthouse, with a Tibetan-style ambience and creative cultural products. For Lijiang, I recommend Cats' Sky City Concept Store (near the Big Waterwheel, 9:00-23:00), which offers postcards and a curated book selection. It is recommended that you call ahead to confirm opening status; some small shops require reservations on weekends.

session_56.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_56.text: Are these shops suitable for writing? For example, how quiet is the environment, and are there power outlets? Also, after coming out of the bookstore, how do you link up the surrounding attractions?

Suggested routes around the area: bookstores in Dali Ancient City → Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple; a 5-minute walk in Lijiang to the Big Water Wheel; in Shangri-La, Aruo Kangba is only 200 meters from Dukezong Ancient City. session_60.text: I plan to go to western Yunnan in June, with Deqin and Shangri-La as the main focuses. Can you help me plan the itinerary and budget? I've saved 4,000 yuan so far, and I mainly want to go hiking and visit independent bookstores.

session_60.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_60.text: Okay! For western Yunnan in June, I recommend 8–10 days. In Deqin, see Meili Snow Mountain and hike in Yubeng; in Shangri-La, go to Songzanlin Monastery and Dukezong Ancient Town. As for budget, round-trip transportation is about 800–1,200 yuan, local accommodation 100–200 yuan per night (your father has already contacted lodging in Deqin, so part of that can be saved), trekking guide fees about 500–800 yuan, meals 80–100 yuan per day, and set aside 500 yuan for emergencies. A total budget of 3,500–4,000 yuan is enough. Do you need a specific route or bookstore recommendations?

session_60.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_60.text: Hiking Yubeng is a must-do for me! But will the weather in June be affected by rain? Also, I want to visit two or three unique independent bookstores.

session_60.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_60.text: Early June is before the rainy season in western Yunnan; there may be occasional showers but they won't matter much. Just bring a waterproof shell jacket and hiking shoes. For the Yubeng trek, I recommend 3 days: Xidang - Shangyubeng - Ice Lake - Xiayubeng - Divine Waterfall. In Dukezong Ancient Town there are 'Faraway Bookstore' and 'Library Under the Snow Mountain', and in Shangri-La city there is 'Zero Hour Bookstore'—all are niche corners that freelance writers would love.

session_60.text: I'm writing the third piece of 'Kunming Slices' and want to dig deeper into the historical stories of Wenlin Street and Qianju Street. Do you have any materials or inspiration to recommend?

session_60.text: Wenlin Street got its name from the crowds of imperial examination candidates in the Ming and Qing dynasties, and Qianju Street was once the site of the coin mint. It is recommended to refer to the old photo collection Old Kunming: The City and Its People, combining old architectural images and personal oral accounts to strengthen the cultural depth of the article.

session_60.speaker: Sun Yuwei

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_81.text: This morning at Dounan Flower Market, my friend and I made a "Spring Revival" installation out of discarded flower materials. Surprisingly, a reporter from "Kunming Is Fun" interviewed us! She asked why I used discarded flowers, and I said I wanted to express circulation and rebirth—discarded things can redefine spring.

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_81.text: You're not just proud of the interview; you also hope someone will deeply understand the emotional devotion behind your creation of “abandonment and rebirth.” You're looking for resonance with the idea of fusing environmental protection and art, right?

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_81.text: Yes! It's not just superficial praise—it's someone truly understanding what it means for me to redefine spring with discarded flowers. That feeling is deeply satisfying, and I want to write this experience into my article too.

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_81.text: I understand. You used discarded flower materials to symbolize overlooked beauty, just like the delicate perception often found in INFPs — 'Spring Revival' is not only about environmental protection, but also a praise of life's resilience. This complete experience, from creation to being understood, deserves to be recorded and carried on.

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_81.text: I want to write an essay about small urban art installations, combining today’s creation with discarded flowers at the flower market and community interaction. But I’m not sure how to elevate personal experience into social observation. Any suggestions?

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_81.text: You could start with a specific scene, such as the gaze of passersby stopping to look during your creation, or a conversation, and then naturally lead into how art in urban public spaces activates everyday communication. In terms of structure, I suggest dividing the article into three parts: personal story, community response, and extended reflection — citing Benjamin's 'Arcades' or de Certeau's 'Practice of Everyday Life' theory to deepen it.

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_81.text: This structure is very clear! I've used Benjamin's ideas before, but how exactly does de Certeau's "everyday practice" connect to community installations? Could you give an example from another city?

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_81.text: de Certeau emphasized the “tactics” of ordinary people in space—passersby taking photos with their phones and children touching installations are their re-creation of art. A similar example is the “Urban Illustration” project in Shanghai’s alleyways: artists painted local stories on old walls, and residents spontaneously maintained and added to the paintings, forming a dynamic community memory. You can cite this analogy.

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_81.text: This case is very apt! I plan to include de Certeau and that Shanghai project in the article. Also, Uncle Qin suggested I submit it to Cultural Vision or a lifestyle WeChat official account—which do you think is more suitable?

session_81.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_81.text: If the piece leans literary and deeply reflective, prioritize the 'City Stories' column of Cultural Horizons; they prefer essays supported by theory. If you want broader public reach, consider the official account under Lifeweek; they've been focusing on community art topics recently. I suggest showing the draft to Uncle Qin first — he can give practical suggestions.

session_82.text: I just bought a white porcelain gaiwan and tea samples of Bangdong raw pu-erh and ten-year-aged ripe pu-erh. I want to systematically learn how to brew them. Could you give me a specific brewing guide for these teas?

Later, we can further discuss tasting points.

session_82.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_82.text: These parameters are very specific, and I'm very interested. Also, when appreciating the aroma and tasting the tea's sweet aftertaste, what details should I focus on?

session_82.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_82.text: When smelling the tea, distinguish hot, warm, and cold sniffs: the hot sniff detects off-odors, the warm sniff identifies the aroma type (such as floral, fruity, or aged), and the cold sniff checks persistence. When tasting, pay attention to how quickly the bitterness and astringency on the tongue dissolves, the location of the sweet aftertaste (for raw pu-erh, usually on both sides of the tip of the tongue), and the thickness of the mouthfeel. After each brew, I suggest you record the water temperature, infusion time, aroma, and flavor changes in your journal to gradually build experience.

session_83.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_83.text: Hello! This morning I used my newly bought gaiwan to brew Bangdong raw pu'er for the first time. It felt slightly astringent at first, then had a great sweet aftertaste. I'd like to ask: what are the characteristics of this tea? How does the pouring technique when brewing affect the flavor? How can you judge quality from the liquor color and infused leaves? And what are the differences in tasting raw pu'er versus ripe pu'er?

session_83.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_83.text: Bangdong raw pu'er comes from the Bangdong tea region in Lincang. It is characterized by a strong wild mountain aura and a distinct clean sweetness with a lingering aftertaste. When pouring water, it is recommended to use a fixed low pour or pour along the wall of the teapot; avoid pouring water forcefully directly onto the leaves, as this can easily produce bitterness and astringency. The water temperature should be around 95°C, and the first few infusions should be decanted quickly. A pale yellow, clear liquor indicates a young vintage; intact, resilient leaves in the bottom are a sign of good-quality raw material. When tasting raw pu'er, focus on astringency, the returning sweetness and salivation, and throat resonance; for ripe pu'er, focus instead on fullness, smoothness, sweetness, and aged aroma. You can record the water temperature, pouring method, infusion time, and changes in taste to improve your tea tasting log.

session_83.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_83.text: Thank you! Then how can I describe the layered flavors of the tea? For example, I can feel the transition from slight astringency to a sweet aftertaste, but I don't know how to note it down in professional terms.

session_83.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_83.text: To describe the layers, you can say: 'The initial astringency is obvious at the entrance, but it dissolves quickly, followed by a clear sweet aftertaste, saliva forming under the tongue, and a cool sensation in the mouth.' You can also record the degree of bitterness and astringency, the duration of the astringency, and the intensity and persistence of the sweet aftertaste. It is recommended to record in a three-part format: 'taste—soup texture—aftertaste,' for example: 'The first stage is slightly astringent, the middle stage is clear and sweet, and the final stage leaves a long-lasting throat resonance.' With more practice, you will become more and more precise.

session_85.text: My mother sprained her ankle today. I applied a warm compress and sprayed Yunnan Baiyao on it, and she feels a bit better. But I'd like to know the proper care methods for an ankle sprain, including the timing of cold and warm compresses, whether massage is appropriate, and what to pay attention to during recovery.

session_85.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_85.text: How long ago did your mother sprain it? Is there obvious swelling or bruising? Usually during the acute phase (within 48 hours), ice is recommended to reduce swelling; only after that can heat be applied to promote blood circulation. Yunnan Baiyao aerosol can be used in the acute phase, but massage may worsen the swelling in the early stage. Would you like to know the specific RICE principles and staged care?

session_85.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_85.text: She sprained it this morning. Her ankle is a bit swollen but there is no bruising. I applied a warm compress to her this evening. Was that wrong? How should the care be adjusted now?

session_85.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_85.text: Within 48 hours after a sprain, apply ice (15–20 minutes each time, with 2–3 hours in between), elevate the injured limb, and reduce activity. A warm compress this evening may be a little early, but if there is no longer any discomfort, you can stop. It is recommended to switch to ice tomorrow and apply an elastic bandage for compression. Also observe whether the swelling worsens. If the pain is severe or you cannot bear weight, go to the hospital for an X-ray to rule out a fracture. session_98.text: This morning I experienced something particularly dramatic—my journal, which I had lost for almost a week, was actually picked up by a stranger on the bus and returned to me intact. I'm still very emotional now; it feels like a dream.

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_98.text: It seems this matter touched you deeply. For you, the journal is probably more than just a notebook—it’s more like a spiritual anchor, isn’t it? Could you tell me more about the scene back then and how you felt?

session_98.text: Yes, it contained many of my creative inspirations and fragments of daily life, so I was especially anxious when I found it was missing. This morning at 7, Uncle Zhao called. We met at the entrance of the residential complex at 8. He kept apologizing, saying he had flipped through a few pages and felt sorry. When I treated him to crossing-the-bridge rice noodles, he told me he had asked around in many community group chats to find me.

session_98.text: In this feeling of losing and regaining, there is actually a rediscovery of details and kindness. You just said you wrote in your journal, “All losses remind us to cherish,” which sounds like the starting point of an essay — do you plan to write it into your work?

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_98.text: Your gratitude and the act of recording are themselves a continuation of this kindness. After the essay collection is completed, perhaps you can keep a chapter honoring 'the kindness of strangers' so that more people can read about this small light that illuminates everyday life.

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_98.text: I am writing a paper on space and power, and I am confused about the spatial power theory in Foucault's Discipline and Punish, especially how to combine it with contemporary cultural spaces?

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_98.text: The core of Foucault's 'spatial power' is that power disciplines through the distribution of space; for example, 'panopticism' reflects the internalization of surveillance. When applying it, one can first extract concepts such as hierarchical observation and normalizing sanction, then select a contemporary case such as an open-plan office or a digital surveillance society for comparative analysis, while avoiding mechanical application.

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_98.text: Yes, I'm just worried that applying "panopticism" directly to modern phenomena will be inaccurate—for example, does cyberspace have a matching surveillance structure?

session_98.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_98.text: I understand your concerns. I suggest using Foucault's 'disciplinary society' framework to analyze data surveillance on online platforms, and comparing it with Lefebvre's 'production of space' theory, to highlight the internalization of power rather than physical structures. For the theoretical section of the thesis, you can first outline Foucault, then move to operationalization—design analytical dimensions: spatial division, disciplinary techniques, and subject resistance. For the case study, I recommend the algorithmic recommendation space of short-video platforms.

session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_101.text: This plan is very specific. I'll try a fixed morning reading practice every day. Also, if I get nervous during the official test and lose control of my speaking pace, are there any techniques to adjust?

session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_101.text: Before the exam, take 3 deep breaths and imagine you are talking to your mother (she is a Chinese language teacher, so you are more relaxed). session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_101.text: This evening I brewed a 2019 White Peony tea cake in a white porcelain gaiwan. The liquor was pale yellow and bright, with a delicate downy aroma, and the taste was fresher and more brisk than the Shou Mei I drank yesterday. But I'm not sure whether 85°C water is the best for White Peony, and what are the finer points of the pouring technique?

session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_101.text: Your observation is spot on! White Peony is made from one bud with one or two leaves, giving it a prominent downy aroma, while Shou Mei is mainly made from mature leaves, resulting in a fuller, more mellow mouthfeel. 85°C water is very suitable for White Peony, as it avoids scalding the buds and leaves and causing bitterness. When pouring, I suggest swirling the water slowly along the cup wall so the leaves infuse evenly. Would you like to hear how the flavor of White Peony changes with age?

session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei
session_101.text: Yes, I noticed this cake of tea has a faint floral aroma and honey sweetness, but I don't know how to describe it more precisely in words. Also, do the production areas of White Peony and Shou Mei have a big influence on quality?

session_101.speaker: Sun Yuwei's Assistant
session_101.text: The floral aroma can be broken down into orchid or gardenia notes, and the honeyed sweetness often comes from amino acids preserved through good processing. When describing it, you can use contrasting imagery such as 'crisp as a spring, flower nectar interwoven.' As for origin, the core production areas of Fuding White Peony, such as Taimu Mountain, are known for clear, sweet, and delicate flavors, while the Zhenghe area is richer and fuller. You can try using 'the breath of the mountain field' to expand your writing inspiration.
