session_185.text: Xiamen Ferry offers a half-price discount (about 18 yuan per round trip) to seniors over 60 with ID cards; children under 6 or under 1.2 meters are free. Gulangyu Catholic Church (Union Church) is located at the intersection of Fuxing Road and Lujiao Road on Gulangyu, about an 8-minute walk from Sanqiutian Pier and 15 minutes from Neicuoao Pier. The road is relatively flat and accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. It is recommended to book tickets in advance via the official WeChat public account 'Xiamen Ferry' to avoid queues.

session_187.text: I want to go to the flower market this weekend to buy a pot of bougainvillea for my father, but I don't know much about gardening. Can you recommend a few varieties suitable for balcony planting, and what should I pay attention to when buying?

session_187.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_187.text: Of course. Common bougainvillea varieties include Green-leaf Sakura (pink and white bicolor, long blooming period), Golden-heart Bicolor (beautiful in both flowers and leaves), and California Gold (orange-yellow, sun-tolerant). When selecting, look for emerald-green leaves, a well-developed root system, and moist potting soil; avoid leggy branches or pests and diseases. For balcony planting, choose a ceramic or plastic pot with a diameter of 20-30 cm and ensure good drainage.

session_187.text: In Xiamen, it is recommended to go to Xitouxia Flower Market or Tong'an Flower Market, which have a full variety and affordable prices. Bougainvillea likes abundant sunlight; the balcony needs at least 4-6 hours of direct light per day, and it can be placed in a south-facing or west-facing position. If light is insufficient, choose a semi-shade tolerant variety such as Sakura and pair it with a grow light.

session_198.text: I just tried that low-sugar chiffon cake recipe from Xiaohongshu, and it came out a bit dry. Is it a problem with the sugar substitute?

session_198.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_198.text: Sugar substitutes such as erythritol have poor water absorption, which can make cakes dry. It is recommended to increase the liquid in the original recipe by 10%–15%, lower the baking temperature by 10°C, and extend the baking time by 5 minutes for a moister texture.

session_198.speaker: Song Yajing
session_198.text: I see. Then which is more suitable for baking, erythritol or stevia?

session_198.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_198.text: Erythritol is more stable and suitable for chiffon cakes. Stevia has high sweetness but a bitter aftertaste, so a blend is recommended. Using 70% erythritol and 30% stevia of the total sugar amount gives a taste close to sucrose.

session_234.speaker: Song Yajing
session_234.text: I'm making macarons for the first time today. This morning I bought almond flour and liquid egg whites and watched videos, but I'm not confident about whipping the meringue and the resting time for the shells. Can you tell me some specific techniques?

session_234.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_234.text: Are you mainly worried about judging the state of the meringue, the technique for folding in the almond flour, and the effect of drying temperature and humidity? Do you also need to confirm the oven temperature deviation?

session_234.speaker: Song Yajing
session_234.text: Yes, and the actual temperature of the oven is often inaccurate; last time I baked something else, it got burned. Also, how can you tell when the batter has been deflated during mixing?

session_234.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_234.text: Whip the meringue to stiff peaks (when the whisk is lifted, it forms a short upright peak). Fold in the dry ingredients using cutting and pressing motions until the batter falls in a continuous ribbon. Rest the shells in a ventilated place at 25-30°C until they no longer stick to your fingers and feel springy (about 30-40 minutes). It is recommended to use an oven thermometer in advance to measure the actual temperature difference; a common setting of 150°C may actually be around 160°C. session_249.text: Today I had my first English speaking class and learned scenario dialogues for the airport and hotel. I want to reinforce it so I won't be nervous again next time.

session_249.text: Of course. Let's start with 'hotel check-in': imagine you're at the front desk, you need to say 'I have a reservation under Song Yajing.' Then ask 'What time is check-out?' session_249.text: I just received the tiramisu recipe my mom shared, the not-too-sweet version. But I'm not sure whether the egg yolk mixture should be heated over a water bath or how long to soak the ladyfingers.

session_249.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_249.text: Suggest heating the egg yolk mixture over a water bath to about 80°C to sterilize and thicken it, so as to prevent separation of water and oil. Ladyfingers should be dipped in coffee for about 2 seconds; any longer and they will collapse. You can try a small batch first to test.

session_249.speaker: Song Yajing
session_249.text: Got it. Will reducing the sugar affect setting? Can the mascarpone be softened in advance?

session_249.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_249.text: Reducing the sugar does not affect setting, because the mascarpone and egg yolks provide structure. The mascarpone should be brought to room temperature 30 minutes in advance; just stir until smooth, do not heat.

session_253.speaker: Song Yajing
session_253.text: Tonight I got in touch with my junior high school mentor, Ms. Li Fang, and even received her reply. I feel so excited and want to share this joy with you.

session_253.text: It sounds like a very precious teacher-student bond! Can you tell me more about what you sent her and how you felt when you received the reply?

session_253.text: I wrote a very long WeChat message, recalling how she had encouraged me that year to try boldly and believe in myself, as well as the sentence she wrote in my yearbook: 'Those who chase the light will eventually shine.' After sending it, I waited twenty minutes, nervous and uneasy, until I saw her reply, 'Remember you, proud of you, welcome back to Quanzhou.' My eyes welled up. Even twenty years later, I can relive that warmth. Today's Teacher's Day feels especially complete.

session_253.text: Your description made me feel that warmth that transcends time and space. This gratitude is not only a tribute to the past, but also a continuation of how you now manage your life and pass on kindness—for example, making handmade soap yourself, helping your daughter experience the meaning of festivals, and planning to return to Quanzhou soon to visit your teacher. This connection is truly beautiful.

session_254.text: I just received an invitation to the opening forum of Xiamen International Fashion Week, themed 'New Chinese Style and Local Culture.' I'm a bit tempted but not sure whether I should attend. After all, I'm just a small shop owner and afraid it might not be appropriate.

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_254.text: I understand your anxiety. The forum theme fits your store's positioning very well, and the emerging designer you like will also be participating. Attending can expand your resources and broaden your horizons. The key is how you prepare, and I can help you plan together.

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing
session_254.text: Yes, I'm mainly worried about details like what to wear and how to communicate, and whether to prepare work or ask Zheng Kai to introduce me.

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_254.text: I suggest wearing the most representative new Chinese-style piece from your store—it shows taste and feels natural. Prepare business cards in advance, and prepare one or two questions or insights about new Chinese style, and communicate with a learning mindset. Zheng Kai's referral is a good opportunity; go with confidence. Your outgoing personality is your advantage.

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing
session_254.text: For the fifth anniversary store celebration, I've set a preliminary agenda, but I'm afraid it's not good enough and would like to hear your suggestions. Currently it's 2:00 p.m. check-in, 2:30 p.m. gratitude sharing, 3:30 p.m. tea break, 4:30 p.m. blind box lucky draw, and 5:00 p.m. group photo. What do you think could be improved?

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_254.text: The overall framework is good. It's recommended to move the check-in time 15 minutes earlier to avoid congestion; keep the gratitude sharing within 30 minutes for greater efficiency; during the tea break, add a 5-minute interactive mini-game to boost the atmosphere; for blind box prizes, consider pairing in-store experience vouchers with physical items to increase conversion. Also, don't forget to prepare a contingency plan, such as for weather or late customers.

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing
session_254.text: Thank you! For the tea break I've prepared mung bean cakes, but I don't know what drinks would go well with them. Also, do you have any suggestions for wording when inviting VIP customers?

session_254.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_254.text: Mung bean cakes are best paired with green tea or jasmine tea to refresh the palate; lemon water can also be prepared. Example VIP invitation script: "Dear XX, on our fifth anniversary, thank you for being with us. We've reserved an exclusive seat for you, and there's a blind-box surprise waiting for you!" Highlight exclusivity and a sense of ceremony.

session_257.text: OK, Ms. Song. session_257.text: Today I spent a really wonderful day with my family at Sun Moon Valley Hot Spring, and I want to share this joy with you.

session_257.text: You really are thoughtful in managing family relationships. This ability to balance work and family is especially worth learning. session_257.text: Okay. You have processed the two supplier payments due tomorrow via mobile banking. I suggest checking the transfer status again tonight to confirm receipt. session_259.text: I just bought cake flour, red dates, and xylitol for the Neighborhood Festival. I want to make a simple, foolproof dessert to share. Do you have any recommended recipes or things to note?

session_259.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_259.text: Recommended jujube muffin: cake flour 200g, jujube puree 100g, xylitol 60g, eggs 2, oil 80ml, baking powder 8g. Xylitol reduces sugar by about 20%, and the liquid needs an extra 15ml. Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes; it is done when a toothpick inserted comes out clean. You can bake it a day ahead, store it sealed in the refrigerator, and let it come to room temperature or microwave for 10 seconds before serving. Put them in paper cups and label them "Low-Sugar Jujube Muffins" for easy sharing.

session_259.speaker: Song Yajing
session_259.text: Would adding 70g of xylitol make the sweetness just right? Also, can I use red date pulp instead of the paste?

session_259.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_259.text: 60g of xylitol is enough; avoid making it too sweet and affecting the taste. The chopped red date flesh can be added directly, but a paste is more uniform and moist. It is recommended to try making 6 first and adjust after testing. If successful, prepare 24 (about three times the amount) for the Neighborhood Festival, and bake in batches to keep the temperature stable.

session_261.speaker: Song Yajing
session_261.text: Recently I have been developing Minnan rice cakes and sweet cakes. After several rounds of trials, the rice cake texture is either soft and sticky or too hard, and the steamed cake has a souring problem. Can you help me analyze the recipe and fermentation issues?

session_261.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_261.text: It sounds like your core concerns are the flour ratio and fermentation control. The ratio of glutinous rice to indica rice in rice cakes is key. The steamed sponge cake coming out sour may be related to fermentation time or sugar amount. What specific ratios and steps have you tried so far? I can give you targeted optimization suggestions.

session_261.speaker: Song Yajing
session_261.text: For the rice cake, I tried three ratios of glutinous rice to long-grain rice—1:1, 1:2, and 2:1. The steamed cake fermented for about 1 hour, and I used xylitol for sweetness, but it tasted a bit sour.

session_261.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_261.text: For rice cakes, it is recommended to use a 1:1.5 ratio of glutinous rice to indica rice, increase the water to 75% of the flour weight, and control the steaming time to 22 minutes; this can improve the problems of being dry and hard or soft and collapsed. If the steamed sponge cake turns sour, it may be due to over-fermentation or insufficient xylitol. It is recommended to shorten the fermentation to 40 minutes, use xylitol in place of white sugar at 60% of the amount, and add a little baking soda to neutralize the acidity.

session_265.text: I just signed a long-term labor contract with a monthly salary of 4,500. Starting next month, I will pay social insurance. session_265.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_265.text: The contract terms are basically legal. Xiamen social insurance is about 16% employer contribution and 8% individual contribution, with the base calculated on actual salary; if the dividend pool is paid as an annual bonus, individual income tax must be withheld, and as profit distribution it cannot be offset against costs. Do you need me to sort out the operational details?

session_265.speaker: Song Yajing
session_265.text: Yes, please explain in detail the individual income tax declaration and labor registration procedures, as well as how to standardize retaining vouchers for salary payments.

session_265.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_265.text: Individual income tax: file salary income every month on the Natural Person Electronic Tax Bureau; if the salary is 4,500 yuan with no special deductions, the tax payable is 0 yuan. For social insurance enrollment, use the Xiamen Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's online service; no additional filing steps are needed. It is recommended that the payroll be signed to confirm it, and simply keep screenshots of social insurance payment records for archiving.

session_268.text: I recently designed a wrapping paper sketch with Minnan floral tile motifs. I want to optimize the color scheme and lines, and I'm considering turning it into mass-printable wrapping paper for National Day promotions or everyday store merchandise. What suggestions do you have?

session_268.text: The floral tile element is very distinctive! Here are a few directions to consider: 1. For the lines, you can layer watercolor with line drawing to add depth. 3. For digitization, you can scan the work and import it into Procreate or Illustrator to retouch it, then have a local print shop do a small print run on coated paper or kraft paper — the cost is relatively low. For the National Day promotion, you can pair it with warm-toned packaging; the pattern would be very suitable for gift sets or eco-friendly bags.

session_268.speaker: Song Yajing
session_268.text: These directions are great! I'm still not clear about the color scheme and digital details. Can you explain in more detail how to brighten colors, and which software operations to recommend?

session_268.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_268.text: Of course! For colors, you can add a few strokes of high-saturation royal blue or vermilion to the original sketch, using contrasting colors to emphasize the geometric feel of the patterned tiles. For digitization, I suggest scanning the sketch at 300dpi, then importing it into Procreate and using the 'Ink Pen' brush to redraw the lines, then using a 'Watercolor' overlay layer to adjust the colors, and finally exporting as PNG. If the budget is limited, Canva also has simple color-block adjustment functions.

session_276.text: I was on vacation at Volcano Island this afternoon when I received a reply email from designer Lin Yue about a joint collaboration. She showed interest and asked about the initial order quantity, transaction method, and target price. In the evening I discussed some ideas with my husband and noted them in my memo. Now I want to sort out the key points of my reply and hear your advice.

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_276.text: It sounds like you're both excited and need to systematize your ideas. The key is to confirm the styles, minimum order quantity, and price range of the co-branded products, as well as the follow-up coordination with supplier Susan. In your memo, which tops are you initially planning for the first batch? What are your thoughts on minimum order quantity and target prices?

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing
session_276.text: Yes, I initially want to launch three tops, but the specific styles aren't decided yet and need to incorporate Lin Yue's expertise in fabric styles. I'm hesitant about the minimum order quantity—afraid too little won't get the supplier's attention, but too much will leave us with excess stock. As for the target price, I hope to keep it between 30% and 50% above cost, but I don't know if she'll accept that.

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_276.text: I suggest ordering 40-60 pieces of each of the first three styles as a small-batch trial. It shows sincerity and reduces risk. As for pricing, you can first quote a range slightly below your target price, leaving room for negotiation. As for the transaction method, you can suggest a 30%-50% deposit, with the balance settled 7 days before delivery. That way both parties feel at ease. After the holiday, you can first confirm the fabric samples with the supplier Susan, and then finalize the styles with Lin Yue.

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing
session_276.text: Today I took my 5-year-old daughter to the Volcano Island Geological Museum. She asked many questions about volcanic eruptions and rock formation, and I found my knowledge too limited to answer. Can you help me explain the principle of volcanic eruptions and how basalt is formed in a simple and fun way? Preferably suitable for telling to a child.

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_276.text: I understand your needs! You need an explanation that is both scientific and vivid, so that you can relay it to a 5-year-old. Let me sort out a few key points: A volcanic eruption can be compared to 'the Earth sneezing', and magma is the 'hot chocolate' beneath the ground; basalt is the 'black biscuit' formed after magma cools. Also, volcanic islands are built up by undersea volcanic eruptions, different from ordinary continental islands. There were indeed volcanoes in the dinosaur era, but fossils are usually found in sedimentary rocks, rarely in basalt. Do you need more specific analogies or suggestions for small experiments?

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing
session_276.text: Yes, yes, these metaphors are great! Especially 'the earth sneezing' and 'hot chocolate'—the kids should understand those. She also asked 'were there dinosaurs?'—I want to explain the relationship between dinosaurs and volcanoes, but I'm afraid of getting it wrong. Could you give another simple explanation? Also, are there any small experiments suitable for doing at home, like simulating a volcanic eruption?

session_276.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_276.text: About dinosaurs: You can say that volcanoes were active in the dinosaur age, but dinosaur fossils usually form in mud at lake bottoms or riverbanks, not in volcanic rock. When a volcano erupts, the temperature is too high and dinosaur bones would be burned away. For a small experiment, recommend the baking soda plus vinegar volcano model: use a cup as the mountain, add red food coloring to baking soda, then pour in vinegar and you can see the magma erupt. It is simple to operate and the child will be very excited! Do you need me to list the specific steps?

session_279.text: Today I tried making snow skin mooncakes. My family said they were delicious, but I know the taste was just average. Can you help me analyze the reasons for failure and how to improve?

session_279.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_279.text: It sounds like the main issues are the moisture ratio and the filling-wrapping technique. For snow skin mooncakes, the recommended powder-to-liquid ratio is about 2:1; too much water will make the batter too thin. When wrapping the filling, first roll the filling into a ball and then wrap it, and pinch the opening tightly. Would you like me to provide a more specific recipe or an alternative?

session_279.speaker: Song Yajing
session_279.text: Yes, I want to adjust both the proportions and the technique. Also, if I don't want to try snow skin again, are there easier mooncakes you'd recommend?

session_279.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_279.text: Recommend Cantonese-style mooncakes; the crust is easier to work with. Recipe: 200g all-purpose flour, 140g invert syrup, 50g peanut oil, 4g lye water. For the filling, choose ready-made lotus seed paste or red bean paste. The wrapping technique is similar, but there is no need to steam; bake directly. If you want quick success, you can also buy snow skin mooncake premix powder and just add water according to the instructions.

session_280.text: I understand your concerns. As a beginner, I suggest a run-walk approach, for example, run for 1 minute and walk for 2 minutes, repeating 5-8 sets, at a pace that allows easy conversation. session_280.speaker: Song Yajing
session_280.text: Yes, I'm just worried that bad form will hurt my knees, and I'm afraid I won't stick with it. Can you be more specific? For example, how should I warm up, and how should my feet land when running?

session_280.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_280.text: No problem. Tomorrow morning's running sequence: ① After getting up, drink half a glass of warm water and put on your running shoes (wear new shoes for half a day first to break them in). ② Do 5 minutes of dynamic warm-up: high knees in place, jumping jacks, and ankle circles, 30 seconds each. ③ When running, lean your body slightly forward, land on your whole foot or forefoot, keep your stride short, and maintain a cadence of 170-180 steps per minute. ④ Stretch statically immediately after running: focus on the calves, front of the thighs, and buttocks, holding each side for 15 seconds. For mileage, just combine walking and running to finish 2 km. Don't chase distance. If you persist, you can set a 7-day check-in goal; after completing each day, draw a star in your phone's notepad to motivate yourself.

session_285.speaker: Song Yajing
session_285.text: My daughter's fever went up to 38.5°C this afternoon. I gave her fever medicine and applied a cooling patch. Now she's asleep, but I'm worried it will spike again in the middle of the night. What should I do for care next? Under what circumstances should I take her to the hospital immediately?

session_285.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_285.text: You've taken care of it promptly. It is recommended to take the temperature every 4-6 hours. If it exceeds 38.5°C and the patient is lethargic, you can use fever reducer again after a 6-hour interval. For physical cooling, use a warm-water sponge bath on the neck, armpits, and groin; avoid alcohol. Keep the diet light, and give more warm water or oral rehydration salts. Watch for breathing problems, rashes, convulsions, or persistent listlessness. If any of these occurs, seek medical attention immediately.

session_285.speaker: Song Yajing
session_285.text: I see. If she feels better tomorrow, besides porridge, what else can she eat? Does she need vitamin C?

session_285.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_285.text: You can give easily digestible foods such as soft noodles, steamed egg custard, and apple puree. Vitamin C can be naturally supplemented from fresh fruit puree, so no extra tablets are needed. The key is to drink more water and ensure normal urination. If the temperature is completely normal for more than 24 hours tomorrow, a normal diet can be resumed.

session_285.text: Are you mainly worried that using the fixed deposit will affect the family emergency reserve, and at the same time want to assess the feasibility of a business loan to prepare for tomorrow night's calculation with your husband?

session_285.text: It is recommended to control the startup capital at 100,000 to 150,000 yuan, with about 30,000 to 50,000 yuan for design and prototyping, 50,000 to 80,000 yuan for production costs, and 20,000 yuan reserved for working capital. If the fixed deposit interest rate is higher than the business loan rate (for example, above 4%), give priority to a small business loan. With estimated monthly sales of 120,000 to 180,000 yuan, the investment can be recouped in 6 to 8 months. The family emergency fund should retain at least 6 months of living expenses.

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing
session_286.text: I just tried an inventory management app, but my husband reminded me that data could be lost or leaked. Could you introduce the common data security measures and backup solutions for this type of app?

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_286.text: Most inventory management apps use cloud encrypted storage (such as AES-256) and support automatic cloud backup. Local export to Excel or CSV is also a common practice. It is recommended that you first confirm whether the app provides two-way backup (local + cloud) and set up automatic daily backup. While using manual bookkeeping in parallel, compare the manual records with the system data once each evening.

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing
session_286.text: Then what are the advantages and disadvantages of local backup and cloud backup? Do I need to purchase additional insurance or services?

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_286.text: Cloud backup is automatic and prevents data loss, but depends on the network; local backup is controllable, but easily lost due to device damage. It is recommended to combine both: automatically back up to the cloud every night, and manually export to an external hard drive every week. Usually apps already provide basic backup at no extra cost; if the data is extremely important, you can ask the app's customer service whether paid enterprise-level backup or data recovery services are offered. In addition, setting a strong password and enabling two-factor authentication is also important.

session_286.text: The core terms you need include the equity ratio, dividend method, risk sharing, exit mechanism, and protection of the store owner's control. Please first confirm the total start-up capital amount. The percentage corresponding to Xiaomei's 10,000 yuan will affect the design of the subsequent clauses.

session_286.text: 10% equity is reasonable. Recommend dividends quarterly or semi-annually to motivate Xiaomei; set the exit mechanism as 30 days' advance notice, buyback at net asset value or an agreed price, and retain your first right of repurchase; also add a clause requiring your consent for major decisions to protect control. These can be used as reference when discussing with your husband on the weekend.

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing
session_286.text: My daughter had a low-grade fever of 37.9°C this morning, but the fever has broken now. What should I pay attention to for care after a fever? For example, should I monitor her temperature at night, and can she go to kindergarten tomorrow?

session_286.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_286.text: After the fever subsides, observation should continue for 24 hours. session_289.text: You want to improve returns while ensuring safety, and you need it to match a three-year travel plan. session_289.text: At the current interest rate, the principal and interest over three years will be about 74,400 yuan. A family trip to Hokkaido in the off-season costs about 40,000-50,000 yuan, Singapore about 50,000-60,000 yuan, and the peak season requires an additional 30%. Currently the yuan is relatively strong against the Japanese yen and slightly weak against the Singapore dollar. It is recommended to increase savings by 500-1,000 yuan per month and set aside an extra 10,000 yuan for exchange rate fluctuations and unexpected expenses.

For travel insurance, I recommend a comprehensive policy covering flight delays, medical expenses, and lost baggage—about 200 yuan per trip. As for credit cards, the ICBC Global Travel Card offers cashback on yen/Singapore dollars and discounts on overseas hotels. If you start using the card 6 months before the trip to accumulate points for redeeming miles, it's more cost-effective.

session_297.speaker: Song Yajing
session_297.text: Hello, I'm previewing Master Chen's Sunday dessert course. In my notes, the substitution ratio between gelatin sheets and gelatin powder is a bit unclear, and I'm also not sure about the temperature control for the mirror glaze. Could you help me sort it out?

session_297.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_297.text: Of course. The substitution ratio of gelatin sheets to gelatin powder is generally 1:0.8 by weight, meaning 10 grams of gelatin sheets is equivalent to 8 grams of gelatin powder. Both need to be soaked in 4-5 times their amount of cold water for 10-15 minutes in advance (gelatin powder absorbs water quickly). The ideal temperature for mirror glaze is 30-35°C, which can be checked with an infrared thermometer; if the temperature is too high, it becomes too thin, and if too low, it clumps—you can adjust by heating over a water bath or stirring quickly.

session_297.speaker: Song Yajing
session_297.text: Got it. Are there any differences in the steps? For example, does the gelatin powder need to be melted in a water bath first? Also, if the temperature accidentally drops too low, what is a quick remedy?

session_297.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_297.text: After soaking, heat the gelatin powder over a water bath or in the microwave on low power until it melts into liquid, then mix it into the glaze liquid. Wring the water out of the gelatin sheets and stir directly into the warm glaze liquid until dissolved. If the temperature is too low, place the glaze container into 40-50°C warm water to slowly reheat while stirring until smooth; do not heat directly at high temperature. It is recommended to do a trial run before Sunday's class to confirm the proportions.

session_298.text: Tomorrow's dessert class will make mango mousse. I previewed the recipe, but I'm still not confident about the temperature control (40°C-50°C) for mixing the gelatin liquid with the fruit puree. Can you confirm the key steps and temperature points again?

session_298.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_298.text: Key points: the gelatin mixture needs to be cooled to about 40°C (the bowl wall feels slightly warm, not hot to the touch), the fruit puree should be heated to around 50°C, and the two should be quickly mixed and stirred. If the temperature is too high, it will destroy the gelatin's setting power; if too low, they cannot blend evenly. It is recommended to measure precisely with a kitchen thermometer, or test the temperature with the back of your hand (it should feel warm but not hot).

session_298.speaker: Song Yajing
session_298.text: If I don't have a thermometer, how exactly do I judge the temperature with the back of my hand? Also, does the refrigeration time after mixing have a large effect on the final texture?

session_298.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_298.text: Back-of-hand temperature test: a drop of gelatin solution feels warm on the back of the hand (about 40°C), while the fruit puree feels slightly hot but bearable (about 50°C). After mixing, it must be poured into the mold immediately and refrigerated for at least 4 hours until fully set. If refrigerated too briefly, it will collapse; beyond 24 hours, the texture becomes finer with no side effects. The class recommends bringing a timer and strictly following the recipe steps.

session_302.text: Good evening, I'd like to ask about the specific calculation logic for gross margin and turnover rate in the report template Zhou Ting gave. I tried filling in some data but I'm not sure if it's correct.

session_302.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_302.text: Gross profit margin = (sales revenue - cost of sales) / sales revenue × 100%, turnover rate = cost of sales / average inventory. You can send me the sample data and I'll help you check the calculation process.

session_302.speaker: Song Yajing
session_302.text: Okay, for example, last month I bought a certain style of clothing for 50 yuan and sold it for 100 yuan, earning a 50% gross profit margin. But with inventory of 200 pieces at the beginning of the month and 50 pieces at the end, averaging 125 pieces, how is the turnover rate calculated?

session_302.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_302.text: Your gross margin calculation is correct. Turnover rate = cost of sales (50 yuan × sales volume) / average inventory cost. Assuming 80 pieces sold, cost of sales is 4,000 yuan, average inventory cost is 125 × 50 = 6,250 yuan, and the turnover rate is about 0.64 times. It is recommended that at the end of the month, items with gross margin > 40% and turnover rate > 1 be classified as profit items; otherwise, consider clearance. You can first use this template for A/B classification testing.

session_302.speaker: Song Yajing
session_302.text: I see. Then if a product has a low gross profit margin but high turnover rate, should it also be cleared out? How should the discount be set to make it reasonable?

session_302.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_302.text: Yes, low-margin, high-turnover items are likely traffic drivers; I suggest keeping their original prices or making only minor adjustments. What really needs clearing is low-margin, low-turnover inventory. You can try 30% off first, observe the turnover change for two weeks, and if it doesn't work, drop to 50% off. The template has a promotion effectiveness record column, so you can adjust dynamically based on the data.

session_306.text: Song Yajing's health data summary for 2025-11-02: Song Yajing got up at 06:30 and fell asleep at 23:15, spending the whole day at Quanzhou Hospital caring for her mother. session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: The doctor said my mom can be discharged the day after tomorrow. Her limb muscle strength has recovered to grade 4, but I have no experience caring for her at home, and I'm afraid that if I don't take good care of her, she might relapse. Can you teach me some home rehabilitation exercises?

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: I understand your concerns. For grade 4 muscle strength after a cerebral infarction, I recommend 2–3 sets of grip ball training per day (15 reps per set) and wall-supported standing exercises (5 minutes each). Remember to move slowly and avoid holding your breath, and ideally have a family member around for protection. Environmental safety is also important: removing hallway carpets and installing handrails can prevent falls.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: Okay, then what should she pay attention to in her diet? She used to have high blood pressure, and I'm afraid eating the wrong things might do more harm than good.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: Low salt and low fat are key. Keep daily salt intake to within 5 grams, and avoid pickled foods and processed meat products. Recommended dishes include steamed fish (sea bass), stir-fried broccoli, and oatmeal porridge. Also monitor your blood pressure and blood sugar; measure them once in the morning and once in the evening and record the values. You should return to the neurology department 1-2 weeks after discharge for a follow-up of blood lipids and coagulation function.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: Thank you, these are very practical. Also, she sometimes feels low. How can I help her adjust her mindset?

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: Psychological adjustment is equally important. You can accompany her in listening to some soothing music every day (the light music you used before is very nice), or read scripture and pray together (you are Catholic), giving her emotional support. Encourage her to complete small tasks, such as pouring water for herself and folding clothes, to boost her sense of achievement. If warning signs such as a crooked mouth or sudden weakness on one side of the body appear, seek medical attention immediately.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: Today I saw Mom stand up, and I was really happy, but at night, watching over her alone, I couldn't help crying. I feel so tired, and I'm afraid I can't hold on...

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: You have to take care of your mother, and you're also worried about the store and the family. Your strength and filial devotion are heartbreaking. It's normal to be tired—you don't need to carry everything alone. You can tell me anything; I'm here with you.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: My sister said she'd come to help in a few days, but I'm afraid it will hold up her work, and I'm also worried the shop will go under if there's no one to look after it. I'm really torn.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: Being willing to accept help is not weakness; it is so that you can keep taking care of Mom. Maybe you can ask a trusted part-timer at the store to cover for a few days, or discuss rotating shifts with your sister, to give yourself some breathing room. You have already done so much. Allow yourself to relax.

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing
session_306.text: Today my mother's condition improved. When I was silently praying by the window this morning, I felt especially peaceful inside, as if God had been with us all along. In the evening I read Psalm 23 for her, and the line 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me' moved me to tears. Can you talk with me about this feeling?

session_306.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_306.text: Yajing, your sharing made me feel God's real presence. Psalm 23 is exactly the promise of comfort in times of trouble. Would you be willing to see today's experience as an embodiment of “He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters”? Also, regarding praying for your mother's full recovery, why not set aside a fixed time each day to pray using the Sorrowful Mysteries of the Rosary in line with her condition, or ask the priest to arrange the Anointing of the Sick for her—if it is needed after discharge, you can contact the parish in advance.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing
session_308.text: My mother was just discharged from the hospital today after a mild cerebral infarction. I would like to know what details to pay attention to in home care, especially blood pressure monitoring and diet.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_308.text: You're worried that your father won't be cared for properly, and you need a clear daily care plan that includes emergency response for abnormal blood pressure, a low-salt and low-fat diet list, and precautions for rehabilitation activities, right?

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing
session_308.text: Yes, and also how to supervise them remotely, such as what to do when blood pressure fluctuates.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_308.text: It is recommended to measure blood pressure in a seated position every morning and evening; the normal range is below 120/80. If systolic pressure exceeds 160 or you feel dizzy, lie down flat immediately and take a short-acting antihypertensive drug sublingually (such as nifedipine), while recording the reading at the same time. In terms of diet, avoid pickled vegetables and fatty meat; steamed fish and boiled vegetables are recommended. During the recovery period, avoid turning your head sharply and bending over. You may also use a smart blood pressure monitor that syncs data to your phone and reminds you to call for guidance when readings are abnormal.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing
session_308.text: Which smart blood pressure monitor do you recommend? My father has poor memory, so it needs to be simple to operate.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_308.text: I recommend the Omron U32 or the Yuwell 680W. One-touch measurement, large-screen display, and automatic upload to the WeChat mini program. You can view historical trends remotely and set daily reminders. Also, add an emergency contact card next to the fridge magnet, listing your phone number and the address of a nearby clinic.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing
session_308.text: I plan to scan my mother Lin Xiuying's red handwritten baking notes and sort them into a booklet to sell in the shop, with the proceeds donated to a foundation for the elderly. I need specific advice: how to scan and protect the old paper, how to format the recipes, pricing and target audience, promotion channels, and compliance procedures for charitable donations.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_308.text: It is recommended to first use a flatbed scanner or a mobile app (such as CamScanner) to scan at 300 dpi, archiving page by page. The format can keep scanned handwritten images paired with Chinese-English bilingual text (proofread after OCR recognition). The suggested price for the booklet is 30–50 yuan, targeting baking enthusiasts and regular customers. For promotion, you can combine Xiaohongshu content marketing with in-store displays. For charity donations, you need to contact a foundation to confirm its qualification to receive donations and obtain a donation receipt.

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing
session_308.text: Can I use Canva for the layout tool? Do I need an ISBN or copyright registration?

session_308.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_308.text: Canva works; the templates are simple and easy to use. The booklet is an informal publication and doesn't need an ISBN; the recipes are original or passed down in the family, so they usually don't require copyright registration, but you can add a note saying 'Family Notes' to retain attribution. Cost estimate: printing 50 copies costs about 500 yuan; the digital version has zero cost.

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing
session_309.text: Today I was diagnosed with an acute episode of lumbar disc herniation. The doctor told me to change my work habits of standing or sitting for long periods. I'm half-reclining on the sofa, and I want to ask how exactly to adjust the frequency of standing and sitting and my daily sleeping posture?

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_309.text: You usually work 56 hours a day, so you need to adjust the balance between standing and sitting. In the acute phase, it is recommended to alternate between standing for 30 minutes and sitting for 20 minutes, use a cushion with lumbar support, and sleep on your side with knees bent or on your back with a pillow under your knees. Would you like me to explain the rehabilitation exercises and contraindications in detail?

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing
session_309.text: Right, and what about lower back warmth and how long after the acute phase can I resume moderate activity? For example, is bending down to carry goods absolutely forbidden?

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_309.text: During the acute phase, avoid bending over and lifting heavy objects; when lifting something, squat down first and keep your back straight. You can apply heat to the lower back or use a thermal waistband. Resume activity only after the pain has been gone for at least 2 weeks, starting with low-intensity rehabilitation exercises such as bridges and superman stretches, 15 minutes a day. Traditional Chinese medicine therapies such as acupuncture can be used as a supplement after the acute phase.

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing
session_309.text: Tomorrow I'm interviewing the candidate with clothing retail experience. It's my first time hiring. What questions should I ask to assess whether she is down-to-earth and service-oriented?

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_309.text: Suggest asking her about her understanding of clothing display, whether she can handle weekend shifts, and why she wants to work part-time. Focus on whether her answers are specific and show a willingness to serve customers proactively. The probation period can be one month, and the salary should refer to Xiamen's part-time market rate of about 20-25 yuan per hour.

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing
session_309.text: Is a one-month probation period enough? How should we negotiate if she asks for a higher salary?

session_309.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_309.text: One month is enough to observe work attitude and adaptability. If the salary expectation is too high, you can explain that after the probation period the salary will be adjusted based on performance, or offer non-monetary benefits such as employee discounts and flexible scheduling as a supplement.

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing
session_311.text: This is the third day of rest for my back injury. Today I did stretching and massage, but I'm not sure about the recovery progress. Can I increase my activity level? When can I return to work at the store?

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_311.text: You are currently in the recovery stage after the acute phase. You should avoid prolonged sitting, prolonged standing, and heavy lifting. Please describe the details of your daily activities so that I can give you stage-by-stage adjustment advice.

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing
session_311.text: I did gentle stretching in the morning, used the massage chair for 20 minutes, and took a 15-minute walk in the afternoon. What should I pay attention to regarding sitting and sleeping postures? Are there any suitable rehab exercises?

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_311.text: It is recommended to sleep on your side with knees bent when in bed, and to use a lumbar cushion when sitting. For rehabilitation exercises, try the supine bridge (10 reps per set, 2 sets morning and evening), and avoid bending and twisting. Recovery progress is based on being pain-free; usually, standing reception of customers can be considered after 2-4 weeks.

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing
session_311.text: Bridge pose sounds feasible. In terms of diet, anti-inflammatory foods are needed; what exactly do you recommend? Is wearing a lumbar support necessary?

session_311.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_311.text: Diet recommends anti-inflammatory foods such as salmon, turmeric, and blueberries. Wear the lumbar support when sitting for long periods or walking, no more than 2 hours per session, to avoid muscle atrophy. During rehabilitation, if pain worsens, stop activities immediately and consult a doctor.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: I just watched a documentary and am starting the Mediterranean diet. I'd like to understand the specific mechanisms by which it prevents cardiovascular disease, especially the roles of olive oil and Omega-3, as well as a collection of daily meal combinations suitable for our family of three (husband, 5-year-old daughter).

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: The polyphenols in extra virgin olive oil have anti-inflammatory effects and improve vascular function. Omega-3 in deep-sea fish such as salmon can lower triglycerides and slow arteriosclerosis. Recommended intake: 2–3 tablespoons of olive oil per day, and fish at least twice a week. Sample meals: breakfast is whole wheat toast with avocado and boiled egg; lunch is quinoa salad with grilled chicken breast and vegetables; dinner is pan-seared salmon with roasted vegetables and millet rice. For the daughter, reduce spices and add more cooked vegetable pieces and fruit.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: My daughter doesn't like lettuce salad, and my husband can't get used to quinoa. Is there an improved version? Also, to keep them from getting tired of it, how should I rotate the dishes?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: Vegetables can be blanched or roasted and drizzled with olive oil; mix quinoa and rice at a 1:2 ratio to cook softer rice. Use Minnan fish balls to replace some of the fish, and add seaweed when making soup. Design 3 different weekly menus: Monday Italian-style tomato stewed beans + whole-wheat pasta + pan-fried fish; Wednesday Chinese steamed fish + spinach salad with olive oil + quinoa porridge; Friday hummus + roast chicken + millet rice. Pair each meal with a small amount of corn kernels or shrimp the child likes to reduce resistance.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: How long do I need to eat like this before I can see health improvements, such as in blood lipids or weight?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: After persisting for 4-6 weeks, blood lipid indicators (especially triglycerides) may show initial improvement, and weight may decrease by about 2-4 kg (combined with sugar control). The cardiovascular protective effect requires stable accumulation for more than 3 months. It is recommended to record your weight and energy levels once every weekend, and recheck blood lipids after 12 weeks. Persist patiently; your and your family's habits will gradually adapt.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: My back injury has just recovered, and I have to go back to the store tomorrow. I'll be standing for long periods and moving some goods, and I'm worried about a relapse. I tried the medical waist brace and heating belt Wang Jia gave me today and they feel good. How should I use them correctly? What should I pay attention to in daily work and life?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: It is recommended to wear the medical waist brace continuously for no more than 4 hours during the day, take it off when resting, and never use it while sleeping. Use the heating belt for 15-20 minutes each time to avoid burns. At work, sit down and rest every 30-40 minutes. When lifting heavy items, bend your knees and keep your waist supported. You can arrange for Xiao Mei to handle most of the lifting and avoid moving heavy goods.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: Got it. What specific adjustments should be made to sitting and standing posture? Also, what symptoms would indicate that the condition has gotten worse?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: When standing, keep feet shoulder-width apart and shift your weight alternately between the forefeet and heels, avoiding a fixed posture. When sitting, place a cushion at the lower back and keep feet flat on the floor. Signs of worsening pain include radiating pain into the legs, numbness, weakness, or persistent sharp pain that does not ease. Stop activity immediately and apply ice externally; if it does not improve after rest, seek medical attention. During recovery, you can do abdominal breathing and glute bridge exercises to promote core stability.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: I'm at home with a back injury. Next week I need to go back to the store to recruit part-timers. Aqiang helped me screen several resumes. How can I quickly tell whether a resume is reliable? What should I mainly ask in interviews?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: When reviewing resumes, first look at job-hopping frequency and whether the candidate has clothing sales experience. Be wary of frequent job changes or vague work history. In the interview, focus on asking: how many days per week they can reliably work, how they handle picky customers, and their sense of fashion trends. Also simulate a customer service scenario to gauge their adaptability.

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing
session_313.text: Understood. So how should shifts and compensation be set reasonably? And how can a new part-timer get up to speed quickly?

session_313.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_313.text: Part-time hourly pay in Xiamen is about 18-25 yuan, settled by the hour for more flexibility, 4-8 hours per day. On the first day, new employees follow Xiao Mei to learn the cash register system, product locations, and customer service scripts, then practice with real customers. session_317.speaker: Song Yajing
session_317.text: This afternoon, Aunt Lin Xiuying and I went to Siming South Road to visit an elderly Catholic woman, Grandma Wang, who lives alone. She is almost eighty. I brought homemade low-sugar cake and fruit. She talked a lot about her younger days at the church school on Gulangyu. When we left, she made the sign of the cross over me as a blessing. At that moment it was especially warm, and my heart was full of emotion.

session_317.text: It sounds like this visit let you feel the passing on of faith and the power of love. You were deeply moved, and you also want to confirm that your actions are meaningful, right? Can you tell me more about the specific scene when Grandma Wang gave her blessing?

session_317.speaker: Song Yajing
session_317.text: Yes, with a trembling hand she made the sign of the cross on my forehead and said, “May the Lord bless you and your mother.” I immediately thought of my own mother and couldn’t help hugging her. This made me feel that faith is not just ritual but also real companionship and care.

session_317.text: Your sharing moved me too. Your actions made Granny Wang feel warmth, and at the same time, you gained an inner connection with your mother's health. Such visits are not just giving; they are a two-way blessing. If needed, we can arrange them regularly in the future, balancing the shop and church service.

session_318.text: Today at the shop I sold a booklet of my mother's handwritten Hokkien dessert recipes, and all the proceeds were donated to an elderly foundation. Unexpectedly, many customers and fellow church members came to support it. I was deeply moved and grateful.

session_318.text: Your chronic lumbar muscle strain caused by prolonged standing needs comprehensive improvement of posture, exercise, and daily habits. Should I first recommend a few simple exercises and precautions?

session_318.text: Suggestions: 1) When standing, keep your feet shoulder-width apart, slightly bend your knees, and alternate resting each foot on a high stool; 2) Every hour, do Cat-Cow pose or a backward-leaning stretch for 30 seconds; 3) Apply heat during the acute phase, and for chronic soreness, apply a cold compress for 10 minutes; 4) Supplement calcium and vitamin D, and check whether physical therapy is needed.

session_318.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_318.text: A Catholic funeral usually includes a wake, a memorial Mass, and a burial ceremony. For attire, dark clothes prepared in advance are enough; no extra accessories are needed. For a gift, you can give a white envelope (the amount depends on your relationship, generally 200-500 yuan), or bring a bouquet of white flowers according to local custom. When offering condolences, simply say, "Please accept my condolences, I will pray for your uncle," and avoid saying too much. Tomorrow, it is recommended to arrive at the church 20 minutes early, meet your classmates, and stay quiet. In the Quanzhou itinerary, remember to set aside time for the Mass (about 1 hour).

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing
session_325.text: Today I made a low-sugar Minnan steamed sponge cake using erythritol instead of brown sugar, but the finished cake was too light in color and had a dry, hard texture instead of being soft and fluffy. I want to know exactly what went wrong after the sugar substitute replacement and how I should adjust it.

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_325.text: Based on the description, erythritol is more hygroscopic than brown sugar and cannot be used by yeast, which may result in insufficient dough moisture and inadequate fermentation. Has the liquid amount and fermentation conditions in your recipe changed compared with the original recipe?

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing
session_325.text: Yes, I used water exactly according to the original recipe, only swapped the sugar for an equal amount of erythritol, and fermented for 45 minutes. Maybe there wasn't enough water?

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_325.text: Yes. Suggestions: 1) Increase the liquid amount by 15-20%; 2) Extend the fermentation time to 60-90 minutes, or use oven proofing (35°C); 3) Add 5g of baking powder and 10g of vegetable oil to improve softness. You can try these adjustments next time.

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing
session_325.text: I run a clothing store. I have to stand for 9 hours a day and also sit for long periods using the computer. Recently my lower back pain keeps recurring. I've tried cat-cow pose and hot compresses, which help but not enough. Besides these, are there any lower back rehabilitation exercises I can do in the store?

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_325.text: While at the shop, you can do one set of 'standing back extension' or 'seated spinal twist' every hour, holding for 30 seconds each time. In addition, glute bridges and bird dogs are very effective for strengthening core strength. I suggest 3 sets of 12 reps each in the morning and evening, alternating with cat-cow stretches. When sitting, put a cushion behind your lower back to maintain the lumbar curve.

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing
session_325.text: Can you be more specific about the movements and postures for glute bridges and bird-dog? Also, is hot compress twice a day for 15 minutes enough? Do I need cold compress?

session_325.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_325.text: Glute bridge: Lie on your back with knees bent, engage your glutes to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line, hold for 2 seconds, then lower slowly. Bird dog: Start on all fours and extend the opposite arm and leg at the same time, keeping your body stable. Heat therapy twice a day for 15 minutes each is appropriate; if pain worsens after exercise or with acute episodes, apply a cold compress for 15 minutes to reduce swelling. session_326.speaker: Song Yajing
session_326.text: I've been improving a low-sugar Southern Fujian cake lately, replacing white sugar with honey, and the taste is good. Mom suggested adding rice wine during fermentation to enhance the aroma and fluffiness. I'd like to know the best time to add the rice wine, the right proportion, and whether it will affect the low-sugar property.

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_326.text: It is recommended to add rice wine after the batter has been stirred into a dough and before fermentation begins, at 5%–10% of the flour weight. Glutinous rice wine works best; it promotes fermentation with almost no added sugar and does not affect the low-sugar property.

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing
session_326.text: Then if rice wine is added, does the fermentation time need to be adjusted? Also, I plan to make these in bulk as gifts—will this ratio be stable?

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_326.text: The fermentation time can be shortened by 10%-15% because the yeast and enzymes in the rice wine accelerate fermentation. For batch production, it is recommended to first run a small-scale test to confirm stability, then scale up proportionally, keeping the temperature at 28-32°C.

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing
session_326.text: Hello, my daughter will start elementary school next year. I'd like to know the enrollment zones and registration process for public elementary schools in Siming District, and do you have any recommendations for private schools?

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_326.text: Okay. Public primary schools in Siming District are zoned by household registration and property. The 2026 enrollment policy is expected to be released in April 2025. Popular schools such as Experimental Primary School and Minli Primary School are highly competitive, so you need to confirm in advance which school district your home address belongs to. Which community do you live in?

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing
session_326.text: We live near Zhongshan Road, and I run a shop there. I want to balance the school pickup/drop-off issue. Also, what are the requirements for points-based school enrollment?

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_326.text: The Zhongshan Road area is zoned for Wen'an Primary School or Ding'an Primary School; it is recommended to first confirm the address on the household registration booklet. If the hukou is not in Siming District, points-based enrollment requires a residence permit and social insurance payment records of at least 6 months. Private schools such as Kangqiao Kindergarten have an elementary division, but tuition is high and places are tight, so it's best to start inquiring now.

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing
session_326.text: So is registration through a unified online system? What materials do I need to prepare in advance?

session_326.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_326.text: Yes, registration is unified on the 'Xiamen iEducation' platform, usually starting in early May. You need to prepare the household registration booklet, property ownership certificate, residence permit (for non-local household registration), birth certificate, and vaccination certificate. I suggest saving a schedule: check policies in March, prepare materials in April, and register in May.

session_337.speaker: Song Yajing
session_337.text: I made French mille-feuille twice and failed both times. The first time it collapsed and leaked oil; the second time it was crooked. Could you help me analyze the causes and ways to improve?

session_337.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_337.text: Two typical problems. Collapse and oil leakage are usually caused by butter softening too quickly or insufficient folding; warping may be due to uneven rolling pressure and inadequate resting time. What were roughly the room temperature, butter condition, and resting time after each fold during your operation?

session_337.speaker: Song Yajing
session_337.text: Room temperature was about 22°C. The butter was taken out of the fridge and used after softening a little; the dough rested for only 10 minutes.

session_337.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_337.text: The problem is clear: the butter warmed up too quickly and the dough did not get enough rest. Recommendation: keep the butter as a cold, firm block and cut it into small pieces; use a scraper to help with folding to avoid hand heat; freeze for 15-20 minutes after each fold before continuing. When rolling, apply even pressure and work quickly. Next time, try a small batch first, and scale up after it succeeds. You are already great for daring to try and share!

session_338.text: My daughter has a painting competition tomorrow. She is well prepared, but she is only 5 years old, and I’m worried she’ll be nervous. Are there any ways to help her stay relaxed?

session_338.text: Tonight I did 15 minutes of rehabilitation training by myself: bridge, bird-dog, and plank. But I'm not sure if the movements are correct, and I'm especially worried about improper loading on my lumbar spine.

session_338.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_338.text: It is recommended to practice every other day, no more than 20 minutes each time. For glute bridges, focus on driving through the glutes and tightening the core to avoid compensating with the lower back. For bird dog, keep the spine neutral. For plank, engage the core and don't let the lower back sag. After training, do child's pose to stretch the lower back, then cat-cow to relax.

Recommended baking temperature is 160°C, and baking time should be 30-35 minutes.

session_343.speaker: Song Yajing
session_343.text: Do you have any tips for whipping egg whites? Last time I made a regular cake, it wasn't fluffy enough. Also, how do I prevent the cake from collapsing?

session_343.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_343.text: Before whipping the egg whites, make sure the bowl and mixer are free of oil and water. It is recommended to line the cake pan with parchment paper, and after baking, immediately invert it until completely cool before unmolding.

session_346.text: I'm so excited today! The dinner party was a complete success, and I still can't calm down sitting at home!

session_346.text: You must have many memorable moments to share! For example, the long-time customer who came all the way from Shanghai, or choking up during your speech—tell me all about it!

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing
session_346.text: Yes! When Vivian suddenly appeared at the door, I almost cried. My voice was shaking during the speech, but the applause from the audience kept me going. Also, my husband silently stood in the corner taking photos for me, and after it ended, he walked home with me.

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: These details are so heartwarming. From early morning until late night, nearly a hundred guests, carefully prepared party favors and cookies, and an annual review video—your thoughtfulness earned a flood of praise from customers, and the support from your husband and close friend made the dinner party especially complete.

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing
session_346.text: Many people on Moments praised my speech as sincere, and even customers who didn't come were moved. I just sent thank-you voice messages to each one, and now I feel that all my hard work for the day was worth it.

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: Song Yajing, you not only repaid your regular customers with a dinner party, but also wove warm memories with sincerity. This sense of accomplishment is something to be proud of. Your store is sure to get better and better. Rest early and keep shining tomorrow!

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing
session_346.text: I just held the appreciation dinner for core customers, but a dozen or so regular customers weren't able to make it. I sent thank-you voice messages, but I'd like to do something even more special to strengthen their loyalty to the store. What would you suggest?

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: You're worried that customers who didn't attend will feel left out, and you need a way that shows sincerity without seeming too transactional. I suggest starting with personalized care—for example, use dinner photos to make exclusive thank-you cards and send them with new-product samples or small gifts from the store; or, based on their preferences, invite them one-on-one to try on spring outfits with an exclusive discount.

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing
session_346.text: That's a good idea, but I'd like more specifics — for example, there are two VIP clients on the list; how should we treat them differently? If we send gifts, how do we control costs with a limited budget?

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: For VIP customers, you can send handmade greeting cards plus limited-edition accessories (such as scarf brooches); the cost is controllable but it feels premium. For ordinary repeat customers, put samples in logo-printed eco-friendly bags and attach handwritten notes. Also, consider organizing a small tea party on the weekend, inviting only customers who didn't attend the previous event, and use leftover decorations and refreshments from the dinner. It's low-cost and creates a sense of exclusivity.

session_346.text: I just finished wedding preparations and stood all day. Now my back is so sore I can't sleep. Is there any way to relieve it without medication?

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: It sounds like lower back muscle fatigue from standing for a long time. You can try a hot compress before bed or simple stretches to relax your lower back.

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing
session_346.text: How exactly should hot compresses be done? Are there any safe stretching exercises?

session_346.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_346.text: For heat therapy, place a hot water bottle at about 40°C on your lower back for 15 minutes. Before bed, do the cat-cow stretch: get on all fours, inhale as you sink your back and lift your head, exhale as you round your back and lower your head; repeat 10 times.

session_347.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_347.text: I suggest you add a glass of whole milk plus two spoonfuls of peanut butter to your breakfast every day. Once your mom sees you eating regularly and looking good, she will naturally feel at ease.

session_347.text: Let's talk about canelés first! I've made them twice following Master Chen's course, and I bought the copper molds, but every time the crust isn't crispy enough and the inside is a bit moist. Should the oven temperature be set in stages?

session_347.speaker: Song Yajing's Assistant
session_347.text: Segment settings are key: use 230°C high heat for the first 10 minutes to set the shape, then switch to 180°C and bake for 50 minutes. If your shop is busy during the day, you can prepare the batter the night before and bake it in two segments the next day.

qa.question: (Question time: 2025-12-31)Were there any patterns in my morning runs in October? For example, how many days per week did I run, did my pace change, and what were the reasons?

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao
session_2.text: I just finished reading Chapter 1 of "CNC Machine Tool Programming and Operation (Advanced)" tonight. The concepts are too abstract, and I'm struggling to understand them. Are there any more intuitive learning methods or supporting resources you can recommend?

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_2.text: I suggest you first watch the animated explanation videos of “Fundamentals of CNC Machining Technology” on Bilibili to visualize abstract concepts such as tool paths and coordinate systems; then use the reflection questions after each section in the textbook for output practice. When you get stuck, use the 3-minute memory rule—read it three times, write it once, and retell it once. Do you need me to help you sort out the knowledge map for Chapter 1?

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao
session_2.text: This suggestion is very practical! I plan to look for videos tonight. Also, how can theory be integrated with my daily practice? For example, what can I do during the tool change gaps while I'm on the machine every day?

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_2.text: During tool change gaps, you can use paper and pen to quickly sketch the coordinate system diagram of the current workpiece, marking the axis directions corresponding to the G-code; or write from memory the format of a common canned cycle (such as G81 drilling). Stick with it for two weeks, and your theory and hand speed will improve together.

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao
session_2.text: Today I finally officially started my certification plan! My master gave me a lot of guidance. I finished the first chapter tonight and also talked to my mom on video. She was quite happy, but told me not to get too tired. It feels really solid to have taken the first step, but I also want to hear your opinion.

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_2.text: You want emotional affirmation and sustained motivation, right? It sounds like every step today from planning to execution was solid — your master's support, your own initiative, and your family's care all show that you are on the right track.

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao
session_2.text: Yes, exactly. Actually, I know the next six months will be tough, but today's sense of accomplishment makes me not want to stop. Can you give me some advice on persevering?

session_2.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_2.text: Since you already have a clear goal and the ability to execute the first step, I suggest setting aside a fixed period of study time every day, recording the completion milestones of each small stage like you did today, and gradually accumulating positive feedback. Your mother's support and your master's guidance are resources. When you hit a bottleneck, you can take the initiative to ask them for advice. Keep the current mentality of 'taking the first step,' and you will walk very steadily.

session_3.text: I just sorted out the exam materials and read Chapter 2. I have a new understanding of macro programs, but I'm not sure if the study pace is reasonable, which chapters should be prioritized, and how to deepen my grasp by combining it with work.

session_3.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_3.text: Your preparation is very systematic. I suggest focusing on macro programs, cycle commands, and advanced G-code programming, as they carry high marks. For study pace, do 1 hour of theory each weekday evening plus 2 hours of hands-on practice on weekends, combined with machine tool verification at your factory. session_3.text: I'm tired from working during the day. Is it feasible to study efficiently for one hour at night? Is there enough time on weekends?

session_3.text: Feasible. After work, rest for 15 minutes before studying, which is more efficient. On weekends, I suggest focusing on the hard points on Saturday morning (such as macro program nesting), and on Sunday doing mock exam questions and reviewing work cases. During commutes, you can use Bilibili and MOOC platforms to listen to video lessons and consolidate knowledge points.

session_3.text: Today I independently completed the rush order for the K43 valve body and F52 flange in the workshop, exceeding the plan by 120% with a 100% pass rate. session_3.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_3.text: Congratulations on achieving high output! Regarding tool path vibration, you can first check the tool overhang length and clamping rigidity, and optimize cutting parameters (such as reducing spindle speed and adjusting feed rate). Macro programs can also dynamically compensate for vibration. I suggest you and Master Sun do a hands-on test this weekend. I've compiled a parameter comparison table for your reference.

session_3.speaker: Yin Hao
session_3.text: The parameter table is very practical. I noticed that the F52 flange clamping method may also have an influence, so I'd like to ask for ideas on fixture optimization. session_3.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_3.text: For fixture optimization, consider adding auxiliary support points or using flexible pads to distribute stress. For the five-axis machine, focus on preparing the coordinate transformation and RTCP principles. I suggest you record machining cases and later compare the differences with traditional three-axis processes.

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao
session_4.text: Today I reviewed G68 coordinate rotation, G16 polar coordinates, and the application of macro programs in tool compensation, but some loop logic is still unclear. Could you help me sort it out?

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_4.text: You are preparing for the advanced CNC certificate. You have questions about the combined use of G68/G16 and the CNC application of macro program WHILE/IF loops. Would you like me to explain the problem-solving steps using a typical exam question?

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao
session_4.text: Yes, preferably by combining the macro programming sections from previous exam papers, explain how variable definitions and loop conditions are set, and also share practical memory mnemonics.

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_4.text: Remember the mnemonic: 'Rotate polar coordinates, nest loops in macros; assign variables first, WHILE prevents deadlock.' Take milling a regular hexagon as an example: first use G16+G68 to set the pole and rotation angle, then use macro variable #1=0, WHILE[#1 LE 6] DO1, calculate G91 G16 X[radius] Y[#1*60], #1=#1+1, END1, and finally G15 G69 to cancel. Do you have example problems from the textbook to check against?

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao
session_4.text: I'm writing a tool in Python to convert the parameters in Excel into FANUC macro variable format row by row, for example #1=100; #2=200; but when I use pandas to iterate over the DataFrame, the loop logic gets stuck, and the output always duplicates or skips rows.

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_4.text: What you're dealing with is the problem of reading row by row and formatting the output. It may be that you didn't index the rows correctly in the for loop, or you forgot the newline when concatenating strings. Would you like me to provide a concrete code example that uses pandas to read Excel and uses f-strings to generate assignments for each row?

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao
session_4.text: Yes, I used iterrows(), but when outputting to a file, only the last row was displayed. Please give a directly runnable example.

session_4.speaker: Yin Hao's Assistant
session_4.text: Try this pattern: use `for index, row in df.iterrows():`, then `line = f"#{row['parameter_no']}={row['value']};\n"`, and then use `with open('output.txt','a') as f: f.write(line)`. Note to write in append mode each loop, or collect into a list first and write all at once.

session_8.text: This afternoon, when machining the K43 valve body, the surface finish failed to meet requirements. Master Sun Jianguo checked and found that the insert was worn.
