session_109.text: I just successfully grew a crop of lettuce, and next I want to try water spinach and amaranth. I'm planting on a balcony in Haikou. Can you give me some specific technical tips, such as seed treatment, watering frequency, and pest and disease control?

session_109.text: You want a practical guide for growing water spinach and amaranth on a balcony in Haikou to ensure successful planting?

session_109.text: Yes, I also want to confirm the flowerpot size and soil selection.

session_109.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_109.text: Water spinach has a well-developed root system; it is recommended to use a pot deeper than 20 cm. Amaranth can be grown in a shallow pot (15 cm). Soak the seeds in warm water for 8-12 hours to promote germination. The temperature in Haikou at the end of April is suitable. After sowing, keep the soil moist and ensure 4-6 hours of direct sunlight every day. Water when the soil is dry and water thoroughly. Apply a dilute liquid fertilizer every 10 days during the growing period. Be careful to prevent aphids; you can hang yellow sticky boards or spray chili water.

session_109.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_109.text: Very clear, thank you! Also, are there any precautions to take for crop rotation with lettuce?

session_109.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_109.text: Lettuce, water spinach, and amaranth are all leafy vegetables, but they belong to different families and genera, so they can be rotated. It is recommended to replace with fresh potting soil or deeply turn the soil and mix in decomposed organic fertilizer to avoid continuous-cropping diseases. After harvest, let the soil rest for a week before planting again.

session_110.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_110.text: Circulating current is like water circulation caused by pressure difference when two water pipes are connected in parallel. Key parameters in the formula: ΔU is the voltage difference between transformers (volts), Xk is the short-circuit impedance (ohms), circulating current I = ΔU/(2Xk). You can think of Xk as pipe resistance; the greater the resistance, the smaller the circulating current. Memory aid: voltage difference divided by double the impedance.

session_110.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_110.text: That analogy is very vivid. Then in actual photovoltaic grid-connected system wiring, what problems can circulating current cause? Do we need to pay attention to it when selecting switches and cables?

session_110.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_110.text: Circulating current will increase transformer losses and heating, and in severe cases may cause protection maloperation. When wiring, it is recommended that: 1) ensure the turns ratio and impedance of parallel transformers match to reduce voltage differences; 2) when selecting the switch rated current, consider the superposition of circulating current, generally sizing at 1.2 times the rated load; 3) verify the cable cross-sectional area according to the maximum possible current (including circulating current). You can first compare with the parameter tables in the textbook and mark the key values.

session_116.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant

session_117.text: I just watched the whole process of the mushroom nail tire repair at the tire repair shop, but I still want to confirm some of the principles and applicable situations. Could you explain it to me systematically?

session_117.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_117.text: Mushroom plug repair: insert a mushroom plug with a rubber stem from the inside of the tire, push the stem through the puncture, fit the rubber patch against the inner liner, and bond it with vulcanizing adhesive. It seals both the inside and outside of the puncture and is suitable for tread punctures with a diameter smaller than 6 mm and an angle close to vertical. Compared with ordinary patches, it is more durable, but the cost is slightly higher; it is not suitable for sidewalls or overly large punctures.

session_117.text: If the damage is on the tire shoulder or there's a crack, does that mean mushroom plugs can't be used? Also, what should I pay attention to when I install the tire myself tomorrow?

session_117.text: Yes, if the tire shoulder is worn or there are cracks, it is recommended to replace the tire. session_117.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_117.text: Tonight I read a post on the electrician forum about inverter air conditioner capacitor faults, but it didn't feel thorough. I just cleaned the air conditioner during the day and found the drain pipe loose and the cooling fins covered in dust. Are these phenomena related to capacitor faults? I'd like you to systematically explain the diagnostic methods.

session_117.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_117.text: Typical symptoms of capacitor failure include difficulty starting, stopping during operation, no cooling or weak cooling. Dust accumulation and drainage problems mainly affect heat dissipation and the air duct; they do not directly cause capacitor failure, but poor heat dissipation may accelerate capacitor aging. Diagnostic method: use the capacitance setting on a multimeter to measure capacitance. Disconnect power and discharge the capacitor, then compare with the rated value (usually within ±5% is normal); if the capacitance drops significantly or the appearance shows bulging or leaking, replacement is required.

session_117.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_117.text: Understood. I plan to put it into practice tomorrow when I go to the customer's home to repair the air conditioner. What safety precautions should I take when replacing the capacitor? For example, in terms of model selection?

session_117.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_117.text: Safety first: after cutting off the power, be sure to use a screwdriver to short-circuit the two poles of the capacitor to release residual charge. Selection principles: the capacitance and withstand voltage must match the original model, and the withstand voltage must not be lower than the original value; it is recommended to use the same brand or a compatible model; during installation, pay attention to polarity (non-polarized capacitors do not need to be distinguished), secure it firmly, and avoid the wiring harness touching metal parts.

session_122.text: Load calculation for old lines usually has three steps: 1. Use the formula ΔU=(P×L)/(C×S) to verify the voltage drop, where C is a coefficient (take 77 for copper wire); 3. Estimate the load density at 3-5kW per household and compare it with the actual load to determine whether it is overloaded.

session_122.speaker: Lu Mingqiang

session_122.text: For the C value, use 77 for copper wire (single-phase 220V) and 46 for aluminum wire. Key measurement points: wiring terminals, knife switch contacts, cable intermediate joints, and the introduction points of three-phase unbalanced loads. If the temperature difference exceeds 10°C, poor contact should be suspected. It is recommended to first measure the main switch of the distribution box, then check each branch one by one.

session_128.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_128.text: Vaseline can form a physical barrier layer to prevent moisture, but it has no effect on conductivity at room temperature; high temperatures may cause it to melt and run off. It is recommended to clean the oxide layer first, apply a thin coat of Vaseline and then use conductive grease, or use a dedicated antioxidant for greater reliability.

session_128.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_128.text: How great is the risk of melting under high temperatures? During my routine inspections, the ambient temperature can reach about 40°C at the highest.

session_128.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_128.text: At 40°C, Vaseline is basically stable, but if there is a current heat effect at the contact point, it may heat up locally. It is recommended to use electrical compound grease (conductive paste) instead of Vaseline alone, as it offers both moisture resistance and conductivity, and the operation is more standardized.

session_133.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_133.text: Teacher, I'm studying the case of 'distance protection range shrinking during a single-phase-to-ground fault.' The principle feels a bit complicated. Can you help sort it out in plain terms? After thinking it over, is it because the fault resistance increases the measured impedance, so the protection range shrinks?

session_133.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_133.text: You're right! In a single-phase-to-ground fault, the transition resistance at the fault point (such as arc resistance) gets connected in series in the measurement loop, making the calculated impedance too large, so the protection mistakenly thinks the fault is farther away and the operating range shrinks. In addition, zero-sequence current also interferes with the measurement. I suggest you look at the impedance trajectory changes together with the waveform.

session_133.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_133.text: So my recording and analysis is right, isn't it? And when you actually encounter this kind of situation on site, are there any little troubleshooting tricks for handling it?

session_133.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_133.text: Your analysis is completely correct. Field tips: 1. Use a transient fault recorder to capture the zero-sequence component and compare it with the normal waveform; 2. Add a section of 'offset impedance' to the setting value to compensate for transition resistance; 3. Verify system operation mode changes more often, such as when switching from dual power supply to single power supply, where misoperation is likely.

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_138.text: How is the balance coefficient of transformer differential protection calculated? Can you explain the principle to me? I am an electrician preparing for the Senior Technician exam, but my theoretical foundation is weak.

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_138.text: The balance coefficient is used to compensate for the amplitude and phase differences caused by differences in the current transformer (CT) ratios and wiring configurations on the two sides of the transformer. Calculation principle: based on the rated voltage, capacity, and CT ratio, convert the secondary currents on both sides to the same reference side, then calculate the ratio. Formula: balance coefficient = (UN2 × CT ratio 1) / (UN1 × CT ratio 2) × wiring coefficient, where the wiring coefficient is 1 for the Y side and √3 for the Δ side. In practical applications, it needs to be verified using the overall ratio and rated current.

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_138.text: Can you give an example to demonstrate? For instance, for a 10kV/0.4kV transformer, what are the CT ratios and how are they calculated? Also, what are common mistakes during commissioning?

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_138.text: Example: 10kV side CT ratio 300/5, 0.4kV side CT ratio 2000/5, rated capacity 1000kVA. First calculate the rated current: 10kV side I1e=57.7A, 0.4kV side I2e=1443A. Secondary current: I1a=57.7/60=0.96A, I2a=1443/400=3.61A. Balance coefficient K=3.61/0.96≈3.76. Common errors: not considering Δ/Y connection phase correction, ignoring CT polarity or incorrect ratio settings, and balance coefficient not rounded causing protection misoperation. It is recommended to let the protection device calculate automatically and then manually verify.

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_138.text: Okay. When inspecting the appearance, look for corrosion on the casing and creases on the copper tubes; turn it on to test cooling speed, outlet air temperature, and noise; focus on listening for any abnormal sounds from the compressor and fan. The compressor lifespan is generally 8-10 years, and the capacitor and motor are prone to failure. Haikou is humid, so pay attention to rust prevention. A reasonable price for a 1.5-horsepower inverter Gree is about 1,500-2,000 yuan, depending on the year.

session_138.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_138.text: Compressor wear can be judged by slow cooling after startup, loud noise, and abnormal current. It is recommended to bring a thermometer to measure the temperature difference at the air outlet; if it is below 10 degrees, be alert. For price negotiation, first quote 20% below the price you have in mind, use any issues found during a trial run as a reason to bargain, and also confirm whether installation and warranty are included.

session_140.text: In the 1980s, Haikou Daqu was commonly seen in 500ml glass bottles, with recessed patterns or raised 'Haikou Daqu' characters on the bottle. session_140.speaker: Lu Mingqiang

session_140.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant

In addition, the genuine plastic gasket is milky white and develops slight yellow spots after aging, while fakes mostly use transparent hard plastic. You can gently press the top of the cap; the genuine one is slightly elastic, while the fake is hard.

session_141.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_141.text: In the simulation software, I practiced the star-delta starting circuit and set errors such as reverse-connected time relay contacts and a main contactor self-locking circuit fault, but I still don't know how to troubleshoot these faults on site with a multimeter.

session_141.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_141.text: Common wiring errors include wrong phase sequence, stuck contacts, and timing errors. When testing, first disconnect the main power supply and use the multimeter's resistance range to measure contact continuity: normally open contacts should read infinite, and normally closed contacts should conduct. Referring to the control circuit diagram, focus on measuring the continuity of the time relay's delay contacts and the contactor's self-locking contacts.

session_141.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_141.text: I see. So can an incorrect delay setting cause a shutdown after startup or a differential protection trip? I encountered this situation in my simulation.

session_141.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_141.text: Yes. If the delay is too short, switching to delta before the star connection has fully started can cause a current surge that may trigger overcurrent or differential protection; if the delay is too long, the motor will overheat. It is recommended to use a clamp meter to measure the starting current curve, compare it with the motor's rated current and the thermal relay setting, and adjust the time relay to the manufacturer's recommended value (usually a star-delta switching delay of 3-10 seconds).

session_144.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_144.text: The dielectric loss test measures the insulation dielectric loss factor tanδ using a dielectric loss bridge. The principle is that the insulator produces leakage and polarization losses under an alternating electric field. Calculation: tanδ = ωR4C4 (when the Schering bridge is balanced). Example: standard capacitor C2 = 100 pF, R4 = 3184 Ω, frequency 50 Hz, C4 = 0.05 μF when balanced, so tanδ ≈ 0.05. Note the influence of temperature and humidity.

session_145.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_145.text: Main features of 1980s Hainan Yedao Deer Turtle Wine bottles: the glaze should be celadon-white or rice-yellow, the bottom mark reads "Hainan Deer Turtle Wine Distillery" with clear lettering, and the cap is either an iron cap or plastic-sealed. The current market reference price is 300 to 800 yuan, with well-preserved bottles worth more. Common fakes have a greenish glaze, blurred bottom marks, and rough caps.

session_145.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_145.text: I noted the mark on the base is 'Hainan Deer-Turtle Distillery', but the lettering is a bit blurry and the glaze has a greenish tint. Could this be a fake?

session_145.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_145.text: A blurred base mark and a greenish glaze are indeed typical flaws of a fake. I suggest you also check whether the bottle cap seal has aged naturally; on genuine pieces the iron cap's rust is even and the plastic seal shows signs of age. Additionally, the bottom of a bottle from the late 1980s should have hand-repaired body marks, whereas fakes are usually too smooth. You can take another close-up photo of the bottle cap to confirm.

I suggest first doing two exercises on dielectric loss factor and temperature conversion, and then looking at a case where insufficient shielding caused errors in field operation.

session_146.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_146.text: Moisture-related decline in insulation resistance is usually associated with moisture penetration and accelerated polarization due to rising temperature. On site, use a megohmmeter at the 500V range and measure the absorption ratio (R60/R15) to judge the severity of moisture. For drying, 60°C constant temperature for 8–12 hours is recommended, during which the resistance should be measured every hour until stable. A curve chart can record daily resistance values; combined with temperature and humidity correction, it can reveal early degradation trends. Unlike the poor crimping in the Jinlianyuan case, moisture is an overall performance decline of the insulator, but both need to be included in your notes classification.

session_163.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_163.text: I've just sorted out the difference between transformer differential protection and overcurrent protection, but the derivation of the ratio restraint formula is still a bit fuzzy. Can you help me work through it?

session_163.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_163.text: Differential protection is based on Kirchhoff's current law, formula I_d = |I1 - I2|, restraining current I_res = (|I1|+|I2|)/2, restraining coefficient K is generally 0.2-0.8. Overcurrent protection is set according to load current, with definite-time and inverse-time characteristics; core formula I_set = K_rel * I_Lmax. The difference is that differential protection operates instantaneously but needs to guard against inrush current, while overcurrent protection has a time delay to coordinate with system selectivity.

session_163.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_163.text: Got it. Differential protection focuses on fast tripping for faults within the protected zone, while overcurrent protection focuses on backup protection, right? Then how can we quickly determine the CT polarity during setting calculation?

session_163.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_163.text: Yes, differential protection is the main protection, and overcurrent protection is backup. CT polarity mnemonic: if the same-name terminals are connected the same way, the differential current is less than the starting value; if the polarity is wrong, the differential current is large, so be alert to protection misoperation. I suggest you draw a vector diagram and compare the current phasors on both sides; if the polarities are opposite, the differential protection will operate.

session_164.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_164.text: The percentage restraint characteristic can be imagined as a 'protection threshold': when the internal fault current is large, the threshold automatically lowers and the protection becomes sensitive; during external faults or normal operation, the restraint current increases and the threshold rises to prevent maloperation. The core formula is Iop = I0 + K*(Ires), where K is the restraint coefficient. Remember: 'be sensitive for internal faults, and reliable for external restraint.'

session_167.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_167.text: Today I used a mind map to memorize the three-phase power formula P=3UIcosφ, and it feels more memorable than copying it out. But why does the power factor cosφ affect equipment heating and energy consumption? Can you explain it using an example from my repair work?

session_167.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_167.text: A low power factor cos φ means large reactive power, which causes additional current, leading to motor coil heating and higher energy consumption. For example, when repairing a three-phase motor, if a clamp meter shows a current higher than the rated value but the voltage is normal, the power factor is likely too low, so you need to check the capacitor compensation or load conditions. Active power = 3UIcosφ is what actually does the work, while reactive power maintains the magnetic field and does not consume energy, but it does increase line losses.

session_167.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_167.text: So what's the relationship between apparent power, active power, and reactive power? I saw in a book that S=√(P²+Q²). Can this be used in actual maintenance?

session_167.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_167.text: Apparent power S is the total capacity, equal to 3UI. P=3UIcosφ, Q=3UIsinφ. In maintenance, to judge whether a transformer or circuit breaker is overloaded, you need to look at apparent power S; electricity bills are calculated by active power P, so improving cosφ can save money. You can split the mind map into three branches: active power (energy that does work), reactive power (heat loss), apparent power (total capacity), and then add measurement methods, such as using a multimeter to measure current and voltage to calculate S, and using a power factor meter to measure cosφ. That way it's more systematic.

session_173.text: Hello, I'd like to learn about the registration requirements and study path for the Senior Technician Certificate in Electrical Work. I am 35 years old this year, with a middle school education, but I have over ten years of hands-on experience.

session_173.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_173.text: Hello, Master Lu! The senior technician certificate (electrical category) is usually issued by the human resources and social security department or the electric power industry association. Generally, applicants must have worked in this occupation for more than 3 continuous years after obtaining the technician qualification. A junior high school education may be a limitation, but some regions allow applicants with senior worker status to register exceptionally. The exam consists of theory and practical operation. Theory covers circuit analysis, PLC control, etc., and the practical part focuses on troubleshooting. It is recommended to first obtain the senior electrician certificate and then advance step by step. You can check the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau website or electric power training institutions. The recommended preparation period is 3-6 months. Companies usually provide subsidies, and salary increases are about 20%-30%.

session_173.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_173.text: Will I be rejected because I only have a junior high school education? Is there any way to directly apply for senior technician? My father also encourages me to learn more while I'm young, and Manager Liu at the company mentioned it.

session_173.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_173.text: A junior high school diploma does need to be supplemented when applying for Senior Technician. It is recommended to first upgrade your education through adult education to a secondary specialized school or associate degree (in an electric-power-related major), while accumulating practical experience at the same time. Directly applying for Senior Technician is usually not feasible; you need to advance step by step: Junior → Intermediate → Senior → Technician → Senior Technician. You can start from Senior Worker and prepare for the theory exam in your spare time. Recommended textbooks include 'Electrical Fundamentals' and 'PLC Programming and Applications', supplemented by online courses. If the company has an internal training policy, you can ask Manager Liu whether there is a tuition subsidy for education upgrading.

session_204.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_204.text: Old Lu, how does PWM control the motor speed? There are too many formulas in the book. Can you explain it simply?

session_204.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_204.text: Easy to understand: imagine a dimmable desk lamp at home where a knob rapidly switches the light on and off to control brightness. PWM is switching the voltage on and off thousands of times per second; by changing the proportion of 'on' time (the duty cycle), the average voltage is adjusted, and thus the motor speed. For example, at a 50% duty cycle, the motor voltage is halved, and the speed is roughly halved too; combined with frequency variation, it becomes more precise—this is called the V/F curve.

session_204.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_204.text: Oh, the duty cycle adjusts the voltage, so what's the frequency change for? What exactly is the relationship in the V/F curve?

session_204.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_204.text: Yes, voltage and frequency must change in sync. For example, a motor rated 380V/50Hz: if the frequency drops to 25Hz, the voltage must also drop to 190V, otherwise the magnetic circuit saturates and the motor heats up. Mnemonic: 'voltage and frequency drop together, constant flux and constant torque.' Belt conveyors and fans of this constant-torque load type are the most typical.

session_205.text: I am studying for the senior electrical technician exam. I'm still unclear about PLC wiring differences and servo drive parameter settings, especially fault code memory, which is easy to forget. Can you help me sort out the key review points for these core exam topics?

session_205.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_205.text: I understand your needs. In the senior technician exam, the PLC section often tests logic errors, such as incorrect contact order in ladder diagrams. For servo drive parameter debugging, you can use the mnemonic: 'adjust the speed gain first to make it stable, then follow with the position loop.' For memorizing fault codes quickly, it is recommended to group them by fault category, such as overload types (Err1-5) and communication types (Err10-15), and memorize them together with practical case studies.

session_205.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_205.text: Thank you! That formula is really practical. I mainly work on elevator control systems. Could you tell me more about the typical easy-to-make mistakes in PLCs and servo drives in modern elevators? For example, parameter debugging when the elevator is leveling.

session_205.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_205.text: Of course. A common mistake in elevator leveling adjustment is that the integral time of the position loop in the servo drive is set too large, causing overshoot. I suggest setting the integral time initially to 0.1 second and then fine-tuning it. Another one is that the interlock logic between the door lock and the run command in the PLC program is easy to overlook, and exam papers often use this as a trap. Remember to check the input signals before drawing the ladder diagram.

session_216.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_216.text: I'm Lu Mingqiang, an electrician. During my lunch break I use the Electrician Exam Pass app to do practice questions, but I always mix up the difference between variable-frequency drive PID adjustment and power factor compensation. Can you help me clarify it in a simple way?

session_216.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_216.text: The core difference is: PID regulation is an algorithm inside the VFD for closed-loop control of motor speed (proportional, integral, derivative), while power factor compensation improves the grid's reactive power by switching capacitor banks in and out. Remember: 'PID adjusts speed, capacitors compensate reactive power.' You can memorize it using the constant-pressure water supply scenario with a motor.

session_216.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_216.text: Got it. So what are the common mistakes? Like mistaking the proportional action of PID for capacitance?

session_216.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_216.text: Correct! Common mistakes include: 1) Confusing P (proportional) in PID with the capacity of compensation capacitors; P regulates response speed, while capacity determines the amount of reactive power compensation; 2) Mistakenly thinking power factor compensation also involves closed-loop integration — in fact, compensation only needs switching control, no integration. A suggested mnemonic is: 'Proportional and derivative need no capacitor; integral and compensation take separate paths.'

session_217.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_217.text: Although Master Li helped me fill in the solutions for resonant circuits and three-phase short circuits, I still feel the principles aren't clear enough. Is there a real-life analogy to help me remember the key points of series resonance and the symmetrical component method?

session_217.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_217.text: Series resonance is like a swing: when the frequency is exactly right, it swings higher and higher; at this time the impedance is smallest and the current is largest. Parallel resonance is like spring resonance: when the frequency is suitable, the amplitude is largest but the impedance is greatest. The symmetrical component method can be imagined as a "decomposition magic" - treating the asymmetric three-phase system as the superposition of three symmetrical components: 'positive', 'negative', and 'neutral', calculating each separately and then combining them, avoiding complex circuits.

session_217.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_217.text: That analogy is easy to remember! Then what does the quality factor Q of resonance correspond to? Also, in three-phase short-circuit calculations, how do you quickly distinguish positive sequence, negative sequence, and zero sequence?

session_217.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_217.text: The Q value is equivalent to the stiffness of a swing—the higher the Q, the sharper the resonance curve, the stronger the frequency selectivity, and the slower the decay after a power outage. Positive sequence is ABC rotating clockwise, negative sequence is counterclockwise, and zero sequence is all three in the same direction with the same amplitude—imagine three soldiers doing 'forward step', 'backward step', and 'lockstep'. Memory mnemonic: 'positive inverse negative, same is zero' (positive sequence counterclockwise, negative sequence clockwise, zero sequence same direction).

session_218.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_218.text: What you are confused about may be the origin of the line voltage leading the corresponding phase voltage by 30° in the phasor diagram, and how to draw the phasor diagram of a symmetrical three-phase circuit? We can start analyzing from the specific wrong problem.

session_218.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_218.text: Yes, it's the 30° phase angle difference and the rotation direction that are easy to mix up. Is there a simple way to remember them?

session_218.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_218.text: Remember the mnemonic 'the line voltage leads the phase voltage by 30°'. When drawing, first draw the three phase voltages Ua, Ub, Uc with 120° differences between them. The line voltage Uab = Ua - Ub, pointing from the end of Ub to the end of Ua, and its direction leads Ua by 30°. It is recommended that you draw it by hand once, marking the start and end points of the phasors in order, to completely avoid rote memorization.

session_222.text: I was debugging the ladder diagram for conveyor belt sequence control today, but during simulated operation, after the feeding process is completed, it cannot stop properly and always gets stuck in a branch. session_222.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_222.text: The situation you described is a return problem with the step instruction. The common cause is that RET is not correctly placed at the end position of the last step, or the branch transfer condition causes the loop not to close. Please confirm whether the RET instruction is used before the end of the last step in your sequence control, and whether the step transfer conditions (such as X0 normally closed) are reasonable. If you have a screenshot of the ladder diagram, I can help you pinpoint it.

session_222.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_222.text: Yes, I added RET before the last step, but I used X0 normally open for the transition condition. It should probably be normally closed. Let me change it and try.

session_222.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_222.text: Yes, the stop signal usually uses a normally closed contact as the step transition condition. This way, when the stop button is pressed, the step condition is broken and the program returns to the initial step. In addition, I suggest adding an interlock condition in the initial step to prevent accidental startup. You can use the monitoring function of the simulation app to check the step state transition process. If you have any more questions, feel free to discuss.

session_224.text: I am self-studying Mitsubishi FX series PLC analog control. I don't quite understand how the analog-to-digital conversion resolution affects accuracy, and how the data comparison instruction should be combined with the actual current value measured on site.

session_224.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_224.text: Do you want to understand the application of resolution and comparison instructions through a concrete example, such as the logic where a temperature sensor signal is converted into a digital value and then triggers an alarm?

session_224.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_224.text: Yes, it would be best to have an example with actual parameters, such as 4-20 mA corresponding to a temperature range, using a comparison instruction to implement an over-temperature alarm.

session_224.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_224.text: Assuming 4-20 mA corresponds to 0-100°C and the resolution is 12 bits (0-4095), each 1°C corresponds to 40.95 digital counts. Use the comparison instruction CMP to compare the current AD value with the preset alarm value (for example, 80°C corresponds to 3276), and the output drives the alarm relay. The actually measured current value can be used with a multimeter to verify the program logic.

session_224.text: My parents are both over 60 and have hardly ever had physical exams. This weekend I'm going to Meilan District to visit them and want to take them for a check-up. session_224.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_224.text: Recommended basic items include complete blood count, urinalysis, liver and kidney function, blood glucose, blood lipids, blood pressure, electrocardiogram, and abdominal ultrasound. For those over 60, add cardiac color Doppler ultrasound, carotid artery ultrasound, bone density, and tumor markers (e.g., carcinoembryonic antigen). Fasting for 8-12 hours is required before the checkup. Chronic disease medications (such as antihypertensive drugs) can be taken as usual, but glucose-lowering drugs should be taken as prescribed. When communicating with parents, approach from the angle of caring about health and preventing disease to avoid triggering resistance.

session_226.text: Do you want to understand the basic rules of PID parameter tuning? For example, excessive proportional gain causes oscillation, integral time eliminates steady-state error but may cause overshoot, and derivative improves dynamics but easily introduces noise, right? session_226.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_226.text: It is recommended to first master the Ziegler-Nichols tuning method: first adjust P to make the system oscillate critically, record the oscillation period and gain, then set PI or PID parameters according to empirical formulas. For temperature control of the incubator, you can first increase Ti to suppress overshoot; for motor speed control, focus on Td to suppress overshoot. I recommend the "PID Control for Beginners" video on YouTube or practice with free simulation software such as Simulink or the Python-control library.

session_233.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_233.text: Okay. Parallel operation of transformers requires three core conditions: 1) The phase sequence must be identical, otherwise circulating current will occur; 2) The voltage ratios must be equal (error ≤ ±0.5%), otherwise no-load circulating current will be excessive; 3) The short-circuit impedance percentages must be equal (error ≤ ±10%), otherwise load distribution will be uneven. For specific calculations, check the nameplate parameters and memorize them in connection with actual working scenarios (such as switching between dual power supply in a substation).

session_233.speaker: Lu Mingqiang

session_233.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_233.text: Assume two transformers have the same capacity, with short-circuit impedances of 4% and 8% respectively. After being connected in parallel, the total load is 1000 kVA. The one with smaller impedance carries a larger load: the first transformer carries about 667 kVA, the second about 333 kVA. If overloaded for a long time, it will cause insulation aging. I suggest you, based on your notes, write the derivation steps for this type of calculation in your error notebook and mark the easily confused points with a red pen.

session_235.text: Tonight I'm doing the "Electrical Safety Technology" special exercises. I always mix up the difference between TN-C and TN-S systems, and also how to choose the trip current for leakage protection. The explanations are too brief—can you help me understand it thoroughly?

session_235.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_235.text: Okay. TN-C is a three-phase four-wire system where the protective and neutral conductors share one wire (PEN); it is low-cost but less reliable. TN-S is a five-wire system with the protective conductor (PE) and neutral conductor (N) separated, which is safer. Mnemonic: 'C mixed, S separated, PE independent truly safe.' Leakage protection operating current: 30 mA for protection against electric shock to humans, 300 mA for line fire prevention. Before using a high-voltage voltage detector, confirm that the sound and light signals are normal and that the insulating rod length matches the voltage level.

session_235.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_235.text: 30 mA is the general value specified in GB 50054 and applies to ordinary handheld equipment; use 15 mA in humid environments. High-voltage detector operation steps: first perform a self-check, then put on insulating gloves, touch each phase with an insulating rod while maintaining a safe distance; a buzzer or flash indicates live parts. Remember: “Self-check, wear gloves, touch phase by phase; only with audible and visual alarm is it safe.”

session_242.text: Mingqiang is reviewing the PLC questions he got wrong. The timer instructions in ladder diagrams always confuse him. Can you explain the difference between them and the time relays in relay circuits?

session_242.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_242.text: PLC timers are like digital hourglasses: when the set time is reached, the state changes, unlike mechanical time relays, which have coils and contacts. For example, with the TON instruction, it starts timing when energized, and when the time is up, the output coil is energized. Think of it as a child playing with an hourglass timer: when time is up, it calls you. Easy to remember.

session_242.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_242.text: What about the counter? For example, CTU, where value overflow is a frequent exam point—how should I understand it?

session_242.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_242.text: CTU is like a garage counting barrier: every time a car enters, it adds one; when it reaches the preset value, the barrier lifts (output action). Overflow is when the value exceeds the upper limit, and it clears to zero and counts again. In the exam, pay attention to the reset instruction R, which is like setting the counter back to zero and starting to count again.

Derivation of the equivalent circuit: at no load, it is equivalent to the magnetizing reactance Xm in parallel with the core-loss resistance Rm; at load, the leakage reactances X1, X2 and winding resistances R1, R2 are considered. Draw the T-type equivalent circuit: on the left, the primary leakage reactance is in series with the resistance; in the middle, the magnetizing branch is in parallel; on the right, the secondary leakage reactance and series resistance are referred to the primary side. The voltage ratio is k=N1/N2.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: Today I picked up a 1968 oil-immersed current transformer from Haikou Power Plant. I gave it a simple cleaning with a dry cloth and WD-40 but didn't dare to do anything major. Do you think I handled it correctly? And how can I look up its historical background and technical specifications?

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: Your initial cleaning approach is correct. WD-40 is fine for rust removal, but don't touch the enamel nameplate, to avoid damaging the lettering. It's recommended to use a soft brush to clean the gaps tomorrow, then apply a thin layer of anti-rust oil. As for the background, you can consult the industrial archives at the Haikou Municipal Archives, or contact retired veteran workers from the power plant. When posting on the forum, include clear photos of the nameplate and keywords such as 'oil-immersed transformer ratio' to make it easier to get professional information.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: I've just finished reviewing current transformers. I want to confirm one thing: why must the secondary side absolutely not be open-circuited? I used the old transformer I picked up this afternoon to compare with the magnetic circuit diagram in the textbook. I feel I understand the principle, but I'm afraid I might have missed something.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: You've hit the key point! When the secondary side is open-circuited, all of the primary current becomes magnetizing current, causing the core flux to surge sharply. This induces high voltage that endangers equipment and personal safety, and the core also overheats. You can use the 1968 physical object and compare it with the magnetic circuit diagram to understand this. This associative learning method is very effective and leaves a deeper impression than simply reading the textbook.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: Yes, and I also noticed that the accuracy class on the old instrument transformer nameplate is 0.5, corresponding to the accuracy ranges for ratio error and phase angle error in the textbook. This one-to-one correspondence makes error analysis much clearer.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: Exactly right! Class 0.5 means that under the specified load, the ratio error does not exceed ±0.5% and the phase error does not exceed ±30 minutes. The fact that you can match the nameplate parameters to the error classes in the textbook shows that associating physical objects has helped you break through abstract concepts. Next, I suggest you review the insulation and heat dissipation principles of oil-immersed instrument transformers using the same method; your old item can exactly demonstrate the role of the oil.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: During my morning run today, a friend recommended an antique restoration workshop in Meilan District. I found a 1968 transformer and an old electrician's knife that belonged to my father, and I want to go take a look this weekend. Do you know the workshop's exact address, business hours, and services?

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: Based on your description, it is most likely 'Haifu Old Street Workshop', located at No. 72 Haifu Road, Meilan District, Haikou (searchable in navigation apps). Business hours: Monday to Sunday, 9:00-18:30. Main services: rust removal and rust prevention for wood and metal items, patina restoration, touch-up painting and antiquing; it can handle old industrial items such as instrument transformers. Prices depend on complexity: generally 50-200 yuan for rust removal and rust prevention, and 100-500 yuan for patina restoration. It is recommended to call ahead for an appointment (0898-6532xxxx). Have you wiped it with WD-40? That may affect subsequent professional treatment.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: Yes, I just wiped the surface with WD-40. Will it affect the repair? Also, do I need an appointment on the weekend?

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: WD-40 leaves an oily residue that may interfere with subsequent rust removal and patina adhesion. It is recommended to clean it with a neutral cleaner, let it dry, and then bring it over. Do not polish it yourself. The place is crowded on weekends, so it is strongly recommended to call ahead the day before to book an appointment, explaining that the item to be repaired is an oil-immersed transformer; the workshop can assess whether special treatment is needed.

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_257.text: Got it, I'll wash it clean first and call to make an appointment tomorrow. Thanks!

session_257.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_257.text: You're welcome! I wish you a smooth weekend repairing these items that are full of stories. Feel free to contact me anytime if you have any other questions.

session_257.text: Today, while organizing the tool cabinet, I found my dad's “Liya” brand electrician's knife from when he was young. It's badly rusted, but the nameplate is still clear. In the afternoon, I also picked up a 1968 instrument transformer from Haikou Power Plant, from the same period as the power plant where my dad used to work. session_257.text: Through these old objects, you are reliving your father's professional memories and feeling a sense of pride in that legacy. Now that I've taken over his job as an electrician for nearly ten years, I truly understand his rigorousness back then. When I found that current transformer, it felt like holding a piece of history in my hands.

session_258.text: You want to combine physical comparison and forum posts to deeply understand the winding structure and insulation characteristics of oil-immersed instrument transformers, and relate common faults of old equipment to modern maintenance methods, right?

session_258.text: Yes, I especially want to know how cable paper and transformer oil work together for insulation, and how the experience mentioned in Master Li's 1980s notes corresponds to current megger test results.

session_258.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_258.text: The windings of oil-immersed instrument transformers often use a multi-layer cylindrical structure, with cable paper and oil ducts for interlayer insulation. Partial discharge can be located by ultrasonic or UHF methods. You can use a megohmmeter to measure insulation resistance and corroborate it with Master Li's experience that 'readings are low on humid days' to judge the degree of dampness.

session_261.text: I just finished organizing a quick-reference comparison table between smart circuit breakers and traditional protection, but I'm not quite sure about the correspondence between smart circuit breaker trip curves and traditional thermal-magnetic tripping. session_261.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_261.text: You mean the equivalent conversion logic between the electronic trip curves of smart circuit breakers (such as LI, LSI) and traditional thermal-magnetic trip (thermal protection + magnetic protection), right? Do you want me to explain it with a comparison of specific parameters?

session_261.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_261.text: Yes, it's about how the long delay and instantaneous settings in the LI curve correspond to the setting values of traditional thermal-magnetic trip units. I also have questions about the connection of the N and PE poles of smart circuit breakers in a TN-C system.

session_261.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_261.text: The LI curve's long-time delay corresponds to thermal protection; the setting value is current multiple × rated current. The instantaneous trip corresponds to magnetic protection and is set according to the short-circuit current. In a TN-C system, the N pole of a smart circuit breaker must be separated from the PE pole. Short-circuiting them inside the circuit breaker is strictly forbidden, otherwise it will cause abnormal current in the PEN conductor. It is recommended that you mark in the quick-reference table: at the TN-C incoming line, use a 4-pole circuit breaker, with no protection on the N pole and the PE pole directly grounded.

session_262.text: I'm reviewing the principles of differential protection. Can you give an example from an actual distribution cabinet of how differential, overcurrent, and ground-fault protection coordinate their operating sequences during a fault?

session_262.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_262.text: It seems you want to combine the exam key points with the actual discussion at Sunday's exchange meeting, and you need clear logic with scenarios. A common configuration is: when a slight inter-turn short circuit occurs inside a transformer, the differential protection should trip instantaneously, while overcurrent protection acts as backup with a time delay; ground protection operates during system ground faults and needs to coordinate with differential protection to avoid misoperation. I suggest drawing a sequence diagram and labeling the operating current and time coordination relationships of each protection. Would you like me to help you sort out a typical setting calculation case?

session_262.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_262.text: Yes, I'm just worried that my understanding of the timing coordination is not thorough enough, and I won't be able to explain it clearly in exam short-answer questions. Can you give me a simplified setting calculation example?

session_264.text: I plan to renovate the electrical circuits during the next repair of the ancestral house. I want to change the exposed wiring to flame-retardant conduit and install a new electrical panel. What materials do I need to prepare? What are the construction steps and precautions?

session_264.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_264.text: It is recommended to prepare flame-retardant PVC conduit (20mm or 25mm), 2.5mm² lighting wire, 4mm² socket wire, 10mm² incoming line, residual current circuit breaker (63A main switch + branch leakage protection), and a distribution box (12-16 positions). Construction steps: 1. Cut off power and test for voltage; 2. Plan the wiring route; 3. Cut grooves or use surface-mounted conduit clips; 4. Pull wires and label them; 5. Install the electrical box and connect wires; 6. Test the leakage protector and grounding. Note that the walls of the old house may be damp, so ensure the conduit is sealed and moisture-proof, and leave an access opening for maintenance.

session_264.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_264.text: My father suggested using metal conduit, but I think flame-retardant PVC conduit is lighter and more convenient. Is there a big difference in safety and cost between the two? Also, I can only do the construction on weekends. How should the schedule be arranged?

session_264.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_264.text: Flame-retardant PVC conduit is cost-effective, corrosion-resistant, and easy to bend, making it suitable for ordinary residences; metal conduit is strong and rodent-proof, but costs 30% more and requires grounding. For your situation, I recommend flame-retardant PVC conduit (compliant with JGJ16). The construction schedule can be planned as follows: the first weekend, remove old wiring and finish routing layout; the second weekend, pull wires and install the distribution box; the third weekend, test and accept. Set aside 2-3 hours each day to avoid mistakes from rushing.

session_266.text: Lu Mingqiang, an electric power emergency repair worker, is preparing for the Senior Technician exam. At noon today he spent 40 minutes studying the lightning protection and grounding chapter and screenshotted three error-prone points in ground resistance measurement, but he hasn't fully digested them. Can you explain in plain terms the core differences, common mistakes, and practical scenarios of the three-pole method, four-pole method, and clamp method?

session_266.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_266.text: Hello Master Lu, it's great that you keep studying after emergency repairs in the rain during the day. The three-pole method is the most common; the easy mistake is the distance between the voltage electrode and the current electrode (generally 20m/15m, or a 0.618 ratio). The four-pole method can eliminate lead resistance, but the exam often tests that it cannot completely replace the three-pole method. The clamp method is most convenient, but it only applies to multi-point grounding systems; using it on an independent grounding electrode is a big trap. With your work, for example, the meter box in Binhai New Village is single-point grounding, so the three-pole method with an auxiliary wire is more suitable.

session_266.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_266.text: Yes, the first easy-to-get-wrong point I screenshotted is 'the clamp method cannot measure an independent grounding electrode.' The second is 'the pole spacing in the four-pole method does not need to be equal' — how should I understand this?

session_266.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_266.text: Very accurate. The clamp method measures loop resistance; a single-point ground has no loop, so the reading tends to be too small. In the four-probe method, the distances of current probe C and voltage probe P need not be equal, but the voltage probe must be in the zero-potential zone (about 0.618 times the distance of probe C from point E). In practice, the four-probe method can be used to eliminate lead-wire error, but the system under test must have independent leads.

session_266.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_266.text: Got it. The third common error is the seasonal coefficient. For example, the measured resistance is a little low after rain, and you need to multiply by the dry-season coefficient to judge whether it is acceptable. Isn't the exam trap exactly this kind of case that needs correction?

session_266.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_266.text: Exactly, this is the exam point. The question may give measured values after rain and ask you to judge whether the grounding is acceptable. Many people directly compare the measured values with the standard and forget to multiply by the seasonal factor of 1.1-1.2. Another trap is asking you to select the measurement method. For urban streetlights (multi-point grounding), using the three-pole method is wrong; you should choose the clamp method. Keep these points in mind in connection with your daily work, and you'll pass the exam.

session_275.text: I am 35 years old with a junior high school education, working in electrical and mechanical installation and repair in Haikou. The exam includes theory (70%) and practical operation (30%). Registration is in March and September each year. You can consult the Haikou Electric Power Training Center. With your work experience, education is not an obstacle.

Focus on drawing flowcharts and simulate operations before hands-on practice. You can also use online question banks to practice high-frequency questions; Haikou Electric Power Training Center has evening classes.

session_282.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_282.text: The essence of the same-name terminals of a mutual inductor is that the magnetic flux directions are consistent. Imagine two coils wound on the same iron core; when current flows in from one end, the two ends where the magnetomotive force directions are the same are the same-name terminals. To determine them, you can use the "DC method" — briefly connect a battery and observe the deflection direction of the voltmeter. When doing calculation problems, first draw the magnetic flux path, then write the equation based on the marked same-name terminals, such as U1/U2 = N1/N2, but take the polarity signs into account. session_286.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_286.text: Today I used the method in Master Li's notes to teach Zhao Qiang to measure three-phase unbalance, first measuring line voltage then calculating deviation. Is this approach correct? Also, the notes mention the phase voltage method and the line voltage method; I want to understand when each is used. Can you explain the principle thoroughly and give a few mnemonics or practice questions to work on?

session_286.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_286.text: Are you trying to confirm whether the operating method you taught Zhao Qiang during the day was accurate, and at the same time hoping to understand the theoretical differences and applicable scenarios of the two testing methods, and to get easy-to-remember mnemonics and practice questions to consolidate your exam preparation, right?

session_286.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_286.text: Yes, that's it. During the day I always felt the line voltage method was easier to apply, but the notes emphasized that the phase voltage method is more accurate in some cases, and I'm afraid I've misunderstood. Please sort it out clearly, preferably with a simulated fault for me to diagnose.

session_286.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_286.text: The method you taught Zhao Qiang is basically correct: the line-to-line voltage method is suitable for delta connections or unknown windings, and unbalance is judged by the deviations among the three line voltages; the phase voltage method only applies to wye-connected windings when the neutral point is measurable. Mnemonic: "Star measures phase voltages, delta measures line voltage differences; zero-sequence is seen in the neutral line, positive/negative sequence is seen in magnitude." Practice problem: For a delta-connected motor, the measured line voltages are Uab=380V, Ubc=380V, Uca=345V. Calculate the three-phase voltage unbalance and determine what type of fault it may be. Answer: The unbalance is about 3.1%, possibly a phase loss or an inter-turn short circuit in the winding. I suggest you go back and recalculate using the formula in your notes to cross-check. Do you need me to further explain the derivation of the formula?

session_287.text: I'm going to take my 8-year-old son to Xinhua Bookstore this Saturday to choose a popular science book on electricity. I'm an electrician myself, and I want to find a book that can tie in with my work. Any recommendations?

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_287.text: Recommend The Wonderful World of Electricity (ages 8-12). It has many illustrations, covers basic circuits and the principles of household appliances, and the content is close to everyday life. After arriving at the store, you can browse the table of contents and the experiment section to confirm whether the child can understand it.

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_287.text: Sounds good. Are there any simple experiments to go with the book? I have wire and a small bulb at home.

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_287.text: You can use a battery, wires, and a small bulb to do a series circuit experiment so the child can observe the light on and off. Books usually have illustrations; when you buy one on Saturday, choose a version with an experiment chapter.

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_287.text: I planted tomatoes on my balcony. Today is the 3rd day. It's 26°C and cloudy, and the seeds haven't sprouted yet. My child is a bit disappointed. I'd like to know how many days they usually take to germinate. Is it normal now? How should I water and provide light going forward?

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_287.text: Common tomato varieties germinate in about 4-7 days, and being on day 3 is within the normal range. 26°C and cloudy weather are fine. The key is to keep the soil surface slightly moist (insert a finger one knuckle deep and it should feel damp). No extra light is needed; before germination avoid direct strong light and keep it in a spot with scattered light. Have the children record the temperature and humidity with a thermometer and hygrometer every day, and draw a germination countdown chart together to increase their involvement.

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_287.text: Do I need to keep the soil surface moist all the time? Should I wrap it in a plastic bag at night to keep it warm?

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_287.text: You don't need to keep it wet all the time. Spray water when the topsoil is slightly dry (about once every 1-2 days). At night, if the room temperature is below 15°C, you can cover it with a transparent plastic bag to retain moisture and keep it warm, and open it during the day for ventilation. I suggest sticking a chopstick into the edge of the pot to mark the water level, so it is easier for the child to observe moisture changes.

session_287.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_287.text: OK. Standard steps for the double-check method: 1. Use a voltage tester on a known live part to confirm the tester works; 2. Test the incoming line side to be measured and confirm there is no power; 3. Test again to confirm. The core principle is to prevent misjudgment caused by a faulty voltage tester. The key theoretical points for senior technician include safety regulations, circuit analysis, and troubleshooting. I suggest you first master the Electrician Safety Operating Procedures and past exam questions.

session_288.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_288.text: The effective value of a non-sinusoidal periodic current equals the square root of the sum of the squares of the effective values of each harmonic. Did you miss higher-order harmonics or ignore phase effects? You can double-check the specific steps.

session_293.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_293.text: In Master Li's notes, the motor forward-reverse control circuit diagram — I didn't quite understand the contactor interlock part. Can you explain it to me?

session_293.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_293.text: Understood. Contactor interlocking prevents the forward and reverse contactors from being energized at the same time, which would cause a short circuit. Usually a normally closed contact is connected in series in the other contactor's coil circuit. For example, the normally closed contact of the forward contactor is connected in series in the reverse starting circuit, so when the forward contactor is energized, the reverse starting circuit is disconnected, ensuring safety. Can you see the connection position of the normally closed contacts in your notes?

session_293.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_293.text: I see it. It's marked NC in the diagram — is that the one? Then will the exam test troubleshooting of interlock circuits?

session_293.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_293.text: Yes, NC means normally closed contact. Common exam points include: short circuits caused by interlock failure, thermal relay setting values, and the principle of dual interlocking of buttons. I suggest you look at the diagram and imagine the current path, then practice wiring on real components, and deepen your memory through simulated fault troubleshooting.

session_296.text: I am 35 years old and usually run three or four times a week, but I have never run a half marathon. A friend has invited me to sign up for a race together in the first half of next year. I'd like to ask about a scientific preparation plan: how should I train and avoid injury?

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_296.text: It is recommended to focus on aerobic running for the first 8 weeks, 3-4 times per week, gradually increasing the distance per session from 5 km to 12 km; add interval runs and tempo runs in weeks 9-14; taper in the 2 weeks before the race. For strength training, do core and leg exercises twice a week. Choose cushioned running shoes, take an energy gel 1 hour before race time, and hydrate every 5 km.

session_296.text: Okay, I'll first buy a new pair of running shoes and try them out. What should I do if my knee hurts during training?

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_296.text: Knee pain is often caused by increasing running volume too quickly or by running form issues. It is recommended to immediately reduce running volume and switch to swimming or cycling for cross-training, while also strengthening the gluteal muscles and quadriceps. If the pain persists, consult a sports medicine doctor.

session_296.text: I've been an electrician for many years. Today, while repairing a power distribution cabinet, I lost time because I didn't understand PLC. I want to learn PLC systematically from scratch. Can you help me plan a learning path and recommend some reliable resources?

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_296.text: Of course. I suggest three steps: first master the basic electrical logic and relay circuits (you already have), then learn PLC working principles and ladder diagram programming, and finally choose a mainstream brand (such as Siemens S7-200 or Mitsubishi FX series) for hands-on practice. Recommended: the "PLC Zero-Basics Introduction" forum column and the "Industrial Control Beginner Crash Course" series of free videos on Bilibili, and also buy a second-hand development board to practice wiring and program downloading.

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_296.text: I've never been exposed to programming before. Is the ladder diagram easy to learn? Are there any hard requirements for PLC certification?

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_296.text: Ladder diagrams are similar to relay circuit diagrams. Since you have an electrical background, you can quickly pick it up. PLC accounts for a large portion of the senior technician certificate exam. You need to master basic programming, fault diagnosis, and simple human-machine interaction. It is recommended to invest 8-10 hours a week, complete the beginner stage within 3 months, and then spend 1 year gaining experience through projects, laying the foundation for the certificate exam and starting a business.

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_296.text: I see. Then I'll first watch videos on Bilibili, and then buy a used Mitsubishi board to practice on. You said 8-10 hours per week earlier. My work schedule is irregular—can I arrange it flexibly?

session_296.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_296.text: Okay. Use lunch breaks and evening spare time to watch videos and study the theory, and focus on 2-3 hours of hands-on practice on weekends. In the early stage, don't insist on a fixed weekly duration; just maintain an average of over one hour per day. The key is to be more hands-on, for example, use a development board to simulate the heating tube control loop and write a program to reproduce the fault scenario you encountered today.

For customer acquisition, you can rely on Wu Gang's connections to solicit advertising and contact property managers, while also facilitating referrals from existing customers. In terms of risk, you need to purchase liability insurance, sign service contracts to clarify rights and responsibilities, and balance your time between your current job and business preparation.

Once trust is built, sign a long-term maintenance agreement at a preferential price. Regarding cooperation with Wu Gang, it is recommended to clearly divide the work: he handles lead generation and introducing clients, while you handle technology and service. Profits can be split proportionally (for example, he receives a 10-15% referral fee), and a written cooperation agreement should be signed to avoid disputes.

session_301.text: Today I installed a new electrical cabinet at Shangbang Baihui City. The PLC module wiring and commissioning succeeded on the first try. I want to systematically summarize the key steps and theoretical points for future review and teaching apprentices.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: So you want to organize a hands-on practice note following the order from wiring points to commissioning and verification, combined with the theory from last night's online course? For example, first confirm the PLC model and the corresponding relationship of the relay control circuit.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_301.text: Yes, the key points are the control circuit logic, the insulation test values, and the method for sectional troubleshooting of tripping. Help me check them.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: OK. The PLC model is a Siemens S7-1200, and the relay control circuit uses an interlock design. For the insulation test, I used a 500V megohmmeter; the standard value is >1MΩ, and the measured value was 2.3MΩ. For the trip troubleshooting, I used a sectional elimination method: first isolating the load and then testing the control circuit, and found that the intermediate relay contacts were stuck. These all match the online course content exactly.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_301.text: No problem, all of these are correct. Next I want to go deeper into PLC and inverter communication control. What suggestions do you have?

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: I recommend starting with the PROFINET bus protocol, and doing experiments with the S7-1200 and G120 frequency converters used today. Read the official manuals first, then wire and adjust parameters. You can use simulation software to test the logic during work breaks.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_301.text: Tonight I studied PLC soft components and scan cycles, but I feel a bit unclear. Can you explain it again using the example I installed?

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: Do you want me to explain in plain terms the definition and classification of soft components (such as auxiliary relays, timers, and counters), as well as the three stages of the scan cycle (input sampling, program execution, output refresh), and to illustrate them with examples?

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_301.text: Yes, especially the auxiliary relays and the scan order—I'm worried about making mistakes during the hands-on operation.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: Okay. Take the PLC you installed tonight as an example: among the soft devices, the auxiliary relay M is like a scratch note on the blackboard, the timer T is like a countdown timer, and the counter C is like a tally counter. The scan cycle is like a ladder diagram: first read the input terminal statuses (input sampling), then execute instructions from left to right and top to bottom in sequence (program execution), and finally update the outputs uniformly (output refresh). Note: within the same scan cycle, the output status changes only during the refresh stage; this is the key to avoiding race conditions.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_301.text: Got it, that explanation is much clearer! Thanks.

session_301.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_301.text: Very glad to be able to help you! During actual programming, you can use the programming software to monitor the scanning process. Feel free to communicate at any time if you have questions.

session_302.text: This evening I studied high-voltage safety regulations. Combined with the daytime operation of replacing the service entrance line in the Binya Low-Rent Housing Community, including powering off, testing for electricity, and attaching temporary grounding wires, I was wondering whether there is a better sequence for attaching grounding wires in the power distribution shafts of multi-story buildings.

session_302.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_302.text: You are concerned about the standard practice and safety of the connection sequence. Normally, for temporary grounding wires, connect the ground terminal first, then the conductor terminal; reverse the order when removing them. But in multi-story distribution shafts, the working space is limited. Did you encounter any specific difficulties, such as which floor to connect first or how to prevent the grounding wires from interfering with each other?

session_302.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_302.text: Yes, the electric distribution well is small in space. I'd like to know whether we can connect from the top floor downward layer by layer, so in case of accidental energization, would the current path be safer?

session_302.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_302.text: Theoretically, it is safer to attach from the bottom up: first attach the bottom grounding end, then work upward attaching the conductor ends layer by layer. This way, if any layer becomes unexpectedly energized, the grounding wire below has already formed a reliable short circuit. When removing, do it from top to bottom. I suggest you add this tip to your notes; it will also help with the certification exam.

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_303.text: In tonight's PLC class, I didn't fully understand the teacher's example of combining timers and counters to achieve a long delay. For instance, how does the timer cyclically trigger the counter, and how should the parameters be set to avoid errors? Can you help analyze it?

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_303.text: You're probably trying to implement an hour-level long delay by cascading multiple timers and counters, and you want to understand the logical details of the ladder diagram so that you can ask in-depth questions when you ask for guidance on the weekend, right?

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_303.text: Yes, that’s exactly what I mean. The logic details and parameter settings are unclear, especially the cyclic triggering mechanism.

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_303.text: Core idea: use timer T1 to generate a fixed cycle (e.g., 10 seconds). Each time T1 times out, its normally open contact triggers counter C1 to count once. When C1 counts to a preset value (e.g., 360), the total delay is 10 seconds x 360 = 3,600 seconds (1 hour). Parameter settings notes: the timer base value must be selected according to the PLC model (e.g., 0.1-second base), the counter preset value must not exceed its maximum (commonly 32,767 for 16-bit), and to prevent the counter from missing counts when the timer repeatedly triggers, a self-resetting timer ladder diagram can be used. Exams often test the calculation and programming of this kind of cascaded extended delay.

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_303.text: I see, so the timer resets itself and cyclically triggers the counter, and the product gives the total delay. But how does the timer self-reset in the ladder diagram? And what about counter overflow?

session_303.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_303.text: Timer self-reset: connect the timer's normally closed contact in series before the timer coil; when the time is up, the normally closed contact opens and the timer resets; at the same time, the normally open contact closes, causing the counter to count once. Counter overflow: if the total delay exceeds the counter's maximum count, you can cascade multiple stages--when the first-stage counter reaches its full count, it triggers the second-stage counter, and so on. Note that each counter's preset value must not exceed the limit, and the reset logic must be independent. I suggest you draw a ladder diagram and try it; asking Master Li with your questions on the weekend will be more efficient.

Given the high temperatures in Hainan, it is recommended to switch to cold-shrink joints to reduce the risk of uneven heat-shrinkage, and use a torque wrench during crimping to ensure consistency.

session_304.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_304.text: Yes, that's the retentive timer RTO. After a power interruption and re-energization, why is the timing value retained while a normal TON automatically clears? I want to understand the internal logic.

session_304.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_304.text: RTO uses non-volatile memory to store the current value, so the value is not lost after a power failure; TON relies on the scan cycle register and clears when power is off. A common application is monitoring cumulative equipment running time. Reset requires a dedicated reset coil (RES). You can test it with a motor start/stop case: use RTO to record total running hours.

session_305.text: I am looking at the ladder diagram. For the self-locking circuit of an intermediate relay, how does it logically ensure continuous output after a start signal?

session_305.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_305.text: Do you need to verify your understanding of the scan cycle of latching logic, or do you want to compare it with the physical latching of a relay?

session_305.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_305.text: Yes, I'm a bit fuzzy on the timing of the self-locking contact state update within the scan cycle. I'm afraid I won't be able to explain it clearly when I ask my mentor tomorrow.

session_305.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_305.text: The key to self-locking: after the output coil is energized, the corresponding normally open contact closes during the input refresh phase of the next scan cycle. Therefore, the start signal only needs one scan cycle, and then the output is maintained by the self-locking contact. It is recommended to run a single-step scan in simulation software to make it more intuitive. When you ask your master tomorrow, you can use this understanding to verify.

session_306.text: This morning I picked up an old mechanical electric meter and several high-voltage porcelain insulators at Haisheng Flea Market. I want to learn about their age, authenticity, and maintenance methods.

session_306.text: You want to confirm the specific year, manufacturer, and authenticity of these items, and learn how to scientifically prevent rust and dampness, so that you can use them as retro decorations in your studio in the future, right?

session_306.speaker: Lu Mingqiang
session_306.text: Yes, I usually like to collect old items, but I'm not sure how to preserve them long-term. I also want to know the market reference prices so I can discuss them with friends.

session_306.speaker: Lu Mingqiang's Assistant
session_306.text: Common brands of vintage mechanical electricity meters include Shanghai Huatong and Hangzhou Instrument Factory. The authenticity can be determined by inspecting the dial inscription and the internal copper coil. High-voltage porcelain insulators are mainly used for insulation support and should be kept away from acid and alkali corrosion. For cleaning, it is recommended to wipe with a soft cloth dipped in neutral detergent, then apply a thin layer of anti-rust oil after drying. Their collectible value depends on condition and rarity, generally ranging from tens to hundreds of yuan.

session_306.text: The imagery is so vivid! That pure joy and the light in the children's eyes are the warmest reward of life. Your full engagement throughout, the children will surely remember. This sense of accomplishment is more real than any award.
