session_245.text: I suggest doing it in three steps: 1) Practice 20 straight shots to the middle pocket over the long table every day with full focus, and use slow-motion video on your phone to calibrate your stroke; 2) For side-spin practice, start with low spin on the half table, controlling the cue ball to stop within a range of 3 balls; 3) One day before the match, simulate the match rhythm with a 90-second time limit per game to get used to the pressure in advance.

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_245.text: Got it. Tonight I'll first try the center pocket straight shot 20 times. When using side spin, I always have poor power control. Is there a more detailed mnemonic for power control?

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_245.text: For side-spin strength, refer to this: “Half-table: small, level stroke; full-table: medium strength; long-table: 70–80% strength.” The key is to keep the cue following through straight, with the wrist driving the forearm. When practicing, first fix a target point (such as the bottom pocket) and repeatedly try different strengths to build muscle memory.

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_245.text: I'm writing The Afternoon at Xiafeifang and just got to the part where the heroine listens to an old gentleman recount the history of cafés in the 1930s. What furnishings were common in the lane cafés on Avenue Joffre back then? How did the coffee beans get there?

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_245.text: Common items included French-style small round tables, brass coffee pots, and hand-crank coffee grinders; coffee beans were mostly imported from Java and Brazil and resold through foreign firms on the Bund. On both sides of Avenue Joffre were mostly Art Deco buildings, and gramophones in the alleys often played jazz. You can add these details to enhance the sense of realism.

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_245.text: The details are very practical! A reader guessed half of the protagonist's background correctly. I want the old gentleman's words to naturally lead into the follow-up, such as introducing a new character. Any suggestions?

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_245.text: Have the old gentleman recall a descendant of a former regular customer of the café and leave clues or keepsakes, which the heroine then follows to investigate. This both echoes history and drives the plot. Be careful to maintain the 1930s Shanghai dialect and dress style (such as long gowns and cheongsams), and avoid a modern tone.

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_245.text: The bar renovation budget is 20,000 yuan, and the first material payment of 13,000 yuan has been paid. How can we avoid going over budget and control construction quality?

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_245.text: It is recommended to strictly split the remaining budget into three parts: electrical and plumbing, panels, and labor, and reserve 10% as contingency. Before construction begins, confirm all milestones and the material list with the foreman in writing to avoid additional items later. Focus on the acceptance checks for embedded electrical and plumbing work and the routing of drainage pipes to ensure compliance.

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_245.text: Yes, water, electricity, and drainage are the key points. Also, during the renovation, how do we keep the shop running normally without affecting foot traffic and online orders?

session_245.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_245.text: It is recommended to set up temporary barriers around the bar area and post renovation notices, while preserving the coffee operation area. Online orders can be temporarily packaged using backup equipment. Communicate with the mall in advance about noisy periods to avoid complaints. Previewing the renovation progress on social media can actually attract customer attention.

session_247.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_247.text: After billiards training yesterday, my shoulders were sore and achy. I even skipped my morning run. I did 15 minutes of stretching, but it didn't help. Do you have any professional advice?

session_247.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_247.text: You first need to determine whether it’s muscle soreness or a strain. Do you feel a persistent dull pain or a sharp pain? Also, how many times a week do you usually play billiards? Does your job require long periods of time at the computer?

session_247.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_247.text: It should be muscle soreness, a persistent dull ache. I play billiards three times a week, and during the day I run the store, standing for long periods and using the computer. I'm worried it might affect my future training.

session_247.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_247.text: Recommendations: 1. Apply cold compresses during the acute phase (within 24 hours), then switch to heat compresses; 2. Billiards-specific stretches: shoulder circles, forearm flexion and extension, neck lateral flexion; 3. Do brief shoulder-and-neck exercises every hour during work breaks; 4. You may also use a massage gun on a low setting to relax the shoulder muscles; 5. If it doesn't improve after 3 days or if movement becomes restricted, see a doctor. In addition, tomorrow you can replace running with low-intensity exercise such as walking in a pool.

session_248.text: I just bought a pour-over coffee set today, including a V60 dripper, a pour-over kettle, and Ethiopian sun-dried beans. The first time I brewed it for my friend, he said it was good, but I think it could be better. Can you give me some tips on pour-over technique?

session_248.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_248.text: Awesome! The Ethiopian natural-process coffee has a bright flavor. Which step do you mainly want to optimize—water temperature, grind size, or pouring technique?

session_248.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_248.text: It's mainly the pouring technique. The clerk said to circle steadily and keep the water flow even, but when I practiced, the flow seemed to vary in strength. And how do you control the blooming time?

session_248.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_248.text: Tip: when blooming, use water twice the weight of the beans (e.g., pour 30 g of water for 15 g of beans), and wait 30 seconds to degas. For the main pour, use a small, slow stream and circle gently, keeping the pour within a coin-sized area and avoiding the edge of the filter paper. A total time of around 2 minutes 30 seconds works best.

session_248.text: Kenyan beans have bright acidity and are suitable for a medium-light roast. Pair them with a cake dripper or V60, and pour the water a little faster (finish within 2 minutes) to bring out the unique flavors of tomato and blackcurrant.

session_249.text: What you need is mechanical correction training for your center-of-gravity shift (for example, using markers to fix your stance), as well as a systematic practice plan for jump shots and curveballs?

session_249.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_249.text: I suggest that next time you practice, first do 10 minutes of center-of-gravity correction with empty cue strokes (put positioning tape on the floor), then practice the jump shot in three steps: 1. high cue, contact point slightly above center; 2. use wrist strength rather than arm; 3. precise cue ball landing. For curve shots, start with low-to-medium spin and gradually increase the sidespin angle. I'll push a few targeted training clips from professional players in the library.

session_259.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_259.text: In the Republic of China era, tailor shops usually had the storefront in front and the workshop behind. Bolts of fabric and account books were placed on the front counter, and a corner could be set up with a small round table, two rattan chairs, and coffee ware. The sewing machine was placed near the window for natural light, and sample garments hung on the wall. In this way, the female lead works at the sewing machine while the writer sits at the small table drinking coffee; their gazes intersect naturally, creating an opportunity for dialogue. For authenticity, one can refer to the shop of the Sun family, the 'old tailors' of Shanghai (1930s), who often had customers who had studied abroad and brought coffee culture with them.

session_270.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_270.text: This afternoon, in the Round of 32 decisive match of the Pujiang Cup, my right hand trembled slightly when I hit the 8-ball. The cue ball lost control and dropped into a pocket, and I lost narrowly 6:7. My friend said my hand bridge was unstable, my center of gravity was off to the right, and my core strength was insufficient, but I feel psychological pressure is the key. Could you help me systematically analyze the reasons, and how to adjust my mentality and improve my technique?

session_270.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_270.text: The problem you're experiencing is very typical: under pressure, muscle tremors often stem from decreased core stability caused by adrenaline secretion, which in turn affects your bridge hand and stroke. The three points Han Dong observed are very accurate—an unstable bridge hand is the surface manifestation, while a right-shifted center of gravity and insufficient core strength are the root causes. I suggest starting with breath control: before every shot, take one deep breath (inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds, exhale for 4 seconds) to activate the transversus abdominis and stabilize your trunk. For training, you can add planks (3 sets per day, 45 seconds each) and one-legged standing stroke practice to strengthen balance. The relevant videos you saved can be used alongside the practice, with a focus on a fixed position-play routine for the 8-ball to reduce decision-making pressure.

session_270.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_270.text: I've noted down the deep breathing and core training. Also, in the last few shots of the deciding game, I actually felt my line judgment was fine; I was just too tense when making the shot. Are there any specific methods for handling pressure? For example, how should I prepare in advance for the next competition?

session_270.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_270.text: Psychologically, you can establish a pre-match routine: 10 minutes before the match, take 3 long breaths plus 7 positive self-suggestions (e.g., 'I've practiced this kind of shot thousands of times'). During key shots in the deciding frame, force yourself to shift attention from 'result' to 'process' — only think about bridge hand position and cue stroke rhythm. In daily practice, simulate high-pressure situations: when playing a tied match with a friend, deliberately let the opponent reach match point first, and force yourself to clear the table under that pressure. Also, it is recommended not to do high-intensity practice the day before the next match, allowing your nerves and muscles to fully recover.

session_270.text: You mainly want to learn how to seamlessly transform the emotional ups and downs and specific details of your personal competition experience into the protagonist's experience, while sustaining the readers' current resonance, and you also want to optimize your daily writing rhythm?

session_270.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_270.text: You can try the technique of 'sensory trigger + inner monologue': use specific body language (such as trembling fingers of a clenched fist, rapid breathing) instead of directly describing winning or losing, and then externalize your complex emotions when observing Liu Zihao (admiration, unwillingness to admit defeat, reflection) through the protagonist's what they see and think, so readers will automatically empathize. Your writing today already has a strong visual quality. If you keep using this 'one event, one feeling' approach to record daily life, your writing process will go more smoothly.

session_287.text: After running, I have soreness and swelling on the outside of my right knee. I looked it up and it might be iliotibial band friction syndrome, and it's affecting my self-driving trip plan to western Sichuan. How should I handle it?

session_287.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_287.text: You are currently in the acute phase, likely caused by excessive friction of the iliotibial band. I suggest stopping running for now, applying ice, and massaging to relax the tensor fasciae latae and the iliotibial band, while avoiding downhill sections and prolonged knee-flexion movements.

session_287.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_287.text: I've already done the ice therapy, but I still want to maintain my exercise habit. Can I switch to swimming or upper-body strength training?

session_287.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_287.text: Yes, swimming (freestyle, backstroke) and upper body strength training have no impact on the knees and are suitable for the recovery period; adding gluteus medius and core strengthening exercises can reduce iliotibial band pressure. It is recommended to rest for 3-7 days during the acute phase, then gradually resume low-intensity exercises such as cycling.

session_287.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_287.text: How long will it take to recover so it won't affect my western Sichuan hike next month? Do I need to see a physical therapist?

session_287.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_287.text: Mild iliotibial band syndrome usually improves within 2–4 weeks. If the pain is significant or lasts more than 1 week, it is recommended to see a sports medicine department or physical therapist as soon as possible for manual release and movement pattern correction. Before the Western Sichuan road trip, focus on gluteal muscle training and gait adjustment to reduce the risk of recurrence.

session_289.text: After I run 5 km, I usually apply an ice pack to my right knee and stretch for 10 minutes. Is this an effective way to take care of my knees?

session_289.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_289.text: Ice packs and stretching are the right acute recovery methods and can effectively relieve inflammation. It is recommended to keep icing to within 15 minutes, and after stretching, add exercises such as wall sits to strengthen the muscles around the knees and prevent injury. Also, your weight is a bit high (BMI 27.04), so when running you should progress gradually, increasing distance and frequency step by step.

session_289.speaker: Lei Mingxuan

session_289.text: The current frequency and intensity are reasonable, but it is recommended to maintain this for 1-2 months before considering an increase. You can increase weekly mileage by 10% every two weeks, while also doing low-impact exercises such as swimming or cycling to reduce pressure on the knees. Replace running shoes every 500 kilometers, and increase protein and calcium intake in your diet to build up stamina for the western Sichuan self-driving trip.

session_290.text: I just met a Hangzhou designer, Chen Xiao. She makes clothes with plant dyes and they're very distinctive. I want to add elements that combine plant dyeing with techwear style to my clothing store's products, but I don't know about the techniques, fabric selection, or cost control. Can you help me analyze the feasibility?

session_290.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_290.text: You need to understand the basic techniques of plant dyeing (such as indigo, madder and other dyes), fabric pretreatment, colorfastness testing, and the practicality of integrating with functional-style design, as well as the cost of small-batch customization. In addition, do you also need to consider how to connect with existing supply chain resources?

session_290.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_290.text: Yes, especially durability and cleaning/maintenance methods, and also how to find a factory for small-batch sampling, and roughly what the cost would be?

session_290.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_290.text: For plant-dyed functional wear, cotton-linen blends or organic cotton fabrics are recommended. Using alum or iron mordant can improve color fastness. When washing, use a neutral detergent and avoid prolonged sun exposure. For small-batch sampling, you can contact plant-dye workshops in Hangzhou or Shaoxing. For the first order of 500 pieces or fewer, the cost is about 30% higher than ordinary dyeing, but limited editions offer more room for premium pricing. You can sign a preliminary cooperation framework with Chen Xiao and first make a few samples to assess market reaction.

session_292.text: I just talked with my college classmate Zhao Min at a wedding banquet about a collaboration on an 'urban techwear × convention pop-up' and jotted down the general framework. I'd like to hear your suggestions to flesh out the plan.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Do you need to refine the plan from the perspectives of theme naming, visual presentation, and co-branded product design, and first determine the key points for the next discussion with Zhao Min?

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_292.text: Yes, especially the target customer group, the feasibility of launching before the Spring Festival, and how to estimate the budget.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Suggested the theme be 'Urban Crossing · Functional Expo,' targeting office commuters and light outdoor sports enthusiasts aged 25–35. The venue should be the mall atrium or an outdoor plaza, with a static exhibition plus interactive experiences (e.g., a loaded-walking test). For the collaboration, Shanghai landmark elements could be included (such as a Bund skyline print). The budget is divided into four parts: venue rental, construction, materials, and promotion; start with an initial range of 50,000–80,000 yuan.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_292.text: This direction is very clear. How about scheduling the exhibition for the week before the Spring Festival? I'll handle product supply and store coordination, and Zhao Min will take care of planning.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: The week before Spring Festival is a golden window, especially combined with the New Year shopping festival traffic. I suggest you first confirm the venue availability and the sampling lead time for the co-branded collection with Zhao Min next week, then refine the task breakdown.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_292.text: Today I drove round trip between Shanghai and Hangzhou, five hours in total. After getting home, I did 15 minutes of stretching, but my lower back is still sore and achy. Is there a more effective way to relieve it?

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Is the soreness mainly in your lower back or your neck and shoulders? Also, you usually exercise, but your weight is on the higher side, and long periods of driving put a lot of strain on your lumbar spine. Would you like targeted lower back stretches and daily prevention advice?

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_292.text: Mainly lower back soreness; neck and shoulders are okay. Yes, I'd like to know specific stretching exercises and how to prevent it while driving.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Two exercises are recommended: cat-cow stretch (on all fours, alternate arching and dipping the back 10 times each) and supine spinal twist (lie on your back with knees bent, let your legs fall to one side, hold for 30 seconds on each side). While driving, stop at a service area every 1–2 hours to rest, and do shoulder shrugs and standing side bends; in daily life, strengthen your core with exercises like the plank. Tonight you can use a heat pack or foam roller to relax your lower back.

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_292.text: OK, I'll try the cat stretch. Also, what are the key points for seat adjustment?

session_292.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_292.text: Adjust the seat so your knees are slightly bent and lower than your hips; let the lumbar support support the natural curve of your lower back; set the steering wheel height so your arms can bend naturally. Every 45 minutes, fine-tune your sitting posture or do some gentle lower-back movements.

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_293.text: I received a street-scene illustration painted by my friend Chen Yu. I want to turn elements like the alleyways and plane trees into hoodie prints or co-branded T-shirts, but I've never done this type of co-branded product, so I need to understand the complete process from illustration to physical product and the copyright collaboration model.

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: As a clothing store owner, what you need is comprehensive advice spanning the entire process, from design conversion, craft matching, and cost budgeting to copyright contracts, to ensure the co-branded collaboration moves forward smoothly, right?

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_293.text: Right, we also need to consider fabric selection, pre-sale timing, and how to promote online and offline.

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: It is recommended to proceed in five steps: 1) Break the illustration into partial elements suitable for hoodie printing, control colors to ≤4 colors, and use screen printing or direct-to-garment digital printing; 2) Choose 280g pure cotton terry cloth for the hoodies, with a cost of about 60 yuan per piece and a price that can be raised to 199-299 yuan; 3) Use a licensing model for the copyright, with a royalty of 10%-15% of sales and a one-year licensing period; 4) Do online warm-up on Xiaohongshu plus a limited numbered release, and set up themed displays in offline stores; 5) The cycle is 2 weeks for design, 1 week for sampling, and 3 weeks for production, 6 weeks in total. It is recommended to start with a small trial batch of 100 pieces.

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_293.text: Just received knee pads and ankle protectors from my father. He prepared them to support my Western Sichuan self-driving trip. I want to plan it carefully, but I don't know much about the route, season, and equipment yet. Can you help me sort it out?

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: You plan to do an in-depth tour of western Sichuan within six months (April to October), and the key things you need are route selection, altitude sickness prevention, and a gear list, right? For example, Daocheng Yading or the small western Sichuan loop — would you like me to compare and recommend?

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_293.text: Yes, mainly I want to compare the Western Sichuan Small Loop and the Daocheng Yading route, and also consider whether the vehicle has to be off-road capable, and what equipment is needed besides protective gear.

session_293.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_293.text: Recommended classic loop: Chengdu - Siguniang Mountain - Danba - Seda - Kangding, 7-9 days, with altitude rising gradually. A sedan is feasible, but an SUV is recommended for rough roads. Essential gear: hardshell jacket, hiking shoes, oxygen canister, Rhodiola, sunscreen; take altitude sickness medication 1 week in advance. If you go the Daocheng route, you need 2 more days and a more capable vehicle.

session_310.text: I just bought a full set of camping gear at Decathlon and I'm going camping with friends at the end of the month. Are there any essential tips and precautions for beginners? Especially for gas stoves and inflatable sleeping pads.

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_310.text: This is your first time using a remote canister gas stove and an inflatable sleeping pad, right? In late November, Shanghai nights can fall below 10°C, so you need to pay attention to the stove's combustion efficiency at low temperatures, as well as the sleeping pad's warmth and packing details. It is recommended that you practice setting it up and packing it away at home first.

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_310.text: Yes, I'm just worried that the gas stove won't work well in cold weather, and how to pack the inflatable sleeping pad so it doesn't take up space. Is the tent reliable in the rain?

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_310.text: At low temperatures, for a gas stove it is recommended to first use a preheat tube (if available) and shield it from the wind; for the inflatable sleeping pad, first roll and press out the air, then fold in half and roll tightly to expel the remaining air. The tent you bought is a blue two-person tent; most Decathlon models have decent rain resistance, but remember to bring a ground sheet and guy lines, and make sure the inner and outer tents are separated.

session_310.text: Recently my right shoulder has been sore, and I can't get up to run in the morning. Do you have any quick ways to relieve it?

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_310.text: You want to relieve shoulder soreness without affecting your daily work (such as sketching and moving goods) and outdoor activities (camping), while also adjusting your morning run schedule? It is recommended to apply a hot compress for 15 minutes first, and try simple shoulder stretches, such as pendulum swings and wall crawls.

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_310.text: Right, my shoulder was even stiffer while drawing the sketch today, and I've already missed my morning run twice this week. Can you give me an adjusted exercise plan?

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_310.text: Pause high-intensity running this week; instead do 15 minutes of shoulder recovery training every day (e.g., YTWL exercises + resistance band external rotation). Gradually resume morning running next week at half intensity. During work breaks, remember to stand up and move your shoulders every 45 minutes to avoid staying in a fixed posture for too long. If the soreness lasts more than a week, consider seeing a doctor.

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_310.text: How exactly do you do YTWL? When I usually draw sketches, the table is a bit low. Should I adjust that too?

session_310.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_310.text: YTWL is a set of four classic shoulder activation movements: Y (raise both arms overhead to form a Y), T (raise both arms to the sides), W (bend elbows and squeeze shoulder blades together), and L (bend elbows with external rotation). Do 10 reps per movement, 2-3 sets per day. When drawing sketches, it's recommended to adjust the chair height so your elbows are naturally at 90 degrees and the screen or paper is parallel to your line of sight, reducing shoulder shrugging. You can try putting a pillow on the chair to raise it first.

session_313.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_313.text: You clearly did two rounds of high-intensity exercise. The back of your thighs (hamstrings) and the outside of your thighs (iliotibial band) are the main tight areas. You want a more complete recovery plan than a foam roller, including time sequence, auxiliary methods, and criteria for judging tomorrow's exercise risk — right?

session_313.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_313.text: Right, especially how to tell the difference between muscle soreness and a strain, and whether I should ice it again tonight?

session_313.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_313.text: Suggestion: Tonight, apply ice for 20 minutes first to relieve acute inflammation, and before bed do 10 minutes of gentle hamstring and iliotibial band stretching. To distinguish pain: symmetrical soreness that is relieved by pressing is normal muscle soreness; unilateral severe pain, worse with pressing, or restricted movement suggests a strain and requires stopping training. If the soreness is below 3 out of 10 tomorrow, you can do low-intensity aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking, to promote recovery; otherwise rest. session_317.text: Tomorrow I'm going to SPD Bank to apply for a business loan, using my father's old house as collateral. What is the specific process and what should I watch out for?

session_317.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_317.text: Tomorrow morning bring all required documents: business license, bank statements, lease agreement, credit report, original and photocopy of the property ownership certificate, your dad's ID card, and certificate of single status. The collateral appraisal will take an extra 2-3 days, with an appraisal fee of about 0.3%. The interest rate can be negotiated at around 3.8%. Also prepare a backup plan: if rejected, switch to a tax-based loan or a consumer loan, which has a slightly higher interest rate but gets approved faster.

session_317.text: Suggestions: 1) Sitting posture: adjust the chair until your thighs are parallel to the floor, the top of the screen is at eye level, and your elbows are at 90 degrees. 2) Every 45 minutes, do 1 minute of neck lateral flexion and rotation stretches. 3) For yoga, add wall angels or cat-cow pose, 3-4 times a week. 4) Tools: a cervical pillow can ease pressure during sleep; a massage gun can relax shoulder muscles, but avoid using it on the cervical spine. If you experience numbness in your hands or persistent pain, it is recommended to get imaging done.

session_339.text: The 24–48 hours after surgery are critical. It is recommended to apply the compress for 20 minutes at a time, with 10-minute breaks in between. Stick mainly to warm or cool liquid foods, such as porridge, rice water, and yogurt, and avoid hot and irritating food. Bone broth is fine, but don't let it be too hot.

session_339.text: Okay, so can I eat normally tomorrow? When can I run? And how do I tell if the wound is infected?

session_339.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_339.text: Wait at least 72 hours before eating normally, starting with a semi-liquid diet first. Pause running and other exercise for 5-7 days to avoid blood pressure fluctuations affecting the wound. Watch for signs of infection: worsening pain after 48 hours, fever, pus or foul odor—contact your doctor immediately.

session_339.text: The classic small loop in western Sichuan takes about 5–7 days and is suitable for first-time exploration; the Daocheng Yading route takes 8–10 days, with magnificent scenery but higher altitude. session_340.text: It's been four days since I had my wisdom tooth pulled. My cheek is still swollen and it hurt a bit this morning. There's a hotpot gathering tomorrow night—can I go? What should I watch out for?

session_340.text: On the fourth day after surgery, swelling and pain are normal and usually subside in 5-7 days. Continue ice compresses, and the day after tomorrow you can switch to hot compresses. Hot pot gatherings are advised against, because spicy and hot food can irritate the wound and increase the risk of bleeding and infection. If you really must go, you can only eat soft cooked vegetables and tofu from the clear broth pot; you cannot eat hard, spicy, or hot food.

session_340.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_340.text: Can I still take the painkillers? I'm still taking the anti-inflammatory and pain medication the doctor prescribed every day. How many steps should I aim for when walking for exercise tomorrow?

session_340.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_340.text: Take painkillers as prescribed; do not exceed the dose. You may reduce the dose if pain lessens. For exercise, avoid strenuous activity for one week after surgery. Daily walking of no more than 5,000 steps is fine, to promote blood circulation without overexertion. High-intensity exercise should wait until the doctor confirms at the two-week follow-up.

session_340.text: What you care about is safely attending the gathering during post-surgery recovery while not spoiling the fun. I need to confirm a few details: are you currently only able to eat liquid or soft food? How much hotpot can you eat?

My father suggests staying at the current location, but I still can't make up my mind and would like to hear your professional analysis.

session_344.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_344.text: Your core conflict right now is cost savings vs. foot-traffic risk. Although the corner space has 30% lower rent, it is near the restroom and foot traffic may drop; the original location has a 15% rent increase but an established location, though the surrounding area will be converted to restaurants. I need more data to calculate for you: your store's current average daily foot traffic, average spend per customer, and how much the restaurant construction during the renovation of the original location will disrupt business.

session_344.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_344.text: Average daily foot traffic is about 200 people, with an average transaction value of 180 yuan. The restaurant construction next to the original location is expected to bring noise and dust for 2 months. I'm worried that the corner unit is too out-of-the-way and regular customers will be lost.

session_344.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_344.text: Based on the data: renewing the lease at the original location for 2 years, a 15% rent increase means paying about 4,500 yuan more per month (assuming current rent is 30,000 yuan), but if the store is closed during the renovation period, the loss is about 72,000 yuan (2 months of revenue). A corner storefront would save 30% on rent, i.e. 9,000 yuan per month, but foot traffic could drop by more than 30%, losing over 200,000 yuan a year. Recommendation: first negotiate with the property management to try to get a rent reduction or half off during the renovation at the original location, and also ask for a longer rent-free period or renovation subsidy for the corner storefront. If an agreement cannot be reached, staying at the original location is more prudent for long-term brand maintenance.

session_344.text: Prepare data: show your rent contribution and customer traffic figures from the past 2 years, and emphasize how the current location drives overall foot traffic for the mall. Propose a compromise: renew the lease at the original location but ask for 3 months of rent exemption during the renovation period, or take a new unit with 6 months of rent-free period and partial decoration costs covered. If the other party insists, you can hint at considering other malls to strengthen your bargaining position.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: Just received a 50,000 yuan investment from my father and want to upgrade the brand collection store. I have a preliminary plan, but I'm not sure where the safest place to start is.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: You want systematic advice from planning to implementation, including designer selection, supplier price comparison, budget allocation, and time management?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: Yes, I especially want to avoid pitfalls, such as how to screen local designers and shelf suppliers, and how to handle scheduling conflicts with the joint promotion with Wednesday Publishing House.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: Recommend a three-step approach: 1) Use 10,000 yuan to hire an independent designer or small studio, requiring past cases and 3D renderings; 2) For shelf suppliers, prioritize those on 1688 with a rating above 4.8 that support sample trial orders, and keep the budget within 15,000 yuan; 3) Stagger the timeline: finalize the design draft before this Friday, finalize the co-branding details with the publisher next week, and avoid advancing both on Monday. Keep the remaining 25,000 yuan as startup capital and for emergencies.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: I just read the chapter on location value in 'Houses in the City'. I'd like to learn about the possibilities and suggestions for buying a home in the core areas of Pudong (such as Lujiazui and Century Avenue). Could you help me analyze it?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: You mentioned a prime location in Pudong, which suggests you care more about the balance between investment value and living in it yourself. Can you tell me your current housing budget or down payment range, and whether you have additional needs such as school districts?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: My annual income is 150,000 yuan. The family has 3 properties, but I live with my parents, and I have some fund investments. I hope to keep the down payment within 2,000,000 yuan. The main goal is self-use plus value preservation; school district doesn't need to be considered for now.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: Understood. In core areas of Pudong such as Lujiazui, the average price of second-hand homes is about 100,000-150,000 yuan per square meter, and around Century Avenue it's 80,000-120,000 yuan per square meter. With a down payment of 2 million yuan, for a total price of about 6-7 million yuan, you could consider a small unit (50-70 square meters) or a newer second-hand home in the Huamu area. Also, Shanghai has purchase restrictions. Since you already own a property in your name, you need to confirm your purchase eligibility (single/married?).

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: I'm single, with no property under my name (the properties are all under my parents' names), so I should qualify as a first-time home buyer, right? I don't want the monthly mortgage payment to exceed 40% of my income, around 6000 yuan. What price range can I afford?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: You qualify for first-time home buyer status, with a 35% down payment. A monthly payment of 6,000 yuan corresponds to a loan of about 1.4 million yuan (30-year term, 4.2% interest rate). Adding the 2 million yuan down payment, the total budget is 3.4 million yuan. You can look at 40–50 sqm nearly new second-hand homes in Huamu or Beicai with unit prices of 60,000–80,000 yuan per sqm. I suggest prioritizing comparison of price increases by area and using your fund returns for long-term planning.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: Tonight I finally persuaded my father to invest 50,000 yuan. With my mother's previous 20,000 yuan, the funds for the brand upgrade are basically complete! The class group chat went wild, and everyone was congratulating me. I feel a strong sense of accomplishment, but also a bit of pressure.

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: I can feel your excitement and fighting spirit! The support from family and classmates is a great starting point. Is your current pressure mainly from a sense of responsibility for the follow-up execution? For example, how to balance your energy between the daily store operations and the upgrade project?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_356.text: Right, I'm just worried about not being able to manage both. After all, the upgrade will take a lot of time, and I still have to keep an eye on the store. Do you have any suggestions?

session_356.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_356.text: My suggestion is to standardize daily operations—for example, train staff to take on basic management and set a fixed weekly review time. Upgrade projects can be promoted in phases, starting with supply chain and brand visual identity, prioritizing the areas that show results quickly. Also, regularly keep your family updated on progress, and pressure can be turned into motivation.

session_357.text: Tomorrow afternoon I'm meeting with Teacher Chen from the publishing house to discuss my novel The Afternoon of Xiafei Lane. session_357.text: First help me refine the core selling points and the topic's appeal, then give some suggestions on publishers' preferences.

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_357.text: Okay. Your novel is set in an old Shanghai longtang and focuses on nostalgia and the changes of the times. I suggest highlighting three selling points: 1) regional uniqueness—the restoration of historical details in Xiafeifang; 2) emotional resonance—urban memories from an ordinary person's perspective; 3) market scarcity—local-themed works have been popular with readers in recent years. Prepare a three-minute synopsis that emphasizes that personal fate is interwoven with spatial change. Also, publishers currently prefer works with cultural depth and the potential to spark conversation, so you could sort out in advance the differentiated advantages of similar books. Do you need me to help you write the synopsis or polish the outline?

session_357.text: I need to organize the to-do lists for the renovation upgrade and the co-branded hoodie project, and confirm key milestones and potential risks.

session_357.text: What you mainly need to clarify: the deadline for submitting the renovation renderings (already asked the property management), the mall's construction regulations (such as nighttime construction restrictions), and the embroidery sampling cycle for the co-branded hoodie. It is suggested to first list the milestones: renderings deadline, construction permit processing, and hoodie sample confirmation date.

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_357.text: Suggestions: 1) Confirm the site survey time with the designer tomorrow and communicate the rendering review requirements; 2) Contact supplier Zhou Tao to confirm the sample garment patterning timeline and quotation to ensure it stays within budget; 3) Confirm construction time restrictions with the property management (e.g., whether it's nighttime only) to avoid fines. I'll generate a Gantt chart to help you track.

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_357.text: Today was my first time doing squats and deadlifts. Now my hamstrings and glutes are sore and a bit shaky. How should I take the muscle-building protein powder I just bought? Before or after training?

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_357.text: It is recommended to drink it within 30 minutes after training; pairing it with carbohydrates (such as a banana) works better. Take once a day, mixed with warm water or milk. After training, do static stretching and use a foam roller to relax the back of the thighs and the buttocks. Tonight you can apply a cold compress to relieve soreness, and tomorrow morning use a hot compress. If the soreness is obvious tomorrow, you can rest for a day and don't force yourself to train.

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_357.text: Can I still do other training tomorrow? Like upper body? Also, how exactly do I do the stretching? Can you teach me?

session_357.speaker: Lei Mingxuan's Assistant
session_357.text: Tomorrow you can do upper-body training, but it is recommended to fully stretch your hamstrings and glutes first (e.g., seated forward bend, supine knee-to-chest), holding each stretch for 30 seconds; roll your hamstrings and glutes with a foam roller for 2 minutes each. If the soreness severely affects your movements, just rest completely. Remember: muscle soreness is a normal reaction, and a full warm-up before the next workout can ease it.

session_358.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_358.text: I just finished my second personal training session tonight. I did box jumps, medicine ball slams, and kettlebell work, then ran for 25 minutes. session_358.text: You're in the recovery period after high-intensity training, so you need to replenish protein and carbs immediately (the golden window), and also do static stretching and foam roller relaxation. I recommend adjusting your diet, reducing high-calorie foods like braised pork, and increasing chicken breast, fish, and shrimp.

session_358.speaker: Lei Mingxuan
session_358.text: I usually enjoy Shanghai-style braised pork, but I'm afraid it will interfere with fat loss. Is there a way to satisfy my taste without disrupting my diet control?

session_358.text: You can try an improved version: use lean meat instead of pork belly, less sugar and oil, and pair it with plenty of vegetables; also control portions and have it once or twice a week as a reward meal. For the meal after training, prioritize protein and complex carbs.

session_358.text: Tonight I read Houses in the City. The space renovation cases in the book gave me a lot of inspiration. I jotted down some ideas and want to talk with you about how to apply them to the store renovation.

session_4.text: I bought a piece of indigo print fabric and want to make it into coasters. Could you tell me what materials I need, what size to cut, and how to sew? It would be best if it's suitable for beginners.

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_4.text: Do you want to use blue calico to make practical heat-insulating, burn-proof coasters, while also hoping to match suitable backing fabric and batting, and add some simple embroidery as decoration?

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_4.text: Recommended size: 10cm × 10cm. Needed: indigo printed cloth (outer fabric), plain backing fabric, batting (or an old towel as substitute), and bias binding tape. Steps: cut three pieces of fabric → stack and baste to secure → sew three sides with hidden stitches → turn right side out and sew the fourth side → optionally embroider small daisies or plum blossoms on the surface. Care: hand wash and dry in the shade. Fabric scraps from home are perfectly usable.

session_4.text: I only have a junior high school education. When tutoring my fourth-grade son Ma Mingzhe in math word problems, I often can’t explain things clearly, such as multi-digit multiplication and division. Are there any simple and easy-to-understand teaching methods?

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_4.text: You want to tutor with examples and steps that the child can understand, while also avoiding teaching conflicts, right? For instance, turning word problems into real-life scenarios and guiding the thinking step by step.

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_4.text: Yes! Whenever he meets a problem, he says he can't do it. I'm also afraid of explaining it wrong and have no idea whether he really understands.

session_4.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_4.text: You can try a three-step method: 1) Turn the problem into a story with objects or drawings, for example, 'A box has 24 apples; how many are in 12 boxes?' Use building blocks to set it up; 2) Have him circle the key numbers and read the problem three times; 3) After explaining, have him restate the logic, and give a similar problem to check whether he truly understands.

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_6.text: Today I went to Tianjin Rural Commercial Bank to ask about education savings. The annual interest rate is 1.75%, with a minimum monthly deposit of 100 yuan and a maximum of 50,000 yuan. But I'm not sure whether this rate is better than a fixed deposit. I want to open an account tomorrow. What materials do I need to bring?

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_6.text: The annual interest rate of 1.75% on the education savings you mentioned is usually higher than that of regular fixed deposits of the same term (about 1.5%), and the interest is tax-free, making it a better option for children's education savings. To open an account tomorrow, you need to bring your own ID card, household registration booklet, and the child's (student's) household registration booklet or ID card, and go to the bank counter to handle it.

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_6.text: Then if the family needs money urgently later, can I withdraw it early? How is the interest calculated? Also, I heard other banks offer deposits with higher interest rates. Is that a scam?

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_6.text: For education savings, if you withdraw before maturity and provide a school certificate (such as an admission notice for non-compulsory education), you can continue to enjoy the preferential interest rate; otherwise, the interest will be calculated as for early withdrawal of an ordinary time deposit, and you will lose part of the interest. As for high-interest products at other banks, be wary of whether they are wealth-management products or insurance; it is recommended to verify whether they are legitimate deposits covered by deposit insurance. When you open the account tomorrow, you can ask the teller to explain the withdrawal rules in detail.

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_6.text: This afternoon I focused on practicing daisy petals. I slowed down to work on the curves, but the embroidery still doesn't look three-dimensional enough. I can't remember some details of the long-and-short stitch technique that Sister Zhou Xiuqin taught, such as the angle of the stitches and how to tie off the thread. Also, do you think, at my current level, I can take on small jobs like embroidering handkerchiefs and tea coasters? Do you have any economical embroidery thread recommendations?

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_6.text: The key to the three-dimensional effect lies in the arrangement of long and short stitches: from the flower center outward, the outer stitches are longer than the inner ones, with a slight tilt (about 15 degrees), and each stitch hugs the root of the previous stitch. When finishing off, hide the thread at the base of the petal to avoid exposed thread ends. For embroidery thread, domestic cotton thread (such as DMC substitute brands) is recommended; it offers good value for money. The details of your work are already fairly neat. You can test the waters by taking simple tea coaster orders from relatives, friends, or community craft markets, and simply use your phone to take a side-angle photo in natural light to show the three-dimensional effect.

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_6.text: My daughter Yuxin has a slight stuffy nose today. She's in good spirits otherwise, but I'm worried it might get worse if we don't deal with it. Are there any home care methods to help relieve it?

session_6.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_6.text: I understand your concern. Common methods for children's nasal congestion: 1. Apply a warm towel to the nose (mind the temperature); 2. Use saline spray or drops for the nose (you can make your own: 1 cup warm water + 1/4 teaspoon salt); 3. Elevate the head when sleeping or use a humidifier; 4. A safe food-based remedy is scallion white water (2 sections of scallion white, boiled in water for 5 minutes). Avoid adult cold medicine. If fever, rapid breathing, or persistent crying occurs, it is recommended to go to a community clinic.

session_8.text: I spend long hours every day with my head down doing embroidery, and my neck often feels sore and achy. What are some daily methods to relieve it?

session_8.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_8.text: It is recommended to do neck stretches every 30 minutes: slowly lower and raise your head for 5 seconds each, and turn your head left and right for 5 seconds each. session_11.text: You want to ensure the quality of the bibs meets customer requirements and reduce rework, right? Let me help you sort out the key points: bib size, choice of overlock stitch, pre-shrinking treatment of the fabric, and delivery schedule planning.

session_11.text: It is recommended to use a tight overlock stitch, such as zigzag or edge-binding stitch, to prevent threads from coming loose. For 10 bibs, I suggest spreading them over 3-4 days, making 2-3 each day to ensure quality.

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_12.text: Tomorrow I need to sew 10 bibs. The fabric is already cut, but I haven't done this in years, so I'm a bit scared. Can you tell me the specific steps and what to pay attention to?

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_12.text: First, check the sewing machine: thread it, adjust the tension (medium), and test-sew on scrap fabric. Standard steps: 1) Sew three sides of the pocket piece, leaving the top open; 2) Attach the pocket piece to the front of the main fabric; 3) Sew around the main fabric and leave a turning opening; 4) Turn it right side out, topstitch, and finish the edges. For batch work, you can overlock the edges first and then sew; working in groups of 5 is faster.

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_12.text: Thanks! My sewing machine is an old model, and the bib fabric tends to slip. Any anti-slip tricks?

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_12.text: Place a piece of thin paper or plastic wrap under the sewing machine presser foot and tear it off after sewing; or use pearl pins to fix the four corners of the pocket fabric, and slightly pull the lower layer of fabric tight while sewing. Also remember to sew two test pieces first to get the feel, then do the batch.

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant

session_12.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_12.text: Your family is truly happy! This photo album not only records the past, but also embodies the love of the whole family at present. Every time you look through it in the future, you will remember today's joy. I believe you will have many more wonderful family moments like this.

session_14.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_14.text: The doctor said I have a neck muscle strain. Today I had physical therapy and applied a medicated plaster, and I plan to go again tomorrow. But I usually have to do housework and take care of three children, so I'm afraid it will recur. Besides these, are there any other rehabilitation methods and preventive measures?

session_14.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_14.text: Recommendations: 1) Apply a hot compress to the neck for 15 minutes per session to relieve stiffness; 2) avoid turning your head suddenly or keeping your head down for too long; when doing housework, try raising the work surface; 3) choose a buckwheat pillow or memory foam pillow that supports the neck curve; 4) after the pain subsides, do gentle “chin tuck” exercises, not “mi” character exercises; 5) reduce head-down activities such as hand embroidery during physical therapy. If you still feel significant discomfort after a week, have a follow-up examination.

session_14.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_14.text: How exactly do you do the chin tuck exercise? My neck is still stiff when I sleep tonight. Can I just apply a hot compress directly?

session_14.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_14.text: Chin tuck: Sit up straight or lie flat, pull your chin back horizontally (like making a double chin), hold for 5 seconds, then relax. Do 3 sets a day, 10 reps per set. You can apply a hot compress now: use a towel at about 40°C for 15 minutes, being careful not to burn yourself. When sleeping, try to lie on your back so the pillow just fills the gap under your neck.

session_15.text: Today I rewarded my oldest son with stationery for his end-of-term progress. My second son was visibly upset. I comforted him, but I'm worried about long-term imbalance. With three children of different ages and personalities, how can I build a fair incentive system?

session_15.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_15.text: Suggest adopting individualized progress standards: set unique goals for each child (e.g., eldest son's academics, second son's habits, youngest daughter's self-care), tie rewards to the effort process; combine a rotation system and family activities (such as weekend park picnics) as non-material incentives, reduce comparisons, and guide mutual appreciation.

session_15.text: That makes sense, but I'm on a tight budget and worried that material rewards would be too expensive. How exactly do non-material rewards work?

session_15.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_15.text: You can set up 'privilege coupons', such as choosing the weekend menu, deciding the family game, or extending bedtime story time. At the same time, use a 'progress notebook' so each child can see their own growth, and publicly praise them at the weekly family meeting to reinforce their sense of achievement.

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_16.text: My son Xuanxuan is in the second year of junior high school, and Chinese reading is his weak point. I just talked with his homeroom teacher, Teacher Han, who suggested he read for half an hour every day and take notes. I bought Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk and Rickshaw Boy. But I'm not sure how to put it into practice or how to check the results. Can you help me think it through?

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_16.text: Sure. I'd suggest 30 minutes a day split into three parts: first, read silently for 10 minutes and mark good words and sentences; then read aloud for 5 minutes to build a feel for the language; finally spend 15 minutes writing simple notes. The note format can be: date, book title, three good words, and one reflection. After reading, you can ask questions to help clarify the main idea, such as 'Why did the protagonist do that?' If you need supplementary workbooks, I recommend One Book: Junior High Chinese Reading Practice Five-in-One or Wanwei High School Entrance Exam Reading Comprehension—just choose the basic level.

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_16.text: This method is quite clear. However, Xuanxuan doesn't like writing reflections much; I'm afraid he'll do it perfunctorily. How can I guide him to write more deeply? Also, he has a lot of schoolwork, so reading time might be hard to squeeze out. How should I balance it?

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_16.text: Reflection can start with a single sentence, such as 'After reading this story, I thought...' to lower the threshold. You can also read together with him and share feelings with each other to create a relaxed atmosphere. As for time, I suggest a fixed period (such as after dinner or before bed) and make reading a daily must-do. If there is a lot of homework, you can shorten it to 20 minutes, but keep doing it every day. On weekends, you can arrange one hour of deep reading plus note-taking, and keep checking in during weekdays.

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_16.text: Okay, I'll try this first. I'll start implementing it tomorrow, and if there are any problems, I'll ask you again.

session_16.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_16.text: Okay, feel free to reach out to me anytime. After sticking with it for two weeks, you can check Xuanxuan's reading notes and oral retelling, then adjust the plan. Wish Xuanxuan great progress in reading during the winter vacation!

session_17.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_17.text: Today I bought white radishes. Aunt Sun taught me how to pickle radishes in soy sauce, but I can't remember the proportions or the time for drawing out the water. I'm afraid of ruining them and wasting food. Can you tell me the detailed steps?

session_17.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_17.text: No problem. After washing and cutting into strips, add salt to draw out water for 2-3 hours; the ratio is 15 g of salt per 500 g of radish. Then squeeze out the water and pickle with light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar. The volume ratio of soy sauce to radish is about 1:3, and add 20-30 g of sugar according to taste. It can be eaten after pickling for 24 hours, and can be stored for two weeks sealed in the refrigerator.

session_17.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_17.text: I only have light soy sauce at home. Is it okay not to use dark soy sauce? And can I add chili?

session_17.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_17.text: Using only light soy sauce is perfectly fine; the color will be lighter but the flavor won't change. Adding chili pepper is also fine—cut it into sections or pickle it with dried chilies for a better flavor. When storing, make sure the liquid covers the radish.

session_18.text: Today my youngest daughter drew a picture of me stir-frying in the kitchen. She used a lot of bright colors, and I was so pleasantly surprised that I stuck it right on the refrigerator. I've been feeling really happy about it. Can you see if this child is especially creative?

session_18.text: I can feel your happiness and pride! This painting is a warm expression of your daughter observing your busy daily life. Her sense of color and detailed depiction are full of talent. You often encourage her to draw, which is very helpful for developing creativity and emotional expression. You are truly a devoted mother.

session_18.text: Yes, she even deliberately drew my apron in red, saying it was the one she liked best on me. Everyone in the family group chat praised how lifelike her drawing was. session_18.text: Such a warm moment is worth treasuring! session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_18.text: Sister Wang recommended Sister Sun's pickled radish method. I'm going to make it the day after tomorrow. Could you give me detailed steps? The key points are how to prepare the radish, the seasoning proportions, and how to prevent mold.

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_18.text: Okay! Let me first summarize Sister Sun's classic method: cut white radish into strips, salt and let sit for 1 hour to drain; use light soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, garlic slices, and small chili peppers (in a 10:5:3 ratio); put in a clean oil-free container, seal and refrigerate for 2 days. Would you like to know more details or different flavors?

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_18.text: Yes, I'd like to know if I can add some Sichuan peppercorns? And if I want to make it sweet and sour, how should I adjust the ratio of sugar and vinegar?

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_18.text: You can add Sichuan peppercorns for aroma; frying them together with dried chili peppers in oil works even better. For a sweet-and-sour taste, adjust the sugar-to-vinegar ratio to 2:3 and use less salt; after pickling, add honey to enhance the flavor. Note that the container must be free of water and oil, otherwise it will easily grow mold.

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_18.text: I only have a middle school education. When I help my fourth-grade son with math problems, I always fail to explain clearly, and he seems to half-understand. Is there any good way?

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_18.text: You can use everyday examples to explain abstract concepts, such as using fruit cutting to teach fractions, and then have the child explain the reasoning again to check whether they truly understand. Recommend the Primary School Math Common Mistakes Collection for targeted practice.

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_18.text: What if the child makes the same mistake again next time?

session_18.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_18.text: Use the mistake notebook to record the original problems and the correct steps. Each week choose 3 problems for him to redo, and break down the steps to ask for the reasons one by one. Give plenty of encouragement when tutoring, and avoid repeated explanations that cause anxiety.

session_19.text: You want to use common and safe materials at home to complete the experiment, and also allow your 6-year-old daughter to participate, right?

session_19.text: My suggestion for you: 1) Change the monthly 200 yuan to a small-amount periodic deposit (annual interest rate about 1.1%, higher than demand deposits), and open three separate accounts, one for each child; 2) Each month, save an additional 50 yuan from your part-time income into a separate travel fund account, with similar interest; 3) Pay attention to local education subsidy policies for low-income families (such as grants and tuition waivers), which can significantly reduce future burdens.

session_23.text: This is acute lumbar muscle soreness caused by long-term strain from housework. You need to first determine whether it is muscle fatigue or a strain. session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_23.text: Cold compresses now can reduce inflammation; tomorrow, hot compresses will promote circulation. Daily recommendations: 1) When lifting heavy objects, bend your knees rather than your waist; 2) Do 5 minutes of core muscle exercises every day (such as planks); 3) Wear a lumbar support brace before heavy cleaning, and take a break every hour to rest and stretch your lower back.

session_23.text: This afternoon I looked through some Chinese New Year's Eve dinner recipes at Jinghai Library. I want to prepare an affordable and festive New Year's Eve dinner for the family. session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_23.text: Do you want to use locally available ingredients, control costs, take your family's tastes into account, and reflect Jinghai's local character? For example, using a traditional earthen stove and iron wok to make sweet-and-sour flavors and traditional dishes?

session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_23.text: Yes, we have a traditional stove and an iron wok at home and want to make the most of that feature. Are there any local Jinghai Spring Festival traditional snacks or dishes we could add? For example, creative ways to reprocess leftover food?

session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_23.text: You could try sweet-and-sour pork tenderloin (reducing the sauce over the earthen stove) and eggs stir-fried with local scallions, plus a Jinghai specialty, 'braised vermicelli with cured beans' (using cured meat, soybeans, and vermicelli prepared in advance as a semi-finished dish). The remaining ingredients can be made into 'vinegar-sautéed mixed vegetables' or 'fried vegetable balls' as snacks, which saves money and is full of festive New Year flavor.

session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_23.text: Hello, I plan to set up a stall at the markets around Jinghai this spring, selling handmade embroidered items and vegetables from my small garden. Could you help me check the times, locations, and stall fees for the main markets in Jinghai District? And how do I apply for a fixed stall?

session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_23.text: Okay. The main markets in Jinghai District include Wangkou Fair (lunar calendar days 1 and 6), Duli Fair (days 3 and 8), Tangguantun Fair (days 4 and 9), etc. The stall fee is generally 10-30 yuan per day. To apply for a fixed stall, you need to register with the urban management or market management office in the township where the market is located; it's recommended to consult two weeks in advance. In addition, selling food at a stall requires a health certificate and food registration. Handmade embroidery generally does not need a business license, but if the volume is large, it's advisable to register as an individual business.

session_23.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_23.text: Reference costs: small pendant materials about 3-5 yuan, suggested price 15-25 yuan; sachet cost 2-4 yuan, price 10-18 yuan. Popular styles include zodiac themes, traditional auspicious patterns (such as the character Fu and koi fish), and car hangings. You can collaborate with your childhood friend Liu Chunmei's fabric workshop to add more variety and customers. When you go to the fabric workshop the next day, you can ask about styles and fabric matching.

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_26.text: This afternoon I embroidered the outline of plum blossoms using running stitch and back stitch, but the petal curves aren't smooth, the stitches are uneven, and the thread tends to tangle. How can I make the petal edges more natural and the stitches more even?

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_26.text: If you want to improve the embroidered outline of the plum blossom, the key is even stitching and curve handling. I suggest practicing the outline stitch first, paying attention to hiding the thread at the starting point and the direction of the needle — push the needle from outside to inside along the petal curve, with each stitch 2–3 mm long, which will improve roundness. Also, keep the stitch spacing consistent when backstitching to avoid too dense or too sparse.

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_26.text: Could you elaborate on the specific thread-hiding techniques for outline stitch? Also, I've collected the complex patterns Zhou Xiuqin posted and want to learn them soon. After mastering plum blossoms, what transitional stitches should I also learn?

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_26.text: Thread hiding: When starting, bring the needle up from the back of the fabric, leave a small thread tail, and press the tail down with the first stitch before pulling tight; at the end, take 2-3 stitches through the back to hide the thread. For transition stitches, it is recommended to first practice satin stitch and long-and-short stitch for filling and gradients. It is recommended to start by embroidering simple geometric patterns (e.g., circles, wavy lines) to get familiar with the direction of the needle.

What ingredients are usually needed for frying New Year snacks (such as fried meatballs, fried lotus root sandwiches, and fried dough twists)? How should we divide the work so it goes smoothly?

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_26.text: You want to plan the ingredient list and cooperation process in advance to avoid being flustered on the day. Common ingredients for traditional fried New Year goods include: pork, lotus root, tofu, eggs, scallions, ginger, Sichuan peppercorn powder, and other seasonings. You can coordinate with Zhang Shufen in advance on the division of work: you are in charge of the batter and frying tools (pot, slotted spoon), and she brings the meat and vegetables. As for the cooking order, first handle the vegetarian filling (fried meatless balls), then the meat filling (fried lotus root sandwiches), and finally fry the mahua twists, which takes a long time, so it can be done last. Keeping the oil temperature at 160-180°C is safer.

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_26.text: Right, I'm worried it'll be a mess when the time comes. So the specific process is: first fry the meatballs and stuffed lotus root, then the dough twists? How do I judge the oil temperature, and how should I store them after frying?

session_26.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_26.text: Process suggestions: ① After Zhang Shufen arrives, handle the ingredients together (chopping vegetables, mixing filling); you mix the flour into a batter in advance; ② fry meatballs first (medium heat) → then fry stuffed lotus root (coated in batter) → finally fry fried dough twists (slowly over low heat). Oil temperature test: drop a small piece of batter; if it quickly floats up and bubbles, it's ready. After frying, let cool, pack into sealed jars, and store in a cool place; if there's a lot, freeze after it is completely cooled. When communicating, remember to agree on a time in advance, and each bring a cutting board and a large bowl.

session_27.text: Xiulan: I just added dark soy sauce and rock sugar to the pickled radish jar, but the flavor still doesn't seem rich enough. I'd like to ask how to adjust it to make it more fragrant? Also, after bottling, how should it be stored so it doesn't go bad easily?

session_27.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_27.text: You want the pickled radish to have a rich sauce aroma and a long shelf life. Do you need specific spice ratios (such as star anise and cinnamon) and airtight refrigeration recommendations?

session_27.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_27.text: Yes, I'm just afraid that I'll add the wrong proportions, or that it will spoil if left at room temperature after bottling. Can you tell me exactly how much spice to add and whether it needs to be refrigerated?

session_27.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_27.text: It is recommended to add 5 g rock sugar, 10 g dark soy sauce, 2 g star anise, and 1 g cinnamon bark per jin of radish. Bring to a boil, cool, and then pickle. When bottling, be sure to tighten the lid and store in the refrigerator (0–4°C). It is safest to finish within a month. If a white film or sour smell appears on the surface of the sauce, it means it has spoiled.

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_32.text: On the fourth day of the New Year, I gave my maternal uncle's family some of my pickled radish in soy sauce, and all the relatives praised it. My cousin's wife and my older female cousin even ordered 8 jars. I'd like to improve it: less salt, mildly spicy, crisp texture, and I also want to try green radish. Can you tell me the exact proportions of salt, sugar, and vinegar, how to keep it crisp, and how to add the mild spiciness?

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_32.text: Suggested base ratio: 10 jin of white radish, 60 g salt (for drawing out water), 200 g soy sauce, 150 g sugar, 100 g vinegar, 500 g cool boiled water. To reduce salt, you can add an extra salting-and-draining step (salt for 30 minutes and squeeze dry) to lower the finished product's salt content. For mild spice, add 5-10 g chili powder or fresh small chili pepper segments. The key to crunchiness: squeeze dry after salting, keep sealed and refrigerated throughout pickling, and season only before eating. Green radish is crunchier but releases less water, so shorten the salting time to 15 minutes.

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_32.text: Then if I make a trial batch of 5 jars, roughly what would the cost be? And which is more cost-effective, green radish or white radish? I'm afraid failure will hurt my reputation.

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_32.text: Cost for 5 jars (about 1 jin net weight each): 5 jin of radish about 10 yuan, seasonings about 15 yuan, 5 jars about 5 yuan, total about 30 yuan. Green radish is slightly cheaper and has better crispness, so it is suggested to first use white radish for the initial batch, and switch after the recipe is stabilized. For small-scale trial production, you can make 2 jars first for relatives and friends to taste, then fine-tune based on feedback before mass production.

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_32.text: I'm a housewife and want to build a family side business with homemade pickled radish, but I lack experience. How do I calculate costs, set prices, and do I need a license?

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_32.text: You're worried about startup costs and compliance risks, and you need a systematic method from cost accounting to testing the market, right?

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_32.text: Yes, I want to calculate the costs clearly first before starting the trial production with peace of mind.

session_32.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant

session_34.text: My son fell in the front yard this afternoon. His knee was scraped and his palm was rubbed red. I disinfected it with iodophor swabs and applied band-aids. Was this the right way to handle it? What should I pay attention to next?

session_34.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_34.text: Your initial treatment was correct. For minor abrasions, iodophor disinfection is very effective. It is recommended to switch to breathable gauze instead of adhesive bandages, keep the wound dry, change the dressing 1-2 times a day, and watch for signs of infection such as redness, swelling, or pus. Protect it with a waterproof dressing when showering and change it immediately afterward.

session_34.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_34.text: Is the switch to gauze because you're worried that band-aids aren't breathable? Then about how long will it take to heal?

session_34.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_34.text: Yes, adhesive bandages have poor breathability and can easily cause the wound to become macerated, increasing the risk of infection. Abrasions usually scab and heal in 5-7 days. During healing, avoid scratching and getting the wound wet. Letting the scab fall off naturally can reduce scarring. You can also teach your child to watch the ground while walking to avoid falling again.

session_34.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_34.text: Thank you. I'm also worried about whether it will leave a scar. Besides not scratching, do I need to apply any ointment?

session_34.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_34.text: After the scab falls off the wound, you can apply a scar cream specially designed for children (such as silicone gel), and pay attention to sun protection. If the wound shows persistent redness, swelling, warmth, or discharge, please seek medical attention promptly. In daily life, remind the child to be careful during play. You've already done a great job.

session_36.text: Of course. For example, with 500 grams of chili peppers, add 30-40 grams of salt and 20-30 milliliters of high-proof baijiu (above 50% ABV). After washing the peppers, dry them in the shade until there is no moisture on the surface. You can cut them into sections or leave them whole. Mix them evenly with the salt and liquor, then pack them into a sterilized jar. Before sealing, make sure the pepper surface has no moisture. Ferment for 15-20 days and they are ready.

session_36.text: I remember the ratio of salt and liquor. Do we need to add garlic and ginger? What's the best way to sterilize the jar?

session_36.text: You can add 50 grams of garlic slices and 30 grams of shredded ginger to enhance the aroma. Scald the jar with boiling water and turn it upside down to dry, or rinse the inside wall with high-proof liquor. During fermentation, do not seal the jar completely; leave a small gap to release air and prevent the jar from swelling.

session_37.text: Today I tried making spicy radish sauce for the first time. After tasting it, I feel it could use a little fermented black beans to enhance the umami. But I'm not familiar with how to use fermented black beans, and I'm afraid I might ruin the flavor. May I ask when to add them and how much is appropriate? Do they need any preparation beforehand?

session_37.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_37.text: It is recommended to use dried fermented black beans, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes to soften, chop them, and add them during the stage of stir-frying the sauce over low heat (after the oil is hot, first stir-fry minced garlic and minced ginger, then add the chopped fermented black beans), so that the aroma can be fully released. For dosage, refer to 15-20 g of fermented black beans per 500 g of shredded radish; this will not overpower the radish flavor. In addition, fermented black beans contain a certain amount of salt, so it is recommended to reduce the amount of salt and soy sauce in the recipe by 10%.

session_37.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_37.text: Got it. So you mean it should be added at the stage when it's stir-fried until fragrant, not at the end, right? After adding the fermented black beans, will the storage method and shelf life change?

session_37.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_37.text: Yes, it's better to add it during the stir-frying stage to bring out the bean aroma. As for shelf life, fermented black beans are a fermented product, so it won't significantly shorten the shelf life, but it's recommended to keep them sealed and refrigerated and eat them within a week. If you want to extend storage, you can increase the oil appropriately (with the oil covering the surface of the sauce) or reduce the moisture. Also, if you want more umami, you can consider adding a little five-spice powder or oyster sauce, but oyster sauce doesn't withstand high heat, so mix it in after turning off the heat.

session_41.text: Aunt Ma, pickled peppers generally don't need to be blanched first, because blanching makes the peppers soft and affects their crisp texture.
