session_50.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_50.text: I was helping my 10-year-old son Ma Mingzhe with math homework. He always mixes up sharing equally and quotitive division. For example, dividing 12 radishes equally among 3 families is one case, but when it's changed to 'each family gets 4 radishes, how many families can be served?' he gets it wrong. Can you teach me a simple way to tell them apart?

session_50.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_50.text: Remember the key: equal sharing is total ÷ number of shares, to find how many each share gets; grouping is total ÷ amount per share, to find how many shares there are. Teach him with everyday examples, like sharing apples: 6 apples for 2 friends, how many does each get? That is equal sharing; 6 apples, 2 for each friend, how many friends can share them? That is grouping. Drawing circle diagrams can also make the comparison intuitive.

session_50.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_50.text: Understood, I'll use dividing radishes as an example: 3 families share 12 radishes, how many does each get? That's equal division; if each family gets 4 radishes, how many families can get them? That's measurement division. Add the mnemonic "equal division looks at the number of shares, measurement division looks at the amount per share". Try it next time you tutor.

session_50.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_50.text: Yes, the mnemonic is easy to remember. You can also let him use real objects or draw circles, for example, take 12 candies, first arrange them into 3 piles to feel equal sharing; then circle them in groups of 3 to feel division by grouping. With more practice, he will be able to tell them apart.

session_54.text: I just finished writing the sauce-pickled radish recipe. My neighbor suggested adding star anise to make it more fragrant, but I don't know how much to use. Also, I calculated the cost myself at about 3.5 yuan per jin, and I'm not sure if it's right. Can you help me take a look?

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_54.text: Of course. Star anise can enhance the savory sauce aroma and the sweet aftertaste, and it suits your recipe. Could you first tell me the specific amounts and unit prices of the radish, salt, sugar, and soy sauce? I'll help you check the cost and recommend spice pairings.

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_54.text: Radishes are 0.8 yuan per jin. For every 10 jin of radishes, use 200g of salt, 300g of sugar, and 500ml of soy sauce. I haven't added the other spices yet. The neighbor said to add star anise, and I also want to add Sichuan peppercorns and cinnamon bark. Roughly how much will these cost? How should I set the total cost and selling price?

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_54.text: Star anise recommendation: add 5-8 grams (about 4-6 pieces) per 10 jin of radishes, and 3-5 grams each of Sichuan pepper and cinnamon bark. Reference prices in Jinghai District: star anise about 0.3 yuan/gram, Sichuan pepper 0.2 yuan/gram, cinnamon bark 0.15 yuan/gram. Plus the ingredients you already have, the total cost per 10 jin is about 13-15 yuan. Suggested selling price is 8-10 yuan/jin, with a profit margin of 30%-40%. For storage, keep it sealed and away from light. After adding star anise, extend the pickling time by 1-2 days for better flavor.

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_54.text: I'd like to learn the specific methods for daily monitoring and health management of hypertension in the elderly. My father is 68 and has high blood pressure. I help him measure his blood pressure every morning and evening, but I'm always afraid I'm not doing it right.

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_54.text: You're very attentive. I suggest measuring blood pressure at fixed times every morning and evening: in the morning after getting up and urinating, before taking medicine, and in the evening before going to bed. The normal range is systolic below 140 and diastolic below 90. For diet, keep it light and use vinegar, scallions, and garlic instead of salt. Walk with your father for half an hour every day. If he suddenly feels dizzy, has a headache, or has blurred vision, take him to the hospital immediately.

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_54.text: Okay, but Father sometimes forgets to take his medicine. How can we help him remember?

session_54.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_54.text: You can set an alarm on your phone, or buy a pill organizer, put the morning and evening medications separately, and keep it in a visible place. When you call him every day, remind him as well, so he can get into the habit.

session_55.text: My father is going to the community clinic this afternoon for a follow-up on his high blood pressure. He is 68 years old and is going alone. Does he need to fast? What documents should he bring?

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: Generally, hypertension follow-up visits do not require fasting, but if the doctor may check blood lipids and blood sugar, it's better to fast. Please bring your medical insurance card, past medical records, recent blood pressure readings, and the medicine packages you are currently taking. If going in the afternoon, have a light breakfast; fasting before lunch is safer.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_55.text: Okay, I'll let him go on an empty stomach. Also, are there any dietary precautions in his daily life? He always loves pickled vegetables.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: It is recommended to strictly control salt intake, no more than 5 grams per day, and eat as little or no pickled vegetables as possible. It is better to recommend low-fat, high-potassium foods such as celery, tomatoes, and bananas, and to eat more whole grains and vegetables. You can teach him to use spices instead of salt for seasoning, and remind him to measure and record his blood pressure at fixed times every morning and evening.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_55.text: I heard that the spring market in Jinghai District opens at the end of March. I'd like to set up a stall for my homemade pickled vegetables. Where should I start preparing?

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: You first need to learn about the market application channels; usually the community or street office will post notices. Prepare a health certificate, a food workshop registration certificate, or a temporary stall permit. The pickled vegetables need to be vacuum-sealed and labeled with ingredients and date. It is suggested to price them by referring to similar products, such as 10-15 yuan per bottle.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_55.text: I understand about the packaging and certificates. Then what should I bring for the stall that day? How do I attract customers?

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: Bring a folding table, uniform price signs, small tasting dishes, and toothpicks; keep the pickled vegetables fresh in an insulated box with ice packs. When setting up, put the brightly colored pickle jars in the front row, offer samples, and call out loudly. You can also add handwritten labels saying 'family secret recipe' to highlight the specialty.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_55.text: I help my children with homework every day, but I only have a middle school education myself, and sometimes I feel inadequate. Today my younger son Mingzhe made two careless mistakes in math calculation, and my older son Mingxuan is confused about series and parallel circuits in physics circuit diagrams. Can you teach me some simple and practical methods?

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: About careless calculation mistakes: you can teach your child to use the “reverse checking method” — after doing addition, use subtraction to check. For example, 23+18=41, so calculate 41-18 and see whether it equals 23. Use the scratch paper in sections, and write each problem in its own vertical calculation format to avoid mixing up the rows. Circuit diagram analogy: a series circuit is like a string of Christmas lights — if one bulb goes out, they all go out; a parallel circuit is like the sockets at home — each light is controlled independently. You can do simple experiments at home with batteries, small light bulbs, and wire, and let the child connect them with their own hands for intuitive understanding.

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_55.text: The calculation checking method and the light bulb experiment sound good, but my child just can't settle down when doing homework. Any solutions?

session_55.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_55.text: For focus, try the Pomodoro Technique: have the child concentrate for 15 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, and slowly extend the time. You can also play a "number spot-the-difference" game — write a string of numbers on paper and ask him to find the one at a specified position (for example, what is the 7th from the left). Practice for 5 minutes a day to improve carefulness.

session_59.text: My neighbor Guilan and I have agreed to start checking in with daily stretching in the WeChat group from tomorrow, March 1st. session_59.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_59.text: Okay! I recommend three groups of basic exercises, rotating daily: Monday and Thursday do shoulder and neck stretches such as shoulder shrugs with neck tucks and lateral neck flexion, Tuesday and Friday do back stretches such as cat-cow pose and seated twists, Wednesday and Saturday do lower-body stretches such as wall calf stretches and lunge presses. Do 10-15 minutes every day, moving slowly to avoid bouncing. When checking in, send each other photos, and you can also leave comments like Finished XX exercise this morning to increase interaction. If you forget a day, just make it up the next day; don't blame yourself.

session_59.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_59.text: These exercises sound good, but I'm not really sure how to do each move. For example, how do I do the wall calf stretch? And what time of day is best for stretching?

session_59.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_59.text: Wall calf stretch: Stand one step away facing a wall, place both hands on the wall, bend one leg forward and extend the other leg back, keep the back heel pressed firmly into the ground, and feel the stretch in the back of the calf. Hold for 20 seconds, then switch sides. Recommended in the morning after getting up or at night before bed, on an empty stomach or one hour after a meal. Each of you can record a 10-second short video and post it in the group to demonstrate to each other—it's intuitive and gives a sense of accomplishment!

session_60.text: Common causes of dizziness in middle-aged and elderly people include high blood pressure, cervical spondylosis, and insufficient blood supply to the brain. session_60.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_60.text: It can be eaten after 3-7 days of pickling. During this period, it must be sealed and refrigerated. After opening the jar, keep it refrigerated, use clean chopsticks to take out the pickles, and finish within a week. The best time to eat is after 5-7 days of pickling, when the texture is moderately crisp. If you want it crunchier, you can reduce the pickling time or add vinegar; if it is too salty, shorten the brining time. Before sharing with mother, it is recommended to try a small amount first to confirm it is safe.

session_64.text: Hello, I'm Ma Xiulan. My son Ma Mingxuan is in the second year of junior high school. Tonight, while doing his physics homework, he came across a problem about buoyancy. I'm not well educated and can't explain it. Could you help me see how to solve it?

session_64.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_64.text: No problem. Could you send me the original problem text? For example, is it about calculating the magnitude of buoyancy or determining whether an object sinks or floats? I can explain the approach and steps in simple terms so you can relay them to the child.

session_64.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_64.text: The problem is: an object weighing 5N with a volume of 600cm³ is submerged in water. What is the buoyant force it experiences? My son's calculation is wrong, but he doesn't know which step he went wrong on.

session_64.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_64.text: OK, the key to this problem is Archimedes' principle: buoyancy = ρ_water × g × V_displaced. When fully submerged, V_displaced equals the object's volume, 600 cm³ (i.e., 0.0006 m³). Substituting ρ_water = 1000 kg/m³ and g = 10 N/kg gives: buoyancy = 1000 × 10 × 0.0006 = 6 N. Your son may have made a mistake in unit conversion, or he used the object's weight to calculate buoyancy. I suggest reminding him that buoyancy only depends on the volume of displaced liquid and the liquid's density, not on the object's weight.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: My father is hospitalized with cardiovascular problems. I bring meals every day, but I'm not sure which foods are more suitable. What should I pay attention to in daily care?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: Would you like to know specific examples of low-salt, low-fat recipes, as well as care points like blood pressure monitoring frequency and nighttime fall prevention?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: Yes, especially whether eggs and meat are okay to eat, and how to recognize signs such as chest tightness and dizziness.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: Recommendations: 1) One egg per day, boiled or steamed as egg custard; dice lean meat and cook it into porridge; 2) Measure blood pressure in the morning and evening, avoid measuring right after meals; 3) Leave a night light on and place a call bell beside the bed; 4) If father has chest tightness, dizziness, or nausea, notify the nurse immediately.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: Today the whole family planted a persimmon tree together. My husband dug the pit, my second son held the tree upright, and I mounded soil around it. We also hung a wooden sign saying 'Planted on March 9, 2025.' I'm really happy! But this is my first time planting a persimmon tree—how should I water, fertilize, and prevent diseases from now on?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: So heartwarming! Planting a tree together as a family is full of ritual. As for maintenance: In spring in the north, water thoroughly right after planting, then water once every 5–7 days afterward to keep the soil slightly moist; after leaf fall in autumn, apply decomposed organic fertilizer once; protect against frost, and in winter whitewash or wrap the trunk. For pruning, cut off diseased and weak branches during the dormant period, and during the growing season, lime sulfur mixture can be used to prevent persimmon cottony scale.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: Thank you! When should I top it? And does the wooden sign hanging there have a meaning?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: Topping can be done when the sapling grows to about 1.8 meters to promote lateral branches. The wooden plaque is both a family keepsake and a good way to record its growth. In the future, the date of each year's fruit harvest can be carved on the plaque, which is especially meaningful.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: I'm soaking my feet and thinking about tomorrow's schedule: take the three kids to school, go to the hospital to see my hospitalized father, and buy pork ribs to make soup. It's a bit tight. Can you help me check whether the order of times is reasonable?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: Are you worried that the school drop-off times conflict with hospital visiting hours? The eldest son's middle school starts at 7:30, the second son's primary school at 8:00, and the daughter's kindergarten at 8:30. The hospital's cardiology department is usually open for visits in the morning. I suggest leaving at 7:00 to take the eldest son, at 7:30 for the second son, at 8:00 for the daughter, and then arriving at the hospital at 8:30. This is tight but you won't be late. The pork rib soup should be skimmed of fat and lightly salted, which suits your father.

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_68.text: Yes, the schedule sounds good. But is pork rib soup really suitable for a cardiovascular patient? Do I also need to bring my medical insurance card and a change of clothes?

session_68.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_68.text: After skimming off the fat and reducing the salt, pork rib soup is safe for cardiovascular patients. You can add winter melon or white radish to increase nutrition. Before setting out tomorrow, check: medical insurance card, change of clothes for your father, and blood pressure monitor (if needed). If the hospital allows, you can bring some cooked congee for your father to drink in the evening. After the morning visit, you can go to the vegetable market in the afternoon to buy ribs.

session_69.text: The nurse measured my dad's blood pressure this morning: systolic 142, diastolic 88. I'm a bit worried — is this considered high for a 68-year-old?

session_69.text: Ms. Ma, your father's blood pressure of 142/88 is in the high-normal range for a 68-year-old, close to the threshold for grade 1 hypertension. The doctor said during rounds that his condition is currently stable, but it needs continuous monitoring. You've been keeping very careful records—keep it up.

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_69.text: Then how should I adjust my diet and massage? My younger sister is covering my shift tomorrow, so I need to make it clear. And what danger signs should I watch out for?

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_69.text: Reduce salt in your diet and eat more celery, wood ear mushrooms, and bananas. The leg massage technique you learned is correct; just avoid the blood clot area. Watch for danger signs such as dizziness, chest tightness, and numbness in the hands or feet. If these occur, call a doctor immediately. When your sister takes over your shift, just write these down and pass them along.

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_69.text: Today I was busy from 5:30 in the morning to 10 at night: taking care of my dad, dropping off the kids, and running to the hospital. I feel like I can't hold on much longer... My dad's hospitalization has made me especially anxious. I'm afraid that if I collapse, no one at home can hold things together.

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_69.text: You have taken on so much alone in a day, and you are physically and mentally exhausted. You not only need to be understood, but also need some quick ways to relax and emotional support.

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_69.text: Yes, I keep worrying that my dad is recovering slowly, and I also feel guilty toward the children. Today my husband came home early and simmered some soup, which warmed my heart a little, but when I lay in bed at night, I still could not fall asleep.

session_69.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_69.text: You've already done very well, and your family will feel your efforts. Try soaking your feet for 10 minutes before bed, combined with deep breathing — inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 7 seconds, exhale for 8 seconds. This can help you relax quickly when you're tired, and also leave some time for yourself tomorrow.

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_70.text: Today I made cold black fungus salad and stir-fried celery with pork following a recipe. I added light soy sauce and black vinegar, but I'm not sure if these seasonings contain hidden salt. Are they suitable for my father's high blood pressure?

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_70.text: Light soy sauce and black vinegar do contain sodium, but using a small amount is not a big problem. For cold dressed black fungus, I suggest replacing some of the salt with minced garlic, minced ginger, and a little lemon juice; for stir-fried pork with celery, you can enhance the flavor with fresh herbs and keep the light soy sauce within 5 ml. Did you weigh it with an electronic scale?

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_70.text: I weighed it: 15 grams of oil, 3 grams of salt, and measured 5 ml of light soy sauce as well. So how do you make eggplant low-salt? Dr. Wang only said to use less salt, without going into detail.

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_70.text: Eggplant absorbs oil, so I suggest steaming it first and then seasoning it. Use garlic paste, a small amount of Sichuan pepper oil, and vinegar instead of salt. You can also try using shiitake mushroom powder or tomato juice to enhance the umami flavor and reduce sodium intake. You can try it out tomorrow.

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_70.text: My father Ma Jianguo was just found to have cardiovascular problems. His ECG is normal today, but after discharge I'm worried he won't watch what he eats, especially since he loves pickled vegetables. Can you give me a systematic set of post-discharge care recommendations? Including diet, monitoring, activity, and psychological support.

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_70.text: I understand your needs. The core of home care for cardiovascular patients: low-salt and low-fat diet; pickled vegetables can be chosen in a low-salt version but should be controlled in quantity; measure and record blood pressure every morning and evening; moderate exercise such as walking for 20-30 minutes after meals; regular follow-ups for ECG and blood lipids; communicate more with your father and avoid emotional ups and downs. The three sisters can take turns caring for him, with each person responsible for one week of meals and monitoring records.

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_70.text: He keeps going on about the pickled vegetables, and we've already made a low-salt batch at home. Is it okay to eat them this way? Also, you said to monitor blood pressure in the morning and evening—are there specific times that matter?

session_70.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_70.text: Low-salt pickled vegetables can occasionally be used as a condiment, but no more than a small dish (about 10 grams) each time, and they are better matched with fresh vegetables. For blood pressure monitoring, it is recommended to measure once after getting up in the morning and before taking medication, and again at night before going to bed. Keep a fixed time and record the readings. If there is significant fluctuation, contact a doctor promptly.

For the main dish, you can choose celery and wood ear stir-fried with lean meat (quick stir-fry with little oil), or oatmeal pumpkin porridge (for breakfast). session_71.text: Common causes include: nervousness, not resting enough after walking, or an incorrect wrist position. It is recommended to measure at a fixed time every day, such as after getting up and before going to bed, sit quietly for 5 minutes before measuring, and record the average value.

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_72.text: My father was hospitalized for high blood pressure and is now recovering at home. I make him a low-salt diet and measure his blood pressure, but I'm worried my methods aren't right. Could you advise on the key points for daily care and monitoring?

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_72.text: You're doing very well! For hypertension patients, the ideal blood pressure should be kept below 130/80 mmHg. In daily life, you need to maintain a low-salt (less than 5 g of salt per day), low-fat diet, get moderate aerobic exercise (such as 30 minutes of walking per day), and keep your emotions stable. When using the new wrist blood pressure monitor, sit up straight with your arm at heart level. It is recommended to measure once every morning and once before bed, and record the results. Regular follow-up is also important—see your doctor every 1 to 3 months.

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_72.text: So I'll make him low-salt noodles and measure his blood pressure, 128/82 and 128/84. Is that right? What else should I pay attention to?

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_72.text: Blood pressure is well controlled! Continue to stick to a low-salt diet. You can add vegetables, whole grains, and high-quality protein (such as fish and soy products). Avoid high-sodium seasonings and pickled foods. For rehabilitation exercise, start with low intensity and avoid exercising during the morning blood pressure peak (6–10 a.m.). If symptoms such as dizziness or chest tightness occur, seek medical attention immediately. In addition, an upper-arm blood pressure monitor is recommended because it is more accurate than a wrist one.

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_72.text: What you need is not just methods for solving problems; you also want to improve your son's low mood caused by his declining grades and the parent-child communication. For an introverted child, when tutoring, it is recommended to empathize first and then explain the problems. For example, use "Wrong answers are reminders of where we need to strengthen" instead of direct correction.

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_72.text: Yes, he takes things to heart. I'm afraid that saying the wrong thing might set him back further. Is there a simple and effective method for inequalities?

session_72.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_72.text: The key to inequalities is 'moving terms changes the sign' and 'drawing a number line to find the solution set.' You can have him verbally explain the rule for each step first, then practice 3 typical problems (such as ones with denominators or absolute values), focusing on whether the direction of the sign is wrong. Spend 15 minutes a day on one type. You can also ask his school teacher Han Mei for some targeted exercises.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_73.text: My 10-year-old son came home from school in a bad mood today. Only after asking did I learn that he had a small conflict with his deskmate. He didn't go into detail at the time, and I plan to talk to him tonight, but I don't know how to guide him to handle it properly. I'm afraid he might feel wronged, and also afraid of hurting his relationship with his classmate.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_73.text: I understand your concern. I suggest starting with listening first and creating a safe atmosphere so that he will proactively share what happened and how he feels. For example, ask, “What happened with your deskmate today that made you unhappy?” Avoid rushing to judge or give solutions. Then guide him to put himself in the other person's shoes: “If you were him, what would you think?” This way, the child can be helped to find a solution on his own.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_73.text: Understood. I'll let him talk about it first. Do I need to contact the homeroom teacher or the other child's parents? I'm afraid that if I handle it improperly, it will backfire.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_73.text: First observe the child's mood and subsequent interactions for a day or two. If the conflict is quickly resolved or the child takes the initiative to make up, parents do not need to intervene; if the child remains in low spirits, the conflict escalates, or it affects studies, then consider communicating with the homeroom teacher, Teacher Yang, but be careful to only describe facts and ask for help, avoiding directly blaming the other child. This both trains the child's ability to resolve conflicts on their own and provides necessary support in a timely manner.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_73.text: For the 'Shishi Ruyi' embroidery pattern that Sister Xiuqin mentioned, I want to embroider persimmon fruits, but I'm not sure which stitch will make the fruits plump and glossy. In terms of color matching, should the main body of the persimmon be orange-yellow or orange-red, and how should I choose the threads for the shadows and highlights?

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_73.text: Recommend using long-and-short stitch or random stitch to show the persimmon's three-dimensional quality. For the main body, use a gradient of orange-yellow (mid-tone) and orange-red (shadow), with light orange-pink added to the highlights. For the persimmon calyx, use emerald green with dark brown thread, and use seed stitch or layered stitch on the calyx to add texture.

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_73.text: How should the long and short stitches be run to simulate the texture of a persimmon? Also, does the stitching method for persimmon leaves need to be distinguished from that for the fruit?

session_73.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_73.text: Long and short stitches run diagonally along the curve of the persimmon. Use long stitches on the outer layer and overlapping short stitches on the inner layer to create a gradient. For the leaves, it is recommended to use even flat stitches with the stitch direction perpendicular to the leaf veins, in dark green and light green, contrasting with the random stitches of the fruit.

session_76.text: I'm going to a handicraft market next month and want to embroider a Hundred Children tapestry, but with so many figures and such a large embroidery area, I feel uncertain. Can you give me some advice?

session_76.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_76.text: The classic Hundred Children motif is often arranged in symmetrical or comic-strip compositions, making it suitable for tapestries. For beginners, long flat stitches and overlapping stitches are recommended; choose linen or cotton fabric, and gradient silk thread will make it more vivid. If time is tight, simplify the pattern and focus on a few core scenes of children.

session_76.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_76.text: Would simplified patterns and stitching be suitable for mass production at the market? I also want to combine traditional symbolism with modern aesthetics.

session_76.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_76.text: You can choose 3-5 representative children's poses, use a rolling stitch to outline the contours, and match the warm color palette preferred by the market. Divide the work with your craft friend Zhou Xiuqin, each embroidering a section and then joining them together, which will improve efficiency.

session_82.text: I want to try making sweet and sour garlic next week, but I've never done it before. Can you give me a classic recipe and some precautions?

session_82.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_82.text: Recommended classic ratio: white vinegar : sugar : water = 1 : 0.8 : 0.5 (for example, 500 ml white vinegar, 400 g sugar, and 250 ml water). Choose fresh purple-skinned garlic, remove the old outer skin but keep the inner layer, soak in salt water for 1 day to remove the spiciness, air-dry, then put into a sterilized container. Pour in the sweet-and-sour vinegar mixture that has been boiled and cooled, seal it, and store in a cool, dark place. It can be eaten after about 20 days. Make sure the container is thoroughly sterilized, keep it free of oil throughout, and avoid mold and souring.

session_82.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_82.text: I heard that to make sweet and sour garlic, you first need to sun-dry the garlic? But I saw you mentioned soaking it in salt water; which is better?

session_82.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_82.text: In the traditional method, sun-drying the garlic removes water, but soaking in salt water can also reduce the spiciness while keeping it crisp. It is recommended to soak it in salt water for one day (about 5% salt water), which shortens the time and avoids over-drying the garlic skin. After soaking, be sure to drain the water thoroughly before pickling.

session_83.text: Spicy cucumber sticks: Cut cucumbers into strips, salt for 30 minutes, and squeeze out the water. session_87.text: A high first reading due to nervousness is common. It is recommended to sit quietly for 5 minutes before each measurement and take the average of 2-3 readings for better accuracy. For a low-salt diet: eat fewer pickled foods, soy sauce, and salted vegetables; use a salt-limiting spoon when cooking; and eat more fresh ingredients. In addition, encourage your father to stay emotionally calm and avoid sudden exertion.

session_93.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_93.text: Congratulations on your success! session_93.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_93.text: How exactly is a salinity of 3%-5% calculated? For example, how much salt should be put in 10 jin of vegetables? Does each kind of vegetable need to be pickled separately?

session_93.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_93.text: For 10 jin of vegetables, use 150-250 grams of salt (3-5 liang). It is recommended to pickle the vegetables separately: cucumbers for 2-4 hours, radishes for 8-12 hours, and finally mix them together. Green peppers can be blanched to remove the raw taste. Before pickling, use salt to draw out water and squeeze dry, which improves the crispy texture.

session_98.text: It is recommended to replace 30%-40% of the total salt with celery juice, that is, for every 500 grams of vegetables, use 5 grams of sea salt plus 15 milliliters of celery juice. session_99.text: The teacher tasted my low-salt pickled vegetables today and suggested adding a few apple slices next time to enhance the flavor. session_99.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_99.text: Understood. You want to reliably replicate the teacher's advice while ensuring the success rate of the low-salt pickles. Let me break down each step in detail: Usually, for the apple slices, it's recommended to choose crisp and sweet Red Fuji apples, cut them 2-3 mm thick, and layer them with the vegetables in the jar. The amount should be about 5%-8% of the total weight of the vegetables. This way, it won't affect the low-salt fermentation and will add a fruity aroma. Do you need me to further explain how to adjust the salt ratio?

session_99.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_99.text: Yes, I'm worried that adding apple slices might make the pickles soft or too sour? Also, should I reduce the salt? This time I used the low-salt recipe the teacher taught, with salt accounting for 3% of the vegetable weight.

session_99.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_99.text: Apple slices are quite crisp; with a thickness of 2-3 mm, a short pickling won't make them soft and mushy, but will add layers of flavor. A low-salt base of 3% is fine; the apple's natural sugar can balance the taste, so there's no need to reduce the salt further. I suggest you start with a small batch when trying it (for example, 500 grams of vegetables with 30 grams of apple), open the jar on the third day to taste the flavor, and if it is too mild, add a bit of salt. Don't make too much the first time; first master the process.

session_99.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_99.text: That way I'll have a clearer idea. Do the apple slices need to be treated in advance? For example, soaking them in salt water to prevent oxidation?

session_99.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_99.text: No need to soak in salt water. Slice the apples and put them directly into the jar, because the pickling environment itself contains salt, which can inhibit oxidation and browning. If you're really worried about discoloration, after slicing, briefly dip them in light salt water (0.5% salt), then immediately remove and drain before use. Also, make sure to remove the apple cores thoroughly to avoid bitterness. Wishing you success next time!

session_108.text: Father has high blood pressure and wants to make low-salt pickled vegetables. Without using a lot of salt, how can you get a sweet-and-sour taste and still preserve them?

session_108.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_108.text: Use white vinegar and white sugar to replace salt: 3 spoons of white vinegar, 2 spoons of sugar, 500ml of cold boiled water, add garlic slices, chili peppers, carrots, and white radish, then seal and refrigerate for 24 hours; the sugar-vinegar ratio can be adjusted, and when storing, make sure the ingredients are completely submerged; it can be kept for 1 week.

session_108.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_108.text: Thank you! Finishing it within a week is no problem. Also, what other low-salt recipes suitable for elderly people are there in summer?

Use steaming, boiling, and cold dressing for cooking, and pair with potassium-rich vegetables to help lower blood pressure.

session_111.text: To register, you need to bring your ID card and a copy, household registration booklet, product list (pickle varieties and embroidery styles), and sample photos. session_111.text: Based on past experience, standard booths are free, but some charge a 50-100 yuan deposit refunded after the exhibition. To attract customers, you can do live embroidery demonstrations (bring an embroidery hoop and stitch a few times on the spot), serve pickles for tasting in small porcelain dishes with toothpicks, and prepare small cards with an embroidered logo to record customer contact information. Also use your phone to shoot a video of the production process and play it on a loop.

session_115.text: Today I brought my parents some newly pickled low-salt vegetables. But my mother tends to cook salty, and my father has high blood pressure. I'm worried she won't remember to use less salt. Could you give me some specific dietary recommendations for high blood pressure?

session_115.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_115.text: What you need is a practical diet plan for your father's high blood pressure, including salt intake control, low-salt recipe recommendations, and how to persuade your parents to change their years-long eating habits, right?

session_115.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_115.text: Yes, and I also want to know whether the low-salt pickled vegetables I brought actually have any benefits, and whether I should regularly measure my parents' blood pressure, and how to judge the severity when they feel unwell.

session_115.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_115.text: It is recommended to keep daily salt intake below 5 grams and to use steamed or cold dishes instead of stir-fried dishes. Low-salt pickles are better than regular pickles, but they should not be eaten in excess; a small plate a day is enough. You can teach your parents to use a salt-restriction spoon and measure their blood pressure at a fixed time every week with a home blood pressure monitor in the morning after waking and before bed. If dizziness, chest tightness, or large blood pressure fluctuations occur, seek medical attention promptly. Blood-pressure-lowering foods such as celery, black fungus, and onion are recommended and can be added to daily meals in moderation.

session_115.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_115.text: Thank you! Is bringing low-salt pickled vegetables the right approach? What else can I do to help my mother gradually get used to less salt?

session_115.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_115.text: Low-salt pickles contain about 30% less salt than ordinary pickles, which is a good transitional approach. You can use naturally umami ingredients such as mushrooms, kelp, and tomatoes to replace part of the salt and gradually reduce the saltiness. In addition, you can bring your parents to the hypertension health lecture at the community hospital so that a doctor can give them guidance in person; they will be more receptive.

session_117.text: I plan to apply for the Jinghai Specialty Agricultural Products Mark. The Agricultural Commission asked me to prepare a product description, a photo of the business license copy, and actual product photos, but I'm not sure about the format and specific requirements. Is there anything else I need to prepare?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: What you are most worried about is the specific standards for the materials, such as how to write the product description, what specifications the photos should meet, and whether other documents like test reports are required? Let me help you sort that out clearly.

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_117.text: Yes, I'm afraid that if I submit it and it's not qualified, I'll have to make another trip. Does the product description need to state the raw materials and preparation method? What size should the photos be? And do we need a testing report?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: The product description should be written clearly according to three points: 'raw materials, traditional craftsmanship, and feature description'; no template is needed. A clear photo of the business license copy is enough; product photos should be taken in natural light from multiple angles. A testing report is not required, but if you have one it can help your application. Materials are usually submitted at the agricultural committee office or on the designated platform; it is recommended to confirm in advance whether an appointment is needed. Review generally takes 10-15 working days.

session_117.text: Next Monday I need to deliver goods to the community fresh produce store, Tuesday morning I have a meeting with Fumanjia Supermarket, and Wednesday afternoon I need to go to Haolinju Supermarket. I have three children to take care of and lots of housework, so I'm worried the schedule won't work out. Can you help me see how to arrange it?

session_117.text: You want a schedule that balances housework and work, and want to prepare in advance for the interview and material organization, right? For example, do you need me to help you sort out the best time slots for each day, or list a preparation checklist before the interview?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: Suggestion: on Monday morning while the children are at school, sort the label materials (9–11 a.m.) and deliver goods in the afternoon; before Tuesday's meeting, prepare samples, business cards, and a 15-character product selling point, leaving a 30-minute buffer; on Wednesday morning handle housework, and negotiate in the afternoon. session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_117.text: I stood at the trade fair all day yesterday, and today I bent over to fertilize again. Now my lower back is very sore and swollen. Although cat stretches helped relieve it a bit, I am worried that doing this long-term will cause problems. Are there any home relief methods and daily lower-back care suggestions?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: I suggest you apply a hot compress to your lower back for 15-20 minutes every day, or take a hot bath to promote blood circulation. When lifting heavy things, squat down first and then stand up, and avoid bending directly at the waist. You can try the superman exercise to strengthen your lower back muscles: the key point is to lie face down with your hands behind your back and raise your upper body and legs at the same time. If the discomfort persists, consider using a lumbar support belt.

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_117.text: How many times a day should I apply a hot compress? How exactly is the "Little Swallow" exercise done, and how many sets?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: Apply a hot compress 2-3 times a day, 15-20 minutes each time. Little Swallow exercise: Lie prone on the bed with your hands at your sides. As you inhale, slowly lift your head, chest, and legs; hold for 3-5 seconds, then lower them as you exhale. Do 10-15 reps per set, 2-3 sets a day. Do not use brute force.

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_117.text: If you've tried these methods and things still don't improve, under what circumstances should you see a doctor?

session_117.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_117.text: If the following conditions occur, seek medical attention: if the soreness and distension lasts more than a week without relief, or is accompanied by leg numbness, pain radiating to the feet, or affects normal walking, bending over and other daily activities. In addition, if sudden severe lower back pain or inability to stand occurs, seek medical attention immediately.

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_122.text: Today I helped my son Mingzhe with math word problems. Although I managed to explain them clearly, I'm afraid I won't be able to teach him when he encounters harder problems later. Do you have any simple, easy-to-understand tutoring methods?

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_122.text: You hope to find tutoring techniques that are suitable for a fourth-grade child and easy to master, to avoid your own educational level limiting the child's learning, right?

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_122.text: Yes, I'm just afraid that I won't know how to teach and will hold the child back. It would be best to use real-life examples so he can understand easily and I can explain easily.

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_122.text: You can try the 'read-the-problem-and-draw-a-diagram' method: have the child draw the numbers and relationships in the problem as a simple line-segment diagram, and then write the calculation. For example, for today's problem, you can draw it using the number of apples, and he'll understand it more easily. I also recommend the 'Primary School Math Sync' app, which has video explanations and real-life examples.

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_122.text: The drawing method is a good idea. I'll try it at home. I'll also download the app and take a look. Thank you!

session_122.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_122.text: You're welcome! Try it first, and feel free to ask me if there's anything you don't understand. When tutoring your child, you can also use “How do you think you should calculate it?” to guide his thinking.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: I'm going to set up a stall at the Jinghai District market tomorrow, selling my homemade pickled vegetables, scented sachets, and coasters. This is my first time selling pickled vegetables at a stall. I'd like to ask for advice on pricing and stall layout.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: Are your main concerns whether the pricing is reasonable, how to attract customers, and the details of stall layout? Also, have you considered the weather and the market management rules?

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: Yes, especially how to lay out the tasting samples, what prices to set, and whether it will rain tomorrow — I need to prepare for that.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: Suggest pricing small jars of pickles at 15-20 yuan, sachets at 10-15 yuan, and coasters at 5-8 yuan. Use small dishes and toothpicks for samples and place them at the front of the stall. Use a warm-colored tablecloth for the signboard to highlight the handmade feel. Tomorrow will be cloudy without rain, but bring a folding umbrella anyway. Peak foot traffic is from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., so take the chance to attract customers. For bookkeeping, a simple notebook separating costs and income is enough.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: What if customers haggle? I'm not good with words and don't know how to handle it.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: You can set a bottom price, for example, at least 12 yuan for pickled vegetables, 8 yuan for sachets, and 5 yuan for coasters. When customers bargain, smile and say, 'You have a good eye, let me round it down for you,' or throw in a small gift (for example, give a small dish with a purchase of pickled vegetables). The key is to keep smiling and be patient. As your mother said, just be friendly and greet customers warmly.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: Tomorrow I'm going to the market alone to sell pickled vegetables. It's my first time facing customers on my own, and I'm a bit nervous. Can you talk with me?

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: Are you worried about how customers will react to the pickled vegetables, or are you afraid you can't handle bargaining? Let's talk, and I'll help you sort it out.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: A bit of everything... and I'm also afraid of what if business is bad, or we run into a city inspector.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: Don't be afraid. The pickled vegetables are made by your own hands, so the taste is definitely fine. Get up at 6 a.m. tomorrow, bring a dark coat and flat shoes. At the stall, set up the sign first and actively greet customers. If someone bargains, smile and say, 'Homemade, give a fair price.' When business is slow, take a deep breath and think about how your husband supports you—he's watching the kids, so you can just run the stall with peace of mind.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_123.text: Hmm, hearing you say that makes me feel much more at ease. Then I'll check things again tomorrow morning and imagine customers praising how delicious the pickled vegetables are.

session_123.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_123.text: Yes, that's it. Set the alarm tonight and go to bed early. Tomorrow you'll be the best pickle stall owner—go for it!

session_124.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_124.text: I met a woman at the market today who wants to custom-order a pair of embroidered pillowcases and left her phone number. I've never taken a custom order before, and I don't know how to communicate about size, pattern, and pricing. Could you give me some advice?

session_124.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_124.text: Don't worry. The key to custom pillowcases is to clarify the requirements. Step 1: During the conversation, first ask about the customer's usage scenario (wedding/housewarming), preferred colors and patterns (such as mandarin ducks, twin lotus flowers), and the pillowcase size (commonly 48×74cm). Step 2: Estimate the labor hours and material cost based on pattern complexity. The local market price is usually 150-300 yuan per pair, so quote a mid-range price to leave room for negotiation. Step 3: Prepare a few photos of your embroidery work or simple sketches to boost the customer's confidence.

session_124.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_124.text: Understood, so I should first ask the client about the dimensions and pattern, and then discuss the price. I usually only know traditional stitches, such as running stitch and seed stitch. Are they suitable for pillowcases? How is the production time generally calculated?

session_124.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_124.text: The flat stitch and seed stitch are very suitable for pillowcases, giving a simple and elegant look. If the client wants exquisite detail, you can add a backstitch border. Estimate the production time based on the complexity of the pattern and 2-3 hours of work per day: simple patterns (such as the Fu character) take about 3-4 days, while complex patterns (such as mandarin ducks) require 7-10 days. Remember to communicate the schedule in advance and allow 2-3 days of buffer time to avoid breaching the agreement.

session_125.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_125.text: In the phone call, first ask about the size (single/double pillow), color preference, and material requirements. Pricing reference: a plain pure-cotton single pillowcase can be quoted at 25-35 yuan, plus 10-15 yuan for embroidery or special craftsmanship. For the sales script, first say, 'What color do you like? About what size?' Then quote the base price and the craftsmanship surcharge. If the customer haggles, you can lower the price by 5 yuan, but not too much.

session_125.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_125.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_125.text: If they think it's too expensive, you can explain that handmade pillowcases are good quality and more durable, and won't lose their shape after years of use, or recommend simplifying the craftsmanship (such as skipping embroidery) to lower the price. The key is to emphasize value while keeping records: name, phone number, needs, and quote, for easy follow-up later.

session_125.text: The pink-white gradient suits the softness of twin lotus flowers beautifully. I suggest using deep pink at the petal tips and transitioning to light pink toward the base, with short stitches of the same color family to blend in between. After finishing the petals, add a light border around the whole thing for a more lustrous look.

I recommend Singapore Math or Learn by Analogy; the problems progress step by step and are good for developing mathematical thinking.

session_127.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_127.text: I am embroidering twin lotus flowers on a bag for my son's graduation. I'd like to ask: how do I embroider the veins of the lotus leaf to make it look three-dimensional? Also, for the color scheme of orchid and bamboo, I used dark and light green, light yellow, and gray — is this combination appropriate? And how should I adjust the density of the short stitch to achieve a fluffy effect?

session_127.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_127.text: For a three-dimensional effect on the veins, it is recommended to use rolling stitch or overlapping stitch, following the direction of the veins. Each stitch should overlap two-thirds of the previous stitch to enhance the embossed effect. For the orchid color scheme, use dark green as the main color, grass green as the supplementary color, light yellow as an accent for the stamens, and gray for the shadows at bamboo joints, keeping the overall look harmonious. Use short stitches to simulate a fuzzy texture, with stitch spacing kept within 1.5mm. Choose fine woolen thread or two-ply silk thread, and keep the density above 30 stitches per square centimeter. After embroidering, gently brush the surface with a soft brush.

session_127.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_127.text: Are there specific rules for the needle direction in the overlapping stitch and rolling needle stitch? I'm worried that if the vein direction is wrong, it will look stiff. And as for the stitching order, isn't it easier to embroider the flowers first and then the stems and leaves?

session_127.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_127.text: The rolling stitch should be worked in one direction from the root to the tip along the direction of the stem veins. Each stitch is about 3-5 mm long, and when overlapping, keep the same slant so the veins look natural and smooth. It is recommended to embroider the main flower body first (twin lotus flowers on one stem), then the stems and leaves, and finally fill in the background, to avoid frequent thread changes. The light gray short stitches you are practicing can be used for shadow transitions after the main colors are done, to enhance the layering.

session_130.text: Low-salt spicy pickled cabbage is suitable at 15–20°C; 20–25°C is too high, so it is recommended to move it to a cooler place indoors. session_130.text: Persimmon vinegar is a viable substitute and can add flavor. Signs of spoilage: mold spots on the surface, off odor (rancid or putrid), and cloudy, bubbly liquid. If everything is normal, low-salt spicy pickled cabbage is ready to taste after 3-5 days, and sweet garlic tastes best after soaking for about two weeks.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_135.text: I just bought a yogurt maker and starter culture, and I want to make healthy yogurt for my little daughter; she is a bit constipated. Can you tell me the specific steps?

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: You want to make sure the first batch turns out as yogurt with plenty of live cultures, controlled sugar, and suitable for children with constipation, right? I suggest heating the milk to 40-45°C, adding the starter powder and stirring evenly, then putting it in a yogurt maker to ferment at a constant temperature for 8-12 hours. Sweeten with a little honey or fruit puree, store it in the fridge, and finish it within 3 days.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_135.text: How exactly do you judge when milk is heated to 40-45 degrees? And what difference does the length of fermentation time make?

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: You can measure it with a food thermometer, or feel the container by hand—it should be warm but not hot to the touch. Fermenting for 8 hours gives a moderate taste; the longer it ferments, the more sour it becomes. It's recommended to try 8 hours the first time. For your youngest daughter, it's best not to add sugar; pair it with natural fruit puree (such as steamed apple or banana) to add sweetness, which can also relieve constipation.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_135.text: Got it, I'll try tomorrow. How should the finished yogurt be stored?

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: After making it, put it in the refrigerator to chill immediately, and store for no more than 3 days. Use a clean spoon each time you take some out to avoid contamination. If your youngest daughter is constipated, let her eat a small bowl every day; pairing it with dragon fruit or prune puree works even better.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_135.text: My youngest daughter Ma Yuxin is 6 years old and has been constipated lately. This morning a health program said you can make yogurt at home. She had chive pockets for lunch. Besides yogurt, what other natural methods can help her regulate her system?

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: You can add high-fiber fruits and vegetables, such as dragon fruit, prune puree, and celery juice. Gently massage around the navel clockwise for 5 minutes every day. Encourage drinking more warm water and developing a regular bowel habit. In emergencies, you can use glycerin enemas, but avoid dependence.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_135.text: I've noted these methods. She's in kindergarten. Is there a probiotic suitable for a 6-year-old? Do we still need to go to the community clinic to see Dr. Wang?

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: You can choose children's probiotic powder. Pay attention to the strain and the number of live bacteria. If constipation has not improved after two weeks of dietary adjustment, or if it is accompanied by abdominal pain or blood in the stool, it is recommended to go to the community clinic and see Dr. Wang for an evaluation to rule out intestinal function problems.

session_135.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_135.text: Recommend taking the high-speed rail round trip (Tianjin West–Beijing South), with adult tickets about 50 yuan and children half price, totaling about 600 yuan in transportation. Accommodation is free. Tickets are mainly for Tiananmen, the Forbidden City, the zoo, and the science and technology museum; with the household registration booklet, children get free or discounted admission, and total tickets are about 500 yuan. For meals, bring some food plus simple dining, with a budget of about 800 yuan. The total is about 1,900 yuan, which can be split as saving about 160 yuan per month. Traveling in the off-season (March–April or October–November) saves more money.

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_136.text: I want to learn how to make homemade yogurt. Can you tell me the detailed steps and things to note? There are kids at home, so I want to make it healthy and frugal.

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_136.text: Of course. Key steps: 1) Boil the container to sterilize it; 2) Heat the milk to about 40°C (not hot to the touch); whole milk tastes better; 3) Stir according to the starter ratio in the instructions; 4) Keep warm and ferment for 6-10 hours (you can preheat the oven and then turn it off, or use the rice cooker's keep-warm mode); 5) After it sets, refrigerate for 2 hours to allow it to mature. Note: you can choose fresh milk or pure milk, but avoid skim milk; buy plain room-temperature starter powder; keep the fermentation temperature at 38-42°C; for children, you can use less sugar and serve with fruit or honey.

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_136.text: If there's no yogurt maker, can I keep it warm with a regular pot? How do I tell if the fermentation has succeeded? Can a very young child eat it?

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_136.text: You can wrap a thick pot in towels to keep it warm naturally, or use the electric rice cooker's keep-warm setting (around 40°C) to ferment. Success criteria: after it sets, there should be no flowing liquid when tilted, and the surface should be smooth with no cracks. It is recommended that children over 1 year old eat it in moderation, starting with a small amount on the first attempt. If you want to save money, you can save some of the homemade yogurt as a starter and use it next time.

session_136.text: The total cost is generally 800–1,500 yuan, including the door body, installation, and removal of the old door. I suggest you contact the manufacturer to confirm the security door rating (Class A/Class B), steel plate thickness, and lock cylinder grade (Class C is best). Before installation, clear the doorway, confirm the dimensions are correct, and ask for an itemized cost breakdown to avoid hidden costs.

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_136.text: Is the 300 yuan deposit reasonable then? About how much more will need to be paid later? What are the acceptance criteria during installation?

session_136.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_136.text: A deposit is reasonable, but remember to ask for a receipt. The balance is usually paid after installation, about 500-1,200 yuan. During acceptance, check that the door opens and closes smoothly, the gaps are even, and the lock cylinder is flexible, and ask for after-sales warranty details. For daily care, just lubricate the hinges and maintain the lock cylinder.

session_137.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_137.text: Just had the security door installed today, feeling much more at ease. But I don't know much about maintenance. With three kids at home, I'm worried they might mess with it. Could you teach me some precautions?

session_137.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_137.text: Of course. The new door should be opened and closed gently in daily use. The lock cylinder needs to be lubricated with graphite powder, not oil (which easily collects dust). Regularly check the weatherstripping on the door frame and replace it promptly if it ages or cracks. Separating your keys into red, yellow, and blue keychains is a good habit. I suggest teaching the children to be careful not to pinch their fingers when opening and closing the door. If conditions permit, you can install a magnetic door alarm to strengthen the sense of security against burglary.

session_137.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_137.text: I don't know about graphite powder. Can't I just use regular oil? And how can I tell if the rubber strip is problematic?

session_137.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_137.text: Ordinary oil absorbs dust and makes the lock cylinder stiff. It is recommended to buy specialized lock cylinder lubricant or pencil lead powder online. If the weatherstripping has become hard, cracked, or the door doesn't seal tightly, it should be replaced. You have made it a habit to check the door lock before bed, and with the 'Neighborhood Watch' sign you posted with your neighbor today, the overall defense is already good. You can also pay attention to community patrol reminders for extra peace of mind.

session_137.text: Sealed and refrigerated, it can keep for 2-3 months, with the best flavor in the first month. session_139.text: Your condition is most likely a shoulder muscle strain. session_139.text: Hello, I planted impatiens seeds a few days ago, and today I found a few small tender sprouts coming up. I'm really happy. But I've never grown flowers before and I'm afraid I'll ruin them. Could you tell me how to water, provide light, and fertilize during the seedling stage? Do I need to thin the seedlings?

session_139.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_139.text: Congratulations on successfully sprouting! Impatiens seedlings like sunlight but avoid direct exposure, so place them in a spot with diffused light. Water when the soil is dry to the touch—water thoroughly after the topsoil dries out. No need to fertilize for now; wait until 4-6 true leaves have grown before applying diluted liquid fertilizer. If the seedlings are too dense (spacing less than 5 cm), you can thin them out or wait until 2-3 true leaves appear before transplanting to ensure good ventilation and light.

session_139.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_139.text: Understood. I'll first pay attention to watering and sunlight. Do I need to thin the seedlings now, or wait a bit longer?

session_139.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_139.text: It is recommended to wait a few more days until the seedlings grow 2-3 true leaves before thinning or transplanting. This way the root system will be stronger and the survival rate higher. Then remove the weak and crowded seedlings, leaving the strongest few.

session_142.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_142.text: I made yogurt with a yogurt maker for the first time. Following the instructions, I put in the starter powder and milk and fermented for about 8 hours. It turned out extremely sour, and neither of the two children would eat it. Did I put in too much starter powder?

session_142.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_142.text: Your situation is most likely caused by fermentation that lasted too long. Generally, a yogurt maker ferments well at about 25°C for 6-8 hours. The longer it ferments, the more sour it becomes. Next time, I suggest shortening the fermentation time to 6 hours and controlling the starter culture ratio: 1 liter of milk to 1 gram of culture (a small packet is usually 1 gram). Also, choose whole milk for more stable fermentation. If it is still sour, you can add a little honey or jam before drinking.

session_142.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_142.text: So what else can this failed yogurt be used for? It would be a pity to throw it away.

session_142.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_142.text: You can keep it for face masks, spreading on bread, or use it in cooking instead of sour cream. Store it in the refrigerator and use it within 3 days. Next time you make it, remember to use a kitchen timer to avoid losing track of time.

session_143.text: Today I successfully made strawberry yogurt! My family all loved it, even the kids drank it all up. My husband even praised it, saying it tastes just like the ones sold in the supermarket.

session_143.text: It sounds like you really have a sense of accomplishment! Could you share how you went from failure to success? Did a friend give you some advice?

At noon I checked, and it had set like pudding. I added strawberry pieces and honey, and the sweet-and-sour taste was just right!

session_143.text: You really put care into the process, no wonder it tastes so good! Chunmei's method is very scientific, and you even added an innovative strawberry touch. Would you like to try other fruit flavors next time, like mango or blueberry?

session_144.text: You can establish a pre-departure checklist: ① tire pressure and wear ② fuel level and engine oil ③ documents (driver's license, vehicle license) ④ emergency items (first aid kit, flashlight, hangover tea). session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: I made homemade yogurt for the first time today and it was a great success! My family and neighbors all said it tasted good. But I'd like to make the texture richer and preserve it longer. Are there any good methods?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: Great! Succeeding on your first try shows you're careful. For a richer flavor, try whole milk with more starter culture and ferment for 10-12 hours; to extend storage, divide into portions and refrigerate, eating within 1 week, or freeze into yogurt ice cream bites.

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: Will it be too sour if the fermentation time is too long? I'm currently wrapping it in a blanket to keep warm — would switching to a yogurt maker make it more stable?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: Yes, the longer the time, the higher the acidity. It's recommended to try the taste after 6-8 hours first. The yogurt maker's constant temperature is more controllable and less likely to become too sour; if you buy starter powder, choose a classic one containing Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus for a higher success rate.

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: My 10-year-old Zhezhe always gets distracted when doing homework. He needs to be reminded several times for math problems. Are there any good ways to help him focus?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: You'd like to find specific ways to help an active, restless child improve focus and reduce the pressure of tutoring, such as adjusting the environment or breaking tasks into smaller steps?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: Yes, he can’t sit still, and I can’t keep watching him all the time. Is there a simple and effective little game or reward system?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: You can try the Pomodoro Technique: break the homework into 15-minute chunks, and after each chunk give him a star. Collect five stars in exchange for one free-play break. Also give him a quiet, fixed study corner with no electronic devices.

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: My husband is a truck driver and is out driving the night shift again tonight. I always worry. Can you tell me some safety precautions for nighttime driving?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: I understand your concern. Key points for night driving: 1. Do not drive continuously for more than 4 hours, rest for 15 minutes every 2 hours; 2. Use high and low beams correctly, switch to low beam when meeting oncoming vehicles; 3. Watch for signs of fatigue, and keep strong tea or mint candies to refresh yourself; 4. In bad weather, reduce speed and turn on fog lights. You can also agree with your husband that he sends a safe message or shares his location at every service area.

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_145.text: These are very practical. I check the doors and windows are locked every night, but I always want to express concern without disturbing him. Do you have any good suggestions?

session_145.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_145.text: You can agree on a simple signal with him, such as sending a specific emoji or short phrase when he reaches a service area, so you can feel at ease when you see it. Also, prepare common medicines, a thermos, and a flashlight in the car for him in advance; these small details can also convey your care.

session_146.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_146.text: Are you worried whether the current care is sufficient, especially water and fertilizer management and pest prevention? At this stage, the key is to supplement phosphorus and potassium fertilizer to promote flowering, while also paying attention to light and bud thinning techniques.

session_146.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_146.text: Yes, yesterday I applied diluted cake fertilizer and watered thoroughly, but I'm not sure whether the frequency is right, and I also need to prevent pests and diseases in advance.

session_146.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_146.text: It is recommended to apply a diluted fertilizer of monopotassium phosphate every 7-10 days, replacing the previous cake fertilizer. Water thoroughly when the soil is dry and keep the plant in sufficient sunlight. If the flower buds are too dense, remove the weak inner buds and keep the robust outer ones. Also check the undersides of leaves every 5 days to prevent powdery mildew and black spot.

session_147.text: I just received an embroidery order for 'Mandarin Ducks Playing in Water', 40 cm square. I'd like to ask about color combinations and stitching techniques. How do I show the layers of the mandarin ducks' feathers and the shimmering light on the lake water?

session_147.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_147.text: Traditional color suggestions: use a blue, green, and purple gradient for the male mandarin duck's feathers, and brown and white for the female; use a dark-green-to-light-green gradient for the lotus leaves and a pink-to-white gradient for the lotus flowers. For stitching, use long and short stitches or random stitch embroidery for the feather layers; use fine silk threads in mixed-color satin stitch for the shimmering lake water, adding a little gold thread to brighten it.

session_147.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_147.text: How exactly are long-and-short stitches and random stitches used on the wings? And what kind of texture of silk thread is better?

session_147.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_147.text: Use dark random stitches as a base at the root of the wing, alternate long and short stitches for the gradient in the middle, and finish the tip with fine, dense flat stitches. For silk thread, mulberry silk is recommended; its luster is soft and it looks more three-dimensional than cotton thread. It is suggested to draw a sketch first to allocate the color proportions.

session_149.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_149.text: I do needlework and housework every day. At night my shoulders feel tight. After stretching in the morning they feel comfortable, but they get tight again in the evening. Are there any more effective ways to relax? For example, something I can do during embroidery breaks, or should I change my pillow?

session_149.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_149.text: Suggestions: 1. While embroidering, every 30 minutes do the 'Angel Against the Wall' exercise (back against the wall, arms sliding up and down along the wall) to relax the shoulder blades. 2. After housework, apply a hot compress to the shoulders and neck for 15 minutes. 3. The pillow height should allow the head and neck to form a straight line with the spine when lying on your side, about one fist height. First adjust your posture, and if there is no improvement in two weeks, consider physical therapy.

session_149.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_149.text: Is the hot compress done at night? Also, how do I tell whether the pillow height is right when I lie down?

session_149.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_149.text: Hot compresses are best before bedtime or after housework to promote blood circulation. To judge pillow height: when lying on your side, your chin should be perpendicular to your sternum, with no feeling of twisting; when lying on your back, your neck should be supported and not suspended. The reference height is about 10-12 cm. After adjusting, observe for a week to see whether the tightness is reduced.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_150.text: Today I took my youngest daughter to the community's Dragon Boat Festival parent-child sachet sewing competition. She won the 'Cutest Award' and I am really proud of her.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_150.text: That sounds like such a warm moment! Would you be willing to tell me more about how Xinxin was making the sachet? I'd really love to hear about that process.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_150.text: Her little hand held the needle, and I guided her hand to sew. The stitches were crooked, but the judges said it was full of childlike charm. When she got the prize, she jumped up and down with joy, and the whole family gave her a thumbs up.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_150.text: This thoughtfulness and companionship are more precious than any award. You have given her the best gift for growing up. I believe this sachet will become a sparkling memory of her childhood.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_150.text: Tomorrow is the Dragon Boat Festival. I've prepared soaked bamboo leaves and glutinous rice and plan to make traditional Tianjin zongzi. The filling will include dates and red bean paste, but I'm not sure how long to cook them so they're fully cooked and hold together. I'd also like to confirm whether there are any wrapping techniques to ensure they're firm and no rice leaks out.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_150.text: When cooking zongzi, the water should cover the zongzi. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn to low heat and cook for 2-3 hours. During this time, you can add boiling water once to maintain the water level. A tip for wrapping them tightly: overlap two bamboo leaves and roll them into a funnel. First add a scoop of rice and press it down, then add the filling, and finally cover with rice until it is 90% full. Press it firmly with your fingers, fold the leaves over to cover, then tie tightly with string, wrapping it around several times and tying a firm knot.

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_150.text: Okay, I'll try. Also, I'd like to confirm the gift list: tomorrow afternoon I'll take the children to my parents' home to give zongzi, and give a few each to the neighbors Wang Guilan and Zhang Shufen. My husband Ma Zhiqiang will be back at noon, and then we'll arrange to watch the children's performance. Is there anything missing from this arrangement?

session_150.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_150.text: The list is very thorough. According to Tianjin customs, you can also hang mugwort and tie five-color braided strings for the children. You can hang the mugwort first thing tomorrow morning. Also, keep the room ventilated when boiling rice dumplings. The weather forecast for tomorrow is sunny, so it's convenient to take the children out. If needed, you can divide the rice dumplings into portions while they are still hot, and giving them as gifts while they are warm and heartfelt shows even more sincerity.

session_151.text: Do you want to increase pickle production and expand sales channels without significantly increasing costs? For example, improve the pickling process, find cheaper raw materials, or try taking orders through community WeChat groups?

session_151.text: It is recommended to start with a small batch test: focus on sample packs at the weekend market, start group buying on WeChat with at least 10 people, and take orders in advance before making. Just wash them clean. For home production, control the quantity to 3-5 jars so it does not take up space.

session_153.text: Tonight while putting up photos, my 10-year-old youngest son suddenly said to me, "Mom, when I grow up and earn money, I'll take you on that Ferris wheel too." I felt a lump in my throat at that moment, and my heart was warm and sweet.
