session_153.text: Moments like this are the most worth cherishing. In your child's growth, your love has planted the seed of gratitude. When the whole family really rides the Ferris wheel in the future, this memory will be even sweeter.

session_153.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_153.text: This morning I pickled garlic radish. This afternoon I tasted it and thought the saltiness was just right, so I've put it in the fridge. I want to know how long to pickle it for the best texture. My child thinks it's a bit spicy; can I add honey instead of sugar to adjust the sourness?

session_153.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_153.text: Garlic-flavored radish tastes best after being pickled in the refrigerator for 24 hours, and the spiciness will lessen over time. Replacing part of the sugar with honey can add a mild sweetness; a 1:1 substitution is recommended. For children's taste, reduce the amount of chili. It can be refrigerated for about 1-2 weeks. If the liquid becomes cloudy or develops an off smell, it has spoiled, and the pickling liquid should not be reused.

session_153.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_153.text: If we're adjusting the spiciness, can we put less garlic? Or would adding some Sichuan pepper oil affect the taste?

session_153.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_153.text: Reducing the amount of garlic does lower the spiciness, but it will weaken the garlic flavor. A small amount of Sichuan pepper oil (about 1 teaspoon) can be added to increase depth without overpowering the other flavors, but note how children accept it. It is recommended to test a small portion first and adjust in batches after confirming the flavor.

session_154.text: My husband drives a truck for a living and was just injured today. I want to buy him accident insurance. Our family income isn't high, so I'd like something low-cost that covers traffic accidents and fractures. Can you recommend one?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_154.text: I understand your needs. You're looking for accident insurance for a truck driver, focusing on traffic accidents and accidental medical coverage. Typically, short-term insurance costs tens of yuan per month or a few hundred yuan per year; long-term insurance is more expensive. Does your husband have social security or any existing commercial insurance?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_154.text: I only have New Rural Cooperative Medical Insurance, nothing else. I'd like to first understand the specific premium and how to buy it. Can you briefly explain?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_154.text: It is recommended to choose a one-year comprehensive accident insurance, and make sure it includes the 'commercial vehicle accident' clause. Monthly premium about 30-80 yuan, annual premium 300-800 yuan. Online purchase is convenient; you need to prepare your ID card, vehicle license, and occupation certificate. Pay close attention to the exclusion clauses, for example, drunk driving is not covered. You can first compare products from several major companies—should I help you sort out the key points?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_154.text: Today I started embroidering a picture of Mandarin Ducks Playing in Water to give to my friend Wang Juan. The draft is done, and I used red, yellow, and blue silk threads for the color scheme. In the afternoon I outlined the lotus leaf with chain stitch, but I'm not sure about the stitches for the petals and the mandarin ducks' feathers next. Do you have any suggestions?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_154.text: Chain stitch is a good base. For the mandarin duck feathers, I suggest using long-and-short stitches to create layers, with a gradient from dark blue to light blue. For the lotus, random stitch embroidery can add a three-dimensional effect, combined with a transition from pink to white. Pay attention to keeping the stitch tension consistent to avoid knots.

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_154.text: How should the transition between long-and-short stitch and random stitch embroidery be handled? Should I switch stitches directly, or should I leave a blank space?

session_154.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_154.text: I suggest first outlining the edge of the lotus leaf with a fine backstitch line as a boundary, then using random stitch for the lotus area and long-short stitch for the feather area. This way the stitch transition is natural and leaves no gaps.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_155.text: My husband Ma Zhiqiang is a truck driver. This morning I disinfected the wound on his right arm with povidone-iodine, applied a blood-activating and stasis-resolving ointment, and re-bandaged it. Currently there is no redness or swelling, but it itches a bit. I'm not sure if my care steps are correct. Do we need to go to the hospital for a follow-up?

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_155.text: Based on your description, the wound has no redness or swelling and is only itchy, which may be a normal sign of healing. But to ensure proper care, I need to confirm the frequency of iodophor and ointment application, the tightness of the bandage, and whether he needs to drive for work, which could affect recovery.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_155.text: Change the dressing with povidone-iodine twice a day, in the morning and evening, and apply only a small amount of ointment. His job requires driving, and I'm worried that movement will affect the wound. I also don't know how long it will be before he can return to work.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_155.text: Recommendations: Change the dressing once or twice a day; too much iodophor may irritate and cause itching. The ointment can be continued. If movement of the right arm is limited while driving, it is recommended to rest temporarily or use the left hand for assistance. Wounds usually take 1-2 weeks to heal, but a follow-up is needed to confirm there is no infection or deep injury. It is recommended to go to the community hospital for a check-up within 3-5 days. Eat more protein and vitamin C, and avoid spicy and irritating foods.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_155.text: Hello, my name is Ma Xiulan. My family's annual income is about 40,000 yuan, mainly from my husband. He was injured recently, and only then did I realize that insurance is necessary. Earlier I asked Dr. Wang in the community about accident insurance and got the salesperson's phone number. I just asked about the terms this afternoon and made an appointment to handle it tomorrow. But I'm not familiar with insurance terms and am afraid of being cheated. Could you help me interpret in detail the coverage, premium, and claim conditions of accident insurance? Ideally it should cover the whole family of three.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_155.text: I understand your situation. You need an affordable family accident insurance policy. The core points to focus on include: accidental medical treatment (reimbursement rate, deductible), disability/death payout, the relationship between premium and sum insured, and whether the sum insured is shared by the whole family. I suggest you focus on the accident medical reimbursement rate and deductible, as these directly affect the actual compensation amount. Also, family packages are usually more cost-effective than buying separately, but you need to confirm whether it covers you and your child.

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_155.text: Yes, what I most want to know is how to cover the whole family with the least money. This afternoon the salesperson said there is a family plan, over 600 yuan per year, with 10,000 yuan in accidental medical coverage per person, a 100 yuan deductible, and 80% reimbursement. But I don't understand whether this deductible and reimbursement ratio are actually worth it. And what materials are needed for claims?

session_155.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_155.text: This plan is within a reasonable range. A 100 yuan deductible means that only the portion of each accident expense exceeding 100 yuan is reimbursed. For example, if the expense is 500 yuan, the reimbursement is (500-100)*80% = 320 yuan. The 80% reimbursement rate is about average in the industry. I suggest you compare similar products from other companies; you may find a plan with a lower deductible (such as 0 deductible) or a higher reimbursement rate (such as 90%), but the premium may be slightly higher. Claims generally require medical records, invoices, an itemized list of expenses, a diagnosis certificate, an ID card, and a bank card, so it is recommended to keep all documents. In addition, pay attention to whether there is a waiting period (accident insurance usually has none) and whether it conflicts with medical insurance (usually it is more cost-effective to use medical insurance first and then commercial insurance for reimbursement).

For the recipe, make sure the saltiness is moderate and the spiciness is adjustable, and you can add a little baijiu to extend the shelf life.

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_157.text: Chunmei is coming on Sunday to taste my pickled cucumbers. I want to ask her to help me sell them on consignment at the supermarket. But this is my first time doing this, and I feel unsure. How should I prepare to make it proper?

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_157.text: I suggest you prepare in four areas: taste, packaging, pricing, and selling points. For taste, make sure the pickled cucumbers are crisp and refreshing; you can make a test batch for your family to taste. For packaging, use clean, sealed glass jars with handwritten labels. For pricing, refer to similar pickled vegetables in the supermarket; I suggest 12-15 yuan per jin. When introducing them, highlight your own pollution-free ingredients and traditional craftsmanship.

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_157.text: I've noted these points. But I'm still afraid that if I price too high they won't sell, and if I price too low I'll lose money. Also, how do I bring up consignment without it being awkward?

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_157.text: As for pricing, for the first cooperation you can set a promotional price of 10-12 yuan per jin, and adjust it later based on feedback. You could say this to the consignment seller: 'Chunmei, these pickles are homemade, but the ingredients are clean. Take two jars to the supermarket and try them out. If customers like them, we can discuss the commission.' This expresses sincerity and flexibility.

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_157.text: Today I'm embroidering an auspicious cloud bellyband. After finishing the coiled-gold embroidery, the thread ends are loose. How should I hide the thread and tie the knot to make it lie flat and smooth? Next I want to embroider cloud patterns. Do you have any stitch line suggestions?

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_157.text: When finishing off, use backstitch to secure twice on the back side. Thread the thread end into same-colored silk thread and hide it; after tying a double knot, gently pull so the stitching disappears into the fabric. For the cloud pattern, it is recommended to stitch from the outer curve inward. Each gold thread should span about 2 cm, and secure the connection points with short stitches. You can refer to the traditional 'gold outlining' technique to prevent loosening.

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_157.text: Got it. How exactly do you tie the double knot? And how do you prevent gold thread from oxidizing?

session_157.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_157.text: Double knot: wrap twice, then pull tight against the fabric, leave a 3 mm thread tail and snip it off. To prevent oxidation: lightly rub the gold thread with white wax before embroidering; after embroidering, store it sealed in a dark place with a desiccant. When you continue embroidering tomorrow, it is recommended to first try a small section of cloud pattern to confirm the stitch spacing, then expand to the larger area.

Guide him to use metaphors, such as 'The dumplings look like little ingots.' For typos, have the child read aloud, circle the incorrect characters for him, and then correct them orally.

session_161.text: The soy-pickled cucumbers I made today were a great success. In just over six hours they were crisp and flavorful, and my husband said they were delicious! But I'm afraid they won't keep long. How can I preserve them for a long time?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_161.text: Congratulations! Since the pickled cucumbers are sealed and refrigerated, I suggest dividing them into small jars, and try to finish each jar within a week. Set the refrigerator temperature to 0-4°C, and avoid freezing so the texture isn't affected. Need specific tips?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_161.text: Dividing into separate containers is no problem. I heard that adding high-proof baijiu can extend the shelf life—is that true? When sealing, should I leave any air in?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_161.text: Yes, a few drops of baijiu can inhibit bacteria and prevent spoilage. When sealing, press down as much as possible to expel air and reduce the air in the jar, then put it in the refrigerator. It is best to consume within two weeks. Next time, you can reduce the sugar to make it last longer.

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_161.text: I just gave the roses a thorough watering, moved the wilted hydrangeas to a shady spot, and also checked on the blue plumbago. In the summer heat, how should these three kinds of flowers be watered, fertilized, and shaded properly?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_161.text: It sounds like you already have some good habits, but you need a more systematic summer care plan. Roses like water but are afraid of waterlogging; hydrangeas wilt easily in high temperatures; blue snowflakes are heat-resistant but need timely pruning. Do you currently water once in the morning and once in the evening? How often do you fertilize?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_161.text: Yes, I usually water in the evening, and occasionally in the morning too. I can't remember exactly about fertilizing—about once every two weeks with compound fertilizer. How long will the hydrangea take to recover after moving it to the shade? How should the blue plumbago be pruned to make it more lush?

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_161.text: Watering in the evening is good, but also check soil moisture in the morning to avoid waterlogging at noon. After hydrangeas are shaded, the leaves usually stand upright in 1-2 days; during this period you can spray water on the leaf surfaces to cool them down. For roses, after the current flowers bloom, promptly cut off spent flowers and apply a phosphorus-potassium fertilizer once a week. For blue snowflakes, after flowering, cut off spent branches to encourage new branches to bloom. To prevent pests and diseases, it is recommended to regularly spray carbendazim or mancozeb, and pay attention to ventilation.

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_161.text: Got it. I'll go deadhead the roses right away, then trim the blue plumbago. I'll keep watching the hydrangea. Thanks for the reminder; I'll buy the insecticide tomorrow.

session_161.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_161.text: You're welcome. Remember to use sterilized scissors when pruning to avoid infection. Don't water at noon in summer; morning or evening is better. If the hydrangea is severely wilted, water it thoroughly and then cover it with a bag to keep moisture in. I wish your garden gets more and more beautiful!

session_168.text: I'm going to see a used Yadea electric bicycle tomorrow. The neighbor says it's 70% new and costs 400 yuan. My husband told me to test the brakes and battery, but I'm afraid of missing other problems. Could you help me list the things to check?

session_168.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_168.text: Okay, Ma Xiulan. Inspecting a second-hand electric bike can begin with the appearance, brakes, battery, motor, tires, lights and electrical equipment, and paperwork. I'll go through it in detail first; you can write it down.

session_168.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_168.text: Hmm, I'm forgetful. Take your time telling me, and I'll get a pen and paper to write it down.

session_168.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_168.text: Okay. First, check whether the frame has rust or deformation, and the welds should be firm. Second, test the sensitivity of the front and rear brakes and check the wear of the brake pads. Third, ask how long the battery has been used, how far it can go on a full charge, and whether the charging port is loose. Fourth, listen for any unusual noises when the motor starts and accelerates. Fifth, check the tire tread depth and whether the sidewalls have cracks. Sixth, test whether the lights, horn, and turn signals work properly. Seventh, ask the seller to show the invoice or receipt, and check whether the frame number and motor number match. If you inspect in this order, you'll have a clear idea.

session_170.text: Today I'm so happy! My eldest son Ma Mingxuan got double A's on the biology and geography mini high school entrance exam! Teacher Han, the homeroom teacher, personally called with the good news. I was buying groceries at the time and was so excited that my hands were shaking.

session_170.text: Two A's! That's really excellent. Ma Mingxuan must have put in a lot of effort. As a mother, you have always been concerned about his studies. This moment of joy is worth savoring.

session_170.text: Yes, this child has been studying late every day recently, so I've been restless too. Tonight the whole family is celebrating, and I've simmered his favorite chicken soup. Even his dad is grinning from ear to ear.

session_170.text: You celebrated with companionship and good food, and the family atmosphere was warm and happy. I believe this recognition will inspire Mingxuan to keep working hard, and the road ahead through high school and university will become smoother and smoother.

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_170.text: I just made some mildly spicy pickled cucumbers. A friend tasted them and said they have a sweet aftertaste and don't irritate the throat. Do you think this flavor has market potential?

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_170.text: It sounds like you've found a great selling point—spicy with a touch of sweetness and low saltiness. Can you tell me the specific ratio of spiciness to sweetness? And what about your pickling process—for example, did you add sugar or a sugar substitute?

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_170.text: The spiciness is about mild, and the sweetness comes from rock sugar; no sugar substitute was added. Now I'm mainly thinking about how to make it in batches, and whether the packaging should use sealed jars or vacuum bags.

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_170.text: Mild spiciness plus the sweet aftertaste of rock sugar is a natural, healthy selling point. For small-batch trial production, I suggest using vacuum bags with oxygen absorbers, which are low cost and keep things fresh. Later, you can consider glass jars to upgrade the presentation. Set the price about 10% higher than similar pickled vegetables in supermarkets, highlighting the handmade and low-salt features.

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_170.text: Besides supermarkets, what other sales channels would you recommend? For example, how do I get started with markets or community group buying?

session_170.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_170.text: You could first set up a tasting stall at the local weekend market, with 50g samples in mini sealed jars; after scanning the QR code to join the group, give away free tasting packs. For community group buying, I suggest finding 3-5 moms to serve as group leaders and offering a 10% rebate, centered on the story of 'traditional craftsmanship + a mildly spicy new flavor.' Online, use Douyin to shoot short videos of the pickling process, with the same-city location tag to drive traffic.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: Today, Director Li from the Jinghai District Cultural Center invited me to participate in next month's folk culture festival, but I still don't know exactly how to participate, such as how to apply for a booth, whether there are fees, and what requirements there are for works.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: It seems you want to learn in advance about the participation process and details of the cultural festival, including booth arrangements, fees, restrictions on types of works, and how to use this opportunity to display handicrafts and increase income?

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: Yes, I mainly do embroidery and also sell some pickled cucumbers. I want to know whether I'm allowed to sell food, whether I need to prepare promotional materials or business cards, and how to price them appropriately.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: Based on past years, the Jinghai District Folk Culture Festival usually provides standard booths for free, and you need to register at the Cultural Center one week in advance. The works are mainly traditional handicrafts; food items may require a food business license. It is suggested that you prepare hand-embroidered samples and simple promotional signs. For pricing, you can refer to market rates: embroidery should be priced by labor cost plus markup, and pickled cucumbers can be considered for small-package tasting promotions. For specific food regulations, you can contact Director Li to confirm.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: At noon today I recorded 180 yuan of market income in the family ledger. What's the best way to use this money? I also want to save up an education reserve fund and a travel fund.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: You have goals of five years of education and one year of travel. It is suggested to allocate this income proportionally: for example, 60 yuan for daily expenses, 60 yuan into an education reserve fund, and 60 yuan for small family pleasures or travel savings.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: That division is fine, but I originally planned to buy pork ribs tomorrow to improve our meals. Wouldn't that conflict?

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: Can adjust the proportions: 70 yuan for daily expenses (including pork ribs), 70 yuan for education fund, 40 yuan for travel fund. This way we can meet small improvements without delaying long-term goals. Keep recording incidental income every week; small amounts add up.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: My childhood friend Chunmei suggested that I either raise the price of the pickled cucumbers or do a buy-one-get-one promotion. I'm not sure what to do. At the market, they've been selling at 15 yuan a bottle, with a cost of about 8 yuan, and there are many regular customers. We're also participating in the cultural festival next week. Do you think this suggestion is workable?

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: Preliminary analysis: cost 8 yuan, selling price 15 yuan, gross margin about 47%, which is low among handmade foods. The suggested price increase is no more than 20% (i.e., 18 yuan), along with small tasting portions or bundling with low-priced embroidery items to attract customers. Gift-with-purchase suits you better than spend-and-save promotions. For example, buy two bottles and get a free pack of pickled radish, which raises the average order value without seeming expensive. If you are worried about losing regular customers, you can notify them a week in advance that the Cultural Festival special price will return to the original price afterward, to manage expectations.

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_171.text: Would raising the price to 18 yuan be too sudden? How exactly should the buy-one-get-one promotion be done to avoid losses? Also, do we need a permit to sell food at the cultural festival?

session_171.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_171.text: It is recommended to do it in two steps: first keep the original price, but launch a ‘Cultural Festival Limited’ new flavor (such as garlic cucumber) selling at 20 yuan to test the market; gradually raise the old product to 18 yuan and give a small side dish as a bonus. For the buy-one-get-one promotion, it is suggested: buy 2 jars of pickled cucumber (original price 30 yuan) and get 1 serving of pickled radish worth 5 yuan (cost 2 yuan), equivalent to a discount of about 13%. Regarding compliance: if you only occasionally sell homemade food at a market, you usually need to register as a small food workshop or obtain a temporary food business license; it is recommended to consult the local market supervision authority to confirm.

session_175.text: I have a lot of housework every day and often have a sore lower back. Stretching and hot compresses only help temporarily, but it keeps recurring. What are some scientific ways to relieve and prevent it?

session_175.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_175.text: You need a systematic waist-care plan fit for busy housework and fragmented time? It is recommended to start by correcting bending posture (such as squatting down to pick things up), doing 10 minutes of bridge and prone back extension exercises every day, and combining hot compresses with proper stretching timing.

session_175.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_175.text: Yes, I'm used to bending over to lift things, and I don't have time to set aside for exercise. How exactly do I do the bridge and the "little swallow" exercise?

session_175.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_175.text: Glute bridge: Lie on your back with knees bent, lift your hips until your shoulders, hips, and knees form a straight line. Hold for 5 seconds and do 10 reps. Superman exercise: Lie face down, lift your head and feet off the ground. Hold for 3 seconds and do 8 reps. Do these between meals or before bed, and be careful to avoid pain. You can add calcium to your diet, such as tofu and milk.

How do you control the recipe? Also, where should the samples be placed, and how should I promote them? I'd also like to hear some WeChat Moments marketing copy.

session_175.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_175.text: For the recipe: use ground dried Erjingtiao chili for the peppers. It has a mild heat, and the proportion should start at 0.5% of the total weight of the pickled vegetables. Control the salt at 3% of the finished product, adding it in two batches (80% during pickling and the remaining 20% after fermentation). Ferment at 25°C for 7 days for best results. For the promotion: place the samples in small dishes with toothpicks, independently portioned, in front of the cashier counter on the main aisle, and keep no more than 10 portions per batch to ensure freshness. For the buy-two-get-one-free offer, price it at cost plus 30% to guarantee gross margin. session_176.text: I was diagnosed with lumbar muscle strain this morning. The doctor taught me the cat stretch and wall-supported waist twists. session_176.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_176.text: Okay, Ms. Ma. For the Cat-Cow stretch, pay attention to four points: 1. Start on all fours, hands shoulder-width apart, knees hip-width apart; 2. Inhale as you arch your lower back and lift your head, exhale as you round your back and lower your head, using a range that does not cause pain; 3. Keep a slow pace, holding each movement for 3-5 seconds; 4. When rounding your back, curl up segment by segment from the tailbone. Wall-assisted waist twist: face the wall, place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart, and slowly twist your waist to one side while keeping your pelvis stable, twisting only to the point of a stretch in the lower back but no sharp pain. Recommended: 2-3 sets per day, 8-10 reps per set. Avoid sudden force or excessive backward leaning. If you feel stinging or numbness, stop and seek medical attention. Would you like me to break the steps down further?

session_176.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_176.text: You explained it very clearly. I want to confirm: in the cat stretch, do I need to arch my back to the highest point? Or is it enough to just feel a stretch? Also, since I make pickles and do embroidery every day, what daily movements should I pay special attention to?

session_176.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_176.text: You don't need to arch up to the highest point. It's enough to move the spine segment by segment and feel a stretch in your back. Over-arching may compress the lumbar spine. Daily precautions: avoid bending over for a long time (for example, washing or cutting vegetables); when sitting to embroider, put a cushion at your lower back and stand up to move around every 20 minutes; when moving pickle jars, use your legs rather than your back; sleep on a firm bed and put a pillow between your knees when lying on your side. If the pain does not improve within a week, a follow-up visit is recommended. Also, may I draw you a simple diagram of the posture?

session_178.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_178.text: I am 41 years old and a homemaker. I do a lot of housework, and lately my lower back has been sore and achy. Besides stretching and heat compresses, what are some simple ways to relieve and protect my back?

session_178.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_178.text: When lifting heavy objects in daily life, remember to squat with knees bent and keep your back straight. During breaks from housework, do a 5-minute wall sit. I also recommend the 'little swallow fly' exercise to strengthen the lower back muscles, 3 times a week, 15 reps each time. Apply heat compresses for 15-20 minutes each time, 2-3 times a day. If the pain persists for more than a week, it is recommended to see a doctor.

session_178.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_178.text: Do I need to buy a back brace or medicated plaster?

session_178.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_178.text: The lumbar support belt can be used when bending over for long periods or lifting heavy objects, but don't rely on it long-term, as it may weaken the muscles. For plasters, choose ones containing nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, such as flurbiprofen gel patches, for short-term relief of soreness. It is recommended to improve the condition fundamentally by exercising the core muscles (such as planks).

session_179.text: Today's promotion of my pickled cucumbers at Hualian Supermarket went very well. The manager said they want long-term cooperation and asked me to discuss details next week. I've never formally worked with a supermarket before. How should I prepare?

session_179.text: You want to understand the preparation before negotiation, including key points such as cooperation model, pricing strategy, and supply qualifications?

session_179.text: Yes, and I'm also unsure about the settlement period and how to sign the contract.

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_179.text: It is recommended that you first confirm whether your family has a food business license or a small workshop permit. Cooperation modes can be consignment (monthly settlement) or direct supply (weekly settlement). When pricing, consider cost plus 20%-30% profit, and reserve room for promotional discounts. The contract should focus on supply volume, settlement cycle, and liability for breach.

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_179.text: Haha, being able to laugh shows you have a great attitude! The lower back soreness stage is indeed suitable for low-impact exercise: I recommend a 30-minute walk every day, or try Baduanjin—the slow movements are kind to your back. Tai Chi is also good, but it's best to learn a few simple moves from videos first to avoid twisting your waist too much. If you want to keep it up at home, you can start with a 5-minute stretch and gradually increase it.

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_179.text: I've been doing cat-cow stretch, wall-assisted waist twists, and hip stretches for a few days now. Today the soreness in my lower back has noticeably eased, and the pain has also relieved. But I'm worried that improper form might hurt my back instead. Can you help me confirm the standard key points of these movements?

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_179.text: Congratulations on the improvement! For the cat stretch, when arching your back, let your spine curl up segment by segment, tuck your chin toward your chest, and do not over-arch your lower back. For the wall-supported waist twist, keep your pelvis stable and rotate only within a pain-free range. For the stretch at the back of the hips, keep your knees slightly bent and feel a stretch, not a sharp pain. I suggest holding each stretch for 15-20 seconds, doing 3-5 reps per set, and doing one set each morning and evening.

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_179.text: OK, I'll pay attention to the details. I feel better now. Can we increase the stretching intensity or add new movements? For example, combine them with daily activities like walking?

session_179.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_179.text: You can increase gradually: keep the current stretching amount for now, add 15–20 minutes of brisk walking every day, and keep your core engaged. Add new exercises like glute bridges (lying on your back and lifting your hips) and planks (starting with 10–15 seconds), 3 sets of each. Avoid suddenly bending over to lift heavy objects, and use a lumbar support when sitting. It is recommended that if you have no discomfort after 1–2 weeks, you can come back for a follow-up evaluation and then decide whether to progress.

session_182.text: That's feasible. When riding the electric bike, make sure every child wears a helmet, and Yuxin sits on the front footboard. For safety, put contact wristbands on the younger children, and agree on a meeting time and a place to disperse.

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_182.text: I set three summer rules and eye-care guidelines for the kids, but they only agreed verbally and haven't followed them yet. I'd like to ask whether these rules are reasonable and how to motivate them to follow them voluntarily.

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_182.text: You hope to assess the scientific validity of the rules and obtain specific implementation strategies, especially for your lively second son, Mingzhe?

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_182.text: Yes, especially study time and eye-protection measures—how do you balance enforcement and encouragement?

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_182.text: For a primary school student, one hour of study time is reasonable; it can be split into 25 minutes of focused work plus 5 minutes of rest. For housework and garden work, a points system is recommended: give a sticker reward for each completed task, and exchange accumulated stickers for small gifts. Add a rule to the eye-care guidelines: look into the distance for 1 minute every 20 minutes, using a timer as a reminder to reduce children's resistance. Mingzhe is active, so you can make him the "little execution squad leader" to supervise himself. Try it and adjust based on feedback?

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_182.text: I do a lot of housework, and my waist is always uncomfortable in the morning and evening. Can you recommend some scientific waist rehabilitation exercises and waist protection methods?

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_182.text: We understand that you have been doing housework for a long time and your lower back shows signs of strain, so you need safe and effective rehabilitation training and daily care guidance. It is recommended to first learn the lower back extension movements in the McKenzie method, as well as the plank exercise to strengthen the core muscles; 10-15 minutes each session is sufficient.

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_182.text: I did some stretching this morning, but I don't know if I was doing it right. How can I protect my lower back when doing housework? Do I need to use a lumbar support belt or go see a doctor?

session_182.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_182.text: The correct bending posture is to squat with knees bent and keep your back straight; using a long-handled mop can reduce strain on your lower back. A lumbar support belt can be used short-term during acute pain, but don't rely on it long-term. If the pain keeps getting worse or you develop numbness in your legs, I suggest going to the community clinic to see Dr. Wang. Today you can start with cat-cow stretch and dead bug exercise, 5 minutes after breakfast and dinner each day.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Today I made a heat-relieving summer soup with mung beans, red beans, and coix seeds at a ratio of 1:1:0.5. The whole family said it tasted good, but I'd like to ask how to adjust the sweetness to make it even better?

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: Suggestion: halve the sweetness; use rock sugar instead of white sugar for a cleaner, more refreshing taste. Adjust the bean ratio to mung beans:red beans:coix seeds = 2:1:1 for better heat-clearing and dampness-removing effects. For children, one small bowl per serving is enough; avoid serving it too cold to protect the stomach.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Will halving it make it too bland? My Mingzhe always wants to drink more, and I'm worried he'll get diarrhea.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: The taste is still good after halving the amount, and you can also add a small amount of lily bulb or mint leaves to enhance the fragrance without adding sugar. For children, each serving should be no more than 200 ml; it is safer to let it sit for 10 minutes after taking it out of the refrigerator before drinking. Next time, you can try mung bean soup with a little dried tangerine peel instead to beat the heat and whet the appetite.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: I'm embroidering tiger-head shoes to give to my neighbor, but the tiger head never looks lively enough. Are there any tips?

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: Do you mean the three-dimensional look of the tiger head's facial features, or the color combination that makes it more lifelike?

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: It's mainly about the three-dimensionality of the facial features - how to embroider the eyes and beard more vividly.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: For the eyes, embroider the outline with backstitch, fill the middle with flat stitch leaving highlights; for the beard, use French knots or long-and-short stitch to add layers. Finish the edges with overcast stitch to keep them neat, and the embroidery will look smoother.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Just finished video chatting with my mom, feeling a bit more at ease, but I'm still worried that my parents won't turn on the air conditioner in Tianjin's muggy weather. I've been busy with the kids lately and haven't had time to go see them. I feel a bit guilty.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: You worry about your parents' health and also feel guilty for being too busy to go home often. You need some practical heatstroke-prevention advice and tips for caring about your parents from afar, right?

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Yes, especially how to explain to them that air conditioning doesn't use much electricity, and what warning signs of heatstroke to watch out for.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: You can tell your parents to set the air conditioner to 26–28°C and to use it with a fan to save electricity; also, open the windows for ventilation twice a day. The warning signs of heatstroke are dizziness, fatigue, and nausea. Once they appear, they should immediately move to a cool place and drink water. I suggest you make a fixed 3-minute phone call every day to ask how they are feeling, so both sides can rest easy.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Today was truly busy and fulfilling, and I feel a deep sense of accomplishment.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: It sounds like you gave a lot to your family today. Would you like to share some specific little joys with me?

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_183.text: Yes, Mingxuan's handwriting is much neater than before, Yuxin has also started putting away her toys by herself, and the summer soup I made was also praised by everyone in the family.

session_183.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_183.text: Your efforts have made the family warmer, and behind every bit of the children's progress is your care. You're really great.

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_184.text: Today I planted mint seeds on the kitchen windowsill. I have never grown them before. Can you tell me how to water them and give them sunlight from now on? My little daughter also wants to help take care of them.

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_184.text: Before mint sprouts, keep the soil slightly moist and just spray water with a watering can every day. Germination requires 20–25°C and sufficient light, but avoid direct scorching sunlight. It usually sprouts in 7–14 days, and no fertilizer is needed before emergence. If your little daughter joins in, you can have her take charge of spraying water daily and recording the growth of the sprouts.

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_184.text: Okay, then how do I prevent mint seedlings from growing too tall (leggy)? Also, how long before I can pick the leaves to use?

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_184.text: To prevent leggy growth: after seedlings emerge, move them to the sunniest windowsill with at least 4 hours of direct light per day, or use a grow light; pinch off the top when the seedlings reach 10 cm tall. Generally, tender leaves can be harvested 40-50 days after sowing, picking one-third each time and leaving the base to keep growing.

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_184.text: Today I finally succeeded in practicing the buttonhole stitch! The first two attempts failed, and the third time I embroidered even buttonhole stitching, which gave me a great sense of accomplishment. Next I want to embroider bamboo leaves, but I always feel the stitch variations aren't realistic enough. Can you recommend some common stitching methods for bamboo leaf embroidery? For example, how to use long-and-short stitch and rolling stitch?

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_184.text: Congratulations on successfully mastering the overcast stitch. This is indeed an important step in advancing your handcraft skills! For the bamboo leaf embroidery, I suggest using long and short stitches to show the layers of the leaves, and rolling stitches to outline the leaf veins; with green gradient thread, it will be more vivid. In addition, you could add a few small flowers or a bow to the handkerchief as decoration, which would be suitable for display at next week's community exchange meeting. Do you need the specific stitch steps?

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_184.text: Could you describe the specific steps of the long-and-short stitch and the rolling stitch in detail? Also, for the color gradient I plan to use a transition from dark green to light green, and I'd like to add some simple little patterns to the corners of the handkerchief. What do you recommend?

session_184.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_184.text: In the long and short stitch, straight stitches of different lengths are arranged alternately to simulate the light and shade of leaves; the stem stitch, on the other hand, uses continuous, tightly spaced small stitches and is suitable for outlining. For color gradients, you can first embroider a dark green base and then add light green for the transition. For the corners of a handkerchief, I recommend embroidering small daisies or four-leaf clovers — simple and cute. There are many illustrated guides on Xiaohongshu. Would you like me to put together an illustrated tutorial for you?

session_185.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_185.text: Tomorrow my husband Ma Zhiqiang is coming home after driving a truck. I want to make him a welcome-home dinner. What's good to eat in summer? I'm torn between steamed sea bass and braised pork ribs. Could you recommend a main dish and give a home-style recipe and shopping list? It should be economical.

session_185.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_185.text: Steamed sea bass is more suitable for summer, light, fresh, not greasy, highly nutritious, and reasonably priced (about 25 yuan per fish). For the main dish, this is recommended, paired with cucumber salad and stir-fried water spinach. Shopping list: 1 sea bass, ginger, scallions, steamed fish soy sauce, cooking wine; 1 cucumber, garlic, vinegar; half a jin of water spinach. Total budget about 50 yuan. Would you like detailed cooking steps and fish-selecting tips?

session_185.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_185.text: This combination is good. Tell me more about how to pick fresh sea bass, and what would you recommend for a simple soup after the meal?

session_185.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_185.text: When choosing a sea bass, check that the eyes are bright and not sunken, the gills are bright red, and the body is firm and springy. For soup, tomato egg drop soup (sweet and sour, appetizing) or mung bean soup (cooling) are recommended, each costing about 5 yuan. Steaming steps: score the fish, rub with cooking wine and ginger slices, steam for 8 minutes after the water boils, pour off the liquid, top with shredded scallions, and drizzle with hot oil and steamed fish soy sauce. Advance preparation: after buying, wash and refrigerate it, and steam it fresh tomorrow.

session_186.text: Today I met neighbor Wang Guilan at the vegetable market. She said she has a new marinade recipe to try next Wednesday when we make pickled vegetables together, but I didn't ask for details. Can you help me think in advance about what ingredients and proportions are common for new-style pickled vegetable marinades?

session_186.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_186.text: Would you like to know in advance the ingredients of the new sauce Wang Guilan might use (such as the proportions of soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, spices, etc.) and the complete pickling process for cucumbers or radishes, including cutting, sun-drying, putting them into the jar, sealing time, and details for preventing spoilage during storage?

session_186.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_186.text: Yes, mainly the recipe and step details, so that next Wednesday I can cooperate well and the taste can be even better.

session_186.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_186.text: Common new-style pickled vegetable sauce: 300 ml soy sauce, 100 ml black vinegar, 80 g sugar, 200 ml boiled cooled water; add 10 Sichuan peppercorns, 2 star anise, and 5 slices of ginger, bring to a boil, then cool. Pickling process: cut vegetables into strips, salt them and let sit for 4 hours to dehydrate, sun-dry for half a day until the surface is slightly dry, put into a jar, pour in the sauce to cover the vegetables, seal and refrigerate for 3-5 days for the best texture. session_189.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_189.text: The cold noodles I learned at my parents' home today were especially delicious, but after returning home I'm afraid I'll forget the details. Can you tell me the proportions of sesame paste, vinegar, and garlic water, and the specific method for boiling and cooling the noodles? Also, how should the leftover noodles be stored?

session_189.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_189.text: No problem! Dilute the sesame paste with warm water until it can flow; the ratio is about 1 part paste to 1.5 parts water. For the garlic water, mash 3 garlic cloves, add 2 spoonfuls of cooled boiled water, and let it steep for 10 minutes. Mix vinegar and light soy sauce at 1:1, and add 1 spoonful to each bowl of noodles. Cook the noodles until just done, then immediately plunge them into ice water (ice water works even better). Soak for 20 seconds, remove, and toss with oil to prevent sticking. Any leftover cold noodles should be sealed and refrigerated and eaten within 24 hours. Before eating, you can add a little hot water and mix them well.

session_189.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_189.text: Then if I use dried noodles instead of hand-pulled noodles, should the cooking time be shorter? And how much chili oil should I add?

session_189.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_189.text: Dried noodles cook faster than hand-rolled noodles; after the water boils, cook for 2-3 minutes, then rinse with cold water as well. Chili oil depends on personal taste; it is recommended to add half a spoonful first and add more if it is not enough. Cucumber shreds and blanched bean sprouts are the best side dishes.

session_191.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant

I suggest your husband consult a doctor first. In addition, combining it with the Shenshu acupoint (1.5 cun lateral to the lower border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra) gives better results. I will send you a set of illustrated instructions and a video of daily health exercises.

session_195.text: You want the exact recipe for traditional pickled cucumbers and radishes so you can guide your neighbor Wang Guilan in making the marinade. Could you tell me how many jin of vegetables you have prepared? That way I can give you the precise gram measurements for the seasonings.

session_195.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_195.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_195.text: Suggestion: 10 jin each of cucumbers and radishes, salt 500 g, and let dehydrate for 2 hours. For the sauce, use 1,500 g light soy sauce, 500 g dark soy sauce, 800 g sugar, and spices (20 g fennel seeds, 15 g cinnamon bark, 20 g star anise). Bring to a boil, then let cool. You can add 100 g high-proof baijiu as a preservative. After filling the jar, seal it and store in a cool place. Turn the jar once a day; it can be eaten after 7 days.

session_197.text: The day before yesterday I moved jars and cut radishes, and now my lower back is really sore. This morning I pressed Zusanli and Hegu acupoints, but it didn't seem to target the lower back. Are there any acupressure methods specifically for relieving lower back pain?

session_197.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_197.text: This is lumbar muscle strain from labor. You need acupoints for the lower back. I recommend Yaoyangguan, Shenshu, and Weizhong acupoints, which can unblock the meridians and relieve soreness.

session_197.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_197.text: Where exactly are these three acupoints? How should I press them myself for it to be effective?

session_197.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_197.text: Yaoyangguan is in the depression below the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra (level with the iliac crest); Shenshu is 1.5 cun lateral to Yaoyangguan; Weizhong is at the midpoint of the popliteal crease. Press and knead each acupoint with the thumb for 2-3 minutes; the effect is better when combined with medicated oil. Before bed, apply a hot compress to the lower back for 15 minutes and then massage, which can reduce the next day's soreness.

session_199.text: Today when practicing Baduanjin, the bending motion strained my lower back. It still feels sore and swollen after soaking in mugwort water in the evening. What are some simple and effective home care remedies?

session_199.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_199.text: You can try applying a hot compress to your lower back for 15 minutes to promote circulation, then rub your palms together to warm them and massage the yaoyan acupoints clockwise, along with cat-cow stretches. Also, when doing housework, try to bend your knees instead of your waist to avoid adding strain.

session_199.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_199.text: How exactly should I do the hot compress and massage? Do I still need to go to the community clinic to see Dr. Wang?

session_199.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_199.text: For heat therapy, use a hot water bottle at 40-45 degrees Celsius and avoid scalding the skin. For massage, press and knead the sorest point in the lower back (Shenshu acupoint) with your thumb for 3 minutes each time. If it doesn't improve within three days, or if you develop numbness in the lower limbs, it is recommended to go to the clinic to see Doctor Wang to check for lumbar muscle strain.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: I took three custom round-fan orders at the market today. I need to embroider lotus flowers, peonies, and a photo pattern provided by the customer. I usually figure things out on my own without professional pattern references. I'd like to ask for advice on composition, color matching, and stitching techniques so I can draw patterns that satisfy customers.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: Understood. For the lotus, I suggest a 'withered lotus' composition to highlight the layered petals, with a pink-to-white gradient and blue-green lotus leaves for color. For the peony, a 'garden full of wealth' composition works, with the main flower in deep crimson or pinkish purple, paired with golden yellow stamens; for the stitching, use flat stitches for the base colors and layered stitches for the outlines. For the client's pattern, first trace it onto the fabric with carbon paper or a water-soluble pen, then adjust the embroidery density according to the original image. Tomorrow I can start with a rough sketch, then refine the colors and stitches.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: The lotus uses a pink-to-white gradient and the peony a deep crimson; this color combination works very well. The client's pattern is quite complicated, and direct tracing would lose details. How can we preserve the original feel?

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: Use a projector or phone screen to enlarge the pattern, place it on a light box or window glass, and trace the outline; if the lines are too fine, first enlarge the spacing with a pencil, then refine with a water-soluble pen. Seed stitch is suitable for small detailed textures (such as flower stamens), while running stitch is suitable for large areas of color. While maintaining a traditional feel, add a refined touch with transitions between light and dark shades.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: Today, for the first time, I set up a stall under the name 'Sister Ma's Handmade'. When I got home, I put all the money into the Beijing trip fund envelope, feeling one step closer to taking the whole family to Beijing.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: That's great! All your hard work from early morning to late night has paid off. The clever food tasting and embroidery demonstration must have helped a lot. With this 180 yuan plus the custom order, the travel fund is growing fuller. The day your family visits the Forbidden City and watches the flag-raising ceremony is getting closer!

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: Tomorrow I'm going to make tomato sauce with neighbor Wang Guilan. I'd like to learn a simple homemade method and precautions.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: Choose fully ripe tomatoes, peel and mash them, add a little salt and sugar. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes. While hot, pack into glass bottles sterilized at high temperature, invert the bottles to release air and seal them. The key to avoiding mold is sealing the lids tightly and sterilizing thoroughly.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: How long should glass jars be boiled to sterilize them? Is it okay not to add sugar?

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: Boil the glass jars and lids for 10 minutes. It can be made without sugar, but adding sugar enhances flavor and preserves; just add a small pinch of salt, not too much.

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_200.text: What are the common failure points? How can we coordinate with Aunt Wang on dividing the work more efficiently?

session_200.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_200.text: Common failures: tomatoes too watery, sticking to the bottom when simmered, and leaking seals. Division of labor suggestion: you take charge of selecting ingredients and peeling; Aunt Wang, who has more experience, can mainly handle the simmering and bottling. With the two of you cooperating, it will go more smoothly.

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_201.text: Today I took my daughter to the painting awards ceremony. Her painting "Mommy Pickles Vegetables" won third prize, and I was really happy!

session_201.text: I can feel your pride and joy! The fact that your child used paintbrushes to record your pickling scene shows that she treasures your company. Can you tell me more about the award ceremony?

session_201.text: What a warm scene! Your family celebration is full of love. When Xinxin grows up and sees this painting and this memory, she will be even more moved. This family happiness is truly precious.

session_201.text: I just set up a savings plan for a Beijing trip, saving 400 yuan a month. Next summer vacation, the whole family of five will go. Can you recommend attractions and estimate roughly how much it will cost?

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_201.text: All right, Ms. Ma. Here is the budget suggestion for a family of five: transportation (train or bus from Tianjin to Beijing, about 500 yuan), accommodation (budget hotel for 3 nights, about 900 yuan), tickets (Tiananmen is free, Forbidden City 240 yuan, Great Wall about 200 yuan, zoo 90 yuan, etc.), and meals about 300 yuan per day. The total is about 3500-4000 yuan. Given that you save 400 yuan a month and 4800 yuan a year, it is basically feasible.

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_201.text: So how should we arrange a few days' itinerary to get the best value? Also want to stop by Daxing to see my sister on the way.

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_201.text: Suggested 3-day itinerary: Day 1, Tiananmen + Forbidden City (children can gain historical knowledge); Day 2, Great Wall (go early to save on transportation); Day 3, Zoo + visiting relatives in Daxing. Stay at a budget chain hotel, and bring a water bottle and snacks to save money.

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_201.text: I just learned the rolling needle stitch and seed stitch from a video, and embroidered a three-dimensional little pink flower on plain white silk. I feel so accomplished! How do you think I should apply these new stitches to the lotus and peony pattern on the round fan next?

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_201.text: Sounds like you're improving quickly! Rolling stitch is suitable for outlining the fine veins of lotus leaves, and seed stitch can express the texture of stamens or petals. When you're currently embroidering small flowers, do you find the tension of the thread easy to control? This will affect the effect on curved outlines later.

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_201.text: True. With seed stitch, if the thread is too tight it clumps up, and if it's too loose it doesn't hold its shape. I tried several times before I got it even. The lotus petals have large curves, and I'm worried the lines will go crooked when turning with the rolling stitch. Do you have any tips?

session_201.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_201.text: When making a turning with the rolling stitch, you can shorten the stitch spacing to 1 mm and keep the thread tail slightly looser on the inside of the turn. For seed stitch used in the dense stamen area, it is recommended to use finer silk thread (for example, 2 strands) so each seed is smaller and more delicate. Next time you can first practice curved turns on a small piece of cloth before starting on the round fan.

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_203.text: Excuse me, I'd like to confirm the roof repair by Master Liu tomorrow. What exact time will he arrive? Do I need to prepare anything in advance?

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_203.text: According to your previous records, Master Liu is expected to arrive at around 9 a.m. tomorrow. It is recommended that you clear the clutter from the roof tonight and move items near the kitchen sink, and prepare buckets to catch water just in case. He has already prepared all the materials; you just need to make sure someone is at home.

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_203.text: Okay, what if it rains again tomorrow? Are there any contingency measures?

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_203.text: The weather forecast shows that the rain will stop and turn cloudy tomorrow, but to be safe, you can spread a waterproof tarp on the roof (Master Liu may bring one) and prepare indoor containers to catch water. If sudden heavy rain occurs during the repair, have him pause and cover temporarily. You can also close the kitchen doors and windows to reduce the risk of water getting in.

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_203.text: Aunt Wu will teach me more complex Suzhou embroidery by video next week. I want to prepare in advance. What stitching methods and materials should I know about?

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_203.text: You have mastered the rolling stitch and the seed stitch. Next week, at the advanced level, you can learn basic Suzhou embroidery stitches such as the satin stitch and the long-and-short stitch. It is recommended that you prepare fine embroidery thread, plain silk gauze, a small embroidery hoop, and simple flower-and-bird pattern templates.

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_203.text: What are the key points of straight stitch and long-and-short stitch? How should the embroidery hoop be secured so it doesn't slip?

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_203.text: The even stitch requires the needle to enter and exit on the same line, with parallel, equal-length stitches; the layered stitch is inserted in staggered layers, so the color transition looks natural. For the embroidery hoop, wrap soft cloth strips around the frame edge, then tighten the fabric, or use tape to secure the corners to prevent loosening.

session_203.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_203.text: My family's annual income is 40,000 yuan. I just decided to set aside 200 yuan a month for a maintenance fund. I also need to save for a trip to Beijing within a year and for an education reserve fund within five years. How should I plan my income and expenses to make it enough?

session_203.text: It is recommended to first calculate monthly fixed expenses and surplus: after deducting the maintenance fund, allocate the remaining amount according to goal priority. The Beijing trip is estimated to need 5,000-8,000 yuan, which can be saved as 500 yuan per month over 12 months; set aside 200 yuan per month for the education reserve fund. For daily groceries and household items, you can make a list and compare prices to save 10%-15% of expenses.

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_204.text: This morning I learned the Zusanli, Hegu, and Fengchi acupoints from Aunt Zhao, but I'm afraid I've misremembered the locations and techniques. Could you explain in more detail?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_204.text: Of course. Zusanli is four finger-widths below the outer knee. Press it with your thumb until you feel soreness and distension, for 3-5 minutes each time. Hegu is in the web between the thumb and index finger on the back of the hand; rub and press it for 2-3 minutes. Fengchi is in the hollows on both sides of the hairline at the back of the head; press upward with both thumbs for 3 minutes. It is recommended to do this in the morning or one hour after meals, and to avoid being overly hungry or too full. Which acupoint's effects would you like to explore in more detail first?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_204.text: I want to know all of it! Also, is there a particular best time for massage? Can it be combined with Baduanjin?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_204.text: Zusanli strengthens the spleen and harmonizes the stomach; the best time is during the Chen hour (7-9 a.m.) when the stomach meridian is active. Hegu relieves pain and unblocks the meridians; it can be pressed for headaches, but it is forbidden for pregnant women. Fengchi dispels wind and clears heat; pressing it in the early stage of a cold or in the afternoon works well. When combined with Baduanjin, pressing each point for 2 minutes before and after practice can enhance the overall health benefits. You can start with one acupoint per day and gradually become proficient.

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_204.text: My son Zhezhe always sits crookedly when doing homework, keeping his eyes too close to the book. My verbal reminders don't work well. Are there any scientific ways to correct his posture and prevent myopia?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_204.text: In addition to maintaining 'one foot, one inch, one fist,' it is recommended to adjust the desk and chair height (about 30 cm from the desktop to the eyes), use a posture corrector or an eye-protection lamp (40 cm in front and to the left), and every 25 minutes take a 5-minute break to look into the distance or do eye exercises.

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_204.text: After 40 minutes of embroidery, my right wrist feels sore and swollen. I've stopped and applied a hot compress. Are there any more effective ways to relieve it? How can I prevent carpal tunnel syndrome in the long run?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_204.text: Do you need immediate relief suggestions for wrist soreness and swelling (such as specific massage movements, stretching exercises) and long-term preventive measures (such as daily hand exercises, wrist brace recommendations, reasonable rest intervals)?

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_204.text: Yes, for example, wrist guards suitable for embroidery and advice on rest breaks.

session_204.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_204.text: Recommend doing five-finger exercises and wrist flexion and extension daily. Take a 5-minute break every 25 minutes of embroidery. Wear an elastic wrist brace. If soreness persists after hot compresses, alternate with cold compresses. Seek medical attention promptly to rule out tenosynovitis.

session_205.text: My right wrist has been sore all day. Baduanjin, embroidery, and playing badminton are all affected. Even with a wrist brace and the rolling-needle embroidery technique, it still feels uncomfortable. Are there any ways to relieve it?

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_205.text: It may be caused by fatigue or improper posture. It is recommended to rest the wrist first and avoid repetitive movements. Within 24 hours of the soreness, apply ice; afterward, apply heat. Also do simple stretches, such as pressing fingers gently with palm facing down.

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_205.text: Should I apply ice or heat now? Do I need to see a doctor?

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_205.text: If your wrist has no redness, swelling, heat, or pain (acute inflammation), apply a warm compress to promote circulation; if it is red, swollen, or stinging, apply an ice compress first. If it doesn't improve after two days of rest or gets worse, go to the hospital for an orthopedic examination.

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_205.text: Got it, thank you. So how should I protect my wrists when doing housework and embroidery on a daily basis?

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_205.text: When doing housework, use a wrist brace to relieve stress and choose long-handled or labor-saving tools. For embroidery, rest every 20 minutes and do wrist extension and fist-clenching exercises to relax. As for Baduanjin, you can do the 'Holding Up the Heavens with Both Hands' movement gently, but don't raise your arms too much.

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_205.text: Ma Xiulan: I'm embroidering a round lotus fan. I use the rolling needle stitch for the petals, but how should I handle the veins of the lotus leaves and the gradient colors without hurting my wrist?

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_205.text: For the lotus leaf, I suggest using long-and-short stitch in color blocks, working outward from the leaf veins. Wear a wrist brace and rest every 15 minutes of embroidery—it saves effort and adds depth.

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_205.text: Yes, I was also thinking of trying the overlapping stitch. By the way, my little daughter is curious about lotus flowers. Do you have any interactive suggestions?

session_205.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_205.text: You can have her help sort the embroidery thread by color, or practice straight stitches with a safety needle on the edge of the cloth. That cultivates her interest and is safe. After it's finished, mount it together and give it to Grandma; that will give you even more of a sense of accomplishment.

session_207.text: I borrowed a dozen or so children's books from my younger sister's house. I want to organize them into the newly freed-up bookshelf at home. How should I sort and arrange them so that the children will love reading them?

session_207.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_207.text: You want to plan the categories according to the ages (13, 10, and 6) and interests of the three children, and create an inviting reading atmosphere, right?

session_207.text: You can layer by age group: put picture books for the 6-year-old on the top shelf, storybooks for the 10-year-old on the middle shelf, and classics for the 13-year-old on the bottom shelf. session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_208.text: Hello, a couple of days ago I carried something heavy while shopping, and my right wrist started to feel sore and swollen. Last night after half an hour of embroidery it became sore again. I've applied a hot water bottle and worn a wrist brace, but they haven't helped much. Do you have any daily care methods?

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_208.text: Hello. Your condition is likely wrist strain or early tenosynovitis. Recommendations: 1) Apply a hot compress for 15–20 minutes, 2–3 times a day, with water temperature at 40–45°C, to avoid burns; 2) Use a towel to elevate your wrist when resting; 3) Do simple stretches, such as slowly moving the palm up and down, making a fist, and then opening it. In addition, avoid lifting heavy objects and prolonged embroidery in the near future.

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_208.text: OK, thank you. I happen to be learning acupoint massage from Aunt Wu. Are there any acupoints on the wrist that can be massaged? Also, how long is suitable for embroidery in the future?

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_208.text: For the wrist, massage Yangxi (the depression at the base of the thumb), Yanggu (the wrist crease on the little-finger side), and Daling (the midpoint of the wrist crease on the palm side). Press each acupoint with your thumb for 30 seconds, using pressure that feels sore but tolerable. While embroidering, rest for 5 minutes every 30 minutes and move your wrists during the break. If the pain worsens or redness and swelling appear, see a doctor promptly to check for tenosynovitis.

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_208.text: I plan to record a video of making family-style pickled vegetables tomorrow morning, but I have never filmed one before. Could you give me some script ideas and filming suggestions?

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_208.text: What you need is a script framework and filming key points for short videos about homemade pickles? For example, ingredient preparation, production steps, precautions, and how to appear on camera naturally?

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_208.text: Yes, I wrote the basic steps in my memo, but I'm not sure how to storyboard it or how to face the camera and speak without being nervous. I hope there's a simple, practical template.

session_208.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_208.text: It's recommended to use a three-part script: 1. Opening introduction (the reason for pickling and showing the ingredients), 2. Close-ups of the key steps (cutting vegetables, putting them into the jar, mixing the sauce, with narration), 3. Showing the finished product and storage tips. Keep the video to 3-5 minutes, and write a short narration script in advance and stick it next to the camera. When shooting, practice smiling at the camera first; mistakes can be edited out later, so don't get nervous and mess up.

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_212.text: Tomorrow I am going to make tomato sauce with my neighbor Wang Guilan. I have prepared ripe red tomatoes, glass jars, and rock sugar. Could you tell me the specific steps? Especially how to thoroughly sterilize the jars, how much sugar to add, and whether I should add citric acid or salt for preservation?

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_212.text: Okay, Ma Xiulan. The traditional steps for making tomato sauce are: peel and chop the tomatoes, add rock sugar while simmering (generally 1-2 jin of sugar for 10 jin of tomatoes), cook until thick, then bottle while hot. To sterilize the bottles, boil them in water for 10 minutes or bake them in an oven at 100°C for 15 minutes. It is recommended to add a little lemon juice (about half a teaspoon per jin of tomatoes) to adjust acidity and help preserve; no need to add salt. After sealing, turn the bottles upside down to cool, which creates a vacuum. They can be stored at room temperature away from light for six months, and refrigerated after opening.

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_212.text: Will inverting the jars to cool create a vacuum seal? After sealing, do I need to boil them again to sterilize them? The children want to help—what safety issues should I watch out for?

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_212.text: Inverting the jars does create a vacuum. When filling, leave a 1 cm gap at the top, tighten the lids, and invert immediately. For extra safety, after bottling you can boil the jars in boiling water for 10-15 minutes (the water should cover the jars). When children join in, let them help wash the tomatoes and pass tools, but keep them away from the hot pot and boiling water, with a parent supervising at all times.

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_212.text: Got it, that puts my mind at ease. Just store it in a cool place, no need to refrigerate, right? I'll follow your ratio for the sugar, thanks!

session_212.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_212.text: That's right. As long as the seal is intact and the jars are successfully inverted, just store them in a cool, dry place. After opening a jar, remember to refrigerate it and finish it within a week. I wish you and Wang Guilan a smooth collaboration, and may the whole family enjoy the delicious tomato sauce!

Also encourage him to write down one life-related physics question every day; discussing topics like car structure with his dad while walking can also spark his interest. In addition to physics, set aside time to solidify other subjects.

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_218.text: For double-sided embroidery, it is recommended to use a rotatable embroidery hoop for easy turning. Alternating between flat stitch and laid stitch can create a gradient effect; to hide thread ends, use the 'backstitch thread-hiding method' by weaving between stitches on the back. It is recommended to borrow a teaching video from Zhou Xiuqin, or search for 'Suzhou double-sided embroidery illustrated tutorial', and focus on practicing the 'seed stitch' for pomegranate seeds. Choose silk or high-density cotton-linen fabric for a finer look.

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_218.text: My son Xuanxuan is in the second year of junior high school. He always says he is confused about buoyancy in physics. I only have a middle school education, so I am not good at explaining it myself. When I was tutoring him in the evening, I found some short videos, but I am not sure whether he understood. Could you recommend some ways to explain buoyancy for beginners? For example, everyday examples or simple experiments?

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_218.text: You'd like to find an intuitive, easy-to-understand way for your child to learn buoyancy, preferably letting children understand the principle through everyday phenomena or hands-on experiments, while reducing your tutoring pressure, right? For example, using swim rings, stories about ships, or experiments with mineral water bottles?

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_218.text: Yes, yes, that's exactly what I need! I don't have much education; formulas are too abstract, and the child won't listen. Can you tell me specifically how to do it? Or do you have any reliable online course platforms to recommend?

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_218.text: You can do this: 1. Explain Archimedes' principle through a story, such as the story of water overflowing from a bath; 2. Do a simple buoyancy experiment: fill a mineral water bottle with water, put in a small stone and a ping-pong ball to observe sinking and floating; 3. Recommend Bilibili's "Physics Master" or Kuaishou education bloggers; search "buoyancy middle school" for animated explanations; 4. Start with basic multiple-choice questions and then move on to calculation problems, using a mistake notebook to consolidate.

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_218.text: The experiment and the story are quite good; I can try them tonight. But how do I know he really understood? I'm afraid he nodded on the surface but didn't actually get it.

session_218.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_218.text: You can have him restate the principle in his own words, for example, “Why does a boat float on water?” Or have him design a simple experiment to verify the relationship between buoyancy and the volume of displaced liquid. In addition, have him do one or two after-class exercises and explain the reasoning behind each step, which better tests his mastery than directly looking at the answers.

session_219.text: I settled with Aunt Sun at the vegetable market today about selling pickled vegetables on consignment, and gave her two jars of sweet garlic. But I don't know how to determine a fair price and profit split, and what varieties should I add later?

session_219.text: Pricing can refer to similar pickled vegetables on the market, with cost plus 30%-50% profit. session_219.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_219.text: Then how can the packaging improve the appearance? Should we pickle more before the Mid-Autumn Festival?

session_219.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_219.text: Use small glass bottles or food-grade sealed jars, and stick on homemade labels reading “Sister Ma's Pickles” and the date.
