session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_289.text: Today I went to my mom's place and learned a few low-fat dishes: steamed sea bass, garlic broccoli, and cold black fungus salad. I made them for my family when I got home, and my husband said the fish was tender and had no fishy smell. I want to organize the steps clearly so I can follow them later and also send them to my sister, but I'm afraid of missing key details. Can you help me sort it out?

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_289.text: I understand you want to systematically save the low-fat recipes you learned today from your mother Li Xiuying, so you can recreate and share them easily. I suggest you dictate the key steps for each dish (such as removing the fishy smell from steamed sea bass, marinating time, and heat control), and I'll organize them into a clear structured list and add some suggestions for adjusting to family tastes. Does that work for you?

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_289.text: Okay, let me first talk about my best dish today, steamed sea bass: the fish should be marinated with ginger slices and cooking wine for 10 minutes in advance. When steaming, put the fish in after the water boils, steam on high heat for 8 minutes, pour off the liquid after taking it out, then drizzle with steamed fish soy sauce and hot oil. When blanching the broccoli, I added a little salt and oil, so the color was bright green. The dressing for the seasoned black fungus, my mom said, was light soy sauce, vinegar, minced garlic, and a little sugar, but I didn't completely remember the proportions.

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_289.text: Noted! I'll help you fill in the recommended ratio for the cold black fungus dressing: 2 tablespoons light soy sauce, 1 tablespoon black vinegar, 1 tablespoon minced garlic, and half a tablespoon sugar. You can add bird's eye chilies to taste. I'll compile the three recipes into an electronic document, including the steps, heat levels, and storage tips. I suggest you also write them down in a small notebook for easy reference. I can also recommend a few similar low-fat dishes: blanched shrimp, steamed chicken breast, and lettuce with oyster sauce. Do you want me to teach you how to make them too?

Her dad and I walked behind chatting about everyday things, and I felt very grounded. I want to remember this moment.

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_289.text: How lovely! It sounds like you enjoyed a peaceful and warm autumn evening. I can help you turn this record into a short story or a family journal for future memories. Want to give it a try?

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_289.text: Okay, write that down for me. Also, I'd like to know how to cultivate children's curiosity about nature, like Xinxin asking about the stars.

session_289.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_289.text: You can arrange an outdoor observation activity once a week, such as using a phone star-identification app, collecting different leaves for specimens, or drawing the scenery during a walk together. Gradually guide them to ask questions and explore.

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_290.text: I am Ma Xiulan, mother of three children. Last night I made a low-fat dinner, and the children said it had no flavor. Zhe Zhe wants ketchup. Is there any way to make healthy dishes taste better?

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_290.text: You want to stay low-fat and healthy while getting your child to accept it. You can use natural seasoning methods: ketchup is low-fat by itself, and you can pair it with lemon juice and minced garlic to enhance the flavor. Let your child participate in choosing seasonings—for example, reduce salt gradually and use spices to replace part of the salt.

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_290.text: Yes, the kids love ketchup and herbs. Do you have any specific recipes? For example, how to use them in steamed fish and cold dishes?

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_290.text: For steamed fish, drizzle with ketchup and steam with ginger strips. For cold dressed spinach, add a little ketchup, aromatic vinegar, and sesame seeds. Multigrain porridge can be paired with diced apple to add sweetness. Gradually reduce salt and oil, and your taste will adapt after two weeks.

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_290.text: Last night the whole family watched 'Havoc in Heaven'. My 13-year-old son Xuanxuan suddenly asked me, 'Why did the Great Sage Equal to Heaven make havoc in Heaven?' My answer was somewhat simple, but I felt I didn't explain it thoroughly. He usually likes to think. I'd like to take this opportunity to guide him to understand the themes behind the story—rebellion, freedom, rules—without sounding too preachy. Can you give me some advice?

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_290.text: You want to explain to a 13-year-old child the deeper motives behind Sun Wukong's havoc in Heaven in a way he finds interesting, while naturally weaving in positive values, right?

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_290.text: Yes, he is very curious, but rather introverted. I'm afraid that if I reason with him directly, he won't take it in. I want a way to answer his questions while also getting him to think for himself.

session_290.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_290.text: You can first turn the question back to Xuanxuan: "If you were Sun Wukong, invited to the Peach Banquet but not given a share, how would you feel?" Let him put himself in the character's shoes to understand the reasons for anger and rebellion. Then point out Sun Wukong's pursuit of equality and freedom, and connect it to real life: pursuing rights also requires following rules, just as a class has class rules. Finally, recommend the youth edition of the original Journey to the West and the relevant episodes of the documentary China in Classics, and encourage him to keep exploring.

session_290.text: Today I was busy from morning to night—exercise, housework, cooking, spending time with the kids... I feel really fulfilled, but also a bit tired. Would you like to hear about it?

session_290.text: It sounds like you had a very fulfilling day, and now you really want to share that satisfaction and exhaustion, right? Tell me, what made you happiest?

session_291.text: Today I used ketchup to draw a smiley face, used a mold to press sweet potatoes into flower shapes, and mixed chopped baby bok choy into the steamed egg with minced meat. session_291.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_291.text: You can try vegetable puree steamed buns or colorful dumplings, such as spinach juice mixed into dough for green wrappers and carrot puree mixed into meat filling; or use pumpkin puree to make noodles. For different age groups, the 6-year-old daughter needs more protein and iron, and the 10-year-old son needs calcium and vitamins; pairing fish, tofu, and seasonal vegetables works better.

session_291.text: Absolutely! Have your daughter help wash vegetables, tear the lettuce, use molds to press out shapes, or whisk the eggs. The second son can be in charge of peeling garlic and weighing the ingredients. A sense of involvement can increase acceptance. I recommend low-cost, high-nutrition ingredients: seasonal spinach, broccoli, tofu, and eggs. Combined, they are both inexpensive and balanced.

session_291.text: Soaking feet in mugwort dispels cold and dampness and helps sleep; Baduanjin regulates qi and blood and strengthens bones and muscles; Zusanli strengthens the spleen; Yongquan point calms the mind. In winter, yam and pork rib soup and red date ginger tea are recommended, simple and easy to make. In addition, water temperature around 40°C for foot soaking with 3–5 minutes of massaging Zusanli works better.

session_291.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_291.text: Can you tell me the exact locations of the Zusanli and Yongquan acupoints again? I'm afraid of pressing the wrong acupoint.

session_291.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_291.text: Zusanli is on the outside of the lower leg, four finger-widths below the lower edge of the kneecap; Yongquan is in the depression at the front third of the sole. Press with the pad of the thumb and you should feel soreness and distension.

session_295.text: Hello, from next Wednesday to Friday I'd like to cook a few home-style dishes, such as corn and pork rib soup, steamed pork ribs with garlic, and pickled fish. Could you tell me the specific recipes and low-oil, low-salt cooking techniques?

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_295.text: It sounds like you want to adjust the cooking method to reduce oil and salt without cutting out the dishes your family loves, while still keeping the flavor. I understand you're worried the children and your husband will get tired of the food, so you need some seasoning ideas, such as using vinegar and ginger to replace some of the salt and soy sauce. Right?

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_295.text: Yes, especially how to make pickled cabbage fish low in oil but still full of flavor, and how to make steamed eggs more tender and silky. These are what I'm not sure about.

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_295.text: For the pickled cabbage fish, first marinate the fish slices in egg white and a little salt, stir-fry the pickled cabbage with a small amount of oil until fragrant, then add water to make the broth. Finally, stir-fry Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies until fragrant and pour over the fish slices, avoiding a large amount of frying oil. For the steamed egg, use a 1:1.5 water-to-egg ratio, steam over medium heat for 8 minutes, turn off the heat and let it sit for 2 minutes, add a few drops of vinegar to remove the fishy smell and enhance freshness, without using oil.

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_295.text: Great, these methods are really practical! Is there a low-oil variation for the corn sparerib soup? Also, from Wednesday to Friday I'd like to add some autumn seasonal vegetables. Could you recommend a few?

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_295.text: For corn and pork rib soup, blanch the ribs and then simmer them in clean water, skim off the surface oil, cut the corn into sections, and add carrots and water chestnuts to enhance the sweetness. No oil is needed. In autumn, wild rice stems, lotus root, and pumpkin are recommended, prepared by blanching or plain stir-frying, seasoned with shredded ginger and vinegar.

session_295.text: Yesterday evening while walking with my husband, we talked about next month's heating fee. Based on previous years, it's about 1,500 yuan. I'd like to confirm in advance the 2025 fee standards, payment methods, and whether there are any ways to save money.

session_295.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_295.text: Central heating for residents in Jinghai District is billed based on floor area, at about 25 yuan per square meter. If your home is about 60 square meters, 1,500 yuan is reasonable. You can pay online via Alipay or WeChat before November 15. There is a heating subsidy for low-income families; it is recommended to consult the community office or heating company about application requirements. To save money: add weatherstripping to doors and windows, set the temperature to 18–20°C before bedtime, and use sunlight during the day, which can save 10%–15% of costs.

session_300.text: I went to Jizhou for a study visit today and learned how to make hawthorn jam and chili sauce, but the recipes I noted down are scattered. session_300.text: You mainly want to confirm the sugar-to-fruit ratio of the jam, the details of sterilization and bottling, and the oil temperature and stir-frying order for the chili sauce, to make sure they can be turned into shelf-stable products for extra income from a side business?

session_300.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_300.text: Right, the farmer said the ratio of sugar to fruit for the hawthorn jam is about 1:3, but I'm not sure whether to add water or lemon juice, or how to sterilize the jars, or when to add the fermented black beans to the chili sauce.

session_300.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_300.text: For hawthorn jam, the recommended sugar-to-fruit ratio is 1:2 to 1:3. Add an appropriate amount of lemon juice to adjust acidity and prevent spoilage. Boil glass jars in water for 10 minutes or dry them in an oven at 120°C. After bottling, turn the jars upside down to create a vacuum. For chili sauce, first stir-fry fermented black beans and spices over low heat to release aroma, then drizzle with cooked oil to bring out the fragrance, and avoid scorching.

session_300.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_300.text: Today at the Moshangyin Guesthouse in Jizhou I saw handmade items on consignment. The owner was interested in my pickled vegetables, so we exchanged WeChat contacts. session_300.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_300.text: Suggested first step: send samples first (3-5 jars of pickled vegetables and a few small embroidered pieces) to the boss for a trial sale, and arrange details in person. Common profit splits are 50-50 or 40-60. For the first batch, I suggest 20 jars of pickled vegetables, using glass jars with simple labels highlighting “Jizhou farmhouse flavor.” The cost is about 5 yuan per jar, and the retail price is 15-20 yuan. Use bubble wrap for shipping to prevent breakage. Start with a small batch to test market response.

session_300.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_300.text: Flavor issue: first hold a tasting event, preparing different levels of spiciness for tourists to vote on. For packaging, transparent plastic bottles are lighter and cheaper, and the label design should be simple and distinctive. In terms of cost, buying bottles and labels in bulk can bring it down to 3 yuan per bottle. Regarding permits: contact the local market supervision and administration bureau to ask whether a small-workshop license is needed. Usually, small-batch homemade goods sold on consignment carry low risk, but it is recommended to first make a verbal agreement and obtain the license later when sales stabilize.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: Aunt Wu suggested adding sugar and vinegar to brighten the chili sauce's color, but I'm not sure exactly how much to add, when to add it, and whether it will affect the saltiness and shelf life. Is the method the same for mildly spicy and medium spicy?

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: Add 15 grams of white sugar and 10 grams of aromatic vinegar per jin of pickle base. Add them in the mid-to-late stage of cooking (5 minutes after the sauce comes to a boil), stir evenly, and let it boil for another 3 minutes before turning off the heat. This ratio does not affect saltiness. The vinegar helps prevent spoilage, so the shelf life remains unchanged. It is suitable for both mild and medium spiciness. If honey or lemon juice is available, it can replace part of the sugar and vinegar, but use half the amount.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: My son Xuanxuan is in the second year of junior high school and has a math problem he can't solve. I only have a middle school education myself and can't explain it clearly. Is there a good way to handle this?

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: What you need is a way to explain middle school math problems in plain language, or reliable free tutoring resources, such as instructional videos or a problem-solving app?

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: Yes, best if it's simple and easy to understand, something the child can understand on their own.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: Recommend using the free videos from Onion Math or Khan Academy to search for relevant knowledge points by grade. Also, encourage the child to read the problem first and draw a picture to list the unknown conditions; you just need to stay with them and help sort out their thinking.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: I sent the pickled vegetable list to the homestay owner three days ago and haven't heard back, so I'm a bit anxious. My husband told me to take the chili sauce to next month's handicraft market and try it out, but I don't know how to contact the owner without seeming presumptuous, and what should I pay attention to at the market?

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: You need communication skills for following up on cooperation, practical guidance for the market, and you also long for confidence support. Don't worry, we'll take it step by step.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: Yes, I just want to get these two things straight first. Otherwise I'll keep worrying—the household expenses and the children's school fees depend on this to make up the difference.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: For the B&B owner, send a gentle WeChat message tomorrow with a line like 'Samples can be sent to you anytime for a taste.' As for the market, it is recommended to apply for a stall first, set prices based on similar products plus a 30% profit margin, and use transparent small bottles with handwritten labels to highlight 'farmhouse homemade,' which can quickly attract customers. In addition, many housewives earn more than 2,000 yuan a month after half a year from a small side business, so you can start by testing the waters at a weekend market.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_302.text: That's a good suggestion. I'll do it tomorrow. But time-wise, I have to take care of the family and prepare for the market, so I'm afraid I won't be able to manage it all.

session_302.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_302.text: You can set aside 8 to 9 pm every evening to focus on preparing the pickles, and your family can lend a hand bottling them on weekends. Don't rush in the early stage; first get one market stall running smoothly, build up repeat customers, and then think about expanding. Your husband supports you; that is your greatest source of confidence.

session_303.text: I just embroidered an auspicious-cloud Ruyi pendant with blue-green silk thread, filled with dried lavender flowers. It took 1 hour and 40 minutes. session_303.text: Yes, the Spring Festival is coming. I'd like to embroider some festive decorations, such as zodiac signs or 'fu' character pendants, but I'm afraid the patterns are too complicated. Practice with thicker stitching first, then upgrade to fine embroidery. For the market, I suggest making a few samples to test the waters, such as small ruyi hanging ornaments or phone charms. They are low-cost and easy to match. You can also provide custom embroidery services. The auspicious cloud pattern you embroidered before was very popular, so you can reuse that element.

session_303.text: You need actionable techniques for developing writing habits and time management methods, and also want to respond to Xinxin's need for parent-child cooking?

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: Great! Your weight and waistline have both gone down, and the discomfort in your waist has also eased. It shows your light diet and morning Baduanjin exercise are really effective. This is the result of persistence!

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_304.text: Yes, last month my back was still hurting badly, but now it feels much more comfortable. I use less oil and salt every day and also keep a health journal. I feel really motivated.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: You're doing very well! Behind these numbers is your daily self-discipline, especially controlling oil and salt and persisting with Baduanjin. Keep it up, and you will definitely become healthier, and your family will be proud of you!

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_304.text: Recently I adjusted our home diet to a lighter taste, cutting down on oil and salt. My husband's acid reflux has improved, and the kids are no longer picky eaters. I want to keep optimizing. What are some low-oil, low-salt recipes that suit the whole family and that children like, and how can I stick with them long-term without getting bored?

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: Try to use more steaming, boiling, stewing, and cold-tossed dishes, such as: tomato fish fillets (low oil), steamed eggs with shrimp, stir-fried broccoli with minced garlic. Use vinegar, lemon juice, and spices (such as rosemary and turmeric) instead of salt. Design a themed dish every week (such as Monday as 'Light Meal Day'), and pair it with Baduanjin morning exercise to boost energy. Keeping a food diary also helps maintain motivation.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_304.text: Baduanjin sounds good; I usually don't have an exercise habit. Also, what if family members sometimes want strong-flavored food? On the weekend I'm going back to my parents' home to tell them about these changes—how can I explain it in a simple and easy-to-understand way?

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: Baduanjin takes just 15 minutes a day, the movements are simple, and you can do it with your family. For strong-flavor cravings, you can leave one free meal per week, but control the portions. When visiting her parents' home, use data to make the point: the reduction in oil and salt, her husband's stomach acid improving, and the children no longer being picky. Emphasize that light cooking benefits the whole family, and her mother will find it easier to accept.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_304.text: Tonight we held our month-end review meeting. The children all made progress: the eldest moved up 5 places in the monthly exam, the second child is more patient with his little sister, and the third learned three embroidery stitches. The whole family also agreed to take a half-hour walk every day and spend less time on phones and more time reading.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: So happy to hear that! Behind your child's every small progress is your devoted companionship, and the family meetings and agreements are a continuation of good habits. This sense of steadiness and satisfaction is worth cherishing.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_304.text: Yes, I hope to keep this kind of family atmosphere. What methods can help the children follow the agreements more proactively?

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: You could try turning the agreement into a visual check-in chart, such as putting a star sticker on it after completing a task each day, and then holding a small commendation meeting at the end of the month. It is both interesting and motivating over the long term, and your husband's encouragement is also an important support.

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: You want the activity to ensure kitchen safety while letting Xinxin participate hands-on, and to add some small games for fun? For example, pressing patterns with molds, counting dumplings?

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_304.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_304.text: For the pancakes, use a low-sugar batter recipe; let the child stir it, then you pan-fry them. When wrapping dumplings, give her small dough pieces to flatten and press into shapes with cookie cutters; intersperse guessing games about quantities to practice math.

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_306.text: I just signed up for a computer training class for middle-aged and older adults, and classes start next Thursday. I don't know anything about computers, so I feel a bit unsure. What will the class teach? Do I need to prepare anything in advance?

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_306.text: Training classes usually start from the very basics, such as turning the computer on and off, using the mouse and keyboard, and typing, and then gradually move on to surfing the internet, chatting on WeChat, and so on. You don't need to be nervous—the course is specifically designed for absolute beginners. I suggest you prepare a notebook and a pen for taking notes; a USB flash drive would be even better for saving study materials. You can simply skim the textbook—you don't have to understand everything, because the teacher will explain in detail in class.

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_306.text: Don't I need to learn typing first? I'm worried I won't be able to keep up with the course pace.

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_306.text: There is no need to learn typing in advance. The teacher will start with pinyin or handwriting input. You can gradually become familiar with it by practicing typing for 10 minutes every day. Ask more questions and take notes in class, and review the textbook whenever you have time at home; you will definitely keep up. Once you learn it, you can video call your sister in Beijing, look up information for your children, and life will be much more convenient. Take it easy, you can do it!

session_306.text: Do you mainly want to save on daily grocery shopping, household supplies, and education expenses? For example, by finding more cost-effective shopping channels, or by planning menus to reduce waste?

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_306.text: Suggest trying community group-buying platforms; there are often discounts after 8 p.m. Go to the vegetable market half an hour before closing to hunt for cheap produce. Make a weekly menu in advance and buy only what you need to reduce waste. For bookkeeping, use a category budgeting method, for example, set a fixed 300 yuan per month for groceries, and deduct any overspending from other categories.

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_306.text: This is a good idea! The child's computer class is too expensive at 150 yuan. Are there any ways to save money?

session_306.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_306.text: You can look into free computer classes at the local library, or study online on MOOC platforms. For educational supplies, buy textbooks on second-hand platforms and save half the money. Each month, force yourself to save 500 yuan in a dedicated account as a reserve fund for the children's education.

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_308.text: I bought Chinese cabbage and radishes today, and the jars are washed and dried. I want to make pickled cabbage and soy-marinated pickled vegetables. How much salt should I put? Should I add spices?

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_308.text: So you'd like to learn the recipe and steps for making traditional pickled Chinese cabbage? Should I provide the salt-to-cabbage ratio, spice options, and methods to prevent spoilage?

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_308.text: Right, there's also the pickling time and how to seal it. I'd like to make radishes along with it.

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_308.text: For pickling Chinese cabbage, the recommended salt amount is 3%-5% of the cabbage's weight. Press it down with a stone and pickle at about 20°C for 15-20 days. For radishes, cut them into strips, dry them in the sun until half dry, and add salt and chili peppers. The key is to seal it from air; add water to the jar mouth or use a sealed bag.

session_308.text: Today I had Zhe Zhe do 5 addition and subtraction problems within 10. He got them all right, so I rewarded him with a cartoon, and he was very happy. But besides doing problems every day, what other ways are there to break his careless habit?

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_308.text: You want to correct his specific type of carelessness (e.g., reading questions too quickly and copying numbers incorrectly) while keeping his interest in learning?

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_308.text: Right, he often misses digits when copying numbers, and he rushes as soon as he starts doing problems. Would rewarding him with cartoons just make him care only about speed?

session_308.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_308.text: You could introduce a 'step check card': after finishing each problem, cross out the original number and check the alignment. For rewards, I suggest combining a points system, with watching cartoons as an accumulated reward. A fully correct problem earns one point, and you watch only after collecting 5 points, cultivating patience.

session_310.text: The teacher assigned homework to make a self-introduction in Word. We need to adjust the font, font size, and alignment, but I'm afraid I'll mix up the steps. Can you teach me how to do it step by step?

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_310.text: No problem. First open a blank document and type, then select the text. Set the font and size: click the Home tab, choose SimHei or SimSun in the Font box, and choose Small Four or Five in the Size box. For color, black is fine. Alignment: click the Center or Align Left button in the paragraph area. Finally press Ctrl+S to save, and name the file “Self-Introduction.”

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_310.text: Should we also set line spacing and first-line indent? What content should generally be written in a self-introduction?

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_310.text: You can set line spacing to 1.5: select the text, right-click Paragraph, and under "Line spacing" choose 1.5 lines. For a two-character first-line indent: in the same Paragraph dialog, under "Special" choose "First line" and set it to 2 characters. For the self-introduction, I suggest you write: name, age, where you're from, family situation, and your original reason for learning computers.

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_310.text: I'm helping my elementary school son with math word problems, but he always doesn't understand the problem, and he doesn't listen when I explain. Are there any good methods?

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_310.text: You can try turning word problems into real-life scenarios, for example using examples of buying groceries or dividing fruit. Or draw pictures to help him understand intuitively. First read the problem and circle the key numbers and the question, then slowly guide him to set up the equation himself. Don't just give him the answer.

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_310.text: Drawing is a good idea, but I'm not well educated and I'm afraid I won't explain it well. Is there a simpler way?

session_310.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_310.text: It's not complicated. For example, use small sticks at home or your fingers as props to show the change in quantity. The key is to ask the child more often, 'What does the problem say? What is it asking us to find?' to develop his habit of reading the problem carefully. Also, encourage him more and don't be anxious; praise him when he does it right, to reduce his fear of difficulty.

session_311.text: This afternoon, neighbors Sun Lihua and Zhao Xiaohong came to my house. I showed them the new fabric hair flowers I had made. They each picked out two, and that sold for 20 yuan altogether! I wrote 'off to a great start' in my ledger.

session_311.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_311.text: You want to first reinforce AutoSum and then practice the basic functions of Word? I suggest you use your household daily expenses as practice: list a few expense items in Excel, select the numbers, and click the ‘AutoSum’ button on the toolbar — it will give you the total. Practice a few more times and you'll remember it.

session_311.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_311.text: Yes, I happen to remember the cost of buying groceries, so I can practice this. How do I resize an image after inserting it into Word? The teacher mentioned it briefly today, and I didn't catch it all.

session_311.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_311.text: After inserting an image, click the image and small squares will appear around it. Drag a small square at a corner to scale it proportionally. To move it, right-click the image, select 'Text Wrap', and change it to 'Square' so you can drag it anywhere. Now you can open Word and follow the steps in the notes to practice; you'll get the hang of it quickly.

I can first help you design a simple spreadsheet, then analyze nearby event opportunities.

session_311.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_311.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant

session_312.text: I'm sewing new hair flowers using the indigo floral fabric my younger sister sent. I want them to look prettier and be more popular in the market. What style and decoration suggestions do you have?

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_312.text: Indigo floral fabric suits a vintage style. A bow-style design is recommended, decorated with light-colored lace or pearls to add layering. You could also try a knotted-button hair flower with small tassels for a more distinctive look.

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_312.text: I'm fairly familiar with the bow style. How exactly should the pearls be added? Is the cost high?

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_312.text: Pearls can be glued to the center of the bow with a hot glue gun or used to decorate the edges. The cost is low; a small pack of pearls is enough. Be sure to choose pearls of uniform size to avoid wrinkling the fabric.

session_312.text: I just pruned and cleaned the fuchsia and begonia and moved them into the enclosed balcony. It's 5°C outside. I'm worried about their winter care. What should I pay attention to?

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_312.text: An enclosed balcony can generally stay above 10°C during the day, but the temperature may drop suddenly at night; it is recommended to keep it between 5-15°C. Water when the soil is dry on the surface but still slightly moist below; water thoroughly after the topsoil has dried out, and stop fertilizing in winter. Pay attention to ventilation and light. You can put a plastic bag over the plant to keep it warm and prevent gray mold.

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_312.text: So how exactly do you determine when to water? Does the plastic bag need to be breathable?

session_312.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_312.text: You can insert a finger 2-3 cm into the soil and water only when it is dry. When covering with a plastic bag, leave small holes for ventilation, or open it during the day for air circulation. If water spots appear on the leaves, clean them up promptly to prevent gray mold.

session_314.text: I just learned the SUM formula, but I still have to hand-calculate the monthly balance in the account book. Is there an easier way?

session_314.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_314.text: Do you want to automatically calculate the monthly balance of income minus expenses? You can use a simple subtraction formula, for example, enter =income cell - expense cell in the balance cell, so that every time you update the income and expense figures, the balance changes automatically.

session_314.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_314.text: Right, that's exactly what I mean. But what if I add an expense row — will the formula be messed up?

session_314.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_314.text: I suggest you write the formula as an absolute reference like =SUM(start cell:end cell), or use the spreadsheet tool to automatically expand the range. You can also learn the SUMIF function to sum by category—for example, mark 'education expenses' and then sum them. Take it step by step, it's not difficult.

session_315.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_315.text: Teacher Yang suggested the 'Daily Clear' method: five calculation problems a day. My son did them but, being careless, still got two wrong. Is there a more systematic approach, such as specific methods for training attention, or should we add other subjects?

session_315.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_315.text: You can try the Pomodoro Technique: let your child focus on studying for 15 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, and gradually extend the time. The Schulte grid (5 minutes a day) can also train visual focus. As for subjects, don't add too many at first. Once arithmetic problems are stable, add Chinese handwriting practice or English words, 10 minutes each time. Gradually switch rewards from watching cartoons to small stickers or an "achievement wall" to cultivate intrinsic motivation.

session_315.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_315.text: Switch the rewards to stickers and an achievement wall. How does that work? Can it make him want to do practice problems on his own?

session_315.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_315.text: First, draw a “progress ladder” with the child. Each time he completes the daily checklist (getting everything right or proactively correcting mistakes), he earns a sticker. Collecting 5 stickers lets him redeem an activity he likes, such as going to the park. At the same time, review with him regularly: look at the accumulated stickers, praise his persistence, and gradually help him feel the sense of accomplishment of “I can control myself,” slowly reducing reliance on rewards.

session_320.text: What you did today is very scientific. I recommend adding cat stretches, wall standing, and towel exercises to your current routine to strengthen your core and back and prevent chronic strain.

session_320.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_320.text: Can these movements be done at home? I do a lot of cooking and mopping, so my back easily gets sore. How exactly do I do the cat stretch you mentioned? Also, my mother is 66 years old and may have similar problems; how can I explain it to her simply and effectively?

session_320.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_320.text: It is completely feasible at home. Cat stretch: kneel on hands and knees; inhale, drop the lower back and lift the head; exhale, round the back and lower the head. Repeat 10 times to relieve lower back stiffness. When relaying this to your mother, emphasize doing one set every morning and evening, combined with soaking feet in warm water, and avoid bending over for long periods. I suggest the two of you read authoritative books such as Prevention and Health Care of Common Diseases in Middle-Aged and Elderly People, and you can mark and share key chapters.

session_322.text: Today at 1:30 p.m. I had a 40-minute face-to-face meeting with homeroom teacher Han Mei at Jinghai Experimental Middle School. She said my son Mingxuan (13 years old, eighth grade) failed history, has been missing homework assignments, and also spaces out in class. session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_322.text: You're very thoughtful, and taking the initiative to communicate with the teacher is already the first step. Teenagers need respect and trust; direct lecturing will cause resistance. I guess what you need are specific, actionable methods—such as how to bring up the history grade, how to balance his favorite science experiments with schoolwork, while avoiding conflict, right?

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_322.text: Yes, he has been really into science experiments lately and puts off his homework until late at night. When I urge him, he gets annoyed. I just don’t know how to bring it up without starting an argument, and I don’t know how to help him manage his time.

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_322.text: I suggest you do this: 1) Start by expressing your feelings with "I noticed...", for example, "I noticed you're very invested in your science experiments, but your history homework is missing. I'm a little worried. Let's see together how to arrange it?" 2) Work out a homework schedule with him, putting history homework in the time slot when he has the most energy every day (such as the first thing after school), and making science experiments a reward for finishing homework. 3) When checking homework and signing, just sign and write an encouraging sentence, such as "Your handwriting in history today is very neat," to gradually build up his sense of achievement. If he can keep it up for a week, you can reward him with an extra hour of experiments on the weekend.

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_322.text: It sounds like you went through a lot of emotional ups and downs today, from calm to sudden tension, and then forcing yourself to handle everything. You've already tried very hard. Would you like to tell me more about how you feel?

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_322.text: Am I being too strict? But I'm afraid that if I ease up, he'll fall even further behind. Neighbor Sister Zhang says children need to take things slowly, but I can't stop blaming myself.

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_322.text: It's not that you're being too strict; it's that you have too strong a sense of responsibility. There is no perfect answer in education. Every worry and effort you make today is an expression of love. I suggest you try setting aside 10 minutes each day, just listen to your child talk about school, don't rush to correct, and first understand his difficulties.

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_322.text: Hmm, I'll try it this way. But I keep worrying that the plan won't be carried out well. What if he's still the same as before?

session_322.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_322.text: You have already done very well. You do not have to expect yourself to solve all problems overnight. A child's growth is a gradual process, and your patience and adjustments are the most valuable support. Take care of yourself first, and continue tomorrow.

session_322.text: Recommend the China Science and Technology Museum and the Planetarium. They are highly interactive, and the kids will love them. The weather is good in autumn, so you can plan about 4 days. Your patience and love are the best foundation of a family.

session_323.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_323.text: Sounds like the early stage of a wind-cold cold. Foot soaking and ginger soup are right. Your nasal congestion affects sleep; you can try steaming your nose with hot water vapor for 5-10 minutes, or rinsing your nose with warm saline, which can quickly clear it. Also, raise your pillow when sleeping, and keep the bedroom warm and humid.

session_323.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_323.text: How exactly do I do steam inhalation for the nose and saline nasal rinse? The cold medicine I'm taking now is leftover from before. Do I need to change it?

session_323.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_323.text: Steam inhalation: pour a cup of hot water, bring your nose close to the cup and breathe in the steam (be careful not to burn yourself). For nasal rinsing, use saline solution or homemade light salt water, and rinse the nasal cavity with a nasal irrigator or dropper. For medication, if the cold medicine contains antipyretic or analgesic ingredients, it can be taken according to symptoms, but it's best to read the instructions and avoid repeated dosing. Drink plenty of warm water, keep your diet light, and temporarily avoid raw, cold, greasy, or fatty foods. If the fever lasts more than 3 days or symptoms worsen, it's recommended to visit a clinic.

session_329.text: I just got lake-blue ice silk thread and a frog-button pattern. It’s my first time trying it. Are there any beginner-friendly patterns and thread-winding tips?

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_329.text: I recommend starting with a butterfly knot or a pipa knot. Ice silk thread slips easily, so make a small knot at the beginning, use a fixing pin to secure the thread end, keep even tension while winding, and press each loop tightly. When you make it tomorrow, follow the pattern step by step.

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_329.text: How many loops exactly does the butterfly knot need? I'm afraid of getting the shape wrong.

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_329.text: Generally wind it 5 to 7 times, leaving space for the buttonhole in the middle. After winding, secure the crossing point with needle and thread, then adjust the curve. Ice silk thread has a smooth surface, so you can spray a little water to help set the shape.

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_329.text: This afternoon I built a little greenhouse for my fuchsia using thin bamboo strips, foam boards, and an old quilt. I left a small vent on the south side and wrote on the desk calendar to water it every 10 days. Now there's a cold wave with strong winds, and I'm worried my method isn't right. Could you help me take a look?

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_329.text: The idea of the greenhouse you built is good, but there are a few key points to note: the overwintering temperature for the fuchsia should ideally be kept at 5-10°C; the vent opening needs to be adjusted according to the weather—on windy days it should be reduced or closed; watering once every 10 days may be too frequent, so it is safer to water only after the potting soil is dry; if the nighttime temperature drops below 0°C, it is recommended to add an extra layer of plastic sheeting over the quilt or use a heating pad. Do you have any other temperature monitoring tools at home?

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_329.text: I don't have a thermometer. The vent is now open about 10 cm wide. Should I close it at night? I've noted the watering. But will the heating pad get too hot?

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_329.text: It is recommended to close the vents tonight and open them again once the temperature rises. Choose a low-power constant-temperature heating pad (about 10W), place it under the flowerpot, and set it to maintain 5-8°C, avoiding direct contact with the plants. On sunny days, you can briefly open the south-facing vent at noon for air exchange. You might also buy a simple thermometer and place it inside the greenhouse to monitor conditions.

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_329.text: Okay, I'll close the vent tonight and buy a heating pad and thermometer tomorrow. Are there any other winter care points to pay attention to?

session_329.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_329.text: In winter, the fuchsia enters semi-dormancy; besides controlling watering, stop fertilizing; place it in a spot with plenty of light; if it is continuously cloudy, use a grow light to supplement light for 4-6 hours a day; also, check the undersides of leaves to prevent pests and diseases caused by poor ventilation. Wait until next spring when it warms up, then gradually increase watering and move it out of the greenhouse. Do you have other flowers that also need winter care?

session_331.text: I understand you want your child to master area conversion in a relaxed way. session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: I just completed the flexible-employment social insurance subsidy eligibility confirmation at the Jinghai Town community office today. Sister Zheng said that next year the application materials need to be prepared three months in advance. I'm afraid I'll forget. Could you explain the precautions to me in detail?

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: Hello! Congratulations on completing the confirmation. Sister Zheng's suggestion is key: next year's subsidy application must be submitted before the end of August. I suggest you start now by setting a monthly reminder on your phone and preparing a dedicated folder to store your ID card, household registration booklet, social security card, both originals and copies, as well as handwritten income records. The community service center is at 022-68XXXXXX, and you can call ahead to ask whether any new policies have been introduced.

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: Okay, then what specific materials need to be prepared three months in advance next year? Does the income certificate need to be rewritten?

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: The list of materials for next year is basically unchanged: ID card, household registration booklet, social security card (make sure it is within the validity period), and the latest handwritten income record (must be totaled by month and consistent with the declared total). It is recommended that the income certificate be rewritten and signed every year; community officials will verify it on the spot. You can go to the Jinghai Town Community Comprehensive Service Center in early August 2026 to find Sister Zheng, bringing all originals and copies, and check a week in advance that everything is complete.

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: Today I used Excel to make a family income and expense table. I successfully used SUM to add up, and I also want to learn averages and sorting. How do I make WordArt labels in Word?

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: You want to make the family accounts more organized and the labels prettier, right? I can teach you Excel functions and Word formatting tricks.

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: Yes, yes, I just want to make the account book neat and put nicer labels on the jars. Teach me how!

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: In Excel, you can use AVERAGE to calculate average monthly expenses, and the sort function to arrange them by amount; in Word, insert WordArt and pictures, save as a template, and next time you can just change the text. Want to try it now?

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: Today my neighbor Wang Guilan showed me a kind of Chinese knotted button pattern that was really pretty. I'd like to learn more about the types and making methods of Chinese knotted buttons, such as the straight-line button and the butterfly button. Are there any tutorials suitable for beginners?

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: The common Chinese knot button types—the straight button, butterfly button, and pipa button—are all suitable for beginners. It is recommended to start with the straight button. You will need 0.3 cm wide cotton cord or silk thread, a lighter, tweezers, and glue. There are detailed slow video tutorials on Bilibili; search for 'straight button tutorial' and you will find them. In addition, the Qiaoshoufang handicraft materials store in Jinghai District, Tianjin, has a complete variety of goods and is a good place for you and Sister Wang to buy thread together.

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_333.text: Great, I happen to want to use it for my granddaughter's clothes. Where exactly is Qiaoshoufang? Sister Wang and I plan to go next week.

session_333.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_333.text: Clever Hands Workshop is at No. 23 Shengli Street, Jinghai District, near the bus stop. Opening hours are from 9 AM to 6 PM. It is recommended that you bring a pattern drawing; the shop owner can help you choose matching threads and accessories. If you want to learn online, you can also follow the Douyin blogger Lao Zhang the Craftsman. His frog button series is very clear, from knotting to application.

session_334.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_334.text: My family had a surplus of 1,350 yuan in November, and the education savings are only 500 yuan short of the year-end goal. Besides having my husband bring lunch next month and eat out less, are there other practical ways to save money? Also, are there any small-amount investment options suitable for someone like me who is extremely risk-averse?

session_334.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_334.text: On saving money: buy vegetables seasonally for storage (such as cabbages and potatoes for winter), shop during discount periods, and optimize electricity use (using high-power appliances during off-peak hours). On financial management: recommend bank time deposits (saving 200-300 yuan per month) or money market funds (such as Yu'ebao and Lingqiantong), which carry extremely low risk and can be withdrawn at any time, suitable for your situation.

session_334.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_334.text: These methods are all very practical; I've noted them down. After the education fund is fully saved by the end of the year, how should I plan the family emergency fund or long-term goals next?

session_334.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_334.text: It is recommended to first set aside 3-6 months of basic household expenses as an emergency fund (about 12,000-24,000 yuan), kept in a demand deposit or money market fund. After that, you may consider opening a dedicated education savings account for the child and depositing a fixed 200 yuan each month. For long-term goals such as the couple's retirement, you can consult the bank about low-risk pension regular investment products, but be sure to complete the emergency fund reserve first.

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: Finally met Aunt Wu today! Her home is just like a handicraft museum. I gave her a peony round fan and homemade pickled vegetables, and she gave me a cartoon bear knitted hat and taught me a complicated crochet stitch.

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: It sounds like this meeting made you very happy and moved—did it feel like finding a kindred spirit? I'm curious what the stitch you learned is called. Did you record it for future practice?

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: Yes, that's exactly the resonance of meeting a fellow enthusiast! The stitch is called a 'popcorn stitch'. I recorded the whole process. Aunt Wu taught me hands-on. From chatting online for half a year to meeting in person, it really feels like a dream.

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: The popcorn stitch has a very textured effect and looks especially great on knit hats or scarves. It's good that you recorded the video. When you get home, you can start by practicing the basic stitches, and once you're proficient, try crocheting a matching bear hat for your family—I'm sure they'll be pleasantly surprised.

session_336.text: According to the record, around 22:00 tonight, Zhiqiang confirmed that the three children had finished washing up and done their homework, and now they were all soundly asleep. session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: Just now Aunt Wu taught me a chili sauce recipe. I want to write it down. Can you help me organize it?

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: Of course. Do you want to record the proportions of bird's eye chili, fermented black beans, and rapeseed oil, as well as the cooking method and storage details?

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: Right, and also buy fresh facing-heaven chili peppers at the morning market tomorrow, and whether we can add other spices

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: Okay. Core recipe: 500 grams of facing-heaven chilies, 100 grams of fermented black beans, and 300 ml of rapeseed oil. Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, then season with salt and sugar. You can add a little Sichuan peppercorn or minced garlic for extra aroma. Let it cool, bottle it, and refrigerate; it can be stored for 1-2 months. The morning market usually has fresh facing-heaven chilies. If you can't find them, you can substitute ordinary red chilies plus dried chilies.

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: This afternoon I am at Yanling Park. I heard from Aunt Wu that this place is connected to Baiyangdian, with reed marshes and folk culture. I want to prepare for bringing my family here for a visit in the future. Can you introduce some historical stories and sightseeing tips about Yanling Park and Baiyangdian?

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: Yanling Park is named after the Yanling Detachment, which operated in the reed marshes of Baiyangdian during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. In winter, Baiyangdian offers views of icy reeds and the chance to experience folk activities such as playing the erhu and playing chess. It is recommended to check transportation from Renqiu to Baiyangdian. It is suitable for family boating and birdwatching, and there are farmstay accommodations nearby.

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_336.text: That's great, so is it convenient from Renqiu to Jinghai? What can the kids play?

session_336.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_336.text: From Renqiu to Jinghai there is an expressway and bus, about a 1-hour drive. Children can take a boat, see reeds, and join craft activities. It is recommended to arrange a one-day itinerary, and you can also combine a visit to Baiyangdian Wetland Park.

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_337.text: I just got back from the community computer training class and learned Excel's IF function, but I got confused as soon as I tried it at home. I want to add a column to the family expense sheet to automatically determine whether an expense is over budget. For example, if the utility budget is 300 and the actual cost is 350, it shows 'Over budget'; otherwise it shows 'Normal'. How should I write the formula?

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_337.text: This requirement can be done with the IF function. Assuming the budget is in column B and actual spending is in column C, you can directly enter the formula in column D: =IF(C2>B2, "Over Budget", "Normal"). After pressing Enter, drag the fill handle down to automatically judge each row.

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_337.text: Oh, I think I've got this. But what if I want to judge multiple conditions together? For example, I need to check not only whether it is over budget, but also whether it exceeds the budget by 10% — if it goes over too much, mark it as severely over budget?

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_337.text: You can nest IF functions. Suppose column C is actual and column B is budget. Write the formula as: =IF(C2>B2*1.1, "Severely over budget", IF(C2>B2, "Over budget", "Normal")). This first checks whether it exceeds 10% of the budget; if so, it marks it as severely over budget; otherwise it checks whether it is over budget. You can try it on a small range first. Feel free to ask me anytime if you have questions.

session_337.text: I often do housework and sit at a table doing handiwork. Recently I've had bad lower back and back soreness. Are there any everyday relief methods suitable for a housewife?

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_337.text: You mainly have lower back strain from bending over while washing dishes, mopping the floor, and sitting for long periods doing handicrafts. You need advice that combines stretching, posture adjustment, and traditional Chinese medicine care, right?

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_337.text: Yes, and I also want to know the correct way to soak my feet in mugwort water and whether I need to go to the hospital for an examination.

session_337.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_337.text: Recommendations: 1) Use a footstool when washing dishes and switch to a long-handled tool for mopping; 2) Do cat stretch and glute bridge 10 times each every day; 3) Soak feet in water at 40-45°C with mugwort and ginger slices for 20 minutes each time, 3-4 times a week. If pain persists for more than two weeks, it is advisable to take an X-ray to rule out lumbar spine problems.

session_338.text: Hello Xiulan! Today I just used Excel to calculate the year's accounts for pickled vegetables, and I find it very convenient. But I want to do more detailed cost accounting and profit forecasting to help expand the business in the future. Can you teach me what to do next?

session_338.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_338.text: Sister Ma, you already have a foundation! To manage it systematically, I suggest starting from three areas: 1. Use Excel to make a raw material cost breakdown table, recording the unit price and quantity of chilies, salt, and jars for each purchase; 2. Generate a monthly profit trend chart to make it easier to forecast the peak season; 3. Link inventory and sales records to avoid overstocking. Would you like to start with a cost table template?

session_338.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_338.text: Right, right. I record the raw material costs on paper and it gets messy easily. If I could use a spreadsheet to automatically calculate the total cost and percentage, that would be great. I would also really like to learn profit trend charts, so I can see which months earn more and arrange to make more pickled vegetables.

session_338.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_338.text: OK! I'll help you organize a simple template: write the ingredient name in the first column, the unit price (yuan/jin) in the second column, the amount (jin) in the third column, and in the fourth column use the formula =unit price*amount to calculate the individual cost, then use SUM at the bottom to total it. For the profit trend chart, you can select the month and net profit columns and insert a line chart to see the fluctuations at a glance. In addition, if you do a market stall in the future, you can add an 'estimated sales volume' column and use a formula to predict revenue, then work backward to decide whether to increase production.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: I just had a physical exam today. The doctor said my bone density, blood sugar, and BMI are all normal, but they also did a gynecological exam. What exactly do these results mean? I just can't stop feeling uneasy.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: You are worried about the meaning of the physical exam indicators, especially whether 'normal' really means there is no problem, and whether a gynecological exam is necessary? Also, you mentioned lower back soreness—do you also want to confirm its relationship to your health?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: Yes, the doctor only said it was normal, but I don't know whether the specific numbers are good or bad. Also, I have back soreness—is it some kind of problem? Is a gynecological exam necessary?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: Normal bone density, blood sugar and BMI show that your bones, blood sugar metabolism and weight are all in healthy ranges, but the specific values still need the official report. Lower back soreness is often caused by fatigue or poor posture. At 41, you should also pay attention to gynecological issues, so adding that check-up makes sense. It is suggested to wait for the report and compare with the reference values, drink more water, eat soy products, and avoid standing for long periods to ease the back soreness.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: Today I used a newly learned stitch to make three children's hair flowers, and my daughter loves them! Do you have other new patterns suitable for fabric scraps?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: That sounds great! Do you want to learn more simple and easy new stitching techniques, or would you like to know the details of how to make pom-poms more secure?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: I'd like to know both, especially how to keep the pom-pom from getting loose.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: You can try wrapping the thread a couple of extra times around the center of the pom-pom before tying it off, or use hot glue to secure the base. Also, lace trim and floral fabric make a great combination for hair ties.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: I use Excel to keep accounts every night. I just recorded today's expenses for registration, groceries, and fabric scraps, but I have to manually calculate the sum every time. Is there a simple formula?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: Do you need the AutoSum function? In Excel, the SUM formula is most convenient. For example, enter =SUM(selected range) at the bottom of the expense column to calculate the total monthly spending.

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_339.text: Yes, that's it. Also, I want to record grocery shopping and doctor visits separately. Can you teach me how to do that?

session_339.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_339.text: You can add a “Category” column in the spreadsheet, use a drop-down list to label each expense, and then use the SUMIF formula or a pivot table to automatically summarize by category. It’s very intuitive.

session_340.text: I just finished the embroidery draft for the order 'Blooming Flowers, Wealth and Honor' this afternoon. I drew blooming peonies and a few butterflies, and I am especially pleased with it!

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_340.text: Sounds great! Peonies symbolize wealth, and butterflies symbolize good fortune. This design has a great meaning. How long did the draft take you to finish?

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_340.text: I spent two hours drawing stroke by stroke by the window. My youngest son came over to watch, and I taught him the symbolic meanings of peonies and butterflies. He listened very carefully.

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_340.text: What a cozy afternoon. The draft composition has just the right balance of density and spacing; the client is sure to like it. Are you ready to pick the threads and stretch the fabric to start?

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_340.text: Next Saturday is my first time going to the market to sell embroidery. What do I need to prepare? Which pieces sell well? What prices should I set?

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_340.text: It is recommended to prepare a stall cloth, small change, price tags, and a simple display rack. Popular embroidered items such as window decorations, handkerchiefs, and small pendants sell better. For pricing, refer to the market conditions: small items 10-20 yuan, medium items 30-50 yuan. Apply for a WeChat payment QR code in advance for convenient payment.

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_340.text: How do I apply for a receiving-code? Should I let the neighboring stall owner know?

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_340.text: You can apply for a WeChat payment QR code for free in WeChat Pay, then print and paste it up. When you get there, take the initiative to greet the neighboring stall owner and chat a little. If necessary, keep an eye on each other's stalls. Having someone to help makes your first time vending go more smoothly.

session_340.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_340.text: Tonight while keeping the accounts I found that my husband spends more than 600 yuan a month on cigarettes. I'm under a lot of pressure. I want to persuade him to smoke less but I'm afraid of hurting our relationship. What should I do?

session_341.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_341.text: Today I practiced single crochet for the first time. The coaster I crocheted isn't round; it's crooked. How can I make it flat and even?

session_341.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_341.text: It is recommended that you use the magic ring method and increase 6 stitches evenly in each round: Round 1: 6 stitches; Round 2: increase 1 stitch in every stitch (12 stitches); Round 3: increase 1 stitch in every other stitch (18 stitches); and so on. Also keep your tension consistent, avoiding tight and loose spots.

session_341.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_341.text: It turns out I need to add 6 stitches each round, but I can't get the placement of the increases right. Also, how can I tell if my tension is even?

session_341.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_341.text: The increase positions can be staggered. For example, don't make an increase in the same stitch on the next round where you increased in the previous round, to avoid forming a polygon. As for hand tension, practice the same stitch more to find the most relaxed and stable way to hold the needle, use your middle finger to help guide the yarn and control tightness, and you can start with a simple small coaster.

session_344.text: I'm embroidering a double-sided peony. When using gold thread for seed stitches on the butterfly antennae, the thread keeps tangling and the curves come out stiff. session_344.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_344.text: Gold thread is stiff and slippery, so it tangles easily. You can try lightly pulling the thread across beeswax twice to increase friction; when starting a stitch, leave a short tail and hold it down with your thumb; before each stitch, smooth the thread with your hand. With even spacing between stitches, the proper tension will emerge.

session_344.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_344.text: I'm helping my fourth-grade son with math word problems, but he just can't understand them, and I find it hard to teach him. Is there a simple and effective way to explain?

session_344.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_344.text: You can try the step-by-step line segment diagram method: use line segments to represent the quantitative relationships in the problem, then replace the characters in the problem with people the child is familiar with, such as you and his younger sister, to lower the barrier to understanding. Encourage the child to first read the problem and draw the diagram themselves, then guide them to explain their thinking step by step, fostering independent thinking.

session_344.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_344.text: This method sounds good. I'll try drawing a line-segment diagram first. But I tend to get impatient when tutoring. What if the child still doesn't understand?

session_344.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_344.text: When tutoring, set a small goal first: spend only 10 minutes on each problem. If the child still doesn't understand after two explanations, set it aside to avoid emotions escalating. Encourage the child to say where they are stuck; you only hint at key points and let them complete the thinking themselves. If you really can't help, find simple free online courses as a supplement (for example, elementary school word problem explanations on Bilibili).

session_345.text: I just received a new order today for "Magpie on a Plum Branch." The client, Wang Lihua, was very satisfied with the previous "Wealth and Honor in Bloom." This time it's a New Year ornament, and I'm working on the composition and color scheme. I'd like to ask: in traditional embroidery, how should magpies and plum blossoms be combined to look vivid?

session_345.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_345.text: It is recommended to use the classic composition of a magpie looking back while perched on a plum branch. In terms of color, red plum blossoms contrast vividly with black feathers and a white belly. For the stitching, the plum blossoms can use the overlapping stitch, and the magpie's feathers can use the rolling stitch to show the silk texture. Adding some gold thread accents will enhance the festive feel.

session_345.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_345.text: Is the overlapping stitch suitable for plum blossom petals? I used to use seed stitch to embroider the stamens. Should the plum blossom stamens also use seed stitch this time?

session_345.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_345.text: Using the overlapping stitch for petals can show gradient layers; seed stitch is very suitable for the stamens. Bright yellow silk thread can be used to create a slight contrast with the red plum blossoms. For the branches, it is recommended to use split stitch or robbing stitch, with thickness variations to reflect old trunks and new branches.

session_346.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_346.text: I just bought dark blue and silver-white sequins today, planning to embroider the magpie feathers of "Magpie on a Plum Branch". But I don't know how to use the sequins to create a gradual shiny effect, and I'm not sure how to attach them securely. What should I embroider first as the next step?

session_346.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_346.text: It is recommended to first secure the sequins with the couching method: pass the needle through the sequin hole, bring the thread around the edge of the sequin and stitch back, with two stitches per sequin. Start from the base of the feather with dark sequins, transition to silver-white at the edges, and overlap them to enhance the layers. For the overall composition, it is recommended to first embroider the outline of the magpie's body, then fill in the sequins, and finally embroider the plum blossoms to avoid deformation.

session_346.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_346.text: I understand the couching method. Do the sequins need to overlap? How should the light and dark sequins be arranged to look more like real feathers?

session_346.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_346.text: They need to be overlapped: lay dark blue sequins on the lower layer, and cover the edges with light blue or silver-white sequins on the upper layer to create a scale-like overlap. Arrange them from dense to sparse according to the direction of feather growth, with dark colors at the base and light colors at the tips, to imitate the natural transition of feathers. For cleaning, it is recommended to wipe gently with a soft cloth; do not soak in water to prevent them from falling off.

session_347.text: You want the album to both reflect warm memories and last a long time. Do you need suggestions on layout style (timeline or themed categories) and long-term care?

session_347.text: Yes, I mainly want to arrange them in chronological order, but there are too many photos of the kids' activities and I'm afraid it'll be messy. Also, can photos taken on a phone have their colors adjusted?

session_347.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_347.text: It is recommended to use a timeline as the main thread, and insert a "highlight" two-page spread for each period, such as a collage of the children's sports day. For phone photos, you can ask a print shop to do basic color grading (brightening, noise reduction); it's not expensive. After picking them up, keep the album away from light and moisture. Ideally, use album protective film.

session_347.speaker: Ma Xiulan

session_347.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_347.text: If your budget is limited, I suggest making one main album first; later, printing additional inner pages with the same cover is cheaper. Alternatively, after you pick up the main album, you can photograph it with your phone and print it online, saving about 30%. For parents, a clear reprint of a family photo is already precious enough.

session_348.text: I want to open a shop on Taobao with a friend to sell handicrafts, but I only have a junior high school education and am not familiar with computers. Can it work? Can I operate it on a phone?

session_348.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_348.text: You can open a store on your phone; Taobao has a dedicated app, and the registration process is simple. You don't need a computer. You have street-stall experience, and you can learn photography and pricing gradually. The initial investment is small and the risk is controllable.

session_348.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_348.text: How much is the deposit? I don't know how to take product photos. How do I set prices? How does shipping work? I'm afraid of being scammed.

session_348.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_348.text: The deposit for a personal shop is 1,000 yuan (refundable). For product photos, just use a phone with natural light and a simple background. First, refer to the pricing of similar products. For logistics, choose Cainiao Station; the cost is low. I suggest you and Xiuqin divide the work: she handles taking photos and putting products online, while you handle production and shipping. Also be cautious about any requests to pay extra fees to avoid scams.

session_348.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_348.text: This gives me a bit more confidence. But if the online store opens, I'm afraid there will be too much to handle at home, and I also need to take care of Chunmei's pickled vegetable orders.

session_348.text: You need to balance family, handicrafts, and an online store? Zhiqiang supports not investing too much money; test the market in the early stage, and adjust the pace once things pick up.

session_348.text: I'm really happy for you, Sister Ma! From the details you shared, having your craft recognized is the greatest sense of achievement. The customers' feedback and your friends' enthusiastic help all prove that your efforts are valuable.

session_348.text: With your family's support and your plans for the future, the online store will definitely take off. session_348.text: Chunmei said the supermarket is almost out of pickled vegetables and asked me to deliver 20 jars next Sunday. But I didn't ask about the specifications, price, or payment method. Can you help me sort out what details I need to confirm?

session_348.text: It is suggested to first contact Chunmei to get the supermarket manager's phone number and confirm packaging requirements and label details. If time is tight, deliveries can be made in batches; in terms of costs, raw materials plus packaging are about 3 yuan per bottle, and a recommended price of 8-10 yuan gives a considerable profit.

session_349.text: For the Shake Head and Wag Tail exercise, suggestions: 1. When squatting, keep your weight on your heels and do not let your knees pass your toes; 2. When turning your head, inhale slowly first, then exhale as you turn to one side, feeling the twist of the spine; 3. Head movements should be gentle; do not turn suddenly. session_349.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_349.text: I pickled cabbage today using the recipe Chunmei taught me, but I'm not sure how much salt to use. Should I change the water halfway through?

session_349.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_349.text: The ratio of salt for pickling napa cabbage is usually 3%-5% of the cabbage weight. First salt it for 2-3 hours to draw out the water, then squeeze it dry and mix in the seasonings; there is no need to change the water. Keep the fermentation temperature at 15-20°C, seal it tightly and press it down, and it can be eaten in about 7 days.

session_349.speaker: Ma Xiulan
session_349.text: Got it. How should the pickled vegetables be stored after they are made so they last longer? Also, I plan to set up a stall at the vegetable market. What price is appropriate?

session_349.speaker: Ma Xiulan's Assistant
session_349.text: Once sealed, the pickled vegetables can be stored in the refrigerator for 1-2 months and should be kept out of direct sunlight. For a street stall, small bag packaging is recommended (about 200g). The spicy cabbage can be priced at 6-8 yuan per bag, and after market research the price can be adjusted according to cost. Use transparent food bags with labels to emphasize that the product is handmade and additive-free.
